summary: The classical étale cohomology of analytic adic spaces that the theory of diamonds uses, layers H0–H3, planned at target level (PROTOCOL §2) within the RS-05 narrowing. H0 gives the classical analytic instances of DiamondsAndVStacks D0's and EnhancedDerivedSheaves E1's sheaf and derived carriers on AdicEtaleGeometry A1's étale sites (sheaves of modules, derived direct images, Leray, Čech-to-derived, Cartan–Leray, pro-étale comparison), torsion local systems, Huber's constructible sheaves, Tate twists, supports and extension by zero, geometric stalks at field pairs with higher-rank plus rings kept, the strict-localisation stalk formula, the pseudo-adic étale site, and Huber's tilde-limits (the topology and density conditions separately) with their affinoid criterion and cohomological continuity. H1 is the umbrella comparing its four sub-stages with each other and with the trait theory of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles (Huber's nearby cycles are RΨ, not RΦ). H1:henselian builds henselian f-adic rings (a complete f-adic ring is henselian, with a public proof), affinoid and pro-special henselisations and Huber's comparison theorems of §3.2; H1:formal-adic-comparison builds the specialisation morphism of a formal scheme of type (S), pseudo-adic supports, the stalk formulas and the comparison i*Rj_*K ≅ Rb_*a*K with its torsion scope, microbial valuation bases and the identification with RΨ; H1:valuation-nearby-cycles and H1:valuation-exports build nearby cycles over arbitrary valuation bases with base change for torsion prime to the residue characteristic, constructibility, invariance for surjective valuation-spectrum maps and finiteness; H2 proves invariance under extension of an algebraically closed complete field in the form ECD Lemma 16.3 uses, and geometric connectedness under base extension; H3 builds proper-support direct images in Huber's classical scope with base change and the dimension bound, and the trace and Poincaré duality for smooth curves. Huber's 1996 book is not public: it is cited only through excerpts verified by reviewed decompositions, statements rest on public restatements (ECD, Berkovich, Orgogozo, Illusie, Lu–Zheng, Hansen–Zavyalov, Bhatt–Hansen, Hansen, the Stacks Project, Huber's public papers), and proof inputs available only in the book are gaps. This planning pass (300 nodes, 302 after its independent review) incorporates arbitrary-preadic ℤ_p/ℚ_p local systems and de Jong analytic monodromy (KL §8.4), Česnavičius’s perfectoid limit of the Noetherian generic-henselization comparison, semistable formal Kummer symbols and the non-quasi-compact BKH filtration (CDN §2.1.1), and arbitrary-dimensional classical traces/prime-to-residue duality with the Guo–Reinecke integral normalization export. Five stages are planned; the two valuation stages and H3 retain exact remaining targets. Complete means that the budgeted planning pass is finished, not that its proof gaps or supplier requests are closed.

nodes.title: The affinoid étale basis is essentially small, so étale sheaf categories are Grothendieck abelian
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair) with small étale site X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site) and affinoid étale basis X_ét^aff (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison: objects isomorphic to chains Spa(D_m) → ⋯ → Spa(D_0) = V ⊆ X of rational localisations and finite étale pairs over open affinoids V of X). Then: (a) X_ét^aff is essentially small: there is a cardinal κ(X), depending only on a chosen open affinoid cover (V_α = Spa(A_α, A_α⁺))_α of X, such that every object of X_ét^aff is isomorphic to Spa(D, D⁺) with |D| ≤ κ(X); (b) consequently, for every ring Λ, the category Sh(X_ét, Λ) of sheaves of Λ-modules on X_ét is equivalent to Sh(X_ét^aff, Λ) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison (c)), has sheafification, and is a Grothendieck abelian category; in particular it has enough injectives; the same holds for sheaves of modules over any sheaf of rings R on X_ét (Mathlib `SheafOfModules`); (c) for X locally noetherian and nonempty, the pro-étale site X_proét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected) is not essentially small; for every cutoff cardinal κ (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal) the full subcategory X_proét,κ of pro-étale objects presented by κ-small cofiltered diagrams of X_ét^aff, with the induced topology, is essentially small, closed under fibre products and under the covers of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/corrected-covers-pretopology refined by κ-small ones, so Sh(X_proét,κ, Λ) and Sh(X_proét,κ, R) are Grothendieck abelian; for κ ≤ κ′ the pullback functors Sh(X_proét,κ, Λ) → Sh(X_proét,κ′, Λ) along the inclusion of sites (left adjoint to restriction) are fully faithful and commute with the cohomology functors H^i(U, −) of objects U of X_ét, and sheaves and cohomology on X_proét are defined as the colimit over κ.
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic; for (c) X locally noetherian analytic.
Λ an arbitrary ring; R an arbitrary sheaf of rings on the site in question.
The cardinal bound is a size statement, not a finiteness statement: X need not be quasi-compact.
proofSteps: (a) Every object of X_ét^aff is covered by the chains of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison; for a chain over V = Spa(A, A⁺), each rational localisation is the completion of A[1/s] with |A⟨T/s⟩| ≤ |A|^ℵ₀ (a completion of a ring with a countable basis of neighbourhoods of zero is a quotient of the set of Cauchy sequences; DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/completion-cardinality-bound), and each finite étale step is a finite projective module over the previous ring, so the cardinality grows by at most ℵ₀-powers at each of finitely many steps; the rational data (finite sets T, s) and finite étale algebras (finite presentations) over a ring of cardinality ≤ κ form a set of cardinality ≤ κ; hence the isomorphism classes of chains over the V_α form a set.

(b) X_ét^aff → X_ét is a dense subsite (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison (c)), so Sh(X_ét, Λ) ≃ Sh(X_ét^aff, Λ) by mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsDenseSubsite.sheafEquiv; on the essentially small X_ét^aff, mathlib:CategoryTheory.Sheaf.isGrothendieckAbelian_of_essentiallySmall with A = ModuleCat Λ (Grothendieck abelian) gives the Grothendieck property; for sheaves of R-modules use the Grothendieck instance of mathlib:SheafOfModules on the small model and transport along the equivalence; enough injectives by mathlib:CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian.enoughInjectives.

(c) Size of X_proét: the objects lim U_i include limits over index categories of every cardinality (products with profinite sets of arbitrary weight, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-set-objects), so no small skeleton exists. With a cutoff cardinal κ, κ-small presentations by objects of the essentially small X_ét^aff form an essentially small category; κ-small refinements of corrected covers exist because a quasi-compact object admits a finite subcover (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-coherence) and each member is a κ-small limit (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal). Full faithfulness of the pullback (transition) functors and independence of κ follow the convention of ECD §14 (definition of D(Y_qproét, Λ) as a colimit over κ with fully faithful transition functors).
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, K⁺) with K a complete nonarchimedean field and K⁺ of rank one, X_ét^aff is equivalent to the opposite of the category of finite étale K-algebras, which is essentially small, and Sh(X_ét, Λ) is equivalent to the category of discrete Gal(K^sep/K)-modules over Λ.
Sh(X_ét, Λ) has enough injectives, so Mathlib's `Functor.rightDerivedFunctorPlus` applies to Γ(U, −) and to g_*.

sources.match: The stable affinoid basis whose essential smallness is proved here; sheaves on X_ét are sheaves on it.

The convention for sites not generated by a set of objects: pass to κ-small subsites and take the colimit over κ, used here for X_proét.

nodes.title: Étale and pro-étale sheaves of modules on analytic adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space with small étale site X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site) and Λ a ring. The category of étale sheaves of Λ-modules is Sh(X_ét, Λ) := `Sheaf (AdicSpace.smallEtaleTopology X) (ModuleCat Λ)`; more generally for a sheaf of rings R on X_ét (the constant sheaf Λ_X, the structure sheaf O_{X_ét} of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf, or O⁺_{X_ét}) the category Mod(X_ét, R) := `SheafOfModules R`; for X locally noetherian the same definitions on X_proét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected; size handled by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/affinoid-etale-basis-essentially-small). Structure: (i) Sh(X_ét, Λ) is Grothendieck abelian with enough injectives and Sh(X_ét, Λ) ≃ Mod(X_ét, Λ_X); (ii) Γ(U, −): Sh(X_ét, Λ) → Mod_Λ, F ↦ F(U), for U ∈ X_ét, left exact; (iii) the constant sheaf M_X := sheafification of the constant presheaf M (Mathlib `constantSheaf`) with Hom(M_X, F) = Hom_Λ(M, F(X)); for every U ∈ X_ét, M_X(U) is the module of locally constant functions |U| → M; (iv) for a morphism g: X′ → X of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces, g_* (sections (g_*F)(U) = F(U ×_X X′)) with exact left adjoint g^{-1} (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site (iv)); (v) for u: U → X in X_ét, restriction u^{-1}F = F|_U identified with Mathlib's `overPullback` under U_ét ≃ X_ét/U (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/slice-site); (vi) stalks F_ξ at geometric points ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → X with C⁺ of any rank (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points) are exact, commute with colimits and jointly detect isomorphisms, monomorphisms, epimorphisms and zero objects (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-enough-points); (vii) change of coefficients along Λ → Λ′ (restriction and extension of scalars); (viii) ν^{-1} and ν_* along ν: X_proét → X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-projection-nu). These are the carriers of D0's ordinary generic sheaf interface (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0) and of E1's module sheaves (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/sheaves-of-modules-and-the-grothendieck-property) on the classical analytic étale and pro-étale sites; no second site is constructed.
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic (locally noetherian for the pro-étale clause).
Coverings are A1's jointly surjective families on all points, including points of higher rank.
Λ is any ring; torsion hypotheses on Λ are imposed only by the theorems that need them.
proofSteps: Category and structure: Sheaf over A1's étale topology with values in mathlib:ModuleCat; Grothendieck abelian with enough injectives by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/affinoid-etale-basis-essentially-small; the equivalence with mathlib:SheafOfModules over the constant sheaf of rings Λ_X is the identity on underlying presheaves.

Constant sheaves: mathlib:CategoryTheory.constantSheaf with its adjunction to sections over the terminal object X; the presheaf U ↦ LC(|U|, M) of locally constant functions is an étale sheaf (a compatible family on a covering (U_i → U) defines a function on |U| because |U_i ×_U U_j| → |U_i| ×_{|U|} |U_j| is surjective, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change, and it is locally constant because étale maps are open, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-open-map), and the map from the constant presheaf M is locally bijective, so LC(|−|, M) is its sheafification.

Direct and inverse image: mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous and mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullback along the base-change functor of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site (iv), which preserves finite limits, hence is representably flat (mathlib:CategoryTheory.flat_of_preservesFiniteLimits, mathlib:CategoryTheory.RepresentablyFlat); on the small models of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/affinoid-etale-basis-essentially-small the left Kan extension along it preserves finite limits (mathlib:CategoryTheory.lan_preservesFiniteLimits_of_flat, stated for small categories), which is the remaining hypothesis of mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.preservesFiniteLimits; so g^{-1} is exact.
Restriction: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/slice-site and mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.overPullback.

Stalks: mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.sheafFiber at the points of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points; detection by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-enough-points (mathlib:CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsConservativeFamilyOfPoints), transferred from sheaves of sets to sheaves of modules because the forgetful functor ModuleCat Λ → Type preserves filtered colimits and finite limits.
Pro-étale: the same constructions on X_proét,κ, with ν from AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-projection-nu.
acceptance: For M ≠ 0 and X = U ⊔ V with |U|, |V| nonempty and connected, the constant presheaf M (value M on every object) is not a sheaf, while M_X(X) = M ⊕ M.

For X = Spa(K, O_K) with K a complete nonarchimedean field (rank-one plus ring) and ξ given by K ⊆ C, F ↦ F_ξ is an equivalence of Sh(X_ét, Λ) with discrete Λ[Gal(K^sep/K)]-modules (de Jong–van der Put §3.3; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic (c)).

nodes.title: Restriction to étale objects and direct image preserve injectives; cohomology of an étale object is cohomology of its étale site
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space, Λ a ring and R a sheaf of rings on X_ét. (a) For u: U → X in X_ét, the restriction u^{-1}: Mod(X_ét, R) → Mod(U_ét, R|_U) has an exact left adjoint u_! (extension by zero: the sheafification of the presheaf left Kan extension along the forgetful functor X_ét/U → X_ét), hence u^{-1} is exact and preserves injective objects; (b) for g: X′ → X, the direct image g_* has the exact left adjoint g^{-1}, hence preserves injective objects; (c) consequently, for F ∈ Mod(X_ét, R) and U ∈ X_ét, the groups H^n(U, F) := R^nΓ(U, −)(F) computed in Mod(X_ét, R) agree with H^n(U_ét, F|_U) computed in Mod(U_ét, R|_U), naturally in F and compatibly with restriction along morphisms of X_ét; (d) the same statements hold on X_proét,κ for X locally noetherian (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-slice).
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic; U ∈ X_ét.
R an arbitrary sheaf of rings (Λ_X is the case of Λ-modules).
proofSteps: (a) Under U_ét ≃ X_ét/U (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/slice-site), u^{-1} is mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.overPullback, i.e. pushforward along the continuous and cocontinuous forgetful functor Over.forget U; its left adjoint is mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullback along Over.forget U, computed as the sheafification of the pointwise left Kan extension; on stalks at a geometric point ξ of X it is ⊕ over the lifts ū of ξ to U of the stalks at ū, a direct sum of exact functors, so it is exact (stalkwise detection: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules (vi)).
Exactness of u^{-1}: it is evaluation of presheaves composed with the slice equivalence, and sheafification commutes with it.
Injectives: mathlib:CategoryTheory.Injective.injective_of_adjoint applied to u_! ⊣ u^{-1} and to g^{-1} ⊣ g_* (both left adjoints are exact, in particular preserve monomorphisms).

(c) Compute H^n(U, F) with an injective resolution F → I^• in Mod(X_ét, R) (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerived via mathlib:CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution); by (a) I^•|_U is an injective resolution of F|_U, and Γ(U, I^•) = Γ(U_ét, I^•|_U).
(d) The same argument on the κ-small pro-étale sites, using AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-slice for the slice equivalence.
acceptance: For U ⊆ X an open subspace, H^n(U, F) computed in X_ét equals H^n(U_ét, F|_U).

For a finite étale Galois cover π: U → X with group G and I injective in Sh(X_ét, Λ), Γ(U, I) is an injective, hence G-acyclic, Λ[G]-module (in general not an induced one): Γ(U, −) has the exact left adjoint M ↦ π_!Λ_U ⊗_{Λ[G]} M, π_!Λ_U being étale-locally free of rank one over Λ[G].

Cohomology of objects is computed with injective sheaves on the ambient site, which is legitimate because restriction preserves injectives.

nodes.title: Higher direct images are sheafifications of cohomology presheaves
nodes.statement: Let u: (C, J) → (C′, J′) be one of the following continuous functors preserving finite limits, defining a morphism of sites f: (C′, J′) → (C, J) with direct image f_*F = F ∘ u: (1) base change U ↦ U ×_X X′ from X_ét to X′_ét for a morphism g: X′ → X of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces (f = g_ét, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site (iv)); (2) the constant-pro-object functor c: X_ét → X_proét for X locally noetherian (f = ν, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-projection-nu); (3) base change along a morphism of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces on pro-étale sites. Let R′ be a sheaf of rings on C′ and F an R′-module. Then for every q ≥ 0 the sheaf R^q f_* F is canonically isomorphic to the sheafification of the presheaf U ↦ H^q(u(U), F) on C, naturally in F and compatibly with the connecting maps. In particular R^qν_*F is the sheafification of U ↦ H^q(c(U), F) with U regarded as an object of X_proét, and R^q g_*F is the sheafification of U ↦ H^q(U ×_X X′, F).
hypotheses: u continuous and finite-limit preserving, so that f_* has the exact left adjoint f^{-1}.
F a sheaf of R′-modules (in particular of Λ-modules or abelian groups).
proofSteps: Choose an injective resolution F → I^• in Mod(C′, R′) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/affinoid-etale-basis-essentially-small gives enough injectives); R^q f_* F = H^q(f_* I^•) (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerived).

The cohomology sheaf of a complex of sheaves is the sheafification of the presheaf cohomology: kernels of sheaves are computed in presheaves and cokernels are the sheafifications of presheaf cokernels, sheafification being exact (mathlib:CategoryTheory.presheafToSheaf is left exact and a left adjoint).

The presheaf cohomology at U is H^q(I^•(u(U))) = H^q(Γ(u(U), I^•)), and this is H^q(u(U), F) because Γ(u(U), −) is computed on the injective resolution I^• (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-restriction-preserves-injectives (c)).
Naturality and δ-compatibility: both sides are δ-functors in F, and the identification is induced by the natural map of presheaves U ↦ H^q(u(U), F) → R^q f_*F(U).
acceptance: q = 0: R^0 f_*F = f_*F, and the presheaf U ↦ F(u(U)) is already a sheaf.
Scholze's Corollary 3.17 (i): R^iν_*ν^*F is the sheaf associated to U ↦ H^i(U, ν^*F) with U regarded in X_proét.

nodes.title: Cohomology of sheaves of modules agrees with cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaves
nodes.statement: Let (C, J) be the étale site X_ét of a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space X, or the κ-small pro-étale site X_proét,κ of a locally noetherian one, and R a sheaf of rings on it. Let forget: Mod(C, R) → Sh(C, ℤ) be the forgetful functor. Then: (a) every injective R-module I is acyclic for every section functor Γ(U, −) on abelian sheaves: H^n(U, forget I) = 0 for n > 0 and every U; (b) hence for every R-module F and U, the natural map R^nΓ(U, −)(F) → H^n(U, forget F) is an isomorphism, compatible with long exact sequences; (c) for a morphism of sites g: (C′, J′) → (C, J) induced by a continuous finite-limit-preserving functor (for example g_ét of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site (iv), or ν of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-projection-nu), a sheaf of rings R′ on C′ and an R′-module F, the higher direct images of F computed in g_*R′-modules and in abelian sheaves agree: forget ∘ R^q g_* ≅ R^q g_* ∘ forget; in particular Rν_* of a sheaf of Ô_X-modules on X_proét is computed on the underlying abelian sheaf.
hypotheses: R any sheaf of rings; the Λ-module case is R = Λ_X.
For (c): g_* of R-modules is the direct image of the underlying abelian sheaves.
proofSteps: Cartan's criterion (SGA 4 V 4.3, recalled in the proof of Scholze's Lemma 3.16 and by Berkovich §4.2): an abelian sheaf is acyclic on all objects iff its Čech cohomology vanishes in positive degrees for every covering of every object; this is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison (b) for abelian sheaves with B all objects (Stacks Tag 03F9), deduced there from the Čech-to-derived spectral sequence of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison, whose statement does not itself contain Cartan's criterion.

For a covering 𝔘 = (U_i → U) the Čech complex of I is Hom_R(K(𝔘), I), where K(𝔘): ⋯ → ⊕ (j_{U_{i0 i1}})_! R → ⊕ (j_{U_{i0}})_! R → (j_U)_! R → 0 is the Čech resolution by extensions by zero (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-restriction-preserves-injectives (a)); K(𝔘) is exact in positive degrees because its stalk at a geometric point (or at an abstract point of the coherent pro-étale topos, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-topos-enough-points) is the free R-module complex of the nerve of a nonempty set, which is contractible; Hom_R(−, I) is exact, so the Čech cohomology of I vanishes in positive degrees.
(b) Take an injective resolution in Mod(C, R); by (a) its image under forget is a Γ(U, −)-acyclic resolution, which computes H^n(U, forget F).
(c) R^q g_* is the sheafification of U ↦ H^q(g^{-1}U, −) in both categories (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/higher-direct-image-sheafification), and the two presheaves agree by (b).
acceptance: For R = O_{X_ét}, H^n(X_ét, O_{X_ét}) computed in O-modules equals the cohomology of the abelian sheaf G_a of de Jong–van der Put §3.2.

nodes.title: Bounded-below derived categories, derived global sections and derived direct images on classical analytic sites
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space, Λ a ring (or R a sheaf of rings) and Sh(X_ét, Λ) the Grothendieck abelian category of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules. Define: (i) D⁺(X_ét, Λ) := `DerivedCategory.Plus (Sh(X_ét, Λ))`, the full subcategory of cohomologically bounded below objects of the ordinary derived category D(X_ét, Λ) = `DerivedCategory (Sh(X_ét, Λ))`; (ii) for U ∈ X_ét, RΓ(U, −) := Γ(U, −).rightDerivedFunctorPlus: D⁺(X_ét, Λ) → D⁺(Mod_Λ) and H^n(U, K) := H^n(RΓ(U, K)); for a sheaf F, H^n(U, F) = R^nΓ(U, −)(F) (Mathlib `Functor.rightDerived`), computed by any injective resolution; (iii) for a morphism g: X′ → X of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces, Rg_* := (g_*).rightDerivedFunctorPlus: D⁺(X′_ét, Λ) → D⁺(X_ét, Λ) and R^q g_* F := H^q(Rg_* F) = (g_*).rightDerived q (F); (iv) for X locally noetherian, D⁺(X_proét, Λ) and Rν_*: D⁺(X_proét, Λ) → D⁺(X_ét, Λ) for ν: X_proét → X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-projection-nu), and Rf_proét,* for morphisms of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces; the same for sheaves of R-modules. Normalisations: H^0(U, F) = F(U); H^n(U, F) = H^n(U_ét, F|_U) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-restriction-preserves-injectives); H^n(X, F) ≅ Ext^n(Λ_X, F) in Sh(X_ét, Λ) (Mathlib `Abelian.Ext`), and for Λ = ℤ this is Mathlib's `Sheaf.H F n`; the cohomology of R-modules agrees with that of the underlying abelian sheaves (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/module-and-abelian-cohomology-agree). These are D0's ordinary derived global sections and direct images (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0) instantiated on A1's sites; the unbounded enhanced versions are E1's, compared in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/ordinary-vs-enhanced-ext-comparison.
hypotheses: X, X′ locally strongly sheafy analytic; locally noetherian for the pro-étale clauses.
Only bounded-below complexes are derived with injective resolutions; unbounded complexes use E1's K-injective replacements.
No torsion hypothesis on Λ is needed for the definitions.
proofSteps: Enough injectives: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/affinoid-etale-basis-essentially-small; Γ(U, −) and g_* are additive (they are evaluation, resp. precomposition), so mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerivedFunctorPlus defines RΓ(U, −) and Rg_* on mathlib:DerivedCategory.Plus, with unit mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit an isomorphism on bounded below complexes of injectives.

H^n of a sheaf: the classical right derived functors mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerived agree with H^n ∘ RΓ(U, −) on sheaves placed in degree 0 (both are computed by an injective resolution, mathlib:CategoryTheory.InjectiveResolution).
H^0(U, F) = F(U): Γ(U, −) is left exact.

Ext comparison: Γ(X, −) ≅ Hom(Λ_X, −) (mathlib:CategoryTheory.constantSheaf adjunction at the terminal object X); Ext^n(Λ_X, −) = mathlib:CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext is a universal δ-functor vanishing on injectives in positive degrees with Ext^0 = Hom (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.addEquiv₀), hence agrees with R^nΓ(X, −); for Λ = ℤ it is mathlib:CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H by definition, with H^0 identified by mathlib:CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H.equiv₀.
Pro-étale: the same on X_proét,κ, independent of κ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/affinoid-etale-basis-essentially-small (c)).
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, O_K) with K a complete nonarchimedean field (rank-one plus ring), H^n(X, F) ≅ H^n_cont(Gal(K^sep/K), F_ξ) for every F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ).

For X = Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) and p odd, H^1(X, ℤ/p) ≅ H^1(Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p), ℤ/p) is two-dimensional over F_p, whereas H^1(X_ét, O_{X_ét}) = 0 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-acyclicity-of-vector-bundles): acyclicity of O says nothing about constant torsion coefficients.

nodes.title: The étale site of a subset of an analytic adic space (pseudo-adic étale site)
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and S ⊆ |X| a subset. The étale site of (X, S) is (X, S)_ét := (X_ét, J_S): the category X_ét of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site with the Grothendieck topology J_S in which a sieve R on u: U → X is covering iff u^{-1}(S) ⊆ ⋃_{(f: V → U) ∈ R} f(|V|); equivalently, it is generated by the families (f_i: U_i → U) with u^{-1}(S) ⊆ ⋃_i f_i(|U_i|). Properties: (i) every covering of X_ét is a J_S-covering, and the identity functor is continuous and finite-limit preserving, giving a morphism of sites i_S: (X, S)_ét → X_ét with i_{S,*} the inclusion of J_S-sheaves and i_S^{-1} = J_S-sheafification, exact; (ii) for a geometric point ξ of X whose support lies in S, the fibre functor of ξ is a point of (X, S)_ét, these points form a conservative family, and (i_S^{-1}F)_ξ = F_ξ; (iii) S = |X| gives X_ét, S = ∅ gives the trivial topos (every sheaf is terminal), and for S = |W| with W ⊆ X an open subspace, (X, S)_ét and W_ét have equivalent sheaf categories via restriction; (iv) a morphism g: X′ → X and S′ ⊆ g^{-1}(S) give a morphism of sites (X′, S′)_ét → (X, S)_ét by base change; (v) T ⊆ S gives i_{T,S}: (X, T)_ét → (X, S)_ét with i_T = i_S ∘ i_{T,S}. When S is convex (closed under the specialisations lying between two of its points) and locally pro-constructible — tested on spectral open neighbourhoods of the points of S, the convention also used by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison/pairs-and-pseudo-adic-supports, under which locally closed subsets of locally spectral spaces qualify — (X, S) is a pseudo-adic space in Huber's sense; for S closed or locally closed and constructible this holds, and (X, S) is in general not an adic space.
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic; S an arbitrary subset of |X| for the construction, convex and locally pro-constructible for Huber's pseudo-adic conditions.
The site is a Grothendieck topology on the category X_ét itself; no adic space structure on S is asserted.
proofSteps: Topology: J_S is a Grothendieck topology (stability under pullback uses that the preimage of S under a composite is the preimage of the preimage and that the image of |V ×_U U′| → |U′| contains the preimage of the image, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change; transitivity is union of images); it contains J because a jointly surjective family covers every subset.

(i) The identity X_ét → X_ét sends J-covers to J_S-covers and preserves finite limits (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardContinuous, mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullback; exactness as in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules).

(ii) Points: for ξ with support s ∈ S, a lift ū of ξ to U maps the closed point to a point of u^{-1}(S); a J_S-covering family covers it, the pullback of the family to Spa(C, C⁺) contains a member whose image contains the closed point, and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (iii) gives a section, hence a lift (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point). Conservativity: a sieve through which every lift of every such ξ factors covers u^{-1}(S), by the proof of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-enough-points restricted to points of S.

(iii) S = ∅: the empty sieve covers every object. S = |W|: the sieve of U generated by U ×_X W → U is J_S-covering, so a J_S-sheaf is determined by its values on objects over W, and those form W_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/slice-site).
(iv), (v): base change preserves the covering condition because preimages of S′ ⊆ g^{-1}(S) map into preimages of S.
acceptance: For X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C algebraically closed and C⁺ of rank 2, and S = {s} the closed point, Sh((X, S)_ét, Λ) is equivalent to Λ-modules via the stalk at s.

For the closed unit disc X over a complete nonarchimedean field K with pseudo-uniformizer ϖ and the quasi-compact open U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, the closed complement Z = X ∖ U gives the pseudo-adic site (X, Z)_ét on which i_Z^{-1} is defined, although Z is not the underlying set of any open or closed adic subspace of X.

nodes.title: Étale sheaves on Spa(C, C⁺): global sections are the stalk at the closed point and higher cohomology vanishes
nodes.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value, C⁺ ⊆ C an open and bounded valuation subring of any rank r ≥ 1, S = Spa(C, C⁺) with closed point s, and Λ a ring. (a) For every F ∈ Sh(S_ét, Λ), Γ(S, F) = F_{id} is the stalk at the geometric point id_S (support s); Γ(S, −) is exact and commutes with all colimits. (b) H^n(S, F) = 0 for all n > 0 and all F. (c) Every étale map V → S is a local isomorphism, so restriction to the opens of |S| is an equivalence Sh(S_ét, Λ) ≃ Sh(|S|, Λ); |S| is the chain, under specialisation, of the valuation rings V with C⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ O_C (r of them when r is finite), and the stalk at the point V corresponds to the geometric point Spa(C, V) → S. (d) For a locally strongly sheafy analytic X and a geometric point ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → X, F_ξ ≅ Γ(Spa(C, C⁺), ξ^{-1}F), naturally in F. (e) Higher rank is retained: for r ≥ 2 the family of stalks at the rank-one points of all such S does not detect nonzero sheaves (the skyscraper at s), and Γ(S, F) is the stalk at the closed point, not at the rank-one point Spa(C, O_C).
hypotheses: C algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean, nontrivially valued; C⁺ open, bounded, a valuation ring of any rank.
For K not algebraically closed the statement fails (Galois cohomology).
proofSteps: (a) The category N(id) of étale neighbourhoods of the geometric point id_S has the initial object (S, id): a neighbourhood (U, ū) receives the unique morphism ū from (S, id) (ū is an S-morphism S → U lifting id). Hence the stalk colimit is F(S) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points (c)), and stalks are exact and commute with colimits (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules (vi)).
(b) Γ(S, −) is exact, so its right derived functors vanish in positive degrees (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image).

(c) Locally on the source an étale V → S is an open subspace of a finite étale W → S′ over an open S′ ⊆ S (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism). The rational subsets of S are the Spa(C, V′) for overrings V′ ⊇ C⁺ generated by one element (field pairs with C algebraically closed) and cover S′; over each of them W splits as a finite disjoint union of copies (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (ii)). Hence W → S′, and so V → S, is a local isomorphism, and sheaves on the site of local isomorphisms over |S| are sheaves on |S| (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (i) for the description of |S|).
(d) AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points (d): (ξ^{-1}F)_{id} ≅ F_{ξ ∘ id} = F_ξ, combined with (a).
(e) The skyscraper i_{s,*}Λ (via (c): the sheaf on |S| with sections Λ on S and 0 on S ∖ {s}) has stalk Λ at s and 0 at every other point.
acceptance: H^n(Spa(C, C⁺), Λ) = 0 for n > 0 and H^0 = Λ.

Non-example: for K a complete nonarchimedean field that is not algebraically closed, H^1(Spa(K, O_K), ℤ/ℓ) = H^1(Gal(K^sep/K), ℤ/ℓ) ≠ 0 for suitable ℓ (for example K = ℚ_p, ℓ = p), and Spa(L, L⁺) → Spa(K, K⁺) is a nonsplit finite étale cover for every nontrivial finite separable extension L (L⁺ the integral closure of K⁺).

sources.match: Global sections on Spa(C, C⁺) are exact and commute with colimits because étale covers split; this is (a).
The stalk at a geometric point is global sections of the pullback to Spa(C, C⁺), which is (d).
The non-example: over a non-algebraically closed field étale covers need not split.
Huber's fibre functors ε_ξ at geometric points, computed here as global sections over Spa(C, C⁺).

nodes.title: Extension by zero, restriction to closed and locally closed subsets, and cohomology with supports
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and Λ a ring. (i) For u: U → X in X_ét, extension by zero u_!: Sh(U_ét, Λ) → Sh(X_ét, Λ) is the left adjoint of the restriction u^{-1} (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-restriction-preserves-injectives (a)); it is exact, (u_!G)_ξ = ⊕_{ū} G_ū over the lifts ū of the geometric point ξ to U, and u_! ≅ u_* when u is finite étale. (ii) For an open subspace j: U ⊆ X with closed complement Z = |X| ∖ |U|, let i: (X, Z)_ét → X_ét be the pseudo-adic site of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site; then j_!, j^{-1}, j_*, i^{-1}, i_* satisfy j^{-1}j_! ≅ id ≅ j^{-1}j_*, i^{-1}i_* ≅ id, j^{-1}i_* = 0, i^{-1}j_! = 0, and i_* is exact. (iii) Sections with support: ℋ_Z(F) := ker(F → j_*j^{-1}F), Γ_Z(X, F) := ker(F(X) → F(U)), i^!F := i^{-1}ℋ_Z(F) (right adjoint of i_*), with derived functors RΓ_Z(X, −), Ri^! on D⁺ and H^n_Z(X, F) := H^n RΓ_Z(X, F). (iv) For a locally closed T = U′ ∩ Z′ (U′ open, Z′ closed), extension by zero from T: i_{T,!} := j_{U′,!} ∘ (i_{Z′∩U′ ⊆ U′})_*, exact and independent of the presentation of T. No closed or locally closed subset is replaced by an adic subspace: (X, Z) is a pseudo-adic space, not an adic space.
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic; U open (for (ii)–(iii)) or étale over X (for (i)).
Λ an arbitrary ring.
proofSteps: (i) u_! is mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPullback along Over.forget U with values in ModuleCat Λ (left Kan extension and sheafification), under U_ét ≃ X_ét/U (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/slice-site); the stalk formula follows from the description of stalks as colimits over neighbourhoods and the cofinality of neighbourhoods of the lifts; exactness from the stalk formula and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules (vi). For finite étale u, the natural map u_! → u_* is an isomorphism: the question is étale-local on X, and étale-locally a finite étale u is a finite disjoint union of copies of the base (induction on the locally constant degree, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (d), splitting off the open and closed diagonal of U ×_X U → U, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal), where both functors are the finite direct sum.

(ii) Stalks at geometric points with support in U, resp. in Z (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/localisation-sequence (b)); i_* exact because i_*G is computed on the same category X_ét and its stalks at points in U vanish while those in Z are stalks of G.

(iii) ℋ_Z is left exact as a kernel; i^! is right adjoint to i_* because a map i_*G → F factors through ℋ_Z(F) (its restriction to U vanishes); derived functors by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image (enough injectives).

(iv) Independence of the presentation: two presentations have a common refinement U″ = U′ ∩ U‴ in which T is closed, and extension by zero along open immersions composes (j_{U″,!} = j_{U′,!} ∘ (U″ ⊆ U′)_!).
acceptance: For the quasi-compact open j: U = {|T| ≤ |p|} ⊆ X = closed unit disc over ℚ_p: Γ(X, j_!Λ) = 0 while Γ(X, j_*Λ) = Λ, and j_!Λ is constructible in the sense of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/classical-constructible-sheaves.
For U = X: j_! = id, Z = ∅ and i^{-1}F = 0.

nodes.title: Ordinary Ext and D⁺ cohomology agree with the shared enhanced derived category
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and Λ a ring; let D(X_ét, Λ) = `DerivedCategory (Sh(X_ét, Λ))`, D⁺(X_ét, Λ) ⊆ D(X_ét, Λ) the full subcategory of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image, and 𝒟(X_ét, Λ) the enhanced derived category of E1 (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/enhanced-derived-category), whose homotopy category is D(X_ét, Λ). Then: (a) for F, G ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) and n ≥ 0, Ext^n(F, G) (Mathlib `Abelian.Ext`) ≅ Hom_{D(X_ét, Λ)}(F, G[n]) ≅ Hom_{D⁺(X_ét, Λ)}(F, G[n]) ≅ π_0 Map_{𝒟(X_ét, Λ)}(F, G[n]); in particular H^n(U, G) ≅ π_0 Map_𝒟(j_{U!}Λ, G[n]) for U ∈ X_ét, with j_{U!}Λ the extension by zero of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero; (b) a bounded below complex of injective sheaves is K-injective, so for K ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ) the value RΓ(U, K) of the D⁺ right derived functor agrees with E1's enhanced RΓ(U, K) computed by K-injective replacement (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/k-injective-and-k-flat-replacements), and likewise Rg_*K and Rν_*K; (c) the comparisons in (a)–(b) are compatible with composition (Yoneda product), with the connecting maps of long exact sequences and with g^{-1}. Consequently every classical statement of H0–H5 formulated in D⁺ is a statement about E1's enhanced objects restricted to bounded-below complexes, and conversely.
hypotheses: Λ an arbitrary ring; the enhanced category is E1's for the ringed site (X_ét, Λ_X).
Only bounded-below complexes are claimed to be computed by injective resolutions.
proofSteps: (a) First two isomorphisms: definition of mathlib:CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext as shifted Hom between single complexes in the localisation at quasi-isomorphisms, and full faithfulness of DerivedCategory.Plus ⊆ DerivedCategory (mathlib:DerivedCategory.Plus is a full subcategory). Third: E1's comparison of the homotopy category of 𝒟(X_ét, Λ) with mathlib:DerivedCategory (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/enhanced-derived-category), under which π_0 of mapping spaces is Hom in the homotopy category. The U-version uses Hom(j_{U!}Λ, −) = Γ(U, −).

(b) mathlib:CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_injective: bounded below complexes of injectives are K-injective; so an injective resolution is a K-injective replacement, and E1's functorial replacement is homotopy equivalent to it (a quasi-isomorphism between K-injective complexes is a homotopy equivalence, mathlib:CochainComplex.IsKInjective.quasiIso_iff); applying Γ(U, −) (resp. g_*, ν_*) to homotopy-equivalent complexes gives isomorphic objects.
(c) Both sides are computed by the same K-injective complexes, and Yoneda composition, connecting maps and pullback are induced by maps of complexes.
acceptance: For U = X and G = Λ_X: H^n(X, Λ) ≅ π_0 Map_𝒟(Λ_X, Λ_X[n]).
The comparison is required for the passage from Huber's D⁺ statements (H1–H3) to ECD's unbounded D_ét on the diamond side.

nodes.title: Composition of derived direct images and the Leray spectral sequence on classical analytic sites
nodes.statement: Let g: X′ → X and h: X → X″ be morphisms of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces and Λ a ring (or R a sheaf of rings). (a) g_* sends injective objects of Sh(X′_ét, Λ) to injective objects, and the natural map R(h ∘ g)_* → Rh_* ∘ Rg_* of functors D⁺(X′_ét, Λ) → D⁺(X″_ét, Λ) is an isomorphism; in particular RΓ(X, Rg_*K) ≅ RΓ(X′, K). (b) For F ∈ Sh(X′_ét, Λ) there are convergent first-quadrant spectral sequences E_2^{pq} = R^p h_* R^q g_* F ⇒ R^{p+q}(h ∘ g)_* F and E_2^{pq} = H^p(X, R^q g_* F) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X′, F), functorial in F. (c) For X locally noetherian the same holds for ν: X_proét → X_ét and for composites of pro-étale and étale direct images: H^p(X_ét, R^qν_*F) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X_proét, F), and R(f_ét,* ∘ ν_{X,*}) ≅ Rf_ét,* ∘ Rν_{X,*} ≅ Rν_{Y,*} ∘ Rf_proét,* for f: X → Y. These are the Leray spectral sequences of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison on A1's sites.
hypotheses: g, h arbitrary morphisms of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces (locally noetherian for the pro-étale clauses).
F bounded below (a sheaf, or an object of D⁺); no torsion hypothesis.
proofSteps: (a) g_* has the exact left adjoint g^{-1} (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules (iv)), so it preserves injectives (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-restriction-preserves-injectives (b)); hence for a bounded below complex of injectives I, Rg_* I = g_* I is again a bounded below complex of injectives on which Rh_* is computed by h_*, and (h ∘ g)_* = h_* ∘ g_* on sheaves (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit is an isomorphism on complexes of injectives). For sheaves of modules over a sheaf of rings R′ on X′ that is not pulled back from X, g_* need not preserve injective R′-modules (its left adjoint R′ ⊗_{g^{-1}g_*R′} g^{-1}(−) is not exact). There cohomology and higher direct images agree with those of the underlying abelian sheaves (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/module-and-abelian-cohomology-agree (b)–(c)), so g_* of an injective R′-module is h_*-acyclic and (a)–(b) follow from the abelian case.

(b) The Grothendieck spectral sequence of the composite h_* ∘ g_* with g_* sending injectives to h_*-acyclics: requested from DiamondsAndVStacks:D0 (the node DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison states only the global Leray sequence, which gives the second sequence), built with Mathlib's spectral objects (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Abelian.SpectralObject.spectralSequence); the second sequence is the case of the structure maps to a point, i.e. h = Γ(X, −).

(c) The same argument for ν_* and f_proét,*, whose left adjoints ν^{-1}, f_proét^{-1} are exact (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-projection-nu), and f_ét,* ∘ ν_{X,*} = ν_{Y,*} ∘ f_proét,* on sheaves (both are precomposition with the same functor of sites).
acceptance: For g = ν and F = ν^*F′: E_2^{pq} = H^p(X_ét, R^qν_*ν^*F′) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X_proét, ν^*F′) degenerates (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/proetale-etale-comparison), giving H^n(X_ét, F′) = H^n(X_proét, ν^*F′).

For g: X′ → X finite étale, R^q g_* F = 0 for q > 0 (stalks are finite products of stalks of F, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-formula-strict-localisation), and the spectral sequence gives H^n(X, g_*F) = H^n(X′, F).

nodes.title: Čech-to-derived spectral sequence and acyclic-basis comparison on étale and pro-étale sites
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and (C, J) its étale site X_ét, or, for X locally noetherian, its κ-small pro-étale site X_proét,κ. Let F be a sheaf of Λ-modules (or R-modules) and 𝔘 = (U_i → U)_{i∈I} a covering in C, with fibre products U_{i₀⋯i_p} = U_{i₀} ×_U ⋯ ×_U U_{i_p}. (a) There is a convergent first-quadrant spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = Ȟ^p(𝔘, ℋ^q(F)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(U, F), where ℋ^q(F) is the presheaf V ↦ H^q(V, F) and Ȟ^p is the cohomology of the Čech complex of 𝔘 (Mathlib `cechComplexFunctor` applied in the slice category C/U, whose finite products are the fibre products over U); the edge map Ȟ^p(𝔘, F) → H^p(U, F) is an isomorphism for p = 0, injective for p = 1, and an isomorphism for all p if H^q(U_{i₀⋯i_p}, F) = 0 for all q > 0 and all (i₀, …, i_p) (Leray acyclicity). (b) If B ⊆ C is a full subcategory stable under the fibre products occurring in Čech nerves, every covering of an object of B is refined by a covering by objects of B, and Ȟ^q(𝔙, F) = 0 for q > 0 for every covering 𝔙 in B of an object of B, then H^q(V, F) = 0 for all V ∈ B and q > 0, and Čech cohomology on B-coverings computes H^*(U, F) for U ∈ B. For X_ét, B may be taken to be the stable affinoid basis X_ét^aff (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison), and it suffices to test the Čech condition on rational coverings and on single faithfully finite étale maps (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction; Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 8.2.21).
hypotheses: Coverings as in A1 (jointly surjective families; corrected coverings on X_proét).
In (b) B is stable under the fibre products occurring in Čech nerves.
proofSteps: (a) and the Leray acyclicity statement: DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison applied to the site (C, J), with the Čech complex of mathlib:CategoryTheory.cechComplexFunctor; the presheaves ℋ^q(F) are those of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-restriction-preserves-injectives (c) (H^q(V, F) computed on V_ét).

(b) Cartan's criterion (SGA 4 V 4.3; Stacks Tag 03F9), by induction on q from (a) applied to B-coverings. If H^i vanishes on B for 0 < i < q, then for a B-covering 𝔙 of V ∈ B the spectral sequence (a) and Ȟ^q(𝔙, F) = 0 give an injection H^q(V, F) → Ȟ^0(𝔙, ℋ^q(F)); every class of H^q(V, F) dies on some covering, which is refined by a B-covering, so H^q(V, F) = 0. Once F is acyclic on B, Čech cohomology of B-coverings computes H^* by the acyclic-basis part of DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison, whose hypothesis is acyclicity on B.

Reduction to rational and finite étale coverings: a property of coverings of basis objects that is stable under refinement and composition and holds for rational coverings and single faithfully finite étale maps holds for all finite coverings (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction, Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.20); universal Čech acyclicity is such a property, as in Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.21.
acceptance: Čech complex of a two-member rational (Laurent) covering of an affinoid computes H^*(U, F) for every F that is acyclic on affinoid étale objects.

For a finite étale Galois covering U → X with group G, the Čech complex is the complex of inhomogeneous cochains of G with values in F(U) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cartan-leray-spectral-sequence).

sources.match: The Čech-to-cohomology spectral sequence (SGA 4 V 3.4) in rigid analytic geometry.
Čech acyclicity on a stable basis for rational and finite étale coverings implies vanishing of étale sheaf cohomology on the basis: part (b) for X_ét.
The degree-zero consequence recorded in (b).

nodes.title: Cohomology on profinite G-sets is continuous group cohomology
nodes.statement: Let G be a profinite group and G-pfsets the site of profinite sets with continuous G-action and the corrected coverings of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-g-sets-site (the erratum's towers of pullbacks of surjections of finite G-sets followed by G-étale maps). For a topological G-module M let F_M be the sheaf S ↦ Hom_{cont,G}(S, M). Then for every i ≥ 0 there is a canonical isomorphism H^i(pt, F_M) ≅ H^i_cont(G, M), where, G-pfsets not being essentially small, H^i is computed on the full subsite of κ-small profinite G-sets for a cutoff cardinal κ exceeding the weight of G (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cutoff-cardinal), and is independent of κ because the Čech computation below takes place in every such subsite with the continuous cohomology of the homogeneous continuous cochains (Mathlib `continuousCohomology`), where pt is the one-point G-set; it is natural in M and compatible with connecting maps for short exact sequences of topological G-modules that are sheaf-exact.
hypotheses: G profinite; M a topological G-module (discrete, or with the topology used by the consumer); corrected coverings.
Scholze's Proposition 3.7 (i) (splitting of arbitrary open surjections of profinite sets) is false and is not used; its replacement is the splitting of towers.
proofSteps: G → pt is a covering: by the erratum, G = lim_{μ<λ} G_μ with each G_μ → G_{<μ} the quotient by a finite normal subgroup, a G-tower (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-group-tower), so G → pt is a corrected covering.

Čech-to-derived for this covering (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison, stated for an arbitrary site; the H0 node of that name is only its instance on X_ét and X_proét,κ): the fibre products are G^{n+1} with free diagonal action, on which sections are exact (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/free-g-profinite-sections-exact), so all higher cohomology of F_M on G^{n+1} vanishes and H^i(pt, F_M) is the cohomology of the Čech complex F_M(G) → F_M(G²) → ⋯.

F_M(G^{n+1}) = Hom_{cont,G}(G^{n+1}, M) is the module of homogeneous continuous n-cochains, and the Čech differentials are the homogeneous coboundaries. Mathlib's mathlib:continuousCohomology is the cohomology of the G-invariants of the iterated mapping spaces C(G, C(G, …, C(G, M))) (n+1 factors, compact-open topology) with the inductive differential d_{n+1} = const − C(G, d_n). For G profinite (compact Hausdorff) the exponential law identifies C(G, C(G^n, M)) with C(G^{n+1}, M) compatibly with the G-actions, and induction on n identifies the inductive differential with the alternating homogeneous coboundary. This comparison is a TODO in Mathlib's ContCohomology/Basic.lean and is a step of this node; with it, H^i(pt, F_M) ≅ continuousCohomology i M.
acceptance: For G = ℤ_p and M discrete, H^1(pt, F_M) = Hom_cont(ℤ_p, M) for trivial action; H^i(pt, F_M) = 0 for i ≥ 2 and M torsion (cd_p ℤ_p = 1).

For X connected locally noetherian analytic, via X_profét ≃ π₁(X, x̄)-pfsets (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-etale-galois-sets), H^i of the sheaf attached to a discrete π₁-module on X_profét is H^i_cont(π₁(X, x̄), M) (the input of the K(π, 1) arguments of PadicHodgeTheory P8).

sources.match: The proof via the cover G → pt and the Cartan–Leray (Čech) spectral sequence.
The erratum shows G → pt remains a covering for the corrected topology, so the proof survives the correction.

nodes.title: Cohomology of ν^*F on quasi-compact quasi-separated pro-étale objects is the colimit of étale cohomology
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian analytic adic space, F an abelian sheaf (or sheaf of Λ-modules) on X_ét and U = lim_j U_j ∈ X_proét quasi-compact and quasi-separated, presented by quasi-compact quasi-separated U_j ∈ X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-coherence). Then for every i ≥ 0 the natural map colim_j H^i(U_j, F) → H^i(U, ν^*F) is an isomorphism. The case i = 0 is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/nu-pullback-sections-qcqs.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic; U qcqs with a qcqs presentation; the corrected coverings of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-site-corrected.
proofSteps: Reduce to F injective (both sides are δ-functors in F, the left one because filtered colimits are exact) and X qcqs (the statement is local around the image of U).

Work on the site X_proét^qc of qcqs objects, which has the same topos. Let F̃ be the presheaf V = lim V_j ↦ colim_j F(V_j); ν^*F is its sheafification (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-projection-nu). By Cartan's criterion (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison (b) on X_proét,κ with B the qcqs objects; Scholze uses SGA 4 V 4.3) it suffices to show that the Čech complex of F̃ for every covering of a qcqs object by qcqs objects is exact; then F̃ = ν^*F on qcqs objects and H^i(V, ν^*F) = 0 for i > 0.

Pass to a finite subcover (quasi-compactness) and combine it into one map V → U. For a corrected covering V → U (a finite-étale tower followed by an étale map), F̃ commutes with the limit along the tower, so the Čech complex of V → U is the colimit of the Čech complexes of the stages; by transfinite induction along the tower (colimits are exact) and AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/pro-etale-surjective-etale-descent, it reduces to étale surjections V_{j′} → U_{j′} at a finite stage of the presentation.

For an étale covering at a finite stage the Čech complex of F is exact because F is injective (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-restriction-preserves-injectives), and the Čech complex of V → U is the filtered colimit over j′ of these, hence exact.
acceptance: If U ∈ X_ét (a constant pro-object), the statement is the tautology H^i(U, ν^*F) = H^i(U, F), i.e. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/proetale-etale-comparison on U.

For V ∈ X_proét quasi-compact and quasi-separated and a pro-finite-étale G-torsor Ṽ → V, H^i(Ṽ × S, ν^*F) = LC(S, H^i(Ṽ, ν^*F)) for profinite S (the hypothesis (★) of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cartan-leray-spectral-sequence).

sources.match: The statement (its display is H^i(U, ν^*F) = lim_j H^i(U_j, F)).
The proof strategy by Cartan's criterion on Čech complexes followed here.
The lemma is kept with the corrected coverings; the reduction to finite stages is then a transfinite induction along the towers.

nodes.title: Cartan–Leray spectral sequences for finite étale and pro-finite-étale Galois covers
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and Λ a ring. (a) If π: U → X is a finite étale Galois covering with finite group G (so U ×_X U ≅ G × U over U), then for F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) there is a convergent spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = H^p(G, H^q(U, F|_U)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X, F), natural in F. (b) Let X be locally noetherian, V ∈ X_proét quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and Ṽ = lim_j Ṽ_j → V a pro-finite-étale G-torsor for a profinite group G (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-galois-cover-is-covering). For a sheaf F of Λ-modules on X_proét there is a convergent spectral sequence with E_1^{pq} = H^q(Ṽ × G^p, F) ⇒ H^{p+q}(V, F); if F satisfies (★) the natural maps LC(S, H^q(Ṽ, F)) → H^q(Ṽ × S, F) are isomorphisms for all profinite sets S (discrete topology on H^q(Ṽ, F)), then E_2^{pq} = H^p_cont(G, H^q(Ṽ, F)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(V, F); (★) holds for F = ν^*F′ with F′ ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/proetale-cohomology-continuity). (c) The edge maps are the inflation H^p(G, F(U)) → H^p(X, F) and the restriction H^n(X, F) → H^n(U, F)^G. Consumers with non-discrete coefficients (completed structure sheaves, period sheaves) supply (★) for the topology they use; this node claims the E_2 identification only under (★).
hypotheses: (a) π finite étale Galois with group G; (b) X locally noetherian, V qcqs, Ṽ → V a pro-finite-étale G-torsor with the corrected coverings.
The continuous-cohomology form of E_2 in (b) needs hypothesis (★); without it only the Čech (E_1) form is asserted.
proofSteps: (a) Čech-to-derived spectral sequence for the covering {U → X} (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison (a)); the (p+1)-fold fibre product is U × G^p, so the Čech complex of the presheaf ℋ^q(F) is the complex of inhomogeneous cochains of G with values in H^q(U, F|_U) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-restriction-preserves-injectives (c) for H^q on U_ét); its cohomology is H^p(G, H^q(U, F|_U)).

(b) Ṽ → V is a corrected covering and Ṽ ×_V Ṽ ≅ Ṽ × G (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-galois-cover-is-covering), so the (p+1)-fold fibre product is Ṽ × G^p (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/profinite-set-objects); the Čech-to-derived spectral sequence gives the E_1 form. Under (★) the E_1 row is Hom_cont(G^p, H^q(Ṽ, F)) with the homogeneous coboundaries, whose cohomology is mathlib:continuousCohomology after the comparison of cochain models made in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/profinite-g-set-cohomology (exponential law for profinite G).

(★) for ν^*F′: H^q(Ṽ × S, ν^*F′) = colim over finite quotients S → S_k of H^q(Ṽ_j × S_k, F′) = LC(S, colim_j H^q(Ṽ_j, F′)) = LC(S, H^q(Ṽ, ν^*F′)) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/proetale-cohomology-continuity, twice; Ṽ × S is qcqs).
(c) Edge maps of the Čech spectral sequence.
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, O_K) and U = Spa(L, O_L) with L/K finite Galois, (a) is the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence H^p(Gal(L/K), H^q(Gal(K^sep/L), M)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(Gal(K^sep/K), M).

Scholze's computation of H^i(V_proét, L ⊗ O⁺/p) via the ℤ_p^n-cover Ṽ = V ×_{T^n} T̃^n → V of a torus chart (proof of his Lemma 5.6) is (b). There (★) is his Lemma 3.16 (the coefficients are pulled back from V_ét), and the almost vanishing of H^q(Ṽ, L ⊗ O⁺/p) for q > 0 (his Lemma 4.12) collapses E_2 to H^p_cont(ℤ_p^n, M). The proof of his Proposition 6.16 (ii) applies (b) to the Γ_k-cover X_K → X, with (★) checked by inspection (PadicHodgeTheory P8).

nodes.title: Étale cohomology agrees with pro-étale cohomology of ν^*F, and ν^* commutes with qcqs direct images
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian analytic adic space and ν: X_proét → X_ét the projection (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/proetale-projection-nu). (i) For every abelian sheaf (or sheaf of Λ-modules) F on X_ét the unit F → Rν_*ν^*F is an isomorphism in D⁺(X_ét); hence H^i(X_ét, F) ≅ H^i(X_proét, ν^*F) for all i and ν^*: D⁺(X_ét, Λ) → D⁺(X_proét, Λ) is fully faithful. (ii) For a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism f: X → Y of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces and F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ), the base-change morphism ν_Y^* Rf_ét,* F → Rf_proét,* ν_X^* F is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: X, Y locally noetherian analytic; f quasi-compact and quasi-separated in (ii).
F a sheaf of abelian groups or Λ-modules on the étale site (not an arbitrary pro-étale sheaf).
proofSteps: (i) R^iν_*ν^*F is the sheafification of U ↦ H^i(U, ν^*F) with U ∈ X_ét regarded in X_proét (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/higher-direct-image-sheafification). For i = 0 this is F by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/nu-pullback-sections-qcqs. For i > 0 and U qcqs, H^i(U, ν^*F) = H^i(U, F) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/proetale-cohomology-continuity with a constant presentation), and every class in H^i(U, F) vanishes étale-locally on U, so the sheafification is zero.
Full faithfulness on D⁺: Hom(ν^*K, ν^*L) = Hom(K, Rν_*ν^*L) = Hom(K, L) by adjunction and (i) applied to the cohomology sheaves of L (way-out argument on bounded below complexes).

(ii) Both sides have i-th cohomology sheaf equal to the sheafification of the presheaf sending a qcqs U = lim U_j → Y in Y_proét to colim_j H^i(U_j ×_Y X, F): the left side by (i) for Y and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/higher-direct-image-sheafification for f_ét, the right side by the same lemma for f_proét and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/proetale-cohomology-continuity applied to U ×_Y X = lim U_j ×_Y X (qcqs because f is qcqs).
acceptance: H^i(X_ét, ℤ/p) = H^i(X_proét, ℤ/p) for every locally noetherian analytic X (used in Scholze's primitive comparison theorem).

Non-example for (ii) without quasi-compactness: for the non-quasi-compact boundary complement j: U → X of a smooth pair, the comparison of ν^*Rj_ét,* and Rj_proét,*ν^* is not asserted (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/boundary-complement-restriction).

nodes.title: Affinoid-local description of étale sheaves, their cohomology and derived direct images
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space, Λ a ring and X_ét^aff the stable affinoid étale basis (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison). (i) Restriction to X_ét^aff is an equivalence Sh(X_ét, Λ) ≃ Sh(X_ét^aff, Λ), exact in both directions, inducing D⁺(X_ét, Λ) ≃ D⁺(X_ét^aff, Λ) compatible with RΓ(U, −) for U ∈ X_ét^aff; a presheaf on X_ét^aff is a sheaf iff it is a sheaf for rational coverings and satisfies descent for single faithfully finite étale maps (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction). (ii) For X = Spa(A, A⁺) affinoid, X_ét^aff is equivalent to the opposite of the category of complete Huber pairs reached from (A, A⁺) by finite chains of rational localisations and finite étale extensions, so an étale sheaf on X is a functor on such A-algebras with these two descent conditions. (iii) Étale-locality on the target: for g: X′ → X and v: V → X in X_ét with g_V: X′ ×_X V → V, restriction commutes with derived direct image, (Rg_*K)|_V ≅ R(g_V)_*(K|_{X′ ×_X V}) for K ∈ D⁺(X′_ét, Λ); in particular R^q g_*F can be computed over any open affinoid cover of X. (iv) For U ∈ X_ét quasi-compact and quasi-separated, H^n(U, F) is the Čech cohomology of any finite covering of U by basis objects on whose finite intersections F is acyclic (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison), and H^n(U, −) commutes with filtered colimits of sheaves (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites, the étale topos of a qcqs X being coherent with generating family X_ét^aff).
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic; in (iv) U quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
K bounded below in (iii).
proofSteps: (i) AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison (c) (dense subsite, mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsDenseSubsite.sheafEquiv); an equivalence of abelian categories preserves injectives, so derived functors correspond; the sheaf criterion is AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction.

(ii) Objects of X_ét^aff over X = Spa(A, A⁺) are the chains of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison, with morphisms the X-morphisms of adic spaces, which on affinoids are maps of complete Huber pairs over (A, A⁺) (anchor Layer 5 morphisms from affinoids; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (c) for the finite étale steps).

(iii) For W ∈ V_ét, ((g_*F)|_V)(W) = F(W ×_X X′) = F(W ×_V (X′ ×_X V)) = ((g_V)_*(F|_{X′ ×_X V}))(W), so restriction commutes with g_* on sheaves; restriction preserves injectives (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-restriction-preserves-injectives), hence commutes with the derived functors.

(iv) Leray acyclicity (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison (a)); a qcqs U has a finite covering by basis objects with basis finite intersections (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison (b)); coherence of the étale topos of a qcqs space from the qcqs generating family X_ét^aff (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/quasicompact-objects-in-a-topos) and then DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites.
acceptance: For X = Spa(K, O_K) (rank-one plus ring), (ii) identifies Sh(X_ét, Λ) with sheaves on the opposite of finite étale K-algebras, i.e. discrete Galois modules.

For an open affinoid cover X = V₁ ∪ V₂ with V₁ ∩ V₂ affinoid, (iii)–(iv) give the Mayer–Vietoris sequence ⋯ → H^n(X, F) → H^n(V₁, F) ⊕ H^n(V₂, F) → H^n(V₁ ∩ V₂, F) → ⋯ (compare Mathlib's Mayer–Vietoris sequence for Sheaf.H).

nodes.title: Étale acyclicity of vector bundles on strongly sheafy affinoids
nodes.statement: Let X = Spa(A, A⁺) with A a complete strongly sheafy Tate ring (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strongly-sheafy-huber-pair) and M a finite projective A-module. Let M̃_ét be the presheaf on X_ét^aff sending Y = Spa(B, B⁺) to M ⊗_A B. Then M̃_ét is a sheaf on X_ét (via AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison) and H^i(Y_ét, M̃_ét) = 0 for every Y ∈ X_ét^aff and i > 0; in particular H^i(X_ét, O_{X_ét}) = 0 for i > 0 and H^0(X_ét, O_{X_ét}) = A. Consequently, on a locally strongly sheafy analytic X, for a vector bundle E on X_an the pullback λ^*E to X_ét satisfies Rλ_*λ^*E = E for λ: X_ét → X_an, and vector bundles on X_an and on X_ét correspond (Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.22 (d)). This is a statement about O-modules; it implies nothing about constant coefficients: H^1(Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)_ét, ℤ/p) ≠ 0.
hypotheses: A complete strongly sheafy Tate ring (so every object of X_ét^aff is a sheafy affinoid); M finite projective.
The coefficient sheaf is M ⊗_A O, not a constant or torsion sheaf.
proofSteps: Rational coverings: for Y ∈ X_ét^aff (strongly sheafy by AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison (b)), the Čech complex of M ⊗_A B on every rational covering is exact (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-module-acyclicity; Kedlaya–Liu 2.4.23).

Faithfully finite étale maps: for a surjective finite étale Spa(B′) → Spa(B), B → B′ is faithfully flat (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (d)), so the Amitsur complex N ⊗_B B′^{⊗(•+1)} of N = M ⊗_A B is exact (Stacks Tag 023M); the fibre products are Spa(B′ ⊗_B ⋯ ⊗_B B′) with the uncompleted tensor products (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change).

These two cases imply universal Čech acyclicity on X_ét^aff (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction; Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.20), hence M̃_ét is a sheaf with vanishing higher cohomology on basis objects (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison (b); Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.21).

For λ: X_ét → X_an: R^qλ_*λ^*E is the sheafification of U ↦ H^q(U_ét, λ^*E) on opens (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/higher-direct-image-sheafification), which vanishes on affinoid U for q > 0 by the above and AdicSpacesPartII:R3/vector-bundle-global-generation; the equivalence of vector bundles then follows from descent of finite projective modules along finite étale covers (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-etale-descent).
Non-example: H^1(Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p)_ét, ℤ/p) = H^1(Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p), ℤ/p) ≠ 0 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image, Galois test).
acceptance: Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 8.2.22 (c): for Y ∈ X_ét^aff, H^i(Y, M̃) = M̃(Y) for i = 0 and 0 for i > 0.
For A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and M = A: H^1(X_ét, O) = 0 while H^1(X_ét, ℤ/p) ≠ 0.

nodes.title: Stalks of j_! and i_*, the localisation sequence and the long exact sequence of cohomology with supports
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space, j: U ⊆ X an open subspace with closed complement Z and i: (X, Z)_ét → X_ét (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero). (a) For a geometric point ξ of X with support x: (j_!G)_ξ = G_ξ if x ∈ U and 0 if x ∈ Z; (i_*H)_ξ = H_ξ if x ∈ Z and 0 if x ∈ U. (b) For F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) the sequence 0 → j_!j^{-1}F → F → i_*i^{-1}F → 0 is exact. (c) For K ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ) there are distinguished triangles j_!j^{-1}K → K → i_*i^{-1}K → and i_*Ri^!K → K → Rj_*j^{-1}K →, and a long exact sequence ⋯ → H^n_Z(X, K) → H^n(X, K) → H^n(U, K) → H^{n+1}_Z(X, K) → ⋯, natural in K. (d) For an injective sheaf I, Γ(X, I) → Γ(U, I) is surjective.
hypotheses: U open, Z its closed complement; supports of geometric points are points of |X|.
proofSteps: (a) A geometric point with support in U has a neighbourhood basis of étale objects over U, on which j_!G = G; with support in Z, every lift to an object over U is impossible (the closed point would map into U), so the colimit defining (j_!G)_ξ is over sections of the Kan extension that vanish; for i_*: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site (ii) and the vanishing of J_Z-sheaves on objects over U (the empty sieve covers them).
(b) Exactness is checked on stalks at all geometric points (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-enough-points; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules (vi)) using (a).
(d) Γ(X, −) = Hom(Λ_X, −), Γ(U, −) = Hom(j_!Λ_U, −) and j_!Λ_U → Λ_X is a monomorphism by (a); Hom(−, I) is exact.

(c) Apply (b) to an injective resolution, use (d) to get the short exact sequence of complexes 0 → Γ_Z(X, I^•) → Γ(X, I^•) → Γ(U, I^•) → 0, and take cohomology (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image); the second triangle is the derived form of 0 → i_*i^!I → I → j_*j^{-1}I → 0 for injective I.
acceptance: For X = Spa(C, C⁺) with C⁺ of rank 2, U = the generic point and Z = the closed point: H^0_Z(X, Λ) = 0, H^1_Z(X, Λ) = 0, since H^n(X, Λ) → H^n(U, Λ) is an isomorphism (both spaces have trivial étale cohomology in positive degrees and Γ = Λ).
The Berkovich analogue: Berkovich Proposition 5.2.6 (ii) and Corollary 5.2.7.

nodes.title: Locally constant sheaves and torsion local systems on the étale site
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and Λ a ring. A sheaf F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) is locally constant if there are an étale covering (U_α → X)_α and Λ-modules M_α with F|_{U_α} ≅ (M_α)_{U_α}; it is locally constant of finite type if the M_α can be chosen finitely generated. A torsion local system of rank r is a locally constant sheaf of Λ-modules for a ring Λ with nΛ = 0 for some n ≥ 1 whose local values M_α are free of rank r (for Λ noetherian, a locally constant sheaf of finite type with finite projective values is called lisse). For ℓ a prime, a lisse ℤ_ℓ-sheaf is an inverse system (L_m)_{m ≥ 1} with L_m a locally constant sheaf of finitely generated ℤ/ℓ^m-modules, such that the system is isomorphic in the pro-category to one with L_{m+1}/ℓ^m ≅ L_m; on X_proét (X locally noetherian) a lisse Ẑ_ℓ-sheaf is a sheaf of Ẑ_ℓ-modules locally isomorphic to Ẑ_ℓ ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} M with M finitely generated, Ẑ_ℓ := lim_m ν^*(ℤ/ℓ^m). The same definitions apply on the pseudo-adic sites (X, S)_ét (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site).
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic (locally noetherian for the pro-étale clause).
Coverings are A1's étale coverings; the local trivialising cover is part of the existence statement, not data.
proofSteps: Definition by the existence of a trivialising covering; the pro-category condition for lisse ℤ_ℓ-sheaves follows Scholze's Definition 8.1.

Closure properties (API): pullback preserves local constancy (g^{-1} commutes with restriction and sends constant sheaves to constant sheaves, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules); kernels, cokernels, extensions, ⊗ and Hom of locally constant sheaves of finite type over a noetherian Λ are locally constant of finite type (a map of constant sheaves on a connected object is constant, and extensions split étale-locally over a common refinement), as Berkovich records for finite locally constant sheaves in any topos.
Equivalence with finite étale covers and π₁-modules: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/local-systems-and-finite-etale-covers.
acceptance: On X = Spa(K, O_K) (K complete nonarchimedean, rank-one plus ring), locally constant sheaves of finitely generated Λ-modules (Λ finite) correspond to finite Λ-modules with continuous Gal(K^sep/K)-action, and torsion local systems of rank r to those free of rank r.
μ_n (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tate-twists) is a torsion local system of rank one over ℤ/n when n is invertible on X.

nodes.title: Locally constant sheaves of finite sets are finite étale covers, and π₁-sets on connected spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space. (a) A sheaf of sets F on X_ét is locally constant with finite values iff F ≅ h_Y := Hom_X(−, Y) for a finite étale X-space Y; Y ↦ h_Y is an equivalence from X_fét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-site) to the category of locally constant sheaves of finite sets. (b) If X is connected and ξ a geometric point, F ↦ F_ξ is an equivalence from locally constant sheaves of finite sets to finite sets with continuous π₁(X, ξ)-action (π₁ of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category); for a finite ring Λ it restricts to locally constant sheaves of finitely generated Λ-modules ≃ finite Λ-modules with continuous π₁(X, ξ)-action (torsion local systems of rank r ↔ modules free of rank r), compatible with ⊗, Hom and pullback along pointed morphisms. (c) For a finite group G, H^1(X, G_X) is in bijection with isomorphism classes of finite étale G-torsors over X.
hypotheses: X locally strongly sheafy analytic; in (b) X connected (|X| connected) with a geometric point ξ.
proofSteps: h_Y is a sheaf and is locally constant: the sheaf property is checked on rational coverings and single faithfully finite étale maps (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction), where morphisms into Y = Spa(C) over V = Spa(A) are A-algebra maps C → B (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-local-to-global (c)) and the Amitsur complex of a faithfully flat map is exact on algebra maps; local constancy: over a cover on which the degree is constant, Y ×_X Y = Δ(Y) ⊔ Y′ with Δ open and closed (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal) and Y′ → Y finite étale of smaller degree, and induction on the degree splits Y étale-locally (Berkovich 4.4.6).

Conversely a locally constant F with finite values is represented on the members of a trivialising covering by finite disjoint unions ⊔_M U_α; the gluing data form a descent datum for finite étale spaces along an étale covering, which is effective: reduce to rational coverings (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-rational-descent) and single faithfully finite étale maps of affinoids (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-covering-reduction), where descent of the finite projective algebra (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-etale-descent) keeps étaleness because the trace pairing is perfect after a faithfully flat base change (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/etale-iff-trace-pairing-perfect); the descended space represents F (Berkovich 4.1.8 for the Berkovich analogue).
(b) Compose (a) with the fibre functor equivalence of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category; for Λ-modules apply it to the finite étale group objects representing torsion local systems.

(c) Čech description of H^1 with coefficients in the constant sheaf G_X (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison in degree one for sheaves of groups) and (a) for the torsor, which is finite étale because it is locally a finite disjoint union of copies of the base.

nodes.title: Constructible sheaves in Huber's classical sense
nodes.statement: Let X be a quasi-compact quasi-separated locally noetherian analytic adic space (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space) and Λ a noetherian ring. A subset S ⊆ |X| is constructible if it is a finite Boolean combination of quasi-compact open subsets, i.e. Mathlib's Topology.IsConstructible (the Boolean subalgebra generated by the retrocompact opens, which on the quasi-compact quasi-separated |X| are exactly the quasi-compact opens). A sheaf F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) is constructible if there is a finite partition |X| = S_1 ⊔ ⋯ ⊔ S_m into locally closed constructible subsets such that for each k the restriction i_{S_k}^{-1}F to the pseudo-adic site (X, S_k)_ét (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site) is locally constant of finite type (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-local-systems). For general locally noetherian X, F is constructible if F|_U is constructible for every quasi-compact open U. A complex K ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ) is constructible if its cohomology sheaves are; D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) denotes the bounded constructible complexes. The condition is on all points of X, including higher-rank points, and on constructible strata that are in general not adic subspaces. This is Huber's notion, the classical analytic constructibility used in H1–H5; it differs from Zariski-constructibility (Bhatt–Hansen), which requires Zariski-locally closed strata of rigid spaces.
hypotheses: X qcqs locally noetherian analytic (locally noetherian for the local version); Λ noetherian.
Strata are locally closed and constructible in |X|; they need not be generalizing or Zariski-closed.
proofSteps: Definition by stratification, using the pseudo-adic restrictions of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site.

Well-posedness under refinement: a refinement of a stratification by locally closed constructible subsets keeps local constancy (restriction from (X, S)_ét to (X, T)_ét for T ⊆ S preserves local constancy, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-local-systems).
Stability properties are ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/constructible-sheaves-stability; the colimit property is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-sheaf-colimit-of-constructible.
acceptance: Every locally constant sheaf of finite type is constructible (one stratum).

For the qcqs open immersion j of a closed disc of radius 1/2 into the closed disc of radius 1, j_!Λ is constructible (strata U and its complement) but is not Zariski-constructible (Bhatt–Hansen Warning 3.2 (2)).

nodes.title: Stability of constructible sheaves: abelian subcategory, pullback, extension by zero and finite étale pushforward
nodes.statement: Let X be a qcqs locally noetherian analytic adic space and Λ noetherian. (a) Constructible sheaves form an abelian subcategory of Sh(X_ét, Λ) stable under kernels, cokernels, images and extensions, and under ⊗_Λ; D^b_c(X_ét, Λ) is a thick triangulated subcategory. (b) For a qcqs morphism g: X′ → X of qcqs locally noetherian analytic adic spaces, g^{-1} preserves constructibility. (c) For a qcqs étale u: U → X (in particular a quasi-compact open immersion), u_! preserves constructibility; in particular u_!Λ is constructible. (d) For π: X′ → X finite étale, π_* preserves constructibility. (e) Stalks of constructible sheaves are finitely generated.
hypotheses: X, X′ qcqs locally noetherian analytic; Λ noetherian; morphisms qcqs.
proofSteps: (a) Given finitely many constructible sheaves, choose a common refinement of their stratifications (finite intersections of locally closed constructible sets are such) and a common trivialising covering of each stratum; on a stratum a map of locally constant sheaves of finite type is étale-locally a map of constant sheaves, so kernels, cokernels and extensions stay locally constant of finite type (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-local-systems, abelian closure); restriction i_S^{-1} is exact (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site (i)).

(b) Preimages under the spectral map |g| of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact open, so preimages of constructible sets are constructible (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/locally-spectral-space); g^{-1} commutes with restriction to strata and preserves local constancy.

(c) For a quasi-compact open j: U → X, stratify X by a constructible stratification of U together with the closed constructible complement, on which j_!F restricts to 0 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/localisation-sequence (a)). For qcqs étale u: cover U by finitely many qc opens U_k each factoring as an open immersion into a finite étale V_k over a qc open of X (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism, local description), write u_!G as a quotient of ⊕ (u_k)_!G|_{U_k} with kernel built from the finite intersections, and use (a) with (d) and the open case.

(d) X has finitely many connected components (it is qcqs locally noetherian); over each choose a finite étale Galois cover q: X'' → X with group G splitting π (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-galois-category). Since q is étale, q^{-1}π_*F(V'') = F(V'' ×_X X′), and X'' ×_X X′ is a disjoint union of copies of X'' given by sections σ_s, so q^{-1}π_*F ≅ ⊕_s σ_s^{-1}F is constructible by (b). Choose a G-stable stratification of X'' on whose strata it is locally constant of finite type (intersect the G-translates of one). For a G-stable constructible C ⊆ X'', q(C) and q(X'' ∖ C) are disjoint because the fibres of q are G-orbits; they are compact for the constructible topology and cover X, so both are constructible. Hence the images of the strata stratify X, and π_*F is locally constant of finite type on each image, because local constancy can be checked after the étale surjection q.
(e) The stalk at ξ is a stalk of the restriction to the stratum containing the support of ξ, which is locally a finitely generated constant module.
acceptance: For the complement Z of a quasi-compact open U in qcqs X, i_*i^{-1}Λ = coker(j_!Λ → Λ) is constructible by (a) and (c).

Hansen's use (proof of Proposition 2.4): for a short exact sequence 0 → F → G → H → 0 on a dense Zariski-open U ⊆ X in which two of the three terms are locally constant of finite type, all three are constructible on U (Hub96 2.7.3 as cited by Hansen).

sources.match: The same stability under kernels, cokernels, images and extensions for constructible sheaves defined by stratifications.
