nodes.title: Every étale sheaf of Λ-modules is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves
nodes.statement: Let X be a qcqs locally noetherian analytic adic space and Λ a noetherian ring. Every F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves, though in general not of its constructible subsheaves (on the closed unit disc, coker(j_!Λ → Λ) for the open unit disc j: U → X has stalk Λ at the rank-two point |T| = 1⁻ outside U, while every constructible subsheaf has constructible support in X ∖ U and every constructible set containing that point meets U); in particular every abelian torsion sheaf is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves of ℤ/n-modules for varying n. Consequently H^q(X, −) and, for qcqs g: X′ → X, R^q g_* commute with filtered colimits, so statements about torsion sheaves reduce to constructible ones.
hypotheses: X qcqs locally noetherian analytic; Λ noetherian.
proofSteps: F is a quotient of ⊕ u_!Λ over pairs (u: U → X qcqs étale, s ∈ F(U)) (each section s gives u_!Λ → F by adjunction, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero); applying the same to the kernel gives a presentation H → G → F → 0 with G, H direct sums of sheaves u_!Λ (ECD proof of Lemma 20.4). Each u_!Λ is compact, Hom(u_!Λ, −) = Γ(U, −) commuting with filtered colimits for qcqs U (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites), so H → G is the filtered colimit of maps H_α → G_α between finite subsums and F = colim_α coker(H_α → G_α), each cokernel constructible by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/constructible-sheaves-stability (a), (c). The images of finite subsums of G in F are quotients of constructible sheaves and need not be constructible.
Torsion sheaves: F = colim_n F[n] with F[n] a sheaf of ℤ/n-modules; apply the first part with Λ = ℤ/n.

Commutation with filtered colimits: the étale topos of a qcqs space is coherent (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/affine-local-description (iv)), so DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites applies to H^q(X, −); for R^q g_* use the sheafification description (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/higher-direct-image-sheafification) on qcqs objects.
acceptance: Hansen's reduction (proof of Theorem 1.7): H^n(X, −) commutes with filtered colimits, so it suffices to treat constructible sheaves.
ECD Lemma 20.4: on a spectral space every sheaf of Λ-modules is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves.

nodes.title: The Kummer sequence and Hilbert 90 on the étale site
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in O_X(X). Let G_m be the sheaf U ↦ O_U(U)^× on X_ét (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf) and μ_n := ker(G_m → G_m, x ↦ x^n). (a) The sequence 1 → μ_n → G_m → G_m → 1 is exact on X_ét. (b) Its connecting map gives δ: O(X)^×/(O(X)^×)^n ↪ H^1(X, μ_n) and an exact sequence 0 → O(X)^×/n → H^1(X, μ_n) → H^1(X, G_m)[n] → 0. (c) H^1(X_ét, G_m) ≅ Pic(X) (Hilbert 90), so H^1(X, μ_n) classifies pairs (L, ψ) of a line bundle L and an isomorphism ψ: L^{⊗n} ≅ O_X.
hypotheses: n invertible on X (for X over Spa(K, K⁺), n prime to the characteristic of K).
X locally strongly sheafy analytic; (c) uses étale descent of line bundles.
proofSteps: (a) Left exactness is the definition of μ_n. Surjectivity of x ↦ x^n: for U = Spa(B, B⁺) ∈ X_ét^aff and f ∈ B^×, B′ = B[T]/(T^n − f) is finite free of rank n and étale over B (the discriminant of T^n − f is ± n^n f^{n−1}, a unit), hence Spa of the finite étale pair (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra) is a faithfully finite étale covering of U on which f becomes the n-th power of T; general U are covered by basis objects (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison).
(b) Long exact cohomology sequence (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image) with H^0(X, G_m) = O(X)^×.

(c) A G_m-torsor on X_ét is an invertible O_{X_ét}-module, and invertible O_{X_ét}-modules are pulled back from line bundles on X_an (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-acyclicity-of-vector-bundles, vector bundles on X_an and X_ét correspond); torsor classification by H^1 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/cech-to-derived-comparison in degree one).
acceptance: If K contains a primitive n-th root of unity ζ and X lies over Spa(K, K⁺), μ_n ≅ ℤ/n on X_ét via ζ, and H^1(X, ℤ/n) ⊇ O(X)^×/n.

Non-example: for K imperfect of characteristic p (e.g. K = 𝔽_p((t))) and n = p, T^p − f is not étale, the p-th power map on G_m is not an epimorphism of étale sheaves on Spa(K, O_K) (for f ∈ K^× not a p-th power), and the Artin–Schreier sequence replaces the Kummer sequence.

nodes.title: Roots of unity and Tate twists on étale and pro-étale sites
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space and n ≥ 1 invertible in O_X(X). (i) μ_n := ker(x ↦ x^n on G_m), with μ_n(U) = the group of n-th roots of unity in O_U(U)^× (Mathlib `rootsOfUnity n (O_U(U))`); it is a torsion local system of free ℤ/n-modules of rank one (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-local-systems), trivialised on the finite étale cover adjoining a primitive n-th root of unity. (ii) For a ℤ/n-algebra Λ: Λ(1) := Λ ⊗_{ℤ/n} μ_n, Λ(r) := Λ(1)^{⊗_Λ r} for r ≥ 0, Λ(r) := Hom_Λ(Λ(−r), Λ) for r < 0, and F(r) := F ⊗_Λ Λ(r) for F ∈ Sh(X_ét, Λ) and for complexes in D⁺(X_ét, Λ). (iii) For a prime ℓ invertible on X: ℤ_ℓ(1) := (μ_{ℓ^m})_{m ≥ 1} with the ℓ-th power transition maps, a lisse ℤ_ℓ-sheaf, and on X_proét (X locally noetherian) Ẑ_ℓ(1) := lim_m ν^*μ_{ℓ^m} with F(r) := F ⊗_{Ẑ_ℓ} Ẑ_ℓ(1)^{⊗r} for sheaves of Ẑ_ℓ-modules. (iv) Canonical isomorphisms Λ(r) ⊗_Λ Λ(s) ≅ Λ(r + s), g^{-1}(F(r)) ≅ (g^{-1}F)(r), (Rg_*K)(r) ≅ Rg_*(K(r)) (projection formula for the locally free rank-one Λ(r)), and stalks (μ_n)_ξ = μ_n(C) at a geometric point Spa(C, C⁺). The exactness of the Kummer sequence is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/kummer-sequence.
hypotheses: n (resp. ℓ) invertible on X; Λ a ℤ/n-algebra in (ii).
Twists are defined for all r ∈ ℤ, with Λ(0) = Λ.
proofSteps: (i) μ_n is a sheaf as a kernel of a map of sheaves (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-structure-sheaf). On the cover given over an affinoid Spa(B, B⁺) by B[T]/(Φ_n(T)), finite étale because Φ_n divides the separable polynomial T^n − 1 (n is a unit; AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/finite-etale-affinoid-algebra), T is a primitive n-th root of unity (Φ_n(T) and T^d − 1 for d | n, d < n, generate the unit ideal over ℤ[1/n]), so μ_n ≅ ℤ/n there. Stalks: filtered colimits commute with kernels, so (μ_n)_ξ is the n-torsion of O_{X_ét,ξ}^×, which maps bijectively to μ_n(C) because O_{X_ét,ξ} is strictly henselian with residue field separably closed of characteristic prime to n (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic (a)) and T^n − 1 is separable.
(ii) Tensor products and internal Hom in Sh(X_ét, Λ) (sheafified), locally free of rank one because μ_n is.
(iii) Inverse systems as in Scholze Proposition 6.7; lisse by (i) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/torsion-local-systems).

(iv) Associativity/commutativity of ⊗ and local freeness; g^{-1} is monoidal and g^{-1}μ_n = μ_n (g^{-1}G_m → G_m); projection formula for a locally free rank-one sheaf checked étale-locally where it is Λ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/affine-local-description (iii)).
acceptance: For X over Spa(ℂ_p, O_{ℂ_p}), a compatible system of roots of unity gives ℤ_ℓ(1) ≅ ℤ_ℓ on X_ét.
For X = Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) and a prime ℓ ≠ p with ℓ ∤ p − 1, μ_ℓ is a nonconstant local system (μ_ℓ(ℚ_p) = 1), whose Galois module is the cyclotomic character mod ℓ.

nodes.title: Huber tilde-limits X ∼ lim X_i: the topological condition and the density condition
nodes.statement: Let I be a small cofiltered category, i ↦ X_i a functor from I to analytic adic spaces (anchor Layer 5; every point analytic) whose transition morphisms f_a: X_j → X_i are quasi-compact and quasi-separated (the X_i themselves need not be quasi-compact), X an analytic adic space and φ = (φ_i: X → X_i)_i a compatible family (f_a ∘ φ_j = φ_i). The pair (X, φ) is a tilde-limit, written X ∼ lim_i X_i, if the two following conditions hold, which are recorded as separate predicates. (a) Topological condition `IsTildeLimit.Homeomorph`: the continuous map |X| → lim_i |X_i| into the limit of the underlying topological spaces (Mathlib `TopCat.limitCone`) is a homeomorphism. (b) Density condition `IsTildeLimit.Dense`: every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U = Spa(A, A⁺) ⊆ X such that the subring E_U := ⋃ im(O_{X_i}(V) → A), the union over i ∈ I and over open V ⊆ X_i with φ_i(U) ⊆ V, is dense in A (Huber's form; Scholze–Weinstein take the colimit only over the open affinoids V = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) ⊆ X_i through which U → X_i factors, and that colimit maps into E_U, so their condition implies (b) for the same U). Variant for pseudo-adic spaces (Huber's Definition 2.4.2): for quasi-compact quasi-separated pseudo-adic spaces (X_i, S_i) and (X, S) with adic transition morphisms (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site), (a) asks S → lim_i S_i to be a homeomorphism for the subspace topologies and (b) is asked at every x ∈ S, U an affinoid open neighbourhood of x in X. Conventions pinned: (i) a tilde-limit is not a categorical limit in adic spaces — X ∼ X₀ may hold with X ≇ X₀, and inverse limits of adic spaces rarely exist; the notation ∼ is never read as lim; (ii) (a) and (b) are independent and both required; (iii) the residue-field variant ∼′ of Scholze 2012 Definition 7.14 (density of colim k(x_i) in k(x)) is weaker and is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit; (iv) for perfectoid X this predicate is PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit, which imports it.
hypotheses: I small cofiltered; transition maps of (X_i) quasi-compact and quasi-separated (Scholze–Weinstein Definition 2.4.1 generality).
X and all X_i analytic adic spaces (sheafy, anchor Layer 5); X need not be quasi-compact or locally noetherian.

Huber's own setting (2.4.1–2.4.2: the category of quasi-compact quasi-separated pseudo-adic spaces, not necessarily analytic, with adic morphisms) overlaps this node in the qcqs analytic case, where every morphism is adic.
proofSteps: Definition as the conjunction of the two predicates; (a) uses mathlib:TopCat.limitCone, (b) the structure sheaves of X and of the X_i on open subsets.
Pseudo-adic variant: the same with the subspaces S, S_i and ambient affinoid neighbourhoods, as in Huber 2.4.2; for S = |X|, S_i = |X_i| it is the adic version.

Spectrality (API): if all X_i are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, lim |X_i| is spectral with spectral projections (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces), hence so is |X| under (a).
Reindexing (API): along an initial functor J → I both the limit of topological spaces and the density union are unchanged.
acceptance: Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.2 / ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion: the completed colimit of a system of affinoid rings with compatible rings and ideals of definition is a tilde-limit.
Strict localisations: Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) ∼ lim V over affinoid étale neighbourhoods of a geometric point ξ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/strict-localisation-tilde-limit).

nodes.title: The adic spectrum of a colimit of Huber pairs is the limit of the adic spectra
nodes.statement: Let I be a small filtered category and (A_i, A_i⁺)_{i∈I} a diagram of Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`) with continuous transition maps, together with rings of definition A_{i,0} ⊆ A_i mapped into one another and finitely generated ideals of definition I_i ⊆ A_{i,0} with I_j = I_i A_{j,0} for i → j (the transition maps are adic). Let A := colim_i A_i with the topology in which A_0 := colim_i A_{i,0} is an open subring carrying the I-adic topology, I := colim_i I_i, and A⁺ := colim_i A_i⁺. Then: (i) (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair and the maps (A_i, A_i⁺) → (A, A⁺) are adic morphisms of Huber pairs; (ii) the map Spa(A, A⁺) → lim_i Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) induced by the Tau Ceti maps `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap` is a homeomorphism onto the limit of topological spaces; (iii) every rational subset of Spa(A, A⁺) is the preimage of a rational subset of some Spa(A_i, A_i⁺); (iv) for the completion (Â, Â⁺), Spa(Â, Â⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism matching rational subsets, so (ii)–(iii) hold for Spa(Â, Â⁺); (v) colim_i A_i → Â has dense image. (vi) Tate re-topologisation: if (A, A⁺) is a Tate Huber pair with pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ A⁺, the Huber ring A′ equal to A as a ring, with A⁺ an open ring of definition carrying the ϖ-adic topology, has Spa(A′, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) with the same rational subsets (both are the valuations v with v(A⁺) ≤ 1 and v(ϖ) cofinal); (vii) consequently, for a filtered system of complete Tate Huber pairs with a compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ (no compatible rings of definition needed), lim_i Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) ≅ Spa(L̂⁺[1/ϖ], L̂⁺), where L̂⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of L⁺ := colim_i A_i⁺. In the Tate case with compatible rings of definition this is PerfectoidSpaces:P5/spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs.
hypotheses: I filtered; in (i)–(v) compatible rings of definition and finitely generated ideals of definition with I_j = I_i A_{j,0}; in (vi)–(vii) complete Tate pairs with a compatible pseudouniformiser.
No perfectoid or noetherian hypothesis.
proofSteps: (i) A_0 is an open subring with a finitely generated ideal I (generated by the image of generators of any I_i); A⁺ is integrally closed in A (an integral equation and its coefficients live at a finite stage, where A_i⁺ is integrally closed), open (it contains the image of an open subgroup I_i^N A_{i,0} ⊆ A_i⁺) and consists of power-bounded elements (images of power-bounded elements under continuous maps).

(ii) Points: valuations on A are compatible systems of valuations on the A_i, since every finite set of elements and relations of A comes from a finite stage (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.comap). Continuity: by Wedhorn Theorem 7.10 and Remark 7.11 (1) (Tau Ceti `mem_spvOfIdeal_extendedIdealOfDefinition_of_isContinuous` and `PairOfDefinition.isContinuous_of_forall_cofinalValue`) a valuation is continuous iff v(a) is cofinal for the finitely many generators a of the ideal of definition, which are images of generators of I_i; the plus-ring condition is checked on each A_i⁺ (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.mem_spa_iff). Hence the map is a continuous bijection (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.continuous_spaComap).

(iii) For R(T/s) with T·A open, finitely many elements of T, s, and of I^N ⊆ T·A are defined at a stage i with I_i^N ⊆ T_i·A_i, so R(T/s) is the preimage of R(T_i/s_i) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset); rational subsets form a basis, so the bijection is open, hence a homeomorphism.

(iv) Wedhorn Proposition 7.48 (Huber 1993 Proposition 3.9): Spa of the completion of an affinoid ring maps homeomorphically onto Spa of the ring, matching rational subsets; the anchor lists it but it is not a pinned declaration (request to tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets).
(v) mathlib:UniformSpace.Completion.denseRange_coe.

(vi) For a Tate ring, continuity of a valuation is cofinality of v(ϖ) for any ring of definition containing ϖ (Wedhorn Remark 7.11 (1) with I = ϖA_0), and T·A is open iff T generates the unit ideal (an open ideal contains a unit ϖ^N); both descriptions are independent of the choice of ring of definition, and A⁺ is open and bounded for its own ϖ-adic topology.

(vii) Apply (vi) to each A_i (ring of definition A_i⁺, ideal ϖA_i⁺; the transition maps stay continuous because ϖ^n A_j⁺ ⊇ image of ϖ^n A_i⁺), then (i)–(iv) to the resulting system, whose colimit has ring of definition L⁺ and completion L̂⁺[1/ϖ].
acceptance: For a constant system the statement is Spa(A, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺).
For A_n = K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩ over a complete nonarchimedean field K: Spa of the completed colimit K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is lim_n Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩).

nodes.title: The affinoid criterion: completed colimits and colimit-presented affinoids are tilde-limits
nodes.statement: (1) Huber-pair form. Let (A_i, A_i⁺)_{i∈I} be a filtered system of complete Huber pairs with rings of definition and finitely generated ideals of definition as in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/spa-of-colimit-huber-pair, such that each X_i := Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) is an adic space (A_i sheafy), and let (B, B⁺) be a complete Huber pair with compatible adic morphisms (A_i, A_i⁺) → (B, B⁺) such that X := Spa(B, B⁺) is an adic space. Suppose (T) the closure B_0 of the image of colim A_{i,0} is a ring of definition of B with ideal of definition generated by the image of I_i (the topology of B is the colimit topology), (D) colim A_i → B has dense image, and (P) B⁺ is the closure of the image of colim A_i⁺; equivalently, (B, B⁺) is the completed colimit (Â, Â⁺). Then X ∼ lim_i X_i (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit) with the density condition holding globally for U = X. (2) Tate form (colimit-presented affinoids). Let the A_i be complete Tate rings with a compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ, L⁺ := colim_i A_i⁺, and (C, C⁺) a complete Tate Huber pair with compatible morphisms (A_i, A_i⁺) → (C, C⁺) such that (P2) the induced maps L⁺/ϖ^n L⁺ → C⁺/ϖ^n C⁺ are isomorphisms for all n ≥ 1; call Spa(C, C⁺) colimit-presented by (Spa(A_i, A_i⁺)). Then Spa(C, C⁺) ∼ lim_i Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) with global density, the kernel of colim A_i → C lies in ⋂_n ϖ^n L⁺, and every rational subset of Spa(C, C⁺) is the preimage of one at a finite stage. The completed colimit in the Tate case is colimit-presented. (3) Condition (T), resp. (P2), cannot be replaced by density and a plus-ring condition alone (non-example below).
hypotheses: Complete Huber (resp. Tate) pairs; all Spa's involved are adic spaces (sheafy). This restricts to honest adic spaces: Scholze–Weinstein state Proposition 2.4.2 for the uncompleted colimit in their larger category of adic spaces (Definition 2.1.5), where Spa(A, A⁺) = Spa(Â, Â⁺) is defined without completeness or sheafiness, so the source statement is correct as written there.
The topology on the target must be the colimit topology (T), or the plus rings must agree modulo every power of ϖ (P2).
proofSteps: (1)(a) By ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/spa-of-colimit-huber-pair (ii) and (iv), Spa(B, B⁺) = Spa(Â, Â⁺) → lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) is a homeomorphism. (1)(b) For U = X and V = X_i, E_X contains the image of colim A_i, dense in B by (D) (spa-of-colimit (v)). The equivalence of (T)+(D)+(P) with (B, B⁺) ≅ (Â, Â⁺) is the uniqueness of completions.

(2)(a) By spa-of-colimit (vi)–(vii), lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) ≅ Spa(L̂⁺[1/ϖ], L̂⁺) and Spa(C, C⁺) ≅ Spa(Ĉ⁺[1/ϖ], Ĉ⁺) (ϖ-adic completions); by (P2), L̂⁺ ≅ Ĉ⁺, compatibly with the maps, so Spa(C, C⁺) → lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) is a homeomorphism and rational subsets come from a finite stage (spa-of-colimit (iii)).

(2)(b) Density: C⁺ = im(L⁺) + ϖ^n C⁺ for every n by (P2), and ϖ^n C⁺ is open, so the image of colim A_i is dense in C. Kernel: if f ∈ colim A_i maps to 0, then ϖ^k f ∈ L⁺ for some k and ϖ^k f maps into ϖ^m C⁺ for every m, so ϖ^k f ∈ ϖ^m L⁺ for every m by (P2).
(2) for completed colimits: Â⁺/ϖ^n = A⁺/ϖ^n because ϖ^n A⁺ is open in A⁺.

Non-example: the constant system A_0 = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ with (B, B⁺) = (ℚ_p⟨T/p⟩, the integral closure of im(ℤ_p⟨T⟩) + B°°): the image is dense (polynomials are dense) and B⁺ is the ring of integral elements generated by the image, but Spa(B, B⁺) maps onto the closure of {|T| ≤ |p|} in Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩), not onto the whole disc, so (a) fails; here (T) and (P2) both fail (T/p ∈ B° is not approximated modulo p by elements of ℤ_p⟨T⟩).
acceptance: Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.2: Spa(A, A⁺) ∼ lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) for the colimit with its colimit topology.
Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ∼ lim_n Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩) for any complete nonarchimedean K of residue characteristic p (the perfectoid case is PerfectoidSpaces P7).

Serves the AdicSpacesPartII R5 request (affinoid criterion for X_∞ ×_L U ∼ lim X_n ×_L U), with hypothesis (T) or (P2) made explicit: density of colim A_n in A and the plus-ring condition do not suffice.

sources.match: The criterion (its conclusion is Spa(A, A⁺) ∼ lim Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) for the colimit with the stated topology), form (1).
The colimit topology must be specified: there is no canonical choice, which is why hypothesis (T), resp. (P2), is part of the criterion.
The density condition verified globally.

nodes.title: Density on rational subsets defined at a finite level, and restriction of tilde-limits
nodes.statement: Let X ∼ lim_i X_i be a tilde-limit (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit) and U ⊆ X an affinoid open satisfying the density condition, i.e. E_U = ⋃ im(O_{X_i}(V) → O_X(U)) is dense in O_X(U). (a) If i ∈ I, V ⊆ X_i is an open affinoid with φ_i(U) ⊆ V and R = R_V(T/s) a rational subset of V, then U′ := U ∩ φ_i^{-1}(R) (a rational subset of U) satisfies the density condition. (b) If all X_i = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) and X = Spa(A, A⁺) are affinoid and colim_i A_i → A has dense image, then for every rational subset W_i ⊆ X_i with preimages W_j ⊆ X_j (i → j) and W ⊆ X, colim_j O(W_j) → O(W) has dense image, and W ∼ lim_j W_j. (c) More generally, for an open U_i ⊆ X_i with preimages U_j, U, the restriction U ∼ lim_j U_j holds whenever U is covered by affinoids satisfying the density condition (for example by (a)). The density of colim O(W_j) in O(W) for an arbitrary affinoid W ∼ lim W_j is not asserted; it is supplied under the hypotheses above.
hypotheses: Tilde-limit X ∼ lim X_i; in (b) global density on the affinoid X.
Rational subsets defined at a finite level.
proofSteps: (a) Pull T, s back to O(U); U′ = R_U(φ_i^*T/φ_i^*s) and O(U′) is the completion of O(U)[1/s] for the rational topology (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocalization), in which the image of O(U)[1/s] is dense (mathlib:UniformSpace.Completion.denseRange_coe). For (j, V′) with φ_j(U) ⊆ V′ ⊆ f_a^{-1}(V), the open V′ ∩ f_a^{-1}(R) contains φ_j(U′) and s is invertible on it, so E_{U′} ⊇ {e/s^m : e ∈ E_U}. Multiplication by s^{-m} is continuous on O(U′) and O(U) → O(U′) is continuous, so E_U dense in O(U) gives {e/s^m} dense in the image of O(U)[1/s], hence in O(U′).

(b) Apply (a) with U = X, V = X_i; the topological condition for W: |W| = φ_i^{-1}|W_i| and preimages commute with limits of topological spaces, so |W| ≅ lim_j |W_j| (restriction of the homeomorphism).
(c) The topological condition restricts as in (b); density is local by definition.
acceptance: For the affinoid criterion (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion) every rational subset defined at a finite level satisfies global density.
Serves the PerfectoidSpaces P8 request (density of lim O(V_i) in O(V)) whenever V is a rational subset defined at a finite level of a globally dense affinoid.

sources.match: Restriction to the preimage of an open (or rational) subset at a finite level is the case of an open immersion Y_i → X_i.
The density condition whose persistence to rational subsets is proved.

nodes.title: The strict localisation of an analytic adic space is a tilde-limit of its affinoid étale neighbourhoods
nodes.statement: Let Y be a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space, ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → Y a geometric point with support y, N(ξ)^aff the cofiltered category of étale neighbourhoods (V, v̄) of ξ with V affinoid Tate (cofinal in N(ξ), AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation), L := colim_{N(ξ)^aff} O(V) = O_{Y_ét,ξ}, L⁺ := colim O⁺(V), m_ξ the maximal ideal of the local ring L, κ(ξ) = L/m_ξ, and (C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) the completion of (κ(ξ), κ(ξ)⁺) where κ(ξ)⁺ is the valuation ring of the valuation at the closed point (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic (a)). Then: (a) L⁺ is the preimage of κ(ξ)⁺ in L, and m_ξ ⊆ ϖ^n L⁺ for every n and every pseudouniformiser ϖ of a neighbourhood; (b) the maps L⁺/ϖ^n → C_ξ⁺/ϖ^n are isomorphisms for all n, i.e. Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) is colimit-presented by the neighbourhoods in the sense of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion (2); (c) hence Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) ∼ lim_{N(ξ)^aff} V is a Huber tilde-limit with global density, and |Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺)| ≅ lim_{N(ξ)} |V|, which is clause (b) of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic, obtained here without its shrinking step; (d) (C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) is an algebraically closed affinoid field with C_ξ⁺ = C⁺ ∩ C_ξ, and the valuation rings of Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) correspond to the vertical generisations of y.
hypotheses: Y locally strongly sheafy analytic; ξ a geometric point with C⁺ of any rank (higher-rank field pairs are kept).
proofSteps: (a) L = colim O_{V,v} over the images v of the closed point (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation (ii)–(iii)); in each stalk O⁺_{V,v} is the preimage of the valuation ring of k(v) and the maximal ideal is the support of the valuation (Wedhorn Proposition 8.6); passing to the colimit gives L⁺ = preimage of κ(ξ)⁺. For f with v(f) = 0, the rational subset {|f| ≤ |ϖ^n|} is an open neighbourhood of v, hence of the image of the lift (open sets are stable under generisation), and on it f/ϖ^n ∈ O⁺ (Wedhorn Proposition 7.52 (1)), so f ∈ ϖ^n L⁺.
(b) Surjectivity: κ(ξ)⁺ = L⁺/m_ξ is dense in C_ξ⁺ and ϖ^n C_ξ⁺ is open. Injectivity: if ℓ ∈ L⁺ maps into ϖ^n C_ξ⁺, then ℓ/ϖ^n has valuation ≤ 1 at the closed point, so ℓ/ϖ^n ∈ L⁺ by (a).
(c) ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion (2), the maps Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) → V being induced by the lifts of ξ.

(d) C_ξ algebraically closed and C_ξ⁺ = C⁺ ∩ C_ξ: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic (a); the valuation of κ(ξ) restricts to that of k(y) along the separable algebraic extension κ(ξ)/k(y), which induces a bijection on convex subgroups, and the canonical map Spa κ(y) → Y is a homeomorphism onto the vertical generisations of y (Wedhorn §8.1).
acceptance: For Y = Spa(K, K⁺) with K⁺ of rank 2 and ξ supported at the closed point, Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) has two points and is the tilde-limit of the Spa(L, L⁺) over finite separable L/K inside C (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic (c)).
For Y a rigid space and ξ of rank one, this is the étale fibre Sp(F_e) of de Jong–van der Put §3.3.

sources.match: Huber's statement that strict localisations of analytic spaces are spectra of algebraically closed affinoid fields, proved here as a tilde-limit.
Step (a): the maximal ideal of the stalk is the support of the valuation of the point.
Step (a): f/ϖ^n lies in the plus ring on the neighbourhood where it is bounded by 1.
The rigid-analytic rank-one case: the étale site of the étale fibre is the limit of the sites of the neighbourhoods.

nodes.title: Base change of colimit-presented tilde-limits
nodes.statement: Let Z = Spa(C, C⁺) be colimit-presented by a system Z_i = Spa(A_i, A_i⁺) of complete Tate affinoids with compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion (2); examples: completed colimits, and strict localisations by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/strict-localisation-tilde-limit). (a) If (A_{i₀}, A_{i₀}⁺) → (B, B⁺) is an adic morphism of complete Huber pairs, topologically of finite type or étale, such that the completed tensor products B_i := B ⊗̂_{A_{i₀}} A_i (i over i₀) and B_C := B ⊗̂_{A_{i₀}} C are sheafy (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product), then Spa(B_C) is colimit-presented by (Spa(B_i)), hence Spa(B_C) ∼ lim_i Spa(B_i). (b) Globally: if Y(ξ) ∼ lim V is the strict localisation of a locally strongly sheafy analytic Y and f: X → Y is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of weakly finite type, then X ×_Y Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) ∼ lim_{N(ξ)^aff} X ×_Y V, locally on X colimit-presented; likewise for the base change of any colimit-presented system along such a morphism. The statement for arbitrary tilde-limits and arbitrary maps Y_i → X_i (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.3, proved there by reference to Huber's Remark 2.4.3) is not claimed.
hypotheses: Colimit-presented tilde-limits of complete Tate affinoids; B topologically of finite type or étale over A_{i₀}, with sheafy completed tensor products.
For (b), f quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of weakly finite type, so that the fibre products exist (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence).
proofSteps: (a) Points, without assuming (P2) for B: put M_i := B⁺ ⊗_{A_{i₀}⁺} A_i⁺, M := colim_i M_i = B⁺ ⊗_{A_{i₀}⁺} L⁺ and M_C := B⁺ ⊗_{A_{i₀}⁺} C⁺, so that M_i[1/ϖ] = B ⊗_{A_{i₀}} A_i and M_C[1/ϖ] = B ⊗_{A_{i₀}} C. By the construction of completed tensor products (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product: ring of definition from B_0 ⊗ A_{i,0}, plus ring the completed integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗ A_i⁺), Wedhorn Proposition 7.48 and tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa_integralClosure, a point of Spa(B_i) is a valuation v of M_i[1/ϖ] with v(M_i) ≤ 1 and v(ϖ) cofinal, and likewise for Spa(B_C) with M_C; so lim_i Spa(B_i) is the set of such valuations on M[1/ϖ] (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/spa-of-colimit-huber-pair (vi)–(vii)). Such a valuation is continuous for the ϖ-adic topology and so corresponds to a unique one on the ϖ-adic completion M̂, and likewise for M_C. By right exactness of ⊗ and (P2) for the A_i, M/ϖ^n = B⁺/ϖ^n ⊗ L⁺/ϖ^n ≅ B⁺/ϖ^n ⊗ C⁺/ϖ^n = M_C/ϖ^n for all n, compatibly, so M̂ ≅ M̂_C and Spa(B_C) → lim_i Spa(B_i) is bijective. Rational subsets are defined at a finite stage (spa-of-colimit (iii)), so it is a homeomorphism. Density: B ⊗ L is dense in B ⊗ C for the topology with ring of definition the image of B_0 ⊗ C_0, because L is dense in C, so colim B_i → B_C has dense image.

Plus rings modulo ϖ^n: an element ℓ ∈ L_B whose image in B_C has |ℓ| ≤ |ϖ^n| at every point of Spa(B_C) (Wedhorn Proposition 7.52 (1): i.e. lies in ϖ^n B_C⁺) satisfies |ℓ| ≤ |ϖ^n| on some stage Spa(B_i): the set {|ℓ| > |ϖ^n|} ⊆ Spa(B_i) is closed constructible with empty preimage in the limit, so it is empty at a finite stage (Stacks Tag 0A30); hence ℓ ∈ ϖ^n L_B⁺. With density of the image of L_B⁺ modulo the open subgroup ϖ^n B_C⁺ this gives L_B⁺/ϖ^n ≅ B_C⁺/ϖ^n, i.e. (P2).

(b) Cover X by finitely many affinoids X_k mapping into affinoids of Y pulled back from a finite stage; fibre products of affinoids are Spa of completed tensor products (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product; for étale V over an affinoid, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-base-change); apply (a) to each X_k and to their pairwise intersections, and glue: the topological condition is local over a cover by preimages of opens at a finite stage, and density is local by definition.
acceptance: For f: X → Y and ξ a rank-one geometric point of a rigid space Y, X ×_Y Spa(C_ξ, O_{C_ξ}) is the étale fibre X_e of de Jong–van der Put, and (b) is the tilde-limit form of their Lemma 3.7.1.
For an étale V_{i₀} → Z_{i₀} the base change is the étale case of Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.3 for colimit-presented systems.

sources.match: Scholze–Weinstein restate Huber's Remark 2.4.3 (base change of tilde-limits); its proof is only in Huber's book, so the colimit-presented case is proved here and the general case is a recorded gap.
Plus rings are the functions bounded by 1 on the adic spectrum, used to compare plus rings modulo ϖ^n.
Quasi-compact opens (and their complements) of a cofiltered limit of spectral spaces come from, and are compared at, a finite stage.
The étale fibre X ×_Y (geometric point) in rigid geometry, the object of (b).

nodes.title: The étale site of a tilde-limit is the colimit of the étale sites (Huber 2.4.4)
nodes.statement: Let X ∼ lim_i X_i be a tilde-limit of quasi-compact quasi-separated locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces (locally noetherian in Huber's setting), the index category having a final object 0. Then: (i) every quasi-compact quasi-separated étale Y → X is isomorphic to Y_i ×_{X_i} X for some i and some quasi-compact quasi-separated étale Y_i → X_i; (ii) for Y_i, Y′_i étale qcqs over X_i, Hom_X(Y_i ×_{X_i} X, Y′_i ×_{X_i} X) = colim_{j → i} Hom_{X_j}(Y_i ×_{X_i} X_j, Y′_i ×_{X_i} X_j); (iii) a finite family of such maps is a covering over X iff it is one over some X_j; hence (iv) the site of qcqs étale X-spaces is the filtered 2-colimit of the sites of qcqs étale X_i-spaces, and the étale topos of X is the projective limit of the fibred topos (X_{i,ét}~)_i. This is proved here for tilde-limits that are locally colimit-presented (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-base-change: completed colimits of affinoid systems, strict localisations and their base changes along qcqs morphisms locally of weakly finite type), which covers every use in H0; for arbitrary tilde-limits of qcqs locally noetherian spaces (Huber Proposition 2.4.4) the finite étale descent step rests on Huber's book and is recorded as a gap.
hypotheses: X, X_i qcqs, locally strongly sheafy analytic; I with final object 0.
Complete proof for locally colimit-presented tilde-limits; the general Huber case is a recorded gap.
proofSteps: Opens: quasi-compact opens of |X| ≅ lim |X_i| come from quasi-compact opens at a finite stage, and inclusions and equalities of such opens are detected at a finite stage (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces; Stacks Tag 0A30), the X_i being spectral.

Reduction: étale maps are locally an open immersion into a finite étale space over an open (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism), so it suffices to descend finite étale algebras, their morphisms and surjectivity over the affinoids of a finite cover by rational subsets defined at a finite stage, which are again colimit-presented: a rational localisation is a base change along a topologically finite type map (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-base-change (a); density by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-density-rational-restriction).

Finite étale descent for Z = Spa(C, C⁺) colimit-presented by Spa(A_i, A_i⁺): FÉt(L) = 2-colim FÉt(A_i) for L = colim A_i, finite étale algebras being of finite presentation (Stacks Tag 00QO for morphisms, and descent of finitely presented algebras for objects). The plus ring A_i⁺ of a complete Tate ring is henselian along ϖ: it is the filtered union of the ϖ-adically complete rings A_i⁺ ∩ R over rings of definition R (Stacks Tags 0ALJ, 0FWT); hence L⁺ = colim A_i⁺ is henselian along ϖ (0FWT), and likewise C⁺. By PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (a) (R = L⁺, resp. C⁺, t = ϖ): FÉt(L) ≃ FÉt(L̂⁺[1/ϖ]) and FÉt(C) ≃ FÉt(Ĉ⁺[1/ϖ]); the ϖ-adic completions agree by (P2), so FÉt(C) ≃ 2-colim FÉt(A_i). Surjectivity of finite étale maps is detected on points, hence at a finite stage.
Gap (general case): for an arbitrary Huber tilde-limit the affinoids of X are not known to be colimit-presented, and Huber's proof of 2.4.4 is not public.
(iv) from (i)–(iii): the description of projective limits of fibred topoi by the 2-colimit of the underlying sites (SGA 4 VI 8.2), requested from DiamondsAndVStacks:D0.
acceptance: For the strict localisation Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) ∼ lim V, every qcqs étale space over Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) is a finite disjoint union of open subspaces of copies of Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) near the closed point (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split) and descends to a neighbourhood.
Scholze 2012 Theorem 7.17 is the perfectoid analogue (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison), proved "as Huber 2.4.4" with the same open-immersion/finite-étale factorisation.

sources.match: Public restatement of the structure of Huber's proof of 2.4.4: local factorisation of étale maps and descent of the finite étale part.
Finite étale algebras over a completed direct limit come from a finite stage, the completed-colimit case of the descent step.
Statement (iv) for general tilde-limits of qcqs adic spaces is conjectural beyond the noetherian and perfectoid cases, which is why the proof here is restricted.
Henselianity of plus rings along ϖ, and of their colimit.
ϖ-adically complete rings of definition are henselian along ϖ.

nodes.title: Continuity of étale cohomology along tilde-limits (Huber 2.4.6)
nodes.statement: Let I be a small cofiltered category with final object 0, (X_i) a system of quasi-compact quasi-separated locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces with quasi-compact quasi-separated transition maps, X a quasi-compact quasi-separated locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space with X ∼ lim_i X_i (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit) for which the conclusion of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-topos-of-tilde-limit holds (in particular every colimit-presented tilde-limit). Let F_0 be a sheaf of sets (resp. groups, resp. abelian groups or Λ-modules) on X_{0,ét}, with pullbacks F_i on X_{i,ét} and F on X_ét. Then for n = 0 (resp. n ∈ {0, 1}, resp. all n ≥ 0) the natural map colim_i H^n(X_i, F_i) → H^n(X, F) is bijective. For a bounded-below complex K_0 the same holds for hypercohomology. The same statement holds for pseudo-adic tilde-limits of qcqs pseudo-adic spaces whose étale topoi satisfy the descent of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-topos-of-tilde-limit; that general hypothesis is exactly where Huber's Proposition 2.4.4 enters.
hypotheses: X, X_i qcqs; transition maps qcqs; final object 0; F_0 pulled back from X_0.
The étale topos of X is the projective limit of the (X_{i,ét}~) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-topos-of-tilde-limit), proved for colimit-presented tilde-limits.
proofSteps: By ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-topos-of-tilde-limit the site of qcqs étale X-spaces is the filtered 2-colimit of the sites of qcqs étale X_i-spaces along continuous finite-limit-preserving base-change functors, every covering of X coming from a finite stage.

All these sites are coherent (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/affine-local-description (iv)), and cohomology on a projective limit of coherent topoi of a sheaf pulled back from a stage is the colimit of the cohomologies (SGA 4 VI 8.7.7; requested from DiamondsAndVStacks:D0, stage-level prerequisite), in degrees 0, ≤ 1, all n for sets, groups, abelian groups; DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites gives the underlying commutation of cohomology with filtered colimits on each coherent stage.

Hypercohomology of bounded-below complexes: induction on the length of truncations and the five lemma, then passage to the limit along the canonical filtration (the maps are compatible with the connecting maps).
acceptance: Continuity along strict localisations: colim_{N(ξ)} H^n(X ×_Y V, F) = H^n(X ×_Y Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺), F) (the input of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-formula-strict-localisation).
For X = Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩) ∼ lim Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩) and a torsion sheaf F_0: H^n(X, F) = colim H^n(Spa(K⟨T^{1/p^n}⟩), F_n).

Česnavičius (4.10.7): on a common-ideal perfectoid completed-colimit system whose qcqs étale site is a filtered 2-colimit, finite locally constant abelian coefficient cohomology is the filtered colimit in every fixed degree.

sources.match: Huber's Corollary 2.4.6, the statement of this theorem.
The same deduction from the limit description of the étale topos via SGA 4 VI 8.7.7, in the diamond setting; the classical case uses the same argument.
The perfectoid restatement of Huber's 2.4.6.
Finite-stage henselizations and coherent-site continuity are separate inputs.

nodes.title: Stalks of higher direct images as colimits over étale neighbourhoods
nodes.statement: Let g: X′ → X be a morphism of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces, F ∈ Sh(X′_ét, Λ) and ξ a geometric point of X with category of étale neighbourhoods N(ξ) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation). Then for every q ≥ 0 there is a natural isomorphism (R^q g_*F)_ξ ≅ colim_{(V, v̄) ∈ N(ξ)} H^q(V ×_X X′, F), and the colimit may be taken over the cofinal subcategory N(ξ)^aff of affinoid neighbourhoods; it is compatible with the connecting maps in F. The same holds for ν: (R^qν_*F)_ξ ≅ colim_{N(ξ)} H^q(V, F) with V regarded in X_proét (X locally noetherian).
hypotheses: g arbitrary; ξ a geometric point (C⁺ of any rank).
proofSteps: R^q g_*F is the sheafification of U ↦ H^q(U ×_X X′, F) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/higher-direct-image-sheafification).

The stalk of a presheaf at a point of a site equals the stalk of its sheafification (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.presheafToSheafCompSheafFiberIso: presheafToSheaf ⋙ sheafFiber ≅ presheafFiber), and the presheaf stalk is the colimit over the category of elements, which is N(ξ) (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.presheafFiber).
Cofinality of affinoid neighbourhoods: AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation (ii) with AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/basis-comparison (a).
acceptance: For g finite étale, V ×_X X′ splits over small neighbourhoods into copies of V (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/local-systems-and-finite-etale-covers), and the formula gives (g_*F)_ξ = ⊕ over the geometric points of X′ above ξ of F at those points, and R^q g_*F = 0 for q > 0 after ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-formula-strict-localisation.

sources.match: The rigid-analytic statement comparing (R^q f_*S)_e with the étale fibre starts from this colimit description.
Higher direct images as sheafified cohomology presheaves, whose stalks are the colimits of this lemma.

nodes.title: Stalks of higher direct images are cohomology of the fibre over the strict localisation (Huber 2.6.1)
nodes.statement: Let f: X → Y be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces which is locally of weakly finite type, ξ: Spa(C, C⁺) → Y a geometric point (C⁺ of any rank) with strict localisation Y(ξ) = Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/strict-localisation-tilde-limit), and F a sheaf of sets (resp. groups, resp. abelian groups or Λ-modules) on X_ét with pullback G to X ×_Y Y(ξ). (a) For n = 0 (resp. n ≤ 1, resp. all n ≥ 0) there is a natural isomorphism (R^n f_*F)_ξ ≅ H^n(X ×_Y Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺), G), compatible with connecting maps and natural in ξ (in particular equivariant for automorphisms of the strict localisation over y); for K ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ), (Rf_*K)_ξ ≅ RΓ(X ×_Y Y(ξ), K|). (b) If ξ is the geometric point built from the completion C of an algebraic closure of the completed residue field k(y)^ (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points (a)), then (C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) = (C, C⁺), so (R^n f_*F)_ξ ≅ H^n(X ×_Y Spa(C, C⁺), F). (c) If y is a point of rank one (a maximal point of the analytic space Y), Y(ξ) = Spa(C_ξ, O_{C_ξ}) is one point and the stalk is the cohomology of the geometric fibre over y (Huber Example 2.6.2). (d) For higher-rank y the fibre over Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) has more points than the fibre over its generic point, and both enter (a). Comparison of the fibre over (C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) with the fibre over a larger algebraically closed field (C, C⁺) ⊋ (C_ξ, C_ξ⁺) is the invariance theorem of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2 (Huber 4.1.1(c)), not part of this node.
hypotheses: f quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of weakly finite type (so that X ×_Y V and X ×_Y Y(ξ) exist and are qcqs, locally strongly sheafy over qcqs V).
ξ a geometric point with C⁺ of any rank; field pairs (C, C⁺) are not replaced by (C, O_C).
proofSteps: (R^n f_*F)_ξ = colim_{N(ξ)^aff} H^n(X ×_Y V, F) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-of-higher-direct-image-as-colimit).

Y(ξ) ∼ lim_{N(ξ)^aff} V is a colimit-presented tilde-limit (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/strict-localisation-tilde-limit), so its base change X ×_Y Y(ξ) ∼ lim X ×_Y V is a colimit-presented tilde-limit of qcqs spaces (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-base-change (b); quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of X ×_Y V from those of f and of the affinoid V).

Replace N(ξ)^aff by its cofinal slice under one neighbourhood (V₀, v̄₀), which has a final object in the sense of the limit, and F by its restriction; apply ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity (its étale-topos hypothesis holds by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-topos-of-tilde-limit for colimit-presented tilde-limits).
Naturality in ξ: a morphism of geometric points transports lifts, hence acts on N(ξ) compatibly with both sides.

(b) For the standard geometric point, κ(ξ) is the separable closure of k(y) in C (étale neighbourhoods have finite separable residue extensions, and every finite separable extension is realised by a finite étale neighbourhood, AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/strict-localisation-analytic (a)); its closure in C is algebraically closed and contains k(y), hence equals the completed algebraic closure C.
(c) A rank-one valuation ring has no proper open overrings in its fraction field other than the field, so Spa(C_ξ, O_{C_ξ}) is a point.
Complexes: way-out argument on bounded-below complexes using (a) in each degree and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image.
acceptance: Finite étale f: the fibre is a finite disjoint union of copies of Spa(C_ξ, C_ξ⁺), so R^n f_*F = 0 for n > 0 by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/geometric-stalks-at-field-pairs.
Huber Lemma 3.8.2 (via the decomposition): (R^n g′_* f′_! F′)_y = H^n(X′ ×_{Y′} Y′(y), L) = 0 is an application of (a).
Bhatt–Hansen, proof of Proposition 3.15: two applications of Huber Example 2.6.2 compute (g^*Rf_*F)_y and (Rf′_*g′^*F)_y at rank-one points y, which is (c).

sources.match: Huber's Proposition 2.6.1, whose hypotheses (weakly finite type, quasi-separated) are those of this theorem.
The formula in the form used in Huber's proof of Lemma 3.8.2.
Scholze restates Huber 2.6.1 for geometric points Spa(L, L⁺) with L⁺ of any rank: the stalk is the cohomology of X ×_Y Spa(L, L⁺).
Bhatt–Hansen restate Huber's Example 2.6.2 at rank-one points, clause (c).
The rigid-analytic rank-one version (étale base change theorem).

nodes.title: Equivalent characterisations of henselian pairs: simple roots, coprime factorisations, étale sections, idempotents, Gabber's criterion
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative ring and I ⊆ A an ideal. The following are equivalent. (1) Mathlib's `HenselianRing A I`: I ⊆ Jacobson radical of A, and every monic f ∈ A[T] with an a₀ ∈ A such that f(a₀) ∈ I and f′(a₀) is a unit modulo I has a root a with a − a₀ ∈ I. (2) (Stacks Definition 15.11.1) I ⊆ rad(A), and every factorisation f̄ = g₀h₀ modulo I of a monic f ∈ A[T] into monic polynomials generating the unit ideal of (A/I)[T] lifts to a factorisation f = gh into monic polynomials. (3) For every étale A-algebra A′ and every A-algebra map σ: A′ → A/I there is an A-algebra map A′ → A lifting σ. (4) For every finite A-algebra B, reduction B → B/IB is a bijection on idempotents. (5) The same for every integral A-algebra B. (6) (Gabber) I ⊆ rad(A), and every polynomial T^n(T − 1) + a_nT^n + ⋯ + a₁T + a₀ with a₀, …, a_n ∈ I and n ≥ 1 has a root in 1 + I; this root is unique. Lean: `HenselianRing.tfae`, with the named directions `HenselianRing.lift_of_etale`, `HenselianRing.idempotent_bijective_of_finite`, `HenselianRing.of_gabber`.
hypotheses: A commutative, arbitrary (no noetherian or local hypothesis).
In (4) and (5) the bijection is between the idempotents of B and those of B/IB.
proofSteps: (2) ⇒ (1): a root ā₀ of f̄ with f̄′(ā₀) a unit gives the factorisation f̄ = (T − ā₀)·h₀ into monic polynomials generating the unit ideal (h₀(ā₀) = f̄′(ā₀) is a unit), and the lifted factor of degree 1 is T − a with a ≡ a₀ modulo I. (1) ⇒ (6): Gabber's polynomial f satisfies f(1) = a₀ + ⋯ + a_n ∈ I and f′(1) = 1 + a₁ + 2a₂ + ⋯ + n·a_n ∈ 1 + I, so (1) applied at the approximate root 1 gives a root in 1 + I, and I ⊆ rad(A) is part of (1). Mathlib's HenselianLocalRing.TFAE is not used: it compares residue-field forms of (1) only.

(3) ⇒ (5) ⇒ (4) ⇒ (2) ⇒ (6) ⇒ (3): the cycle of Stacks Lemma 15.11.6 (Tag 09XI), whose own order is (2) ⇒ (4) ⇒ (3) ⇒ (1) ⇒ (5) ⇒ (2) in Stacks' numbering: étale algebras are locally standard étale, idempotents of a ring correspond to its open and closed subsets of the spectrum, an integral algebra is the filtered union of its finite subalgebras, and Gabber's polynomial is the universal instance of lifting the idempotent decomposition of T^n(T − 1) modulo I.
Uniqueness in (6): two roots in 1 + I give two lifts of the same idempotent of A[T]/(f) modulo I, which agree by (4).
acceptance: For a local ring (A, 𝔪) and I = 𝔪, condition (1) is Mathlib's HenselianLocalRing A (through Mathlib's instance HenselianLocalRing → HenselianRing A 𝔪), and Mathlib's HenselianLocalRing.TFAE adds only residue-field forms of (1); the forms (2)–(6), in particular the étale form (3), are not in Mathlib (Mathlib/RingTheory/Henselian.lean lists them as a TODO) and are supplied by this node.

Gabber's test detects non-henselian pairs: for (ℤ_(3), 3ℤ_(3)) the polynomial T² − T + 3 = T(T − 1) + 3 has the root (1 + √−11)/2 ≡ 1 mod 3 in ℤ_3 but no root in ℤ_(3) (−11 is not a square in ℚ), so (6) fails, as it must.

nodes.title: A henselian pair depends only on the radical of the ideal
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring and I, J ⊆ A ideals with the same radical (equivalently V(I) = V(J) in Spec A). Then HenselianRing A I ↔ HenselianRing A J. Lean: `HenselianRing.iff_of_radical_eq`.
hypotheses: No hypothesis on A; I and J need not be finitely generated.
proofSteps: For every integral A-algebra B, V(IB) = V(JB) in Spec B, so B/IB and B/JB have the same idempotents (idempotents correspond to open and closed subsets of the spectrum, and the two spectra are the same closed subset of Spec B).
Conclude with characterisation (5) of henselian-pair-characterisations (Stacks Tag 09XJ).
acceptance: (ℤ_p, pℤ_p) and (ℤ_p, p²ℤ_p) are both henselian.

For a ring of definition A₀ of a Huber ring with ideal of definition J₀: (A₀, J₀) is henselian iff (A₀, A₀ ∩ A°°) is, because an element of A₀ is topologically nilpotent iff some power lies in J₀, i.e. √J₀ = A₀ ∩ A°°.

Fujiwara–Kato remark that henselianity of an I-adic ring depends only on the I-adic topology; for finitely generated I and J with equal radicals the I- and J-adic topologies agree, so this is a special case of the lemma.

nodes.title: A henselian pair depends only on the ideal as a non-unital ring
nodes.statement: Let φ: A → A′ be a ring homomorphism, I ⊆ A and I′ ⊆ A′ ideals such that φ restricts to a bijection I → I′ (so I ≅ I′ as non-unital rings). Then HenselianRing A I ↔ HenselianRing A′ I′. In particular, if R ⊆ R′ are rings and J is an ideal of both R and R′, then (R, J) is henselian iff (R′, J) is. Lean: `HenselianRing.iff_of_bijOn_ideal`.
hypotheses: φ need not be injective or surjective; only its restriction I → I′ is assumed bijective.
proofSteps: Jacobson condition: I ⊆ rad(A) iff for every x ∈ I there is y ∈ I with (1 + x)(1 + y) = 1, i.e. x + y + xy = 0 (Gabber–Ramero Claim 5.1.3); this equation lives in the non-unital ring I and transfers along φ|_I.

Gabber's criterion (henselian-pair-characterisations (6)): writing a root as 1 + β, the equation (1 + β)^n β + Σ a_i(1 + β)^i = 0 for a_i ∈ I is a polynomial identity with integer coefficients all of whose terms lie in I; existence and uniqueness of β ∈ I therefore depend only on the non-unital ring I and transfer along φ|_I (Gabber–Ramero Remark 5.1.9(ii); Bhatt, proof of Lemma 7.2.3(3)).
acceptance: For rings of definition B₀ ⊆ B₀′ of a Tate ring with ϖⁿB₀′ ⊆ B₀, the ideal ϖ^{n+1}B₀′ is common to both, so (B₀, ϖB₀) is henselian iff (B₀′, ϖB₀′) is (with henselian-pair-radical-invariance).
(ℤ + pℤ_p⟨T⟩, pℤ_p⟨T⟩) is a henselian pair, because pℤ_p⟨T⟩ is also an ideal of the p-adically complete ring ℤ_p⟨T⟩.

sources.match: The invariance: the henselian property depends only on I as a non-unital ring.
The use made of it for rings of definition of Tate rings.

nodes.title: Henselian pairs are invariant under universal homeomorphisms of spectra
nodes.statement: Let φ: B → R be a ring homomorphism such that Spec(φ): Spec R → Spec B is a universal homeomorphism (equivalently: φ is integral and Spec(φ) is universally injective and surjective, Stacks Tag 04DF), and let I ⊆ B be an ideal. Then HenselianRing B I ↔ HenselianRing R (I·R). Lean: `HenselianRing.iff_of_isUniversalHomeomorph`.
hypotheses: No finiteness hypothesis on φ.
proofSteps: ⇒: φ is integral, and integral base change preserves henselian pairs (Stacks Tag 09XK; Gabber–Ramero Remark 5.1.9(v)).

⇐: let C be a finite B-algebra. The maps Spec(C ⊗_B R) → Spec C and Spec((C/IC) ⊗_B R) → Spec(C/IC) are base changes of Spec R → Spec B, hence homeomorphisms, compatible with the closed immersions of Spec(C/IC) and of Spec((C ⊗_B R)/I(C ⊗_B R)) = Spec((C/IC) ⊗_B R). Idempotents of a ring correspond to the open and closed subsets of its spectrum (Mathlib `PrimeSpectrum.isIdempotentElemEquivClopens`, Stacks Tag 00EE), so C → C/IC is bijective on idempotents iff the finite R-algebra C ⊗_B R → (C ⊗_B R)/I(C ⊗_B R) is, which holds by characterisation (4) of henselian-pair-characterisations for (R, IR). Hence (B, I) is henselian by (4). This replaces Bhatt's argument through the topological invariance of the étale site (Stacks Tag 04DZ), which no prerequisite of this node supplies.
acceptance: A surjection B → B/N with N a nil ideal is a universal homeomorphism, so (B, I) is henselian iff (B/N, I(B/N)) is (Gabber–Ramero Remark 5.1.9(i)).
For a Tate ring with ring of definition A₀ ∋ ϖ, A₀ → A₀ + A°° is integral and a universal homeomorphism, which transfers henselianity from (A₀ + A°°, A°°) to (A₀, ϖA₀) (Bhatt Lemma 7.2.3(3)).

sources.match: Bhatt's argument for the ⇐ direction, through the étale site; the proof step above uses the idempotent characterisation instead.

Topological invariance of the small étale site, the input of Bhatt's form of the ⇐ argument; the excerpt also records that a universal homeomorphism is the same as an integral, universally injective and surjective morphism, as used in the statement.
The ⇒ direction.

nodes.title: Henselian f-adic rings: independence of the open subring and the open ideal (Huber 1996, Lemma 3.1.1)
nodes.statement: Let A be a Huber (f-adic) ring (Tau Ceti `Huber.IsHuberRing`), A° its power-bounded subring and A°° ⊆ A° the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements (Tau Ceti `powerBoundedSubring`, `topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`). A *henselian datum* of A is a pair (B, I) with B ⊆ A° an open subring and I an ideal of B that is open in A and contained in A°°. Then (a) for fixed B, HenselianRing B I ↔ HenselianRing B (B ∩ A°°); (b) the truth of HenselianRing B (B ∩ A°°) does not depend on B. Hence Huber's four conditions are equivalent: (i) some henselian datum is a henselian pair; (ii) every henselian datum is a henselian pair; (iii)/(iv) for some/every open subring B ⊆ A°, Spec B is henselian along the closed set of its open prime ideals, which is V(B ∩ A°°). No completeness, noetherian or Tate hypothesis enters. Lean: `Huber.henselianRing_iff_of_isOpen`.
hypotheses: A an arbitrary Huber ring (the §3.1 convention of Huber's book: arbitrary f-adic rings).
Subrings are unital; 'open' refers to the topology of A.
proofSteps: (a): I ⊆ B ∩ A°°, and each x ∈ B ∩ A°° has xⁿ ∈ I for n large because xⁿ → 0 and I is open; so √I = B ∩ A°° in B and henselian-pair-radical-invariance applies. The same argument shows that a prime of B is open iff it contains B ∩ A°°, which gives (iii)/(iv).
Reduction: for open subrings B, B′ ⊆ A°, B ∩ B′ is an open subring of A°, so it suffices to compare C ⊆ B.

For open subrings C ⊆ B of A°, choose a ring of definition A₀ ⊆ C with a finitely generated ideal of definition J (A₀ ∩ C is open and bounded, hence a ring of definition, and every ring of definition has a finitely generated ideal of definition: Huber 1993, Proposition 1). Put R := C + JB, a subring of B containing C in which JB is an ideal.
(R, JB) is henselian iff (B, JB) is, by henselian-pair-shared-ideal-invariance; JB is open in A and consists of topologically nilpotent elements, so by (a) these are the conditions for R and for B.

C → R is a universal homeomorphism on spectra: every element of JB is topologically nilpotent, so a power lies in A₀ ⊆ C and it is integral over C; C/(C ∩ A°°) → R/(R ∩ A°°) is an isomorphism since R ∩ A°° = (C ∩ A°°) + JB; and for x ∈ J the localisations C_x → R_x are isomorphisms because for b ∈ B the singleton {b} is bounded, so J^m b ⊆ A₀ ⊆ C for m large. Hence Spec R → Spec C is integral, bijective with trivial residue field extensions, an isomorphism over Spec C ∖ V(J) (Stacks Tag 04DF).
henselian-pair-universal-homeomorphism-invariance gives HenselianRing C J ↔ HenselianRing R (JR); with (a) (JR is an open ideal of R inside A°°) this is the condition for C versus R.
acceptance: Tate case: for a Tate ring A with ring of definition A₀ ∋ ϖ, (A₀, ϖA₀) is henselian iff (A°, A°°) is iff (A⁺, A°°) is — the statement of PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (c) and Bhatt Lemma 7.2.3(3).
Discrete A: A° = A and A°° is the nilradical, which is locally nilpotent, so every henselian datum is a henselian pair (Stacks Tag 0ALI): discrete rings are henselian.

sources.match: Huber's §3.1 drops his standing hypotheses; Lemma 3.1.1 (the equivalence of (i)–(iv)) is stated for arbitrary f-adic rings. The proof above uses only public inputs.
The Tate case of the lemma.
Existence of the finitely generated ideal of definition J used in step 3.

nodes.title: A ring of definition of a complete Huber ring is adically complete
nodes.statement: Let A be a Huber ring whose uniform structure is complete and Hausdorff (CompleteSpace A, T2Space A), and let (A₀, J) be a pair of definition (Tau Ceti `Huber.PairOfDefinition`: A₀ open, J ⊆ A₀ finitely generated, subspace topology J-adic). Then A₀ is J-adically complete in the algebraic sense: Mathlib `IsAdicComplete J A₀` (Hausdorff and precomplete for the filtration Jⁿ). Lean: `Huber.PairOfDefinition.isAdicComplete`.
hypotheses: Completeness and Hausdorffness refer to the topology of A; J finitely generated.
proofSteps: A₀ and every Jⁿ are open additive subgroups of A, hence closed.
Hausdorff: ⋂ₙ Jⁿ = 0 because the Jⁿ form a neighbourhood basis of 0 in the Hausdorff ring A.

Conclude with Mathlib `IsAdic.isAdicComplete_iff` (IsAdicComplete J A₀ ↔ CompleteSpace A₀ ∧ T2Space A₀ for the J-adic topology of A₀, which is its subspace topology): A₀ is closed in the complete space A, hence complete (Mathlib `IsClosed.completeSpace_coe`), and it is Hausdorff as a subspace of A. The hand argument (a sequence with x_{n+1} − xₙ ∈ Jⁿ is Cauchy in A and its limit lies in A₀ with x − xₙ ∈ Jⁿ) is the content of that Mathlib lemma.
acceptance: For A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ with A₀ = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ and J = pA₀, A₀ is p-adically complete.
Completeness of A is needed: for ℚ with the 3-adic topology (A₀ = ℤ_(3), J = 3ℤ_(3)), ℤ_(3) is not 3-adically complete.

nodes.title: A complete f-adic ring is henselian: every henselian datum of a complete Huber ring is a henselian pair
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete Hausdorff Huber ring. Then for every open subring B ⊆ A° and every ideal I of B that is open in A and contained in A°°, the pair (B, I) is henselian (Mathlib `HenselianRing B I`). In particular (A°, A°°) and (A⁺, A°°) are henselian pairs for every ring of integral elements A⁺ (Tau Ceti `IsRingOfIntegralElements`), and if A is a Tate ring with pseudo-uniformiser ϖ, then (A°, ϖA°) and (A⁺, ϖA⁺) are henselian pairs. The proof uses neither Huber's book nor henselian-f-adic-ring-independence. Lean: `Huber.henselianRing_of_completeSpace`.
hypotheses: A complete and Hausdorff; no noetherian, Tate or uniformity hypothesis; A° may be unbounded.
proofSteps: Fix a ring of definition A₀ ⊆ B (A₀ ∩ B is open and bounded). For a finite subset S ⊆ B the subring A₀[S] is open and bounded (Tau Ceti `isBounded_subringClosure`: finitely many power-bounded elements generate a bounded subring; products and additive spans of bounded sets are bounded in a nonarchimedean ring), hence a ring of definition (Huber 1993, Proposition 1(ii)); so B is the directed union of rings of definition B_λ ⊆ B.

Each B_λ has a finitely generated ideal of definition J_λ (Huber 1993, Proposition 1(iii)) and is J_λ-adically complete by ring-of-definition-adically-complete; hence (B_λ, J_λ) is henselian (Mathlib instance `IsAdicComplete.henselianRing`; Stacks Tag 0ALJ).
I ∩ B_λ and J_λ are open ideals of B_λ consisting of topologically nilpotent elements, so they have the same radical and (B_λ, I ∩ B_λ) is henselian by henselian-pair-radical-invariance.
(B, I) is the directed union of the pairs (B_λ, I ∩ B_λ), hence henselian (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (b); Stacks Tag 0FWT).
Special cases: A° and A⁺ are open subrings of A° and A°° is open and topologically nilpotent; for Tate A, ϖA° and ϖA⁺ are open (ϖ is a unit) and lie in A°°.
acceptance: ℤ_p⟨T⟩ = (ℚ_p⟨T⟩)° is henselian along pℤ_p⟨T⟩.
Non-uniform instance: A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩[ε]/(ε²) with ring of definition ℤ_p⟨T⟩[ε]; A° = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ ⊕ εℚ_p⟨T⟩ is unbounded and is henselian along A°° = pℤ_p⟨T⟩ ⊕ εℚ_p⟨T⟩.
The instance requested by AdicEtaleGeometry:A4: for a complete Tate ring A, (A°, ϖA°) is a henselian pair.
Completeness cannot be dropped: ℚ with the 3-adic topology has (ℚ°, ℚ°°) = (ℤ_(3), 3ℤ_(3)), not henselian (X² − 7 has the simple root 1 modulo 3 and no root in ℤ_(3)).

nodes.title: Henselian f-adic rings and henselian affinoid rings (Huber 1996, Definition 3.1.2)
nodes.statement: A Huber ring A is *henselian* (`Huber.IsHenselian A`) if the pair (A°, A°°) is henselian: `HenselianRing (powerBoundedSubring A) (topologicallyNilpotentIdeal A)`. By henselian-f-adic-ring-independence this holds iff some, equivalently every, henselian datum (B, I) — B ⊆ A° an open subring, I an ideal of B open in A with I ⊆ A°° — is a henselian pair. A Huber pair (A, A⁺) (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`) is henselian (`Huber.Pair.IsHenselian`) iff its underlying Huber ring is; the plus ring plays no role, and (A⁺, A°°) is then a henselian pair. Conventions: completeness is not assumed; the topology enters only through A° and A°°; on Tate rings the notion coincides with `Huber.IsTopologicallyHenselian` of PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-pairs-colimits-and-completions (c).
hypotheses: A a Huber ring (any f-adic ring); no completeness, noetherian or Tate hypothesis.
proofSteps: The definition is the canonical henselian datum (A°, A°°); the equivalent descriptions are henselian-f-adic-ring-independence.

Open subrings: for an open subring C ⊆ A (a Huber ring for the subspace topology), bounded subsets of C and of A contained in C agree because C is open, so C° = C ∩ A° and C°° = C ∩ A°°; C° is an open subring of A°, so C is henselian when A is (henselian-f-adic-ring-independence (ii)).
acceptance: Every complete Huber ring is henselian (complete-f-adic-ring-is-henselian), every discrete ring is henselian, and ℚ with the 3-adic topology is not.

nodes.title: In a henselian Huber ring the unit group is open, maximal ideals are closed, and units are detected on Spa
nodes.statement: Let A be a henselian Huber ring (henselian-f-adic-ring) and A⁺ a ring of integral elements. Then (a) 1 + A°° ⊆ A^× and the unit group A^× is open in A; (b) every maximal ideal of A is closed; (c) every proper ideal J of A is contained in supp v for some v ∈ Spa(A, A⁺); hence f ∈ A is a unit iff f ∉ supp v for every v ∈ Spa(A, A⁺), and a finite T ⊆ A generates the unit ideal iff no point of Spa(A, A⁺) kills all of T. Completeness is not assumed. Lean: `Huber.IsHenselian.isOpen_setOf_isUnit`, `Huber.IsHenselian.isClosed_of_isMaximal`, `Huber.IsHenselian.isUnit_iff_forall_mem_spa_notMem_supp`.
hypotheses: A henselian (in particular A°° ⊆ Jacobson radical of A°); A⁺ any ring of integral elements.
proofSteps: (a): (A°, A°°) is a henselian pair, so A°° lies in the Jacobson radical of A° and 1 + A°° ⊆ (A°)^× ⊆ A^×; 1 + A°° is an open neighbourhood of 1 (A°° contains an ideal of definition) and u(1 + A°°) ⊆ A^× for every unit u.
(b): Tau Ceti `Ideal.isClosed_of_isMaximal_of_isOpen_isUnit`.

(c): the proof of Tau Ceti `exists_mem_spa_le_supp_of_ne_top` (Wedhorn Proposition 7.51) uses completeness only through the openness of A^×: the closure of a proper ideal J is proper (Tau Ceti `Ideal.closure_ne_top_of_isOpen_isUnit`), so 1 is not in the closure of 0 in A/J and the quotient pair has non-empty Spa (Tau Ceti `spa_eq_empty_iff_one_mem_closure_zero`); a point of it pulls back to v with J ⊆ supp v.
acceptance: For the henselian, non-complete field A = ℚ_p ∩ ℚ̄ with the p-adic topology, Spa(A, A°) is one point with support 0 and the criterion says that the non-zero elements are the units.
The criterion is what makes f(s) a unit in rational-henselization (ii) for henselian, not necessarily complete, targets.

nodes.title: Henselization of an f-adic ring and of an affinoid ring (Huber 1996, Lemma 3.1.3), with plus ring, ideal of definition and completion
nodes.statement: Let A be a Huber ring and (D, I) a pair of definition (D open and bounded, I ⊆ D a finitely generated ideal of definition). The *henselization* of A is A^h := A ⊗_D D^h, where (D^h, ID^h) is the henselization of the pair (D, I) (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselisation-of-pairs); D^h → A^h is injective (D^h is flat over D) and A^h is topologised so that the image of D^h is a ring of definition with ideal of definition I·D^h (neighbourhood basis {IⁿD^h} of 0); ι: A → A^h is the canonical map. (i) A^h is a henselian Huber ring (henselian-f-adic-ring) and ι is continuous and adic. (ii) Universal property: every continuous ring homomorphism φ: A → B into a henselian Huber ring factors uniquely as φ = ψ ∘ ι with ψ: A^h → B continuous; hence A^h does not depend on (D, I) up to unique isomorphism. (iii) D/Iⁿ ≅ D^h/IⁿD^h for all n, so ι induces isomorphisms of the completed rings of definition and of completions Â ≅ (A^h)^ (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completion`), with Â = Â₀ ⊗_{A₀} A. (iv) ι is an isomorphism iff A is henselian; in particular complete Huber rings are their own henselizations (complete-f-adic-ring-is-henselian). Affinoid case: for a Huber pair (A, A⁺) choose D ⊆ A⁺; then (A⁺)^h := A⁺ ⊗_D D^h is the henselization of the Huber ring A⁺, it equals the integral closure of the image of A⁺ ⊗_D D^h in A^h, and (A, A⁺)^h := (A^h, (A⁺)^h) is a henselian Huber pair, universal among continuous homomorphisms of Huber pairs to henselian Huber pairs, whose completion is (Â, Â⁺). Section-wide convention (Huber 1996 §3.1): no noetherian or completeness hypothesis on A. The henselian notion itself (Huber 1996, 3.1.1–3.1.2) is henselian-f-adic-ring-independence and henselian-f-adic-ring, and the clause 'complete f-adic rings are henselian' is complete-f-adic-ring-is-henselian.
hypotheses: A an arbitrary Huber ring; D ⊆ A⁺ may be chosen because D ∩ A⁺ is again a ring of definition.
Henselization of pairs is the left adjoint of Stacks Tag 0A02, filtered colimit of étale D-algebras E with D/I ≅ E/IE.
proofSteps: Topology: for a ∈ A, a·I^N ⊆ D for N large (continuity of multiplication by a), so a·I^{N+n}D^h ⊆ IⁿD^h; the {IⁿD^h} define a ring topology in which the image of D^h is open and bounded with the finitely generated ideal of definition ID^h, so A^h is a Huber ring and ι is adic.
Henselian: (image of D^h, ID^h) is a henselian pair and a henselian datum of A^h, so A^h is henselian by henselian-f-adic-ring-independence.

Existence in (ii): for a continuous φ: A → B and a ring of definition B₀ of B, D′ := D ∩ φ^{-1}(B₀) is a ring of definition of A with a finitely generated ideal of definition I′; φ(I′) consists of topologically nilpotent elements, and (B₀, B₀ ∩ B°°) is henselian (B henselian, henselian-f-adic-ring-independence), so the universal property of the henselization of the pair (D′, I′) gives D′^h → B₀ and hence A ⊗_{D′} D′^h → B, continuous because (φ(I′)B₀)^m tends to 0 (it is generated by finitely many topologically nilpotent elements). A ⊗_{D′} D′^h is henselian and satisfies the same universal property, which identifies it with A ⊗_D D^h.

Uniqueness in (ii): let ψ₁, ψ₂ be continuous with ψ₁ ∘ ι = ψ₂ ∘ ι. For an étale D′-algebra E with D′/I′ᵏ ≅ E/I′ᵏE one has E = D′ + I′ᵏE, and continuity gives ψ_i(I′ᵏE) ⊆ B₀ for k large, so ψ_i(E) ⊆ B₀. The two maps E → B₀ agree modulo φ(I′)B₀; the idempotent of E ⊗_{D′} E cutting out the diagonal maps to an idempotent f of B₀ with 1 − f ∈ φ(I′)B₀ ⊆ rad(B₀), so f = 1 and ψ₁ = ψ₂ on E; E ranges over a cofinal system of D′^h.

(iii): Stacks Tag 0AGU gives D/Iⁿ ≅ D^h/IⁿD^h; hence the I-adic completions of D and D^h agree, and (A^h)^ = A^h ⊗_{D^h} (D^h)^ = A ⊗_D D̂ = Â (Huber 1993, Lemma 1.6, as recalled in the Berkeley lectures).
(iv): if A is henselian, (D, I) is a henselian pair (henselian-f-adic-ring-independence) and D^h = D.

Plus rings: A⁺ ⊗_D D^h is integrally closed in A ⊗_D D^h because integral closure commutes with étale base change (Stacks Tag 03GE) and with filtered colimits; it is open, contains the ring of definition D^h and consists of power-bounded elements (for a ∈ A⁺, Iᵏaⁿ ⊆ D for all n implies (ID^h)ᵏaⁿ ⊆ D^h), so it is a ring of integral elements; the universal property for pairs follows from (ii) applied to (D, I) → (B⁺, B⁺ ∩ B°°), and (A⁺)^h = A⁺ ⊗_D D^h is Huber's (A^h)⁺ = (A⁺)^h.
acceptance: A complete Huber pair is its own henselization; the henselization does not change the completion (Huber 1996, Lemma 3.1.3.ii).
(A^h)⁺ = (A⁺)^h: the plus ring is henselized along with the ring and is recovered in every completion as Â⁺.
For ℚ with the p-adic topology (D = ℤ_(p), I = pℤ_(p)): A^h = ℚ ⊗ ℤ_(p)^h = ℚ_p ∩ ℚ̄, and (A^h)^ = ℚ_p = Â.

nodes.title: The henselization of an affinoid ring along a rational subset (Huber 1996, Lemma 3.1.4 and (3.1.5))
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair and U = R(T/s) ⊆ Spa(A, A⁺) a rational subset (T ⊆ A finite with T·A open, s ∈ A). Let (A(T/s), A(T/s)⁺) be the uncompleted rational localisation: the localisation A_s with the Huber topology of Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.localization`/`locTopology` (ring of definition A₀[t/s : t ∈ T], ideal of definition generated by an ideal of definition of A₀) and A(T/s)⁺ the integral closure of A⁺[t/s : t ∈ T]. Define G_A(U) := (A(T/s), A(T/s)⁺)^h (henselian-f-adic-rings-and-henselization) with h: (A, A⁺) → G_A(U). (i) G_A(U) is a henselian Huber pair and Spa(h) is a homeomorphism of Spa G_A(U) onto U carrying rational subsets to rational subsets. (ii) Every continuous homomorphism of Huber pairs f: (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) with B henselian and Spa(f)(Spa(B, B⁺)) ⊆ U factors uniquely through h; hence G_A(U) depends only on U. (iii) The completion of G_A(U) is the completed rational localisation (O_X(U), O_X⁺(U)) (Tau Ceti `completionLocalization`), plus rings included. (iv) (3.1.5) A(U) := the underlying ring of G_A(U), the *henselization of A along U*, is a presheaf of rings on the rational subsets of Spa(A, A⁺) (restrictions from (ii)); completing it gives the structure presheaf on rational subsets. Lean: `Huber.Pair.rationalHenselization`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) an arbitrary Huber pair; completeness and sheafiness are not assumed.
proofSteps: (i): Spa of the uncompleted localisation maps homeomorphically onto R(T/s) (Tau Ceti `spaLocalizationHomeomorph`, for a pair of definition with A₀ ⊆ A⁺, HasDenominatorPower being supplied by the openness of T·A); henselization does not change the completion (henselian-f-adic-rings-and-henselization (iii)), and Spa of a Huber pair equals Spa of its completion (Wedhorn Proposition 7.48).

(ii): f(s) is a unit in B: no point w of Spa(B, B⁺) has f(s) ∈ supp w (its pullback lies in R(T/s); Tau Ceti `valuation_ne_zero_of_mem_rationalSubset`), and units of a henselian Huber ring are detected on Spa (henselian-affinoid-unit-criterion). f(t)/f(s) ∈ B⁺ because it has value ≤ 1 at every point (Tau Ceti `vle_one_of_comap_mem_rationalSubset`, Wedhorn Proposition 7.52(1)). So f factors through A_s; the factorisation is continuous because its composite with B → B̂ is the continuous map of Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset` and the topology of B is induced from B̂ (open subgroups correspond). Then use the universal property of the henselization.
(iii): henselian-f-adic-rings-and-henselization (iii) for the Huber pair (A(T/s), A(T/s)⁺).
(iv): for V ⊆ U rational, the pair G_A(V) receives (A, A⁺) with image in U, so (ii) gives G_A(U) → G_A(V); uniqueness gives the presheaf identities.
acceptance: U = Spa(A, A⁺) = R({1}/1): G_A(U) is the henselization (A, A⁺)^h, and A(U) = A for complete A.
For A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and U = R((T, p)/p) = {|T| ≤ |p|}, the completion of G_A(U) is ℚ_p⟨T/p⟩.

nodes.title: Special and pro-special subsets of Spa A (Huber 1996, Definition 3.1.6)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair and X = Spa(A, A⁺). For t ∈ A and finite subsets D, E ⊆ A such that the ideal (D ∪ E ∪ {t})·A is open, put S(D|E / t) := {x ∈ X : |d(x)| ≤ |t(x)| ≠ 0 for all d ∈ D, and |e(x)| < |t(x)| for all e ∈ E}. A subset U ⊆ X is *special* if U = S(D|E / t) for such data, and *pro-special* if it is an intersection of special subsets. Every rational subset R(T/s) = S(T|∅ / s) is special; X = S(∅|∅ / 1); pro-special subsets are stable under arbitrary intersections. Relative to a rational subset R: S(D|E / t) = R ∖ ⋃_{e ∈ E} R_e with R := R((D ∪ E ∪ {t})/t) and R_e := {x ∈ R : |t(x)| ≤ |e(x)|}. Functoriality (generalising the rational-localisation and completion cases of Huber 1996, Corollary 3.1.9): for an adic homomorphism of Huber pairs f: (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), Spa(f)^{-1}(S(D|E/t)) = S(f(D)|f(E) / f(t)), and special subsets of Spa A and of Spa Â correspond under Spa Â ≅ Spa A. Lean: `Huber.specialSubset`, `Huber.IsSpecialSubset`, `Huber.IsProSpecialSubset`.
hypotheses: |a(x)| denotes the value of a at the continuous valuation x; D, E finite; the openness of (D ∪ E ∪ {t})·A is part of the data.
Functoriality is stated for adic homomorphisms, for which f(D ∪ E ∪ {t})·B is open.
proofSteps: S(D|E/t) = R ∖ ⋃ R_e: on R the element t is invertible at every point, and |e(x)| < |t(x)| fails exactly on R_e (values are totally ordered).
Preimages: |f(a)(y)| = |a(Spa(f)(y))| for y ∈ Spa B, and adic maps carry open ideals to ideals generating open ideals.
acceptance: Every rational subset is special; the tube {|T| < 1} = S(∅|{T}/1) in Spa(ℤ_p[T], ℤ_p[T]) (p-adic topology) is special and not open.

nodes.title: Special subsets are locally closed and constructible; pro-special subsets are convex and pro-constructible (Huber 1996, Corollary 3.1.8)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair and X = Spa(A, A⁺), a spectral space (Tau Ceti `spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition`). Every special subset S = S(D|E / t) is locally closed and constructible in X (Mathlib `Topology.IsConstructible`): S = R ∖ ⋃_{e ∈ E} R_e with R := R((D ∪ E ∪ {t})/t) quasi-compact open and each R_e := {x ∈ R : |t(x)| ≤ |e(x)|} quasi-compact open. Consequently every pro-special subset U is pro-constructible (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets), hence quasi-compact, and convex: if x, z ∈ U and x specialises to y which specialises to z, then y ∈ U. Hence (X, U) satisfies Huber's conditions for a pseudo-adic space whenever X is an adic space. Lean: `Huber.IsSpecialSubset.isLocallyClosed`, `Huber.IsSpecialSubset.isConstructible`, `Huber.IsProSpecialSubset.isProConstructible`, `Huber.IsProSpecialSubset.isConvex`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) any Huber pair.
proofSteps: R is a rational subset, open (Tau Ceti `isOpen_val_preimage_rationalSubset`) and quasi-compact (Tau Ceti `isCompact_of_mem_spaRationalFamily`).

R_e is open and quasi-compact: under the homeomorphism Spa(A(T/t), A(T/t)⁺) ≅ R (Tau Ceti `spaLocalizationHomeomorph`, T := D ∪ E ∪ {t}, for a pair of definition with A₀ ⊆ A⁺) it is the rational subset R({1}/(e/t)) of the rational localisation ({1} generates the unit ideal).
S = R ∩ (X ∖ ⋃ R_e) is the intersection of an open and a closed set, and a Boolean combination of quasi-compact opens, hence locally closed and constructible.

Convexity: a locally closed set O ∩ C is convex, since y lies in the closure of x (so in C) and generalises z ∈ O (so lies in O); intersections of convex, resp. pro-constructible, sets are convex, resp. pro-constructible.
acceptance: S(∅|{T}/1) ⊆ Spa(ℤ_p[T], ℤ_p[T]) (p-adic topology) is closed, constructible and not open.

nodes.title: Henselization of an affinoid ring along a pro-special subset: triples, construction, universal property and examples (Huber 1996, 3.1.11–3.1.13)
nodes.statement: (3.1.11) A *triple* (K, L, M) is a ring K, a subring L ⊆ K and an ideal M of L; it is henselian if (L, M) is a henselian pair; its henselization is (K ⊗_L L^h, L^h, ML^h), where (L^h, ML^h) is the henselization of the pair (L, M) (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselisation-of-pairs); its saturation replaces L by its integral closure in K and M by the radical of the extended ideal. (3.1.12) Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair, A^▷ its underlying ring, and U = ⋂_{i ∈ Λ} S(D_i|E_i / t_i) a pro-special subset of Spa(A, A⁺) with a chosen presentation; let (B, P) be a pair with B ⊆ A⁺ a subring over which A⁺ is integral and P ⊆ B ∩ A°° an ideal of B with P·A open (for example (A⁺, A⁺ ∩ A°°)). Put F := A^▷[1/t_i : i ∈ Λ], G := B[d/t_i, e/t_i : i ∈ Λ, d ∈ D_i, e ∈ E_i] ⊆ F and J := (P ∪ {e/t_i : i ∈ Λ, e ∈ E_i})·G, and define A(U) := F^h, where (F^h, G^h, J^h) is the henselization of the triple (F, G, J): the *henselization of A along U*, a ring without topology (used with the discrete topology). Then (i) A(U) is independent of the presentation of U and of (B, P) up to unique isomorphism; (ii) U ↦ A(U) is a presheaf of rings on the pro-special subsets of Spa(A, A⁺) whose restriction to rational subsets is the presheaf A(U) of rational-henselization; (iii) a continuous homomorphism of Huber pairs f: (A, A⁺) → (A′, A′⁺) and pro-special U ⊆ Spa A, U′ ⊆ Spa A′ with Spa(f)(U′) ⊆ U induce a ring map A(U) → A′(U′), compatibly with restrictions. (3.1.13) Examples: (i) for A with an I-adic topology, the henselization of (A, A⁺) along Spa(A, A⁺) is the henselization of A along I; (iii) for s ∈ A and B = (A, A)(1/s), λ^{-1}(P) is a pro-special subset of Spa B and (A^h)_s is the henselization of B along it — the bridge to formal generic fibres (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/formal-generic-fibre-analytic-locus); (iv) the henselization of an affinoid field (K, K⁺) along its closed point is the henselization of K with respect to the valuation ring K⁺. Lean: `Huber.Triple`, `Huber.Pair.proSpecialHenselization`.
hypotheses: (A, A⁺) any Huber pair (arbitrary f-adic A^▷); U pro-special.
A(U) carries no natural Huber topology when U is not rational (Huber's remark after (3.1.5)); it is used as a discrete ring.
Inputs of the source's proof: EGA IV 18.12.15 (henselization and integral closure; here replaced by Stacks Tag 03GE) and Huber 1993 (valuation spectra and the retraction r: Spv A^▷ → Spv(A^▷, Q)).
proofSteps: Construct (F, G, J) from the presentation and (B, P); henselize the pair (G, J) and base change to F; saturate.

For a triple X = (K, L, M) let V(X) ⊆ Spv K be the valuations bounded by 1 on L and < 1 on M. The source proves: (1) (X^c)^h ≅ (X^h)^c; (2) for a henselian saturated triple, L and M are recovered from V(X), and every prime of K is the support of some v ∈ V(X); (3) the saturation Y of the henselization of (F, G, J) is universal among henselian saturated triples Z with im V(f) ⊆ r^{-1}(U); (4) r^{-1}(U) is the set of primary generalisations of U. These four steps are only in Huber 1996 (gap); (i)–(iii) follow from (3).
