nodes.title: Cohomology of henselian tubes (Proposition 3.6.1)
nodes.statement: Let A be an affinoid ring (not necessarily complete), J ⊆ I ideals of A⁺ such that A⁺/J is henselian along I/J, and let T := {x ∈ Spa A : |i(x)| < 1 for all i ∈ I} ⊆ U := {x ∈ Spa A : |j(x)| < 1 for all j ∈ J}, closed subsets of Spa A regarded as pseudo-adic subspaces. Let f: X → Spec A^▷ be a morphism of schemes satisfying conditions (a) and (b) of Theorem 3.2.10, or with A^▷ discrete, and X_T := X ×_{Spec A^▷} T → X_U := X ×_{Spec A^▷} U the induced morphism of pseudo-adic spaces (Huber's fibre products (3.2.7), ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/relative-comparison-3-2-9-3-2-12). Let F be an abelian torsion sheaf on (X_U)_et and F' its preimage on (X_T)_et. Then the restriction map H^n(X_U, F) → H^n(X_T, F') is bijective for every n ≥ 0.
hypotheses: A⁺/J henselian along I/J; X satisfies (a),(b) of 3.2.10 or A^▷ is discrete; F torsion
proofSteps: (I) Reduce to A^▷ discrete, via the discrete affinoid ring A^d and (3.4.2)/(3.4.3); (II) to X = Spec A^▷; (III) to J = 0, by henselising the triple (A^▷, A⁺, J) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/henselization-along-pro-special-subset) and (3.3.4); (IV) to A^▷ noetherian of finite Krull dimension, writing (A^▷, A⁺, I) as a filtered colimit of henselisations of finitely generated triples ([KPR, 2.8.2]) with the constructible reductions (2.3.13.i), (2.7.8), (2.7.10.i) and the limit theorem (2.4.6).

Induction on m = dim A^▷: (V) for constructible convex S = {|a_i| < |b_i|} and constant coefficients, from the isomorphism of henselisations A(S) ≅ A(S ∩ T) and Theorem 3.2.1 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/pro-special-comparison-theorem-3-2-1).

(VI) for closed constructible S and constant coefficients, by the closed-covering spectral sequence (2.6.10), local cohomology along Z = {a = 0} through strict henselisations of A^▷ and the induction hypothesis on A^▷/aA^▷; (VII) for G = j_!P with P constant on an open constructible subset, by the five lemma.

(VIII) for f_*(j_*G) with f finite, by the Čech-type spectral sequence (2.6.9); (IX) for general torsion F by the constructible dévissage (2.7.12.ii) after reducing to constructible Z/mZ-modules ((2.3.13.i), (2.7.8)).
Each step is a separate lemma of the source proof (pp. 211–219); none has a public restatement, so the steps are recorded as a gap rather than as nodes.
acceptance: For a complete affinoid A with A⁺ henselian along I = (A^▷)°°·A⁺ ∩ A⁺, the cohomology of a Zariski-open W ⊇ (Spa A)_a equals that of the closed tube over the special fibre; this is the mechanism behind Theorem 3.5.8(ii).
The induction is on the Krull dimension of a discrete noetherian ring obtained after henselisation; completeness is not used.

sources.match: Proposition 3.6.1 and its hypotheses.

Step (IX): the closing dévissage.
The scheme-level shadow of the tube comparison (Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change), used in the henselian reductions.

nodes.title: Henselian tube comparison for Zariski opens and their closed subsets (Corollaries 3.6.2–3.6.3)
nodes.statement: Let A be an affinoid ring with A⁺ henselian along an ideal I ⊆ A⁺, let W ⊆ Spa A be a Zariski-open subset containing all analytic points of Spa A, and T := {w ∈ W : |i(w)| < 1 for all i ∈ I}. (3.6.2) For every abelian torsion sheaf F on W_et with preimage F' on the pseudo-adic space (Spa A, T), H^n(W, F) → H^n(T, F') is bijective for all n. (3.6.3) More generally, for a closed subset S ⊆ W (so that (Spa A, S) and (Spa A, S ∩ T) are pseudo-adic spaces) and a torsion sheaf F on (Spa A, S)_et with preimage F' on (Spa A, S ∩ T), H^n(S, F) → H^n(S ∩ T, F') is bijective for all n. (3.6.2) is the case S = W.
hypotheses: A⁺ henselian along I; W Zariski-open containing (Spa A)_a; S closed in W; F torsion
proofSteps: (3.6.2) is Proposition 3.6.1 (node henselian-tube-comparison-3-6-1) with J = 0 and X the open subscheme of Spec A^▷ corresponding to the Zariski-open W. (3.6.3) follows from (3.6.2) applied to the torsion sheaf i_*F on W, where i: (Spa A, S) → W is the closed inclusion of supports. i_* is exact (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero (ii)), so H^n(S, F) = H^n(W, i_*F), and the restriction of i_*F to T is the pushforward of F′ along S ∩ T ⊆ T: both have stalk F_ξ at geometric points supported in S ∩ T and 0 at the other points of T, because S is closed in W. A closed subset S of the adic space need not be cut out by a closed subscheme of Spec A^▷, so a reduction through such an X covers only Zariski-closed S. The pseudo-adic sites are ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site.
acceptance: Applied to the completed strict henselisation C of node formal-strict-localisation-system-3-5-7 (henselian along its maximal ideal), with W = Spa(C, C)_a and S the support over f⁻¹(L), it gives node stalk-formula-closed-point-3-5-8-ii.

nodes.title: Stalks of R^nλ_*F via the closed point of the completed strict localisation (Theorem 3.5.8(ii))
nodes.statement: In the situation of node stalks-of-higher-direct-images-lambda (Y_∞^ of type (S)), assume moreover that F is a torsion sheaf. Let z be the closed point of Y_∞^ and F_∞ the preimage of F'_∞ on d(Y_∞^, {z}) ⊆ d(Y_∞^, f⁻¹(L)). Then (R^nλ_*F)_x̄ ≅ H^n(d(Y_∞^, {z}), F_∞) for every n ≥ 0: only the analytic points specialising to the closed point contribute.
hypotheses: Y_∞^ of type (S); F torsion
The distinction between F'_∞ on d(Y_∞^, f⁻¹(L)) and its preimage F_∞ on d(Y_∞^, {z}) is the source's
proofSteps: By node stalks-of-higher-direct-images-lambda, (R^nλ_*F)_x̄ = H^n(d(Y_∞^, f⁻¹(L)), F'_∞).

The completed strict henselisation C := (O^sh)^_J is henselian along its maximal ideal (C is J-adically complete, so (C, JC) is a henselian pair, and C/JC = O^sh/JO^sh is a henselian local ring as a quotient of the strictly henselian O^sh; hence (C, m_C) is henselian by Stacks Lemma 15.11.9 (Tag 0DYD); C need not be complete for its maximal ideal), so the henselian tube comparison applies: Corollary 3.6.3 (node henselian-tube-closed-subsets-3-6-2-3-6-3) for Spa(C, C)_a ⊇ closed tube over z when A is noetherian, and for Spa(C(1/s), D) (D the integral closure of C in C(1/s)) when A is not noetherian, gives H^n(d(Y_∞^, f⁻¹(L)), F'_∞) ≅ H^n(d(Y_∞^, {z}), F_∞).
acceptance: X = Spf Z_p⟨T⟩, L = |X|, x = (p, T): the stalk is the cohomology of the pseudo-adic space d(Y_∞^, {z}) whose support is the set of points of Spa of the completed strict henselisation specialising to z; the points specialising only to the generic point of the special fibre do not contribute.

nodes.title: The filtered stalk formula without the type-(S) hypothesis (Theorem 3.5.9)
nodes.statement: In the situation of node formal-strict-localisation-system-3-5-7, without assuming that Y_∞^ is of type (S), let F be a torsion sheaf on d(X, L)_et and F_i its preimage on d(Y_i^, {z_i}) (z_i = u_i(ȳ)). Then for every n ≥ 0: (R^nλ_*F)_x̄ ≅ colim_{i∈I} H^n(d(Y_i^, {z_i}), F_i). This is the formula to use when the completed strict localisation is not of type (S); it involves only the type-(S) formal schemes Y_i^ and no analytic space attached to Y_∞^.
hypotheses: F torsion; no hypothesis on Y_∞^
In the non-noetherian case the ideal of definition of B is principal (J = sB)
proofSteps: Noetherian case: Y_∞^ is of type (S) (node formal-strict-localisation-system-3-5-7); combine node stalk-formula-closed-point-3-5-8-ii with the tilde-limit d(Y_∞^, {z}) ~ lim d(Y_i^, {z_i}) and Corollary 2.4.6 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity).

Non-noetherian case (source proof, §3.6): auxiliary pseudo-adic spaces P_i = (Spa(C_i, C_i⁺), N_i) ⊇ Q_i built from the localisations (B_i)_s with the discrete topology, the tube comparison Corollary 3.6.3 (node henselian-tube-closed-subsets-3-6-2-3-6-3) for Q_∞ ⊆ P_∞, Corollary 2.4.6 for P_∞ ~ lim P_i and Q_∞ ~ lim Q_i, and Huber's (3.4.2.ii, iii.b) to transport cohomology between d(Y_i^, L_i) and P_i; the inputs (3.4.2)–(3.4.3) are available only in Hub96 (gap recorded).
Both cases: the stalk is colim_I H^n(d(Y_i^, f_i⁻¹(L)), F) (node higher-direct-images-of-lambda), and at each finite stage the passage from f_i⁻¹(L) to {z_i} happens only in the colimit.
acceptance: The stage requirement 'without that assumption use the filtered formula 3.5.9, not a nonexistent analytic strict-localization space' is exactly the hypothesis-free form of this node.
For X = Spf O_K with K complete discretely valued, each d(Y_i^, {z_i}) = Spa(K_i, O_{K_i}) for the unramified extensions K_i, and the formula gives colim H^n(K_i, M) = H^n(K^nr, M).

nodes.title: Stalks of R^nλ_*λ^*G: the cohomology of the generic locus of the strict localisation (Theorem 3.5.10)
nodes.statement: In the situation of node formal-strict-localisation-system-3-5-7, let G be a torsion sheaf on (X, L)_et and F = λ^*G. Let V := Y_∞ − (Y_∞ ×_Y Spec B/J), the open complement of V(J) in the strict localisation (V = Spec O^sh_{Y,ȳ}[1/s] when J = sB), and M the constant sheaf on V_et with value G_x̄. Then (R^nλ_*F)_x̄ ≅ H^n(V, M) for every n ≥ 0. No type-(S) hypothesis on Y_∞^ and no completion appears on the right-hand side; the torsion of G may be divisible by the residue characteristic.
hypotheses: G torsion (any torsion, including p-torsion)
No type-(S) hypothesis on Y_∞^
proofSteps: Noetherian case: by node stalk-formula-closed-point-3-5-8-ii, (R^nλ_*F)_x̄ = H^n(d(Y_∞^, {z}), F_∞), and F_∞ is constant with value G_x̄ (node constructibility-and-stalks-of-lambda-pullback); the comparison Theorem 3.2.10 applied to the Huber pair (O^sh, O^sh) with the J-adic topology (completion (C, C)), the pro-special subset U = {x : |c(x)| < 1 for all c in the maximal ideal} (whose analytic points form the support of d(Y_∞^, {z})) and the open subscheme V of Spec O^sh (its non-open primes, so condition (b) holds trivially), the henselisation of O^sh along U being O^sh itself, (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/relative-comparison-3-2-9-3-2-12) identifies it with H^n(V, M).

Non-noetherian case (source proof, §3.6): the functor e(T) = (Spa(T_s, D), {|s| < 1}) on affine Y-schemes, the sites T_{et,•} and the equivalence (Y_0)~ ≅ Y~_{et,•} of Huber's Appendix A.5, Corollary 3.6.3 and Theorem 3.2.1 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/pro-special-comparison-theorem-3-2-1) for e(Y_∞)'; Appendix A.5 is available only in Hub96 (gap recorded).
acceptance: X = Spf O_K with K complete discretely valued, x the closed point, G = Z/ℓ with ℓ ≠ p: V = Spec of the fraction field of O_K^sh, so (R^nλ_*Z/ℓ)_x̄ = H^n(I_K, Z/ℓ) = Z/ℓ, Z/ℓ(−1), 0 for n = 0, 1, ≥ 2.
The same X with G = Z/p: (R^1λ_*Z/p)_x̄ = H^1(K^nr_h, Z/p) is infinite (Artin–Schreier or Kummer theory): the theorem makes no prime-to-p restriction.

nodes.title: R⁺λ_* commutes with restriction to a smaller support (Corollary 3.5.11(i))
nodes.statement: Let X be a formal scheme of type (S), L' ⊆ L locally closed subsets of |X|, i: (X, L') → (X, L) the morphism of pairs given by the identity of X, d(i): d(X, L') → d(X, L) the inclusion of supports, λ = λ_(X,L), λ' = λ_(X,L') and E a torsion ring. Then the base-change morphism of functors D⁺(d(X, L)_et, E) → D⁺((X, L')_et, E), i^* ∘ R⁺λ_* ⟶ R⁺λ'_* ∘ d(i)^* (node pair-specialization-functoriality-3-5-4), is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: E a torsion ring; L' ⊆ L both locally closed
proofSteps: Reduce to a sheaf K of E-modules in degree 0 (way-out argument on D⁺, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image).

The topoi have enough points (geometric points of (L'_red)~, node pair-topos-reduced-subscheme-3-5-5 and Mathlib `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.HasEnoughPoints`); at a geometric point x̄ of L', by the filtered formula (node stalk-formula-filtered-3-5-9) both stalks equal colim_I H^n(d(Y_i^, {z_i}), K_i): the formula only uses the restriction of K to the supports over the points z_i, which lie over x ∈ L'.
The map between the two colimits is the identity of the colimit system.
acceptance: The compatibility holds in D⁺ with torsion coefficients, exactly the scope of 3.5.9.

nodes.title: R⁺λ_* commutes with extension by zero from an open support (Corollary 3.5.11(ii))
nodes.statement: In the situation of node restriction-and-extension-by-zero-3-5-11, assume L' open in L, and let i_! and d(i)_! be the extensions by zero along the open inclusions of supports (node pair-etale-site, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero). Then the natural morphism of functors D⁺(d(X, L')_et, E) → D⁺((X, L)_et, E), i_! ∘ R⁺λ'_* ⟶ R⁺λ_* ∘ d(i)_!, is an isomorphism for every torsion ring E. nodes.title: Completion data: the sites i, j, a, b attached to a scheme and a closed subscheme (3.5.12)
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme, 𝓘 ⊆ O_X a quasi-coherent ideal of finite type, Y = V(𝓘) with closed immersion i: Y → X, U = X − Y with open immersion j: U → X, and X^ the formal completion of X along Y (the formal scheme of finite ideal type attached to the thickenings V(𝓘^{n+1}), AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings; affine-locally Spf of the 𝓘-adic completion, Stacks 05GG). Hypothesis (3.5.12), at least one of (both may hold, e.g. X = Spec O_K with 𝓘 = (ϖ)): (α) X is locally noetherian; or (β) 𝓘 is locally generated by one element and X^ is of type (S). Under (α), X^ is locally noetherian, hence of type (S). The completion data consist of: the morphisms of sites i: Y_et → X_et and j: U_et → X_et; b: d(X^)_et → Y_et, the composite of λ_{X^} (node specialization-morphism-of-sites-lambda) with (X^)_et ≃ (X^_red)_et = (Y_red)_et ≃ Y_et (node reduced-special-scheme-equivalence and topological invariance); and a: d(X^)_et → U_et, induced by the morphism of locally ringed spaces σ_{X^}: d(X^) → X of (1.9.4) (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison), whose image lies in U, via a⁻¹(Z) := Z ×_X d(X^) (Huber's fibre product of a scheme locally of finite type over X with an adic space over X, AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification) for Z étale over U.
hypotheses: 𝓘 of finite type; (α) X locally noetherian, or (β) 𝓘 locally principal and X^ of type (S) — exactly as in Huber (3.5.12)
Without (α) or (β), X^ need not be of type (S) and d(X^) is not defined
proofSteps: σ_{X^}(d(X^)) ⊆ U: points of d(X^) are analytic, so their supports do not contain 𝓘 (they are not open primes), hence map to U (Huber (3.2.8) as recorded in the reviewed decomposition).

a is a morphism of sites: Z ×_X d(X^) → d(X^) is étale for Z étale over U by (1.7.3) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-structure); fibre products are preserved by transitivity of Huber's fibre product (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/scheme-fibre-product-analytification); coverings go to coverings because base change along d(X^) → X preserves surjectivity: for a jointly surjective family (Z_i → Z), ⊔_i Z_i → Z is surjective and locally of finite type, hence so is ⊔_i Z_i ×_X d(X^) → Z ×_X d(X^) (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytification-surjective; Z_i ×_X d(X^) = Z_i ×_Z (Z ×_X d(X^)) by transitivity).
b is a morphism of sites as a composite of λ_{X^} with an equivalence of sites; (X^)_red = Y_red because |X^| = |Y| and both are reduced.
(α) ⇒ type (S): X^ is locally noetherian (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion), hence of type (S) via (a) (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-schemes-of-type-S).
acceptance: For X = Spec O_K (K complete discretely valued) and 𝓘 = (ϖ): Y = Spec k, U = Spec K, X^ = Spf O_K, d(X^) = Spa(K, O_K); a is the equivalence between finite étale K-algebras seen algebraically and analytically, b is λ of Spf O_K.

nodes.title: The comparison map i^* ∘ R⁺j_* → R⁺b_* ∘ a^* (Theorem 3.5.13(i))
nodes.statement: Let (X, 𝓘) be completion data (node completion-comparison-data-3-5-12). For Z ∈ Et/X let Z^ ∈ Et/X^ be its completion along Y ×_X Z and φ_Z: d(Z^) → Z ×_X d(X^) the comparison morphism of Huber (1.9.5) (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison). The φ_Z are natural in Z and form a natural transformation φ: b⁻¹ ∘ i⁻¹ ⟶ a⁻¹ ∘ j⁻¹ of functors Et/X → Et/d(X^) (b⁻¹i⁻¹Z = d(Z^), a⁻¹j⁻¹Z = Z ×_X d(X^)). On sheaves this gives j_* ∘ a_* ⟶ i_* ∘ b_* and, by adjunction, for every ring E and every sheaf K of E-modules on U_et, the morphism ψ_K: i^* j_* K ⟶ b_* a^* K, natural in K. Deriving: since i^* is exact, R⁺(i^* ∘ j_*) = i^* ∘ R⁺j_*, and composing R⁺ψ with the canonical R⁺(b_* ∘ a^*) ⟶ R⁺b_* ∘ a^* gives the natural transformation (*) i^* ∘ R⁺j_* ⟶ R⁺b_* ∘ a^* of functors D⁺(U_et, E) → D⁺(Y_et, E), defined for every ring E. It is natural with respect to étale Z → X (restriction of completion data) and to isomorphisms of completion data, and on H⁰ of a sheaf in degree 0 it is ψ.
hypotheses: (X, 𝓘) completion data; E any ring for the construction (torsion only for the isomorphism, node scheme-completion-comparison-3-5-13)
proofSteps: φ_Z exists and is natural (Huber (1.9.5), AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison).

Direct images along morphisms of sites are restrictions along the inverse-image functors; a natural transformation of inverse-image functors u_1 ⟶ u_2 induces F(u_2 Z) → F(u_1 Z), i.e. (j_* a_* F)(Z) → (i_* b_* F)(Z).
ψ_K: the composite j_*K → j_*a_*a^*K → i_*b_*a^*K (unit of a^* ⊣ a_*), transposed along i^* ⊣ i_*.

Derived form: universal property of right derived functors on D⁺ (Mathlib `CategoryTheory.Functor.rightDerivedFunctorPlus`; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image for the sheaf-theoretic instances; EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1 for K-injective replacements).

nodes.title: Cohomology of the henselised generic locus equals that of the generic fibre of the completion
nodes.statement: Let (X, 𝓘) be completion data with X = Spec A affine, J = 𝓘(X), and Z = Spec B affine étale over X, Z^h = Spec B^h for the henselisation (B^h, J^h) of the pair (B, JB), and Z^ = Spf B^ (J-adic completion). The composite d(Z^) → Spec B^ − V(JB^) → Spec B^h − V(JB^h) = U ×_X Z^h induces, for every torsion sheaf K on U_et, isomorphisms H^n(U ×_X Z^h, K) ≅ H^n(d(Z^), a^*K), n ≥ 0. Case (α): d(Z^) = Spa(B, B)_a with B carrying the JB-adic topology, and the statement is Theorem 3.2.10 for the pro-special subset Spa(B, B) and the scheme Spec B − V(JB). Case (β) (J = sA): d(Z^) = Spa(B(1/s), C) with C the integral closure of B in B(1/s), U ×_X Z^h is the spectrum of the henselisation of the affinoid ring (B(1/s), C) along Spa(B(1/s), C), and the statement is Theorem 3.2.9.

proofSteps: The map exists because B^ is J-adically complete, hence henselian along J (so B → B^ factors through B^h), and d(Z^) maps to the complement of V(J).

Case (α): Spa(B, B) = Spa(B^, B^) is a pro-special subset whose henselisation is B^h (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/henselization-along-pro-special-subset, Example 3.1.13.iii); Theorem 3.2.10 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/relative-comparison-3-2-9-3-2-12) applied to X' = Spec B − V(JB) → Spec B gives the isomorphism.

Case (β): d(Z^) = Spa(B(1/s), C) (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-functor-d, case (b)); the henselisation of the affinoid ring (B(1/s), C) along Spa(B(1/s), C) is B^h[1/s] (Example 3.1.13.iii); Theorem 3.2.9 compares the cohomology of its spectrum with that of the pro-special subset.

nodes.title: The nearby-cycle comparison for completions: i^*R⁺j_*K ≅ R⁺b_*a^*K for torsion coefficients (Theorem 3.5.13(ii))
nodes.statement: Let (X, 𝓘) be completion data (node completion-comparison-data-3-5-12): X a scheme, Y = V(𝓘) for a quasi-coherent ideal 𝓘 of finite type, U = X − Y, X^ the completion along Y, and either (α) X locally noetherian or (β) 𝓘 locally principal and X^ of type (S) — exactly as in (3.5.12). Let E be a torsion ring. Then the natural transformation (*) i^* ∘ R⁺j_* ⟶ R⁺b_* ∘ a^* of node completion-comparison-map-3-5-13-i is an isomorphism of functors D⁺(U_et, E) → D⁺(Y_et, E). The torsion scope is the source's: every torsion ring, with no prime-to-residue-characteristic hypothesis; that narrower restriction belongs to the valuation-base-change theorem (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles), not to this comparison.
hypotheses: (α) or (β) exactly as (3.5.12)
E torsion for the isomorphism; the transformation exists for every ring E
Imports: Theorems 3.2.9 and 3.2.10 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/relative-comparison-3-2-9-3-2-12), whose proofs in Hub96 §§3.3–3.4 are Hub96-only (gap recorded there)
proofSteps: Way-out reduction to a sheaf K of E-modules in degree 0; the statement is étale-local on X, so assume X = Spec A affine with (α) A noetherian or (β) 𝓘 = sA and A^ satisfying (S)(b).
Fix a geometric point ȳ of Y and the category C of ȳ-pointed affine étale X-schemes (Z, u); let Z^h be the henselisation of Z along Y ×_X Z.
(i^*R^n j_*K)_ȳ = colim_C H^n(U ×_X Z, K) (stalks of R^n j_* at geometric points of Y, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2).

(R^n b_* a^*K)_ȳ = colim_C H^n(d(Z^), a^*K): the Z^ with the induced pointing are cofinal étale neighbourhoods of ȳ in (X^)_et ≃ Y_et (node etale-lifting-along-special-fibre, node reduced-special-scheme-equivalence), and node higher-direct-images-of-lambda (ii).
For each (Z, u): H^n(U ×_X Z^h, K) ≅ H^n(d(Z^), a^*K) (node henselised-generic-locus-cohomology), compatibly with the maps induced by φ_Z.

lim_C (U ×_X Z^h) ≅ lim_C (U ×_X Z) = U ×_X Spec O^sh_{X,ȳ} (henselising along Y does not change the strict localisation), and étale cohomology commutes with such cofiltered limits of qcqs schemes with affine transition maps (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2); so colim_C H^n(U ×_X Z^h, K) = colim_C H^n(U ×_X Z, K), and the resulting isomorphism of stalks is (*)_ȳ.
Isomorphism on all stalks at geometric points of Y ⇒ isomorphism (Y_et has enough points).

nodes.title: The pseudo-adic space over the closed point of d(Spf A) for a microbial valuation ring A (setup of 3.5.16)
nodes.statement: Let A be a microbial valuation ring (Wedhorn Definition 5.46: A has a prime ideal of height one; equivalently A with its valuation topology is adic and non-discrete) with fraction field K and its valuation topology, I ⊆ A a finitely generated ideal of definition (so I = sA for a nonzero topologically nilpotent s), η and s_0 the generic and closed points of Spec A, and X a scheme locally of finite type over A with fibres X_η, X_{s_0}. Let X^ be the completion of X along X ×_A Spec A/I. Then: (1) X^ is of type (S) and does not depend on the choice of I; (2) (X, I·O_X) is completion data of type (β) (node completion-comparison-data-3-5-12): I·O_X is principal and X − V(I·O_X) = X_η, because (0) is the only prime of A not containing s; (3) d(Spf A) = Spa(K^, A^) (Huber 1.9.2(i)), whose points are the valuation rings between A^ and K^° (a chain with a unique closed point c_A, corresponding to A^ itself); (4) T := the preimage of c_A under d(X^) → d(Spf A) equals λ_{X^}⁻¹(X_{s_0}), so Z := (d(X^), T) = d(X^, X_{s_0}) is a pseudo-adic space (node pairs-and-pseudo-adic-supports; X_{s_0} is closed in |X^| = |X ×_A Spec A/I|); (5) c: Z_et → (X_η)_et is the restriction to Z of the morphism a of the completion data. The base need not be a discrete valuation ring and need not have rank one; if A has rank one, d(Spf A) is a point and Z = d(X^).
hypotheses: A microbial valuation ring with its valuation topology (any rank; not necessarily complete, discrete or noetherian); I finitely generated ideal of definition; X locally of finite type over A
proofSteps: (1): Spf A^ is of type (S) (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-schemes-of-type-S, API spf_microbial; Huber §1.9), and the completion of a morphism locally of finite type preserves type (S) (API FormalScheme.IsTypeS.completion, Huber (1.9.5)); two finitely generated ideals of definition have cofinal powers.
(2): a finitely generated ideal of a valuation ring is principal; the primes of A not containing s are those not containing the height-one prime √(sA), i.e. only (0).
(3): AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-functor-d (API genericFibre_spf_microbial) and Wedhorn Example 7.17 (K^° is the rank-one valuation ring dependent on A).
(4): for t ∈ d(X^), its image in Spa(K^, A^) is the valuation ring of t restricted to A; it is A^ exactly when the centre of t lies over the closed point of Spec A, i.e. when λ_{X^}(t) ∈ X_{s_0}.
(5): node completion-comparison-data-3-5-12 and restriction to the support (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero).
acceptance: For A of rank two and X = Spec A, T = {v_2} is closed and not open in d(X^) (for general X, T is closed, and not open as soon as it is nonempty, since the rank-one generisation of a point of T maps to the rank-one point of Spa(K^, A^); T is empty, hence open, e.g. for X = Spec K): Z is a pseudo-adic space which is not an adic space.

nodes.title: Huber's 'complex of vanishing cycles' RΨ_η is the nearby-cycle complex of LPV.0, not the cone RΦ
nodes.statement: Let A be a henselian discrete valuation ring with separably closed residue field (a strictly henselian trait S = Spec A with generic point η and closed point s), k = Frac A, k̄ an algebraic closure, Ā the integral closure of A in k̄ (a henselian valuation ring of rank one, not discrete, with residue field purely inseparable over k(s)), S̄ = Spec Ā = {s̄, η̄}, X locally of finite type over A, X̄ = X ×_A Ā with ī: X_s̄ → X̄ and j̄: X_η̄ → X̄. For a torsion ring E and K ∈ D⁺((X_η)_et, E), Huber's complex RΨ_η(K) ∈ D⁺((X_s)_et, E) of Corollary 3.5.17 is ī^* R⁺j̄_*(K|_{X_η̄}), transported to (X_s)_et along the universal homeomorphism X_s̄ → X_s (topological invariance). With the action of Gal(k̄/k) = I (the inertia group, the residue field being separably closed) induced by its action on X̄ over X, this is the object RΨ_η(K) = (RΨ(K))_η of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0 (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.2.3, S̄ the normalisation of S in k(η̄)) in D⁺(X_s ×_s η, E): the nearby-cycle complex. It is not the vanishing-cycle cone RΦ(K), which for K on X sits in the distinguished triangle sp^*i^*K → RΨ_η(K_η) → RΦ(K) → of LPV.0. Huber's statement only uses the underlying complex; the Galois action is added here and is used in node formal-nearby-cycles-comparison.
hypotheses: A strictly henselian DVR; E torsion; K bounded below

LPV.0 states its theory for coefficients prime to the residue characteristic; the definition ī^*R⁺j̄_* uses no such hypothesis, and for torsion divisible by p this node uses the same formula (request to LPV.0 recorded)
proofSteps: Unwind LPV.0's definition: RΨ_η(K)_η̄ = ī^* R j̄_* K_η̄ on X_s̄ with its continuous Gal(η̄/η)-action (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0/derived-nearby-cycles-RPsi-and-vanishing-triangle, LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0/functor-psi-and-functorialities, conventions LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0/henselian-trait-conventions-and-galois-sheaves).

Huber's X ×_A Ā (proof of 3.5.17) is LPV.0's X̄ = X ×_S S̄; its closed fibre X_s̄ → X_s is a universal homeomorphism (k(s̄)/k(s) purely inseparable), so (X_s̄)_et ≃ (X_s)_et (Stacks 04DZ), and sheaves on X_s ×_s η are sheaves on X_s̄ with continuous I-action (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0/fibre-product-topos-Y-times-S).

RΦ ≠ RΨ: for X = S and K = E constant, Ā is strictly henselian and X_η̄ = Spec k̄ has no higher cohomology, so RΨ_η(E) = ī^*R⁺j̄_*E = E in degree 0 for every torsion E, while RΦ(E) = cone(E → E) = 0; so the right-hand side of 3.5.17 is RΨ.
acceptance: X = S = Spec A, K = E: RΨ_η(E) = E in degree 0 with trivial action, RΦ(E) = 0; 3.5.17 gives R⁺Γ(Spa(k̄^), E) = E, consistent with RΨ and not with RΦ.
X smooth over A, K = Z/ℓ with ℓ ≠ p: RΨ_η(Z/ℓ) = Z/ℓ and RΦ(Z/ℓ) = 0.

nodes.title: Nearby cycles of X agree Galois-equivariantly with the formal nearby cycles of the completion
nodes.statement: In the situation of node huber-vanishing-cycles-are-nearby-cycles, let π be a uniformiser of A, X̄^ the π-adic completion of X̄ = X ×_A Ā along X_s̄, λ̄: d(X̄^)_et → (X̄^)_et ≃ (X_s̄)_et ≃ (X_s)_et the specialization morphism (node specialization-morphism-of-sites-lambda) and c: d(X̄^)_et → (X_η)_et the composite of the morphism a of the completion data (X̄, π·O_X̄) with X_η̄ → X_η. Then: (i) (X̄, π·O_X̄) is completion data of type (β), and d(X̄^) ≅ d(X^) ×_{Spa(k^, A^)} Spa(k̄^, O_{k̄^}) = Ȳ, the base change of the generic fibre of X^ to the completed algebraic closure; (ii) for every torsion ring E and K ∈ D⁺((X_η)_et, E), the comparison (*) of node completion-comparison-map-3-5-13-i for (X̄, π·O_X̄) is an isomorphism RΨ_η(K) = ī^*R⁺j̄_*(K|_{X_η̄}) ≅ R⁺λ̄_*(c^*K) in D⁺((X_s)_et, E); (iii) this isomorphism is Gal(k̄/k)-equivariant for the action on RΨ_η(K) (node huber-vanishing-cycles-are-nearby-cycles) and the action on R⁺λ̄_*(c^*K) induced by the continuous action of Gal(k̄/k) on k̄^, hence on X̄^ and d(X̄^) over X^ and d(X^); in particular the inertia actions on R^qΨ_η(K) and on the formal nearby-cycle sheaves R^qλ̄_*(c^*K) agree, and the latter action is continuous.
hypotheses: A strictly henselian DVR; E any torsion ring; K bounded below
Ā is neither noetherian nor complete; its completion is O_{k̄^}
proofSteps: (i) π·O_X̄ is principal. Affine-locally X = Spec B with B of finite type over A; the π-adic completion of B ⊗_A Ā is topologically finitely presented over O_{k̄^}, so X̄^ is locally tfp over O_{k̄^} and of type (S) via (b) (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-schemes-of-type-S, API IsTypeS.of_isLocallyTFP). X̄^ = X^ ⊗̂_{A^} O_{k̄^}, and d commutes with this completed base change (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products (b)).
(ii) node scheme-completion-comparison-3-5-13 for (X̄, π·O_X̄): X̄ − V(π) = X_η̄ and V(π) = X_s̄; transport along (X_s̄)_et ≃ (X_s)_et (Stacks 04DZ).

(iii) σ ∈ Gal(k̄/k) acts on Ā over A, hence on X̄ by X-automorphisms preserving X_s̄ and X_η̄, on X̄^ and on d(X̄^); these are isomorphisms of completion data, and the comparison (*) is natural for them (node completion-comparison-map-3-5-13-i, API derivedComparison_natural). So (*) intertwines σ^* on both sides. Continuity of the action on RΨ_η(K) is part of LPV.0 (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0/derived-nearby-cycles-RPsi-and-vanishing-triangle) and transfers through the isomorphism.
acceptance: X = A^1_A, K = Z/ℓ (ℓ ≠ p): R⁺λ̄_*(Z/ℓ) is the constant sheaf Z/ℓ on A^1_{k(s)} with trivial inertia action, matching RΨ_η(Z/ℓ) = Z/ℓ for the smooth X.

X = Spec A[x, y]/(xy − π) (the nodal trait family of LPV.0's acceptance tests), K = Z/ℓ with ℓ ≠ p: at the node x̄, R^1Ψ_η(Z/ℓ)_x̄ ≅ Z/ℓ(−1) (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.2), (ii) identifies it with (R^1λ̄_*Z/ℓ)_x̄, the H^1 of the support over the node in the generic fibre of the completion (an annulus over k̄^), and (iii) makes the two inertia actions agree.

nodes.title: Cohomology of the geometric rigid generic fibre of the completion via nearby cycles (Corollary 3.5.17)
nodes.statement: Let A be a henselian discrete valuation ring (of rank one) with separably closed residue field, k its fraction field with the valuation topology, k^ its completion, k̄^ the completion of an algebraic closure k̄, η and s the generic and closed points of Spec A, X a scheme locally of finite type over A, E a torsion ring, K ∈ D⁺((X_η)_et, E), and RΨ_η(K) ∈ D⁺((X_s)_et, E) Huber's 'complex of vanishing cycles of K', i.e. the nearby-cycle complex of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0 (node huber-vanishing-cycles-are-nearby-cycles; not RΦ). Let Y be the rigid analytic variety over k^ attached to the completion X^ of X along X_s (so r(Y) = d(X^), AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre), Ȳ := Y ⊗̂_{k^} k̄^, and c: Ȳ_et → (X_η)_et the natural morphism. Then R⁺Γ(Ȳ, c^*K) ≅ R⁺Γ(X_s, RΨ_η K), with X_s the closed fibre itself (its residue field is separably closed), and the isomorphism is Gal(k̄/k)-equivariant. No properness is assumed.
hypotheses: A a henselian DVR with separably closed residue field; E torsion (any, including p-torsion); K bounded below
Rigid and adic étale topoi are identified by Huber's 2.1.4 (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-and-rigid-comparison)
proofSteps: Source proof: apply Corollary 3.5.14 (node generic-fibre-cohomology-3-5-14) to the scheme X ×_A Ā and its closed subscheme X_s ×_A Ā, i.e. to the completion data (X̄, π·O_X̄) of node formal-nearby-cycles-comparison, and identify d(X̄^) with r(Ȳ) (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products (b), AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre) and Ȳ_et with d(X̄^)_et (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-and-rigid-comparison).

Equivalently: apply R⁺Γ(X_s, −) to the equivariant isomorphism RΨ_η(K) ≅ R⁺λ̄_*(c^*K) of node formal-nearby-cycles-comparison and use Leray for λ̄ (node higher-direct-images-of-lambda (iii)); equivariance follows from that node.
acceptance: X proper and smooth over A, K = Z/ℓ (ℓ ≠ p): RΨ_η(Z/ℓ) = Z/ℓ, and Ȳ = (X_{k̄^})^an, so H^n(X_{k̄}, Z/ℓ) ≅ H^n(Ȳ, Z/ℓ) ≅ H^n(X_s, Z/ℓ): the specialisation isomorphism.

X = A^1_A (not proper), K = Z/ℓ, ℓ ≠ p: Ȳ is the closed unit disc over k̄^ and both sides are Z/ℓ in degree 0; with K = Z/p the theorem still applies (no prime-to-p hypothesis), although RΨ_η(Z/p) is then in general not the constant sheaf (smooth morphisms are locally acyclic only for torsion prime to p).
The Galois/inertia action is matched by node formal-nearby-cycles-comparison (iii), not only the abstract cohomology groups.

nodes.title: Valuation-base quadruples (X, S, η, s)
nodes.statement: A valuation-base quadruple (X, S, η, s) consists of: a valuation ring V (an integral domain whose ideals are totally ordered by inclusion; mathlib:ValuationRing) with fraction field K and S = Spec V; two points η, s ∈ S with η a generization of s, i.e. 𝔭_η ⊆ 𝔭_s for the corresponding primes (s lies in the closure of {η}); and a scheme X with a morphism f: X -> S; subject to the condition that the local ring O_{S,s} = V_{𝔭_s} is strictly henselian (henselian local, mathlib:HenselianLocalRing, with separably closed residue field k(s), mathlib:IsSepClosed). The case η = s is allowed. Pinned notation: p_s is the characteristic exponent of k(s); k(η) = Frac(V/𝔭_η), the residue field of the valuation ring O_{S,η} = V_{𝔭_η}; X_s := X ×_S Spec k(s) is the fibre (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.fiber) with its canonical morphism i: X_s -> X; X_η := X ×_S Spec k(η). The quadruple is of finite type (resp. of finite presentation) if f is locally of finite type (resp. locally of finite presentation). The points of S lying between η and s are the primes 𝔭 with 𝔭_η ⊆ 𝔭 ⊆ 𝔭_s; they form a chain. Nothing is assumed about the rank of V or about discreteness of its value group, and V need not be noetherian.
hypotheses: V is an arbitrary valuation ring: any rank, any value group; V is not assumed noetherian, complete or of finite rank.
O_{S,s} strictly henselian is a condition on the pair (V, s) only; O_{S,η} is then a localization of O_{S,s} and in general has a residue field k(η) that is not separably closed.
η = s is allowed; η need not be the generic point of S and s need not be the closed point of S.
proofSteps: The data are a ring V with mathlib:ValuationRing, two prime ideals 𝔭_η ⊆ 𝔭_s, a morphism of schemes f: X -> Spec V, and the proposition that V_{𝔭_s} is strictly henselian (mathlib:HenselianLocalRing for V_{𝔭_s} and mathlib:IsSepClosed for its residue field mathlib:IsLocalRing.ResidueField).
The fibre X_s is mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.fiber f s; no further construction is involved.
acceptance: For a strictly henselian valuation ring V with value group ℤ × ℤ (lexicographic) and primes 0 ⊊ 𝔭 ⊊ 𝔪, the admissible pairs (η, s) are exactly (0, 𝔪), (𝔭, 𝔪) and (𝔪, 𝔪): for the value group ℤ × ℤ (lexicographic) V/𝔭 is a discrete valuation ring, so the residue field Frac(V/𝔭) of V_𝔭 has Kummer extensions of every prime degree ℓ ≠ char and is not separably closed; s = 0 is excluded because K = V_0 is not separably closed (x^ℓ − a with v(a) = (1, 0) is irreducible and separable for ℓ ≠ char, a root having value (1/ℓ, 0) ∉ ℤ × ℤ).
A strictly henselian discrete valuation ring with η the generic point and s the closed point is a quadruple; this is the trait situation of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0.

nodes.title: The strict localization of a valuation spectrum at a geometric point
nodes.statement: Let V be a valuation ring with fraction field K, 𝔭 ⊂ V a prime, A := V_𝔭 (a valuation ring of K with residue field κ(𝔭)), and L a separable closure of κ(𝔭). Let A^sh be the strict henselization of A with respect to κ(𝔭) -> L and S(𝔭̄) := Spec A^sh. Then: (a) A^sh is a valuation ring, strictly henselian with residue field L, and A -> A^sh induces an isomorphism of value groups Γ_A ≅ Γ_{A^sh}; (b) A^sh is the localization (Y^I)_{𝔮 ∩ Y^I} of the fixed ring Y^I, where Y is the integral closure of A in a separable closure K^s of K, 𝔮 a maximal ideal of Y, and D ⊇ I the decomposition and inertia subgroups of 𝔮 in Gal(K^s/K); (c) D/I ≅ Aut(κ(𝔮)/κ(𝔭)) = Gal(L/κ(𝔭)) (with L identified with the separable closure of κ(𝔭) in κ(𝔮), the residue field of A^sh; κ(𝔮) itself is a normal extension of κ(𝔭), an algebraic closure when 𝔭 ≠ 0, purely inseparable over L) acts on A^sh by A-algebra automorphisms, and this action identifies Gal(L/κ(𝔭)) with the group of A-algebra automorphisms of A^sh; (d) if 𝔭 = 0 then A^sh = L and S(𝔭̄) = Spec L; if A is already strictly henselian (for instance 𝔭 = 𝔭_s in a quadruple) then A^sh = A and L = κ(𝔭).
hypotheses: V is any valuation ring; no rank or discreteness hypothesis.

The strict henselization of a local ring at a separable closure of its residue field, with its universal property, is supplied by the scheme-level étale owner (request to SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2:EtaleBaseChange:3-8).
proofSteps: (a) Gabber–Ramero Lemma 6.2.5: the strict henselization of a valuation ring is a valuation ring with the same value group; strict henselianity and residue field L are part of the definition of strict henselization (supplier).
(b) The construction in the proof of Gabber–Ramero Lemma 6.2.5 (via [60, Ch. X §2 Th. 2]): R^sh = (W^I)_{p^I} for R integrally closed local; A is a valuation ring, hence integrally closed.

(c) Gabber–Ramero (6.2.3): D_𝔮 -> Aut(κ(𝔮)/κ(𝔭)) is surjective with kernel I_𝔮, and κ(𝔮) is a normal algebraic extension of κ(𝔭) whose separable part is L, so restriction Aut(κ(𝔮)/κ(𝔭)) -> Gal(L/κ(𝔭)) is bijective (κ(𝔮)/L purely inseparable); D and I are mathlib:ValuationSubring.decompositionSubgroup and mathlib:ValuationSubring.inertiaSubgroup of the valuation subring Y_𝔮 of K^s; the action of D on Y^I factors through D/I and preserves 𝔮 ∩ Y^I. Bijectivity onto the A-automorphisms of A^sh is the universal property of strict henselization (supplier) applied to the automorphisms of L over κ(𝔭).
(d) For 𝔭 = 0, A = K and its strict henselization at L is L; for A strictly henselian the identity is a strict henselization (universal property).
acceptance: For V a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring and 𝔭 = 0: S(𝔭̄) = Spec K^s and Gal(L/κ(𝔭)) = Gal(K^s/K).

For V of rank 2 with primes 0 ⊊ 𝔭 ⊊ 𝔪 and V strictly henselian: V_𝔭 is a henselian rank-one valuation ring and (V_𝔭)^sh is a strictly henselian rank-one valuation ring with value group that of V_𝔭 (Γ/Δ for the value group Γ of V and its nonzero proper convex subgroup Δ), residue field a separable closure of Frac(V/𝔭).

nodes.title: Morphisms of quadruples and the chosen map of strict localizations
nodes.statement: Let (X, S, η, s) and (X', S', η', s') be quadruples (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/valuation-base-quadruple), with chosen separable closures L of k(η) and L' of k(η'). A morphism φ = (g, h, ι): (X', S', η', s', L') -> (X, S, η, s, L) consists of a morphism of schemes h: S' -> S (equivalently a ring map V -> V') with h(η') = η and h(s') = s, a morphism g: X' -> X with f ∘ g = h ∘ f', and a k(η)-embedding ι: L -> L' extending the residue map k(η) -> k(η'). By the universal property of strict henselization (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/strict-localisation-of-a-valuation-ring), ι determines a unique local morphism h̃: S'(η̄') -> S(η̄) over h inducing ι on residue fields; this is the 'chosen compatible map of strict localizations'. ι also determines the continuous homomorphism φ_#: Gal(L'/k(η')) -> Gal(L/k(η)), σ' ↦ ι^{-1} ∘ σ' ∘ ι (well defined because ι(L) is the separable closure of k(η) in L', which every σ' preserves). φ is Cartesian if the square (g, f', f, h) is Cartesian, i.e. X' -> X ×_S S' is an isomorphism; φ is dominant if the local homomorphism O_{S,s} -> O_{S',s'} induced by h is injective. Composition is componentwise ((g, h, ι) ∘ (g_1, h_1, ι_1) = (g ∘ g_1, h ∘ h_1, ι_1 ∘ ι)) and identities are (id, id, id).
hypotheses: h(s') = s makes O_{S,s} -> O_{S',s'} a local homomorphism of valuation rings; no injectivity, flatness or finiteness of h is part of the definition.

The embedding ι is part of the data: two morphisms with the same (g, h) and different ι differ by the action of Gal(L/k(η)) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-equivariant-transport).
proofSteps: Composition and identity laws are componentwise; the laws for h̃ follow from the uniqueness in the universal property of strict henselization (strict-localisation-of-a-valuation-ring).
φ_# is a continuous homomorphism of profinite groups because restriction along ι is continuous for the Krull topologies (mathlib:separableClosure gives ι(L) as the separable closure of k(η) in L').
acceptance: For a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring V, a finite separable extension K'/K and V' the integral closure of V in K' (again a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring), (X ×_V V', Spec V', generic, closed, L) -> (X, Spec V, generic, closed, L) with ι = id is a Cartesian dominant morphism and φ_# is the inclusion of the open subgroup Gal(L/K') ⊆ Gal(L/K).

nodes.title: The nearby-cycle functor RΨ_L = i^* Rj_* j^* of a quadruple
nodes.statement: Let (X, S, η, s) be a quadruple (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/valuation-base-quadruple), L a separable closure of k(η), η̄ = Spec L, and S(η̄) = Spec (O_{S,η})^sh the strict localization of S at η̄ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/strict-localisation-of-a-valuation-ring) with its canonical morphism S(η̄) -> S (which factors through Spec O_{S,s}). Put X_η̃ := X ×_S S(η̄), let j: X_η̃ -> X be the projection (an affine morphism) and i: X_s -> X the special fibre. For a ring Λ and F ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ) define RΨ_L(F) := i^* Rj_* j^* F ∈ D^+(X_{s,et}, Λ) and R^qΨ_L(F) := H^q(RΨ_L(F)). This is a Λ-linear triangulated functor RΨ_L: D^+(X_et, Λ) -> D^+(X_{s,et}, Λ), and the unit id -> Rj_* j^* gives the specialization transformation sp: i^* -> RΨ_L. Conventions pinned: (i) j is the base change of the strict localization S(η̄) -> S, not of η̄ -> S: RΨ_L is formed with Milnor tubes; the version RΨ_L^geo(F) := i^* R(jk)_*(jk)^* F formed with the geometric fibre k: X_η̄ := X ×_S η̄ -> X_η̃ receives the natural map RΨ_L(F) -> RΨ_L^geo(F) from the unit id -> Rk_*k^* (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/comparison-with-geometric-generic-point); if η is the generic point of S then S(η̄) = η̄ and the two agree. (ii) If η = s then S(η̄) = Spec O_{S,s}, j is a limit of open immersions containing X_s, and RΨ_L = i^*. (iii) RΨ_L is the nearby-cycle object; the cone of sp (vanishing cycles RΦ) is not part of this node. (iv) The derived functors are computed in the Grothendieck abelian category of sheaves of Λ-modules on the small étale sites (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isGrothendieckAbelian_sheaf_smallEtaleTopology), bounded below, and commute with restriction of scalars along ring maps Λ' -> Λ.
hypotheses: No finiteness assumption on f, on F or on Λ is needed for the definition; theorems about RΨ_L carry their own hypotheses (finite type, torsion prime to p_s, constructibility).
L is a choice; dependence on it is controlled by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-equivariant-transport.
proofSteps: Sheaves of Λ-modules on X_et and X_{s,et} form Grothendieck abelian categories (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isGrothendieckAbelian_sheaf_smallEtaleTopology over mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.smallEtaleTopology), so injective resolutions and the right derived functor Rj_* on D^+ exist (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/k-injective-and-k-flat-replacements; bounded-below injective resolutions suffice on D^+).

i^* and j^* are exact (pullbacks of étale sheaves along arbitrary scheme morphisms, supplied by SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2:EtaleBaseChange:3-8), so RΨ_L := i^* ∘ Rj_* ∘ j^* is a triangulated functor on D^+ (mathlib:DerivedCategory).
sp is i^* applied to the unit of j^* ⊣ Rj_*.

Convention (ii): for η = s, S(η̄) = Spec O_{S,s} (strict-localisation-of-a-valuation-ring (d)), j is a cofiltered limit of open immersions of quasi-compact opens containing X_s, and j^*Rj_* ≅ id by continuity (request to AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2); since i factors through j, RΨ_L = i^*.
Compatibility with restriction of scalars: Rj_* is computed on underlying abelian sheaves (supplier).
acceptance: For X = S, any quadruple and any Λ: RΨ_L(Λ) = Λ in degree 0 with trivial Galois action, because the Milnor tube S_(s̄) ×_S S(η̄) = S(η̄) is strictly local.

For V a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring with uniformizer π, η generic, n ≥ 1 prime to p_s, X = Spec V[t]/(t^n − π): X_s is one point and R^0Ψ_L(Λ) = Λ^{Hom_K(K(π^{1/n}), L)} ≅ Λ^n, R^qΨ_L(Λ) = 0 for q > 0.

nodes.title: The continuous action of Gal(L/k(η)) on RΨ_L
nodes.statement: In the situation of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-over-valuation-base put G_η := Gal(L/k(η)) with its Krull topology. Each σ ∈ G_η extends uniquely to an automorphism σ̃ of S(η̄) over S inducing σ on L (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/strict-localisation-of-a-valuation-ring (c)), hence to an automorphism σ̃_X := X ×_S σ̃ of X_η̃ over X, with j ∘ σ̃_X = j. Transport of structure along σ̃_X^{-1} gives isomorphisms j^*F ≅ (σ̃_X)_* j^*F and hence automorphisms ρ_F(σ) of Rj_* j^* F and of RΨ_L(F), natural in F ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ), with ρ(στ) = ρ(σ) ρ(τ) and ρ(1) = id (a left action). The action is continuous: for every q, every quasi-compact étale U -> X_s and every section a ∈ R^qΨ_L(F)(U) the stabilizer of a in G_η is open; equivalently each stalk (R^qΨ_L F)_x̄ = H^q(X_(x̄) ×_S S(η̄), F) is a discrete G_η-module, because S(η̄) is the limit of the spectra of the local finite étale O^h_{S,η}-algebras whose residue fields are the finite separable subextensions of L/k(η) and cohomology commutes with this limit. The specialization map sp: i^*F -> RΨ_L(F) is G_η-invariant. If k(η) is separably closed (in particular if η = s) then G_η = 1. If V is strictly henselian at s and η is the generic point, G_η = Gal(L/K) is the inertia group of K.
hypotheses: G_η acts on RΨ_L(F) through automorphisms of X_η̃ over X; it does not act on X_s (k(s) is separably closed).
proofSteps: Extension of σ to σ̃: universal property of strict henselization (strict-localisation-of-a-valuation-ring (c)).

ρ is a homomorphism because σ ↦ σ̃ is (uniqueness in the universal property); naturality in F is transport of structure for the exact functors j^*, (σ̃_X)_* and the derived functor Rj_* (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/k-injective-and-k-flat-replacements).

Continuity: by the stalk formula for higher direct images along the affine morphism j (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2, request item (G)(a); milnor-tube-stalk-formula cannot be cited because it depends on this node) the stalk is H^q(X_(x̄) ×_S S(η̄), F); writing S(η̄) = lim S(η̄)^{L'} over finite separable L'/k(η) inside L (S(η̄)^{L'} the spectrum of the local finite étale O^h_{S,η}-algebra with residue field L', O^h_{S,η} the henselization; Gal(L/L') acts trivially on it), continuity of étale cohomology for limits of qcqs schemes with affine transition maps (request to AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2) shows every class is fixed by the open subgroup Gal(L/L') for some L'; discrete modules are those with open stabilizers (mathlib:continuousSMul_iff_stabilizer_isOpen; tauceti:TauCeti.IsSmoothDiscrete).
Inertia statement: Gabber–Ramero (6.2.10) for the henselian valuation ring V with separably closed residue field.
acceptance: For V a strictly henselian DVR, π a uniformizer, n prime to p_s and X = Spec V[t]/(t^n − π): G_η = Gal(L/K) acts on R^0Ψ_L(Λ) ≅ Λ^{Hom_K(K(π^{1/n}), L)} by permuting the n embeddings through the quotient Gal(K(π^{1/n})/K) ≅ μ_n, i.e. through the tame character.

nodes.title: Henselian localization: stalks of RΨ_L are cohomology of Milnor tubes
nodes.statement: Let (X, S, η, s) be a quadruple, L a separable closure of k(η), F ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ), and x̄ a geometric point of X_s (with image x ∈ X_s). Let X_(x̄) = Spec O^sh_{X,x̄} be the strict localization of X at x̄. Then X_(x̄) -> S factors through S_(s) = Spec O_{S,s} (which is strictly henselian), X_(x̄) ×_S S(η̄) = X_(x̄) ×_{S_(s)} S(η̄) is an affine scheme (the Milnor tube at (x̄, η̄)), and there is a natural isomorphism (RΨ_L F)_x̄ ≅ RΓ(X_(x̄) ×_S S(η̄), F), in particular (R^qΨ_L F)_x̄ ≅ H^q(X_(x̄) ×_S S(η̄), F), compatible with the Galois actions (σ acting through X_(x̄) ×_S σ̃) and with the base-change maps (nearby-cycles-base-change-map (e)). It is the stalk at the point (x̄, η̄ ⤳ s̄) of Deligne's nearby-cycle complex on the vanishing topos X ×←_S S. No finiteness assumption on f.
hypotheses: j: X_η̃ -> X is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated; this is what the stalk formula for Rj_* needs.
proofSteps: (i^*G)_x̄ = G_x̄ for x̄ viewed as a geometric point of X; geometric points of X_{s,et} and X_et are points of the small étale sites (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.pointSmallEtale), which form a conservative family (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isConservativeFamilyOfPoints_pointSmallEtale').

For the quasi-compact quasi-separated j: (R^q j_* G)_x̄ ≅ H^q(X_(x̄) ×_X X_η̃, G), the stalk formula for higher direct images, proved by writing X_(x̄) as the limit of affine étale neighbourhoods and using continuity (request to SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2:EtaleBaseChange:3-8 for the strict localization of schemes and the formula; request to AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2 for continuity of cohomology along limits of qcqs schemes with affine transition maps).
X_(x̄) ×_X X_η̃ = X_(x̄) ×_S S(η̄); the factorization through S_(s) holds because O_{S,s} -> O^sh_{X,x̄} is local and O_{S,s} is strictly henselian (universal property of strict henselization).
Galois and base-change compatibilities: functoriality of the stalk formula for morphisms of pairs (geometric point, qcqs morphism) (supplier).
acceptance: For X = S: X_(x̄) = S_(s) and the Milnor tube is S(η̄), a strictly local scheme, so (RΨ_L Λ)_s̄ = Λ in degree 0.
For η = s: the Milnor tube is X_(x̄) itself and (RΨ_L F)_x̄ = F_x̄.

nodes.title: The base-change map of nearby cycles for a morphism of quadruples
nodes.statement: Let φ = (g, h, ι): (X', S', η', s', L') -> (X, S, η, s, L) be a morphism of quadruples (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/morphism-of-valuation-quadruples), h̃: S'(η̄') -> S(η̄) its map of strict localizations, g̃ := g ×_h h̃: X'_η̃' -> X_η̃ and g_s: X'_{s'} -> X_s. For F ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ) the base-change map c_φ(F): g_s^* RΨ_L(F) -> RΨ_{L'}(g^* F) is the composite g_s^* i^* Rj_* j^*F ≅ i'^* g^* Rj_* j^*F -> i'^* Rj'_* g̃^* j^*F ≅ i'^* Rj'_* j'^* g^*F, where the middle arrow is i'^* applied to the base-change morphism g^* Rj_* -> Rj'_* g̃^*, adjoint to j'^* g^* Rj_* ≅ g̃^* j^* Rj_* -> g̃^* (counit of j^* ⊣ Rj_*), and the outer isomorphisms are the equalities i ∘ g_s = g ∘ i' and j ∘ g̃ = g ∘ j'. Properties: (a) naturality in F; (b) equivariance: c_φ ∘ g_s^* ρ_F(φ_#(σ')) = ρ'_{g^*F}(σ') ∘ c_φ for σ' ∈ Gal(L'/k(η')) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/galois-action-on-nearby-cycles); (c) c_id = id and c_{φ ∘ ψ} = c_ψ ∘ ψ_s^* c_φ; (d) compatibility with specialization: c_φ ∘ g_s^* sp = sp' (under i'^* g^* ≅ g_s^* i^*); (e) on stalks at a geometric point x̄' of X'_{s'} with image x̄ it is the restriction map RΓ(X_(x̄) ×_S S(η̄), F) -> RΓ(X'_(x̄') ×_{S'} S'(η̄'), g^*F) along X'_(x̄') ×_{S'} S'(η̄') -> X_(x̄) ×_S S(η̄). When c_φ is an isomorphism is the content of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/valuative-base-change-for-nearby-cycles; for non-Cartesian φ it is in general not an isomorphism.
hypotheses: φ arbitrary; no Cartesian, dominance or torsion hypothesis is needed to construct c_φ.
proofSteps: The base-change morphism g^*Rj_* -> Rj'_*g̃^* for a commutative square of schemes is the standard adjunction construction on D^+ (supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2:EtaleBaseChange:3-8 for pullback/pushforward of étale sheaves along arbitrary morphisms; derived functors via EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/k-injective-and-k-flat-replacements).

(b) The square is compatible with σ̃ and σ̃' because h̃ ∘ σ̃' = (φ_#σ')~ ∘ h̃ (uniqueness in the universal property of strict henselization, strict-localisation-of-a-valuation-ring (c)); base-change morphisms are natural for isomorphisms of squares.
(c) Composition of base-change morphisms for pasted squares (supplier).
(e) Stalks via ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/milnor-tube-stalk-formula applied on both sides.
acceptance: For the localization morphism (X ×_S Spec O_{S,s}, Spec O_{S,s}, η, s) -> (X, S, η, s) (Cartesian, dominant) c_φ is an isomorphism (nearby-cycles-equivariant-transport (b)).

nodes.title: Independence of RΨ_L of the choices, up to equivariant transport, and localization at s
nodes.statement: Let (X, S, η, s) be a quadruple. (a) For separable closures L_1, L_2 of k(η) and a k(η)-isomorphism τ: L_1 -> L_2, the morphism of quadruples φ_τ := (id_X, id_S, τ): (X, S, η, s, L_2) -> (X, S, η, s, L_1) has an isomorphism as base-change map, c_τ: RΨ_{L_1}(F) ≅ RΨ_{L_2}(F), natural in F ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ), with c_τ ∘ ρ_1(σ) = ρ_2(τ σ τ^{-1}) ∘ c_τ for σ ∈ Gal(L_1/k(η)); for σ_0 ∈ Gal(L_1/k(η)), c_{τ ∘ σ_0} = c_τ ∘ ρ_1(σ_0). Thus the pair (RΨ_L(F), ρ) is independent of L up to an isomorphism that is unique modulo the Galois action. (b) Localization: for S_(s) := Spec O_{S,s} and X_(s) := X ×_S S_(s), the Cartesian dominant morphism (X_(s), S_(s), η, s, L) -> (X, S, η, s, L) has an isomorphism as base-change map RΨ_L(F) ≅ RΨ_L(F|X_(s)) (the special fibres coincide), compatible with Galois actions; so every statement about RΨ_L may be proved after replacing S by the spectrum of the strictly henselian valuation ring O_{S,s}, in which s is the closed point.
hypotheses: No finiteness or torsion hypothesis.
proofSteps: (a) τ extends uniquely to an S-isomorphism τ̃: S(η̄_2) -> S(η̄_1) (strict-localisation-of-a-valuation-ring (c)); the base-change map of φ_τ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-base-change-map) has X-isomorphism X ×_S τ̃ as its tube map and identity special fibre, so it is the transport of structure along an isomorphism of squares, hence an isomorphism. The intertwining and the dependence on τ are nearby-cycles-base-change-map (b), (c) with φ_{τ∘σ_0} = φ_{σ_0} ∘ φ_τ ((id, id, σ_0) ∘ (id, id, τ) = (id, id, τ ∘ σ_0) by the componentwise rule), so c_{τ∘σ_0} = c_τ ∘ c_{φ_{σ_0}}, and c_{φ_{σ_0}} = ρ_1(σ_0) fixes the convention of ρ.

(b) S(η̄) -> S factors through S_(s) because O_{S,s} -> O_{S,η} -> (O_{S,η})^sh; so j factors as X_η̃ -> X_(s) -> X with u: X_(s) -> X a cofiltered limit of open immersions of quasi-compact opens containing X_s. Then i^* Rj_* = i_(s)^* u^* Ru_* Rj_(s)* and u^* Ru_* ≅ id on D^+ by continuity of étale cohomology along the limit (request to AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2); stalks agree by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/milnor-tube-stalk-formula.
acceptance: For a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring with η generic, any two choices of L give Gal(L/K)-equivariantly isomorphic RΨ_L(F), the isomorphism being unique up to the action of Gal(L/K).

sources.match: The Milnor tube depends only on the strict localization S(t), and may be formed over S or over its strict localization S(s) at s; this is (b), and (a) is the transport along isomorphisms of strict localizations.
The Galois group of the residue field extension acts on the strict henselization; any two identifications differ by it, which is the ambiguity in (a).

nodes.title: Étale locality, proper push-forward and the projective reduction for RΨ_L
nodes.statement: Let (X, S, η, s) be a quadruple and Λ a ring. (a) Étale locality: for an étale morphism u: U -> X, with (U, S, η, s) the induced quadruple, the base-change map of the morphism (u, id_S, id_L) is an isomorphism u_s^* RΨ_L(F) ≅ RΨ_L(u^* F) for all F ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ), compatible with Galois actions. (b) Proper push-forward: if Λ is a torsion ring and h: X -> Y is a proper S-morphism (so (Y, S, η, s) is a quadruple), there is a natural G_η-equivariant isomorphism RΨ_L^Y(Rh_* F) ≅ Rh_{s*} RΨ_L^X(F) for F ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ). (c) Projective reduction: let X be affine of finite type over S, z: X -> A^N_S a closed immersion and w: A^N_S -> P^N_S the standard open immersion, e := w ∘ z. For F ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ) with Λ torsion, RΨ_L^X(F) ≅ z_s^* w_s^* RΨ_L^{P^N}(w_! z_* F) (the restriction to X_s of the nearby cycles of the extension by zero), compatibly with Galois actions and with the base-change maps of Cartesian morphisms of quadruples. Consequently, for a class of pairs (X, F) stable under these operations, constructibility of the R^qΨ_L and bijectivity of the base-change maps for (P^N_S, G) with G ∈ D^+(P^N_{S,et}, Λ) imply the same for (X, F); and every quadruple of finite type is covered by affine opens of finite type to which (a) applies.
hypotheses: (b) and (c) need Λ torsion (proper base change). (a) holds for every Λ.
Extension by zero along w changes RΨ at the boundary P^N_s \ A^N_s; only the restriction to A^N_s is used in (c).
proofSteps: (a) u is étale, hence u^* Rj_* ≅ Rj_{U*} ũ^* (étale base change for qcqs j is the restriction to an étale object; supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2:EtaleBaseChange:3-8), so the base-change map of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-base-change-map is an isomorphism.

(b) j_Y^* Rh_* ≅ Rh_{η̃*} j_X^*: base change along S(η̄) -> S, a cofiltered limit of étale maps, for the qcqs morphism h (continuity, request to AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2, with étale base change); then i_Y^* Rh_* ≅ Rh_{s*} i_X^* by proper base change for torsion coefficients along the arbitrary morphism Spec k(s) -> S (supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2:EtaleBaseChange:3-8). Equivariance by naturality of these base-change isomorphisms.

(c) z is a closed immersion, hence proper, so (b) gives RΨ^{A^N}(z_*F) = z_{s*} RΨ^X(F) and z_s^* z_{s*} = id; (a) for the open immersion w gives w_s^* RΨ^{P^N}(w_! G) = RΨ^{A^N}(w^* w_! G) = RΨ^{A^N}(G). Compatibility with base-change maps: (a), (b) are themselves base-change isomorphisms and base-change maps compose (nearby-cycles-base-change-map (c)).
Finite-type quadruples are locally affine of finite type; closed immersions into affine space exist for affine finite type X (a finite set of generators).
acceptance: For V a strictly henselian DVR and h: X' = Spec V[t]/(t^n − π) -> X = S finite (hence proper), (b) gives RΨ_L(h_* Λ) ≅ h_{s*} RΨ_L(Λ) ≅ Λ^n, consistent with the Kummer computation of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-over-valuation-base.

nodes.title: Radicial invariance: RΨ_L is unchanged by a purely inseparable extension of the valuation base
nodes.statement: Let (X, S, η, s) be a quadruple with S = Spec V, K = Frac V, K'/K a purely inseparable algebraic extension, V' the integral closure of V in K' and S' = Spec V'. Then: (i) V' is a valuation ring, the unique extension of V to K' (the valuation extends uniquely); (ii) h: S' -> S is integral, universally injective and surjective (a universal homeomorphism), so there are unique η', s' ∈ S' over η, s, η' ⤳ s', and O_{S',s'} is strictly henselian (its residue field is purely inseparable over the separably closed k(s)); (iii) with L' := the separable closure of k(η') in an algebraic closure containing L, restriction Gal(L'/k(η')) -> Gal(L/k(η)) is an isomorphism, ι: L -> L' the inclusion, and the Cartesian dominant morphism φ: (X', S', η', s', L') -> (X, S, η, s, L), X' = X ×_S S', has maps g: X' -> X, g_s: X'_{s'} -> X_s, g̃: X'_η̃' -> X_η̃ that are universal homeomorphisms; (iv) the base-change map c_φ(F): g_s^* RΨ_L(F) -> RΨ_{L'}(g^* F) is an isomorphism for every F ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ) and every ring Λ, equivariant along the isomorphism of Galois groups, and g^*, g_s^* are equivalences of étale sites. Consequently, in positive characteristic RΨ_L may be computed after replacing V by its integral closure in the perfect closure of K.
hypotheses: No torsion hypothesis: topological invariance holds for all sheaves.
proofSteps: (i) Gabber–Ramero Example 6.1.4(ii): the extension of a valuation to a purely inseparable algebraic extension is unique; its valuation ring is the integral closure of V (standard: integral closure of V in K' is the intersection of the valuation rings above V).

(ii) K'/K purely inseparable makes V -> V' integral with purely inseparable residue extensions and radicial (universally injective); surjective by lying over. Strict henselianity of O_{S',s'}: integral over the henselian O_{S,s}, local, with separably closed residue field.

(iii) S(η̄) ×_S S' -> S(η̄) is again integral, universally injective, surjective, and (S(η̄) ×_S S')_red is the strict localization S'(η̄') (universal property: it is strictly henselian local and ind-étale over O_{S',η'} after reduction); base change of universal homeomorphisms along X -> S, X_s -> s, X_η̃ -> S(η̄).

(iv) Topological invariance of the small étale site (Stacks, Theorem 04DZ): a universal homeomorphism induces an equivalence of small étale sites (supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2:EtaleBaseChange:3-8); under these equivalences i^*, Rj_*, j^* correspond, so c_φ is an isomorphism (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-base-change-map (e) on stalks).
acceptance: For V = 𝔽_p[[t]]^sh (a strictly henselian DVR of characteristic p) and K' = K(t^{1/p}), V' = V[t^{1/p}]: nearby cycles of X ×_V V' over V' equal those of X over V.

sources.match: Topological invariance of the small étale site, used in (iv).
The hypotheses verified in (ii)–(iii).
Uniqueness of the extended valuation in (i).

nodes.title: RΨ_L commutes with filtered colimits; reduction to constructible coefficients
nodes.statement: Let (X, S, η, s) be a quadruple with f quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and (F_a) a filtered system of sheaves of Λ-modules on X_et. Then for every q the natural map colim_a R^qΨ_L(F_a) -> R^qΨ_L(colim_a F_a) is an isomorphism, compatibly with Galois actions and with base-change maps of morphisms of quadruples. If moreover n ∈ ℤ_{≥1} and X is of finite presentation over S, every sheaf of ℤ/n-modules on X_et is the filtered colimit of its constructible subsheaves, and a sheaf of abelian groups whose local sections are killed by integers prime to p_s is the filtered colimit of its n-torsion subsheaves over n prime to p_s. Hence a statement 'c_φ(F) is an isomorphism for all F' (or 'R^qΨ_L(F) vanishes for q > m') holds for all torsion F prime to p_s once it holds for constructible sheaves of ℤ/n-modules with n prime to p_s, and extends from sheaves to D^+ by truncation (R^qΨ_L(F) depends only on τ_{≤q} F).
hypotheses: The Milnor tubes X_(x̄) ×_S S(η̄) are affine for every f (milnor-tube-stalk-formula); f qcqs makes X qcqs for the colimit presentation; the colimit reduction to constructible sheaves uses f of finite presentation (constructible = finitely presented sheaves on a qcqs scheme).
proofSteps: By ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/milnor-tube-stalk-formula the stalks are H^q of the affine (hence qcqs) Milnor tubes X_(x̄) ×_S S(η̄); étale cohomology of a qcqs scheme commutes with filtered colimits of sheaves (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites, applied to the small étale site, whose qcqs objects generate); stalks detect isomorphisms (conservative family of points).
Every sheaf of ℤ/n-modules on a qcqs scheme is the filtered colimit of constructible (finitely presented) subsheaves (supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2:ConstructibleEtale:7-9, SGA 4 IX 2.7).

Truncation: RΨ_L is a right derived functor of a left exact functor, so RΨ_L(τ_{>q}F) ∈ D^{>q}, whence H^q(RΨ_L F) = H^q(RΨ_L τ_{≤q+1}F) and bounded complexes are handled by induction on length with the five lemma.
acceptance: The constant sheaf ℤ/ℓ^∞ := colim_m ℤ/ℓ^m (ℓ ≠ p_s) has R^qΨ_L(ℤ/ℓ^∞) = colim_m R^qΨ_L(ℤ/ℓ^m).

sources.match: The colimit presentation used to reduce to constructible coefficients (stated there on the vanishing topos; the same statement on X_et is the supplier's).
The SGA 4 IX 2.7 generators j_!Λ behind the colimit presentation.

nodes.title: Comparison with the geometric generic point: Milnor tube versus Milnor fibre
nodes.statement: Let (X, S, η, s) be a quadruple of finite type, L a separable closure of k(η), η̄ = Spec L the closed point of S(η̄), k: X_η̄ = X ×_S η̄ -> X_η̃ the closed fibre of X_η̃ -> S(η̄), n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k(s) and Λ a ring with nΛ = 0. Then for every F ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ) the natural map RΨ_L(F) = i^* Rj_* j^* F -> i^* R(jk)_*(jk)^* F = RΨ_L^geo(F) (induced by the unit id -> Rk_* k^*) is a Gal(L/k(η))-equivariant isomorphism. Equivalently, for every geometric point x̄ of X_s, restriction from the Milnor tube to the Milnor fibre RΓ(X_(x̄) ×_S S(η̄), F) -> RΓ(X_(x̄) ×_S η̄, F) is an isomorphism. If η is the generic point of S then k = id; if η = s both sides are F_x̄. Nothing is asserted when p_s divides n.
hypotheses: f locally of finite type; n invertible in k(s) (hence in O_{S,s} and in every k(t) for t between η and s).
The comparison is needed only when η is neither the generic point nor s, i.e. when V_{𝔭_s} has rank ≥ 2.

nodes.title: Cohomological amplitude of RΨ_L: vanishing above twice the generic-fibre dimension
nodes.statement: Let (X, S, η, s) be a quadruple with f of finite type, N := dim X_η (the dimension of the fibre over η; RΨ_L = 0 if X_η = ∅), and n ≥ 1 invertible in k(s). Then R^qΨ_L(F) = 0 for every q > 2N and every sheaf F of ℤ/n-modules on X_et (and every sheaf of Λ-modules for a ring Λ with nΛ = 0); consequently RΨ_L maps D^b(X_et, Λ) to D^b(X_{s,et}, Λ), sending D^{[a,b]} into D^{[a, b+2N]}.
hypotheses: n invertible in k(s): the proof goes through the tube-versus-fibre comparison, which is only asserted for prime-to-p_s torsion.
proofSteps: Reduce to X affine (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-locality-and-proper-pushforward (a)) and to F constructible (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-commute-with-filtered-colimits; X affine of finite type is closed in A^M_S of finite presentation, and z_* is exact).
By ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/comparison-with-geometric-generic-point the stalk at x̄ is RΓ(X_(x̄) ×_S η̄, F), the cohomology of the Milnor fibre.

X_(x̄) ×_S η̄ is the cofiltered limit, along affine transition maps, of U ×_S η̄ over affine étale neighbourhoods U of x̄; each U ×_S η̄ is of finite type over the separably closed field L with dimension ≤ N, so has étale cohomological dimension ≤ 2N (supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2:ConstructibleEtale:7-9); continuity (request to AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2) gives H^q = 0 for q > 2N.
Λ-modules: restriction of scalars to ℤ/n commutes with RΨ_L (nearby-cycles-over-valuation-base).
acceptance: For X = A^1_S, N = 1 and R^qΨ_L(ℤ/n) = 0 for q ≥ 3; in fact for X smooth over a strictly henselian DVR, RΨ_L(ℤ/n) = ℤ/n in degree 0 (LPV.0, local acyclicity of smooth morphisms).

nodes.title: Wild inertia is the pro-p Sylow subgroup; the tame quotient is Hom(Γ ⊗ ℤ_(p)/Γ, μ_(p))
nodes.statement: Let K be a field with a henselian valuation ring V whose residue field κ is separably closed, p the characteristic exponent of κ, Γ the value group, K^s a separable closure and G_K = Gal(K^s/K) (which equals the inertia group, mathlib:ValuationSubring.inertiaSubgroup of the unique extension of V to K^s, by Gabber–Ramero (6.2.10)). Let K^t ⊆ K^s be the maximal tame extension, the union of the finite Galois extensions E/K in K^s with [E : K] prime to p. Then: (i) there is a natural isomorphism of profinite groups Gal(K^t/K) ≅ Hom_ℤ(Γ ⊗_ℤ ℤ_(p)/Γ, μ_(p)), where ℤ_(p) is ℤ localized at p (denominators prime to p) and μ_(p) is the group of roots of unity of order prime to p in K; in particular Gal(K^t/K) is abelian and its supernatural order is prime to p; (ii) for every finite Galois E/K in K^s the map Gal(E/K) -> Hom_ℤ(Γ_E/Γ, μ(κ)), σ ↦ (γ ↦ σ(x)/x mod 𝔪_E for |x| = γ), is surjective with kernel a p-group, and E ∩ K^t is the fixed field of that kernel; (iii) hence P := Gal(K^s/K^t) is a closed normal pro-p subgroup of G_K of index prime to p, i.e. the unique p-Sylow subgroup of G_K (the wild inertia subgroup). For p = 1 (κ of characteristic 0), P = 1 and G_K ≅ Hom(Γ ⊗ ℚ/Γ, μ). This is the valuation-theoretic pro-p Sylow/tame comparison in the form used by this stage.
hypotheses: V henselian with separably closed residue field (e.g. V strictly henselian, or the strict henselization of any valuation ring, strict-localisation-of-a-valuation-ring); Γ arbitrary (any rank, not necessarily discrete or finitely generated).
proofSteps: (ii) Gabber–Ramero Proposition 6.2.12 (under (6.2.10)): the pairing map (6.2.11) is surjective with p-group kernel H_E. Since μ(κ) has no p-torsion, the image is abelian of order prime to p, so E^{H_E} ⊆ K^t; conversely Gal((E ∩ K^t)/K) has order prime to p, so the p-group H_E acts trivially on E ∩ K^t; thus E^{H_E} = E ∩ K^t.
(i) Gabber–Ramero Definition 6.2.16 and (6.2.17) (here K^sh = K because V is henselian with separably closed residue field).

(iii) P = lim_E H_E is pro-p; [G_K : P] = |Gal(K^t/K)| is prime to p by (i); a normal closed pro-p subgroup of index prime to p is the unique p-Sylow subgroup (tauceti:TauCeti.isProPSylow_iff_isClosed_and_isProP_and_not_dvd_profiniteIndex and uniqueness of a normal Sylow pro-p subgroup, tauceti:TauCeti.IsProPSylow.eq_of_normal; pro-p is tauceti:TauCeti.IsProP; for p = 1 the claim P = 1 is direct).
acceptance: V a strictly henselian DVR (Γ = ℤ): Gal(K^t/K) ≅ ∏_{ℓ ≠ p} ℤ_ℓ(1), the classical tame inertia of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.1.

V strictly henselian of rank one with value group ℤ_(p) ⊂ ℚ (for example the valuation ring of the maximal tamely ramified extension of the maximal unramified extension of ℚ_p): Γ ⊗ ℤ_(p) = Γ, so Gal(K^t/K) = 1 and G_K = P is pro-p (a nondiscrete rank-one regression case).
V strictly henselian with Γ = ℤ × ℤ (lexicographic): Gal(K^t/K) ≅ ∏_{ℓ ≠ p} ℤ_ℓ(1)^2 (a higher-rank regression case).

nodes.title: Prime-to-p Galois cohomology is computed on the tame quotient
nodes.statement: In the situation of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/tame-quotient-of-a-henselian-valued-field let P ⊆ G_K be the wild inertia subgroup and M a discrete G_K-module each of whose elements is killed by an integer prime to p. Then (i) H^q(P, M) = 0 for all q > 0; (ii) the inflation maps H^n(G_K/P, M^P) -> H^n(G_K, M) are isomorphisms for all n ≥ 0, with G_K/P = Gal(K^t/K); (iii) consequently cd_ℓ(G_K) = cd_ℓ(Gal(K^t/K)) for every prime ℓ ≠ p. The same holds for any closed normal pro-p subgroup P of a profinite group G in place of the wild inertia.
hypotheses: M discrete (open stabilizers) and prime-to-p torsion; no finiteness of M.
proofSteps: (i) H^q(P, M) = colim_U H^q(P/(P ∩ U), M^{P∩U}) over open normal U (finite-quotient colimit description, tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteCohomology#layer-10-continuous-cohomology-in-all-degrees); each P/(P ∩ U) is a finite p-group and multiplication by its order is invertible on M, so its positive-degree cohomology vanishes (restriction–corestriction, ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.2/finite-index-descent (i)–(ii) with U = 1).

(ii) The Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence E_2^{a,b} = H^a(G_K/P, H^b(P, M)) ⇒ H^{a+b}(G_K, M) for the closed normal subgroup P and discrete M, with edge map inflation (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.2/hochschild-serre-spectral-sequence, stated for discrete modules on mathlib:continuousCohomology; the collapse is ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.2/hochschild-serre-degeneration (i)); by (i) it is concentrated on b = 0.
(iii) From (ii) applied to ℓ-primary M.
acceptance: V a strictly henselian DVR, M = ℤ/n with n prime to p and trivial action: H^1(G_K, ℤ/n) ≅ Hom(∏_{ℓ≠p} ℤ_ℓ(1), ℤ/n) ≅ ℤ/n(−1), H^q = 0 for q ≥ 2 (cd_ℓ ℤ_ℓ = 1).
Value group ℤ_(p): G_K is pro-p and H^q(G_K, M) = 0 for q > 0 and every prime-to-p torsion M.

nodes.title: The Gauss valuation ring V(T) of a valuation ring
nodes.statement: Let V be a valuation ring with fraction field K, residue field κ, maximal ideal 𝔪 and valuation |·|: K -> Γ ∪ {0} (multiplicative notation; mathlib:ValuationRing.valuation). The Gauss valuation (centre 0, radius 1) on K[T] is |a_0 + a_1 T + … + a_m T^m|_G := max_i |a_i|; it is multiplicative (Gauss's lemma) and extends uniquely to a valuation |·|_G: K(T) -> Γ ∪ {0} with the same value group Γ. Its valuation ring is V(T) := {h ∈ K(T) : |h|_G ≤ 1}. Properties: (a) V(T) = V[T]_{𝔪V[T]}, the localization of V[T] at the prime 𝔪V[T]; equivalently V(T) is the local ring of A^1_V at the generic point of the special fibre A^1_κ; (b) V(T) ∩ K = V and V(T) dominates V; (c) the residue field of V(T) is κ(T), purely transcendental over κ; (d) the value group of V(T) equals Γ (in particular V(T) has the same rank as V, and is not discrete if V is not); (e) iterating (or directly: |Σ a_α T^α|_G = max |a_α|) gives the Gauss valuation ring V(T_1, …, T_d) = V[T_1, …, T_d]_{𝔪V[T_1,…,T_d]}, the local ring of A^d_V at the generic point of A^d_κ, with residue field κ(T_1, …, T_d) and value group Γ. For a quadruple with base V, the strict henselization of V(T_1, …, T_d) (strict-localisation-of-a-valuation-ring) is a strictly henselian valuation ring with value group Γ: the 'Gauss valuation base' used for induction on the dimension of the generic fibre.
hypotheses: V arbitrary valuation ring (the trivial valuation V = K is allowed and gives the trivial valuation on K(T)).
proofSteps: Multiplicativity on K[T]: choose c_f, c_g coefficients of maximal absolute value; f/c_f and g/c_g lie in V[T] with nonzero reduction in κ[T], a domain, so (fg)/(c_f c_g) has nonzero reduction, i.e. |fg|_G = |f|_G |g|_G; the ultrametric inequality is coefficientwise. Extension to K(T) by |f/g| := |f|/|g|.
(a) If |f| ≤ |g| write g = c g' with |g'|_G = 1 and f = c f'' with f'' ∈ V[T]; then f/g = f''/g' with g' ∉ 𝔪V[T]; the converse inclusion is clear. 𝔪V[T] is prime because V[T]/𝔪V[T] = κ[T].
(b), (c), (d) are read off from (a) and the formula: constants have |a|_G = |a|, and V[T]_{𝔪V[T]}/𝔪 = κ[T]_{(0)} = κ(T).
(e) Same argument with multi-indices (Gabber–Ramero Example 6.1.4(iv)).
Compatibility with the rank-one real case: mathlib:Polynomial.gaussNorm with c = 1 and its multiplicativity mathlib:Polynomial.gaussNorm_mul.
acceptance: For V = ℤ_p: |1 + pT|_G = 1, |p T^2|_G = |p|, and V(T) = ℤ_p[T]_{(p)} has residue field 𝔽_p(T), a purely transcendental extension of the residue field of V (Gauss's lemma).
The value group of |·|_G on K(T) equals that of V: the Gauss valuation is residually transcendental, not value-transcendental.

nodes.title: Along a strictly henselized Gauss extension the tame quotients agree
nodes.statement: Let V be a strictly henselian valuation ring with fraction field K, value group Γ and residue characteristic exponent p; let W be the strict henselization of the Gauss valuation ring V(T_1, …, T_d) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/gauss-valuation) at a separable closure of κ(T_1, …, T_d), E := Frac W, and choose a separable closure E^s of E containing a separable closure K^s of K. Then (i) W is a strictly henselian valuation ring with value group Γ; (ii) the maximal tame extension of E is E^t = E · K^t; (iii) restriction Gal(E^t/E) -> Gal(K^t/K) is an isomorphism, compatible with the identifications of both sides with Hom(Γ ⊗ ℤ_(p)/Γ, μ_(p)) of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/tame-quotient-of-a-henselian-valued-field; (iv) consequently, for every discrete G_K-module M of prime-to-p torsion on which the wild inertia P_K acts trivially (a tame module), restriction H^n(G_K, M) -> H^n(G_E, M) is an isomorphism for all n. The statement concerns only the tame quotients; it makes no claim that Gal(E^s/E) -> Gal(K^s/K) is surjective on wild inertia, and without that surjectivity (iv) fails for modules on which P_K acts nontrivially (M^{P_E} can be larger than M^{P_K}).
hypotheses: V strictly henselian; d ≥ 0 (d = 0 gives W = V).
proofSteps: (i) ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/strict-localisation-of-a-valuation-ring (a) and gauss-valuation (d).

(ii) E is transcendental over K, so Gabber–Ramero (6.2.18) (for separable algebraic E ⊆ K^s) does not apply as stated; argue as in its proof: by Gabber–Ramero Corollary 6.2.14 every finite tame Galois extension of the strictly henselian field E is generated by m-th roots (m prime to p) of elements a ∈ E^×; by (i) a = c·u with c ∈ K^×, |c| = |a| and u ∈ W^× an m-th power (W strictly henselian), so E(a^{1/m}) = E(c^{1/m}) ⊆ E · K^t.

(iii) Injectivity of restriction from (ii). The pairing (6.2.9) is natural in the field: for σ ∈ Gal(E^t/E) and x ∈ K^t with |x| = γ, σ(x)/x mod 𝔪 is the same computed in E^t or in K^t; by (i) both tame groups are Hom(Γ ⊗ ℤ_(p)/Γ, μ_(p)) with the same Γ and the same μ_(p) (all prime-to-p roots of unity lie in K), and restriction is the identity on this description, hence bijective (tame-quotient-of-a-henselian-valued-field (i)).

(iv) The image of P_E = Gal(E^s/E^t) in G_K fixes K^t ⊆ E^t, so lies in P_K and acts trivially on M; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/prime-to-p-cohomology-through-tame-quotient (ii) for K and for E identifies both sides with the cohomology of the tame quotients, which (iii) identifies.
acceptance: V a strictly henselian DVR and d = 1: W is the strict henselization of the DVR V[T]_{(π)}, a strictly henselian DVR with the same uniformizer π, and both tame quotients are ∏_{ℓ≠p} ℤ_ℓ(1) generated by the action on π^{1/n}.
