nodes.title: Cartesian change of valuation base: the base-change map of nearby cycles is an isomorphism for prime-to-p torsion
nodes.statement: Let φ = (g, h, ι): (X', S', η', s', L') -> (X, S, η, s, L) be a Cartesian and dominant morphism of quadruples (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/morphism-of-valuation-quadruples): X' = X ×_S S', and the local homomorphism O_{S,s} -> O_{S',s'} of valuation rings is injective. Assume f: X -> S locally of finite type and let n ≥ 1 be invertible in k(s) (equivalently prime to the residue characteristic exponent p_s). Then for every ring Λ with nΛ = 0 and every F ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ), the base-change map c_φ(F): g_s^* RΨ_L(F) -> RΨ_{L'}(g^* F) of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-base-change-map is an isomorphism, equivariant along φ_#: Gal(L'/k(η')) -> Gal(L/k(η)). In particular, for every torsion abelian sheaf F on X_et whose local sections are killed by integers prime to p_s, g_s^* R^qΨ_L(F) ≅ R^qΨ_{L'}(g^* F) for all q. No constructibility or finiteness of F is assumed. Nothing is asserted for torsion divisible by p_s, for non-Cartesian φ, or for non-dominant h.
hypotheses: φ Cartesian: X' = X ×_S S' (for non-Cartesian φ the map is not an isomorphism in general, nearby-cycles-base-change-map test nearbyCyclesBaseChange_not_iso_nonCartesian).
φ dominant: O_{S,s} -> O_{S',s'} injective; this is the case of valuative bases dominating S covered by Hub96's argument as described by Orgogozo, Remarque 4.4.
n invertible in k(s); Λ an arbitrary ℤ/n-algebra; f locally of finite type; F ∈ D^+ arbitrary.
proofSteps: Localize both bases at s and s' (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-equivariant-transport (b)); the localized morphism is still Cartesian and dominant.

In positive characteristic replace V and V' by their integral closures in the perfect closures of their fraction fields (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/radicial-invariance-of-nearby-cycles, applied over S and over S', with the base-change maps composing by nearby-cycles-base-change-map (c)).

Reduce to F a constructible sheaf of ℤ/n-modules (nearby-cycles-commute-with-filtered-colimits, restriction of scalars and truncation), to X affine of finite type (nearby-cycles-locality-and-proper-pushforward (a)), and then to (P^N_S, w_! z_* F) (nearby-cycles-locality-and-proper-pushforward (c)); all reductions are compatible with c_φ.

On stalks (nearby-cycles-base-change-map (e) and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/comparison-with-geometric-generic-point on both sides) the claim is that restriction RΓ(X_(x̄) ×_S η̄, F) -> RΓ(X'_(x̄') ×_{S'} η̄', F) of Milnor-fibre cohomology is an isomorphism.

Prime-to-p torsion only sees tame quotients: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/tame-quotient-of-a-henselian-valued-field and prime-to-p-cohomology-through-tame-quotient (Hochschild–Serre, ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.2/hochschild-serre-spectral-sequence); along Gauss valuation bases the tame quotients agree (gauss-extension-tame-inertia-comparison).

Induction on N = dim X_η, fibring P^N over P^{N-1} and passing to the strictly henselized Gauss valuation rings at the generic points of special fibres (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/gauss-valuation): gap: Hub96 induction on generic-fibre dimension via Gauss valuations; the wild part of the comparison of Galois groups along these extensions: gap: Hub96 4.2.10 Galois-surjectivity/defectless calculation.
Conclusion from the induction and the reductions; injectivity of c_φ on each R^qΨ is part of the same argument (Orgogozo, Remarque 4.4).
acceptance: Traits: for strictly henselian discrete valuation rings V -> V' (dominant) this is the commutation of nearby cycles with dominant changes of traits (Deligne, SGA 4½ Th. finitude, recalled by Illusie §1.1(b)).

Nondiscrete rank one: V a strictly henselian DVR and V' = O_C for C the completion of an algebraic closure of K (O_C is henselian with residue field the algebraic closure of k(s), purely inseparable over k(s), so a quadruple with η' generic); the theorem identifies nearby cycles of X_{O_C} over O_C with g_s^* RΨ_L(F), forgetting the Galois action (Gal(L'/k(η')) is trivial).
η = s (and η' = s'): c_φ(F) is the identity-type isomorphism g_s^* i^* F ≅ i'^* g^* F.
Regression (no claim): for p_s | n the theorem says nothing; for a morphism that is not dominant, such as Spec(V/𝔮) -> Spec V for a nonzero prime 𝔮 ⊆ 𝔭_η, the theorem says nothing.

nodes.title: From ℤ/n to noetherian coefficient rings annihilated by n
nodes.statement: Let (X, S, η, s) be a quadruple with X affine of finite presentation over S and n ≥ 1 invertible in k(s). Assume that (i) for every constructible sheaf G of ℤ/n-modules on X_et, RΨ_L(G) ∈ D^b_c(X_{s,et}, ℤ/n), and (ii) R^qΨ_L vanishes for q > m on sheaves of ℤ/n-modules (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-cohomological-amplitude, m = 2 dim X_η). Then for every noetherian ring B with nB = 0 and every constructible sheaf F of B-modules on X_et, RΨ_L(F) ∈ D^b_c(X_{s,et}, B); in particular each R^qΨ_L(F) is a constructible sheaf of B-modules.
hypotheses: X affine of finite presentation (the general case follows by locality, nearby-cycles-locality-and-proper-pushforward).
B noetherian: constructible sheaves of B-modules then form an abelian category stable under kernels and extensions.
proofSteps: RΨ_L commutes with restriction of scalars along ℤ/n -> B (nearby-cycles-over-valuation-base).

For U -> X étale quasi-compact, j_{U!}(ℤ/n) is flat, and RΨ_L preserves finite Tor-dimension (Orgogozo 6.3, via SGA 4 XVII 5.2.11), so by (i) RΨ_L(j_{U!} ℤ/n) ∈ D^b_{ctf}(X_s, ℤ/n) (supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2:ConstructibleEtale:7-9).

Projection formula for constant coefficients: RΨ_L(j_{U!}ℤ/n ⊗ M) ≅ RΨ_L(j_{U!}ℤ/n) ⊗^L_{ℤ/n} M for every ℤ/n-module M, first for finite free M, then for all M by filtered colimits (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-commute-with-filtered-colimits) and the amplitude bound (ii) (derived tensor product: EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/presentability-and-derived-tensor). For M = B: RΨ_L(j_{U!}B) ∈ D^b_c(X_s, B), because a D^b_{ctf} constructible ℤ/n-complex tensored with B has constructible B-module cohomology (B noetherian; supplier).

F is a quotient of a finite sum of sheaves j_{U!}B and the kernel is again constructible (generators j_!B of SGA 4 IX 2.7 and noetherianity of B; supplier), giving a resolution … -> P_1 -> P_0 -> F by finite sums of j_{U!}B. By (ii), H^q(RΨ_L F) is determined by the stupid truncation of the resolution in degrees ≥ −(q + m + 1), a bounded complex of objects with RΨ_L in D^b_c; triangles and the thickness of constructible sheaves give constructibility.
acceptance: B = 𝔽_ℓ[t] (ℓ ≠ p_s), X = S, F = B: RΨ_L(B) = B, a constructible B-module although not a finite abelian group.

sources.match: Preservation of finite Tor-dimension by nearby cycles, used for the projection formula with coefficients B.
The generators j_!Λ of the constructible Λ-modules used for the resolution.
Noetherianity of constructible sheaves, which keeps kernels constructible.

nodes.title: Constructibility of R^qΨ_L over a valuation base
nodes.statement: Let (X, S, η, s) be a quadruple with f: X -> S locally of finite type, B a noetherian ring with nB = 0 for an integer n invertible in k(s), and F a constructible sheaf of B-modules on X_et (each quasi-compact open of X has a finite partition into constructible locally closed subschemes on each of which F is locally constant with finitely generated stalks). Then for every q the sheaf R^qΨ_L(F) on X_{s,et} is a constructible sheaf of B-modules (X_s is locally of finite type over the field k(s)), R^qΨ_L(F) = 0 for q > 2 dim X_η, and for X quasi-compact RΨ_L(F) ∈ D^b_c(X_{s,et}, B); the action of Gal(L/k(η)) on each R^qΨ_L(F) is continuous. Nothing is asserted when p_s divides n, and the statement is not deduced from the trait case by writing V as a limit of discrete valuation rings.
hypotheses: f locally of finite type (not necessarily of finite presentation; X need not be noetherian).
B noetherian with nB = 0 and n invertible in k(s); B may be infinite (for example 𝔽_ℓ[t]).
proofSteps: Localize at s, pass to perfect closures in positive characteristic, and restrict to affine opens (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/nearby-cycles-equivariant-transport (b), radicial-invariance-of-nearby-cycles, nearby-cycles-locality-and-proper-pushforward (a)); for X affine of finite type use the closed immersion into A^M_S and the extension by zero to P^M_S (nearby-cycles-locality-and-proper-pushforward (c)); constructibility is preserved by z_s^* w_s^* and by z_*, w_!.

Reduce the coefficients to B = ℤ/n (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/noetherian-coefficient-change-for-constructibility), using the amplitude bound nearby-cycles-cohomological-amplitude.

Tame reduction and induction on dim X_η via Gauss valuation bases, as in valuative-base-change-for-nearby-cycles: tame-quotient-of-a-henselian-valued-field, prime-to-p-cohomology-through-tame-quotient, gauss-valuation, gauss-extension-tame-inertia-comparison; gap: Hub96 induction on generic-fibre dimension via Gauss valuations; gap: Hub96 4.2.10 Galois-surjectivity/defectless calculation.

Relative curve case: construct a constructible subsheaf of R^qΨ_L(F) equal to it off finitely many closed points of X_s, and finish at those points by proper base change and finiteness of the cohomology of proper curves over k(s) (supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2:ConstructibleEtale:7-9, proper base change from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2:EtaleBaseChange:3-8): gap: Hub96 4.2.5 controlling constructible submodule (pp. 249–250).
Continuity of the Galois action: galois-action-on-nearby-cycles.
acceptance: Traits: for a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring this is Deligne's constructibility theorem (SGA 4½ Th. finitude 3.2, recalled by Illusie §1.1(b)).
X = S: RΨ_L(B) = B in degree 0.
Kummer example (V a strictly henselian DVR, X = Spec V[t]/(t^n − π), n prime to p_s): R^0Ψ_L(B) ≅ B^n, constructible (a skyscraper at the unique point of X_s).

Higher rank (regression): V strictly henselian with value group ℤ × ℤ (lexicographic). V is not a directed union of discrete valuation rings along injective local homomorphisms, since a directed union of archimedean ordered groups along order embeddings is archimedean; the theorem applies to V directly.
p-torsion (regression, no claim): for V of mixed characteristic (0, p) and B = ℤ/p the theorem asserts nothing.

sources.match: Constructibility of nearby cycles over a general base after modification; over a valuative base the modification has a section (Remarque 4.4), which gives the public restatement of the node for B = ℤ/n and f of finite presentation.
Public statement that Hub96 §4.2's results on nearby cycles over valuative bases include the base-change and constructibility theorems.
Illusie's Theorem 3.2, to which this remark applies, contains both constructibility and base change; the remark attributes the valuative case to Huber (the stage places constructibility in 4.2.5).
The trait case of the constructibility and base-change theorems (same sentence).

nodes.title: Surjective maps of valuation spectra
nodes.statement: Let A and B be valuation rings (integral domains whose ideals are totally ordered by inclusion; every rank is allowed, including rank 0, i.e. fields) and let φ: A → B be a ring homomorphism. φ is a surjective map of valuation spectra if Spec(φ): Spec B → Spec A, the map p ↦ φ^{-1}(p) on prime spectra, is surjective. For valuation rings the following are equivalent: (i) Spec(φ) is surjective; (ii) φ is injective and local, i.e. φ^{-1}(m_B) = m_A; (iii) B is a faithfully flat A-module through φ. In this case Spec(φ) maps the generic point to the generic point and the closed point to the closed point. The predicate involves no topology. For microbial valuation rings (A has a prime p_A of height one, B has p_B) with their valuation topologies, φ is continuous if and only if φ(p_A) ⊆ p_B, and a continuous surjective map of valuation spectra satisfies φ^{-1}(p_B) = p_A. For an extension C_3 ⊆ C_1 of algebraically closed nonarchimedean fields with open and bounded valuation subrings C_3^+ ⊆ C_1^+, the induced map Spa(C_1, C_1^+) → Spa(C_3, C_3^+) is surjective if and only if C_3^+ → C_1^+ is a surjective map of valuation spectra, if and only if C_1^+ ∩ C_3 = C_3^+.
hypotheses: A and B are valuation rings (integral domains with totally ordered ideals), of arbitrary rank
φ: A → B is a ring homomorphism
for the continuity clause: A and B are microbial and carry their valuation topologies
for the Spa clause: C_3 ⊆ C_1 is a continuous extension of algebraically closed nonarchimedean fields and C_i^+ ⊆ C_i are open and bounded valuation subrings with C_3^+ ⊆ C_1^+
proofSteps: (i) ⇒ (ii): locality is mathlib:IsLocalHom.of_comap_surjective; for injectivity, the zero ideal of A equals φ^{-1}(q) for some prime q of B, so ker φ ⊆ φ^{-1}(q) = 0.

(ii) ⇒ (iii): B is a domain and φ is injective, so B is a torsion-free A-module; a valuation ring is a Bézout domain (mathlib:ValuationRing.iff_local_bezout_domain), so B is flat over A (mathlib:Module.Flat.flat_iff_torsion_eq_bot_of_isBezout); a flat local homomorphism of local rings is faithfully flat (mathlib:Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom).
(iii) ⇒ (i): mathlib:PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat.
Generic and closed points: φ^{-1}(0) = 0 by injectivity and φ^{-1}(m_B) = m_A by locality.

Continuity: in a microbial valuation ring the valuation topology is the a-adic topology for any nonzero a ∈ p_A, and rad(aA) = p_A, so the topologically nilpotent elements are exactly p_A; hence φ is continuous iff φ(p_A) ⊆ p_B. If moreover Spec(φ) is surjective, choose q with φ^{-1}(q) = p_A; were φ^{-1}(p_B) ⊋ p_A, then q ⊊ p_B (primes of a valuation ring form a chain and contraction preserves order), forcing q = 0 and p_A = 0, a contradiction.

Spa clause: the points of Spa(C, C^+) are the valuation rings C^+_q for the nonzero primes q of C^+ (the continuous valuations of C bounded by C^+), with the closed point given by m_{C^+} (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/geometric-stalks-at-field-pairs); the map induced by C_3^+ → C_1^+ sends nonzero primes to nonzero primes (continuity) and 0 to 0 (injectivity), so surjectivity on Spa is (i). Finally C_1^+ ∩ C_3 is a valuation ring of C_3 containing C_3^+, whose maximal ideal is m_{C_1^+} ∩ C_3; it equals C_3^+ iff the inclusion is local, since a valuation ring is maximal for domination among local subrings of its fraction field.
acceptance: For an extension C ⊆ C' of complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean fields, O_C → O_{C'} is a surjective map of valuation spectra (rank one, nondiscrete).

For a rank-two open bounded valuation subring C^+ ⊊ O_C, the inclusion C^+ → O_C is injective and not local: Spec O_C → Spec C^+ misses the closed point, and Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C, C^+) is not surjective.
Any homomorphism of fields K → L (valuation rings of rank 0, η = s) is a surjective map of valuation spectra.

nodes.title: A valuation ring with algebraically closed fraction field is strictly henselian
nodes.statement: Let V be a valuation ring whose fraction field K is algebraically closed. Then V is absolutely integrally closed (every monic polynomial over V is a product of linear factors over V), and V is a strictly henselian local ring: it is henselian and its residue field is algebraically closed. In particular, for an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field C and an open and bounded valuation subring C^+ ⊆ C (for instance C^+ = O_C, or a rank-two C^+ ⊊ O_C), Spec C^+ with its generic point η = Spec C and closed point s is the base of a quadruple (X, Spec C^+, η, s) of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles for every C^+-scheme X, and the strict localisation of Spec C^+ at η is η itself.
hypotheses: V is a valuation ring
the fraction field K of V is algebraically closed
proofSteps: A valuation ring is a normal domain (integrally closed in its fraction field).
A normal domain with algebraically closed fraction field is absolutely integrally closed (Stacks Tag 0DCQ).
The localisation of an absolutely integrally closed ring at a prime is strictly henselian (Stacks Tag 0DCS); apply it at the maximal ideal of V.

For C^+: an open and bounded valuation subring of C is a valuation ring with fraction field C; C is algebraically closed, so the previous steps apply. The strict localisation of Spec C^+ at its generic point is Spec of a separable closure of C, which is C.
acceptance: V = O_C for C = the completion of an algebraic closure of Q_p: strictly henselian with residue field an algebraic closure of F_p.
V = C^+ of rank two inside O_C: strictly henselian, residue field algebraically closed.
Non-example of the hypothesis: Z_p is henselian but not strictly henselian (residue field F_p), and its fraction field is not algebraically closed.

uses.how: makes C_i^+ strictly henselian bases so that i^*Rj_* is the nearby-cycle functor of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles

sources.locator: More on Algebra chapter, Lemma 14.5 (Tag 0DCQ), version ed88ff78

nodes.title: The invariance map on nearby-cycle cohomology along a surjective valuation base change
nodes.statement: Let φ: A → B be a surjective map of valuation spectra between strictly henselian valuation rings whose fraction fields K ⊆ L are separably closed; put S = Spec A, S' = Spec B, g = Spec(φ), with generic points η, η' and closed points s, s', so that g(η') = η and g(s') = s. Let f: X → S be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, X' = X ×_S S' with projection g_X, i: X_s → X and j: X_η → X the inclusions of the fibres (i', j' on X'), and g_s: X'_{s'} = X_s ⊗_{k(s)} k(s') → X_s. Let Λ be a torsion ring and F ∈ D^+((X_η)_et, Λ) with pullback F' = g_{X,η}^*F on X'_{η'}. Since A is strictly henselian and K is separably closed, (X, S, η, s) is a quadruple of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles whose strict localisation at η is η, so RΨF = i^*Rj_*F, and (X', S', η', s') → (X, S, η, s) is a morphism of quadruples whose compatible map of strict localisations is η' → η, given by K ⊆ L. The invariance map is the composite inv_φ(F): RΓ(X_s, RΨF) → RΓ(X'_{s'}, g_s^*RΨF) → RΓ(X'_{s'}, RΨF') of pullback along g_s and RΓ(X'_{s'}, bc_φ(F)), where bc_φ(F): g_s^*RΨF → RΨF' is the base-change map of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles. Its degree-n components are inv_φ^n(F): H^n(X_s, RΨF) → H^n(X'_{s'}, RΨF'). The construction is natural in F (a morphism of triangulated functors on D^+((X_η)_et, Λ)) and in X for S-morphisms.
hypotheses: A, B strictly henselian valuation rings with separably closed fraction fields K ⊆ L
φ: A → B a surjective map of valuation spectra
f: X → S quasi-compact and quasi-separated
Λ a torsion ring
F ∈ D^+((X_η)_et, Λ)
proofSteps: By ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-exports/surjective-valuation-base-change, φ is injective and local, so g(η') = η and g(s') = s and X'_{s'} = X_s ⊗_{k(s)} k(s').
K separably closed: the strict localisation of S at η is Spec K; A strictly henselian: S is its own strict localisation at s. Hence RΨ of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles is i^*Rj_* for these quadruples.
The base-change map bc_φ(F) is the map of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles for the morphism of quadruples and the map of strict localisations η' → η.
Pullback along g_s on étale cohomology of the scheme X_s (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2), followed by RΓ(X'_{s'}, bc_φ(F)).
Naturality in F from the naturality of bc_φ and of pullback; functoriality in X from the functoriality of RΨ and bc for S-morphisms.
acceptance: For X = S and F = Λ: RΨΛ is the constant sheaf Λ on s (its stalk is RΓ(Spec K, Λ) = Λ), and inv_φ is the identity of Λ.
For fields A = K ⊆ B = L: η = s, RΨ is the identity and inv_φ is pullback H^n(X, F) → H^n(X ⊗_K L, F).

nodes.title: Reduction of finite type to finite presentation over a valuation ring with noetherian spectrum
nodes.statement: Let A be a valuation ring such that Spec A is a noetherian topological space (for instance A of finite rank, i.e. of finite Krull dimension), S = Spec A, and f: X → S a morphism of finite type with X affine. Then there is an S-scheme Y of finite presentation with Y_red ≅ X_red over S. The closed immersions X_red → X and X_red → Y are universal homeomorphisms, so they induce equivalences of étale sites X_et ≃ (X_red)_et ≃ Y_et, compatible with the fibres over every point of S and with base change along any S' → S; hence the functors i^*, Rj_*, RΨ, the base-change maps and the invariance maps for X and for Y correspond. For quasi-compact X the same holds étale-locally on X, which suffices for sheaf-level statements about RΨ and its base change.
hypotheses: A a valuation ring with Spec A a noetherian topological space
f: X → Spec A of finite type, X affine (quasi-compact for the étale-local form)
proofSteps: If Spec A is noetherian, the spectrum of a finite type A-algebra R = A[x_1, …, x_n]/I is noetherian (the result of [OP68] quoted by Orgogozo, Remarque 4.5).

In a ring with noetherian spectrum the radical of every ideal is the radical of a finitely generated ideal (Orgogozo, Remarque 4.5); choose J ⊆ I finitely generated with rad J = rad I in A[x_1, …, x_n] and put Y = Spec A[x_1, …, x_n]/J, of finite presentation over S with Y_red = X_red.

A closed immersion defined by a nil ideal is a universal homeomorphism; topological invariance of the étale site (Stacks Tag 04DY, requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2) gives the equivalences, compatibly with base change since nil ideals stay nil after base change.
RΨ = i^*Rj_* and the base-change maps are defined on étale sites of X, its fibres and their base changes, so they correspond under these equivalences.
For a finite rank valuation ring, Spec A is a finite chain of primes, hence a noetherian space.
acceptance: A = C^+ of rank two, X = Spec C^+[x]/I for an ideal I that is not finitely generated: Y exists with Y_red = X_red, so the invariance theorem applies to X.
A of rank 0 (a field): every finite type algebra is of finite presentation and Y = X.

tests.name: finiteTypeReduction_test_nonNoetherianSpec
tests.statement: For a valuation ring of infinite rank whose primes contain an infinite strictly increasing chain p_1 ⊊ p_2 ⊊ …, Spec A is not noetherian (the closed sets V(p_n) strictly decrease), and the lemma does not apply.

sources.match: Gabber's remark as recorded by Orgogozo: statements for finitely presented morphisms extend to morphisms of finite type when the underlying space of S is noetherian; this is the finite-dimension alternative.
The mechanism: X_red is the reduced scheme of an S-scheme of finite presentation, as in the lemma.

nodes.title: The support triangle along the special locus and its comparison with nearby cycles
nodes.statement: Let A be a valuation ring, S = Spec A with generic point η and closed point s, S_0 ⊆ S a closed subset with s ∈ S_0 and η ∉ S_0, and U_S = S ∖ S_0. Let f: X → S be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, X_0 = f^{-1}(S_0) with closed immersion i_0, U = f^{-1}(U_S) with open immersion j_U, j: X_η → X and i: X_s → X, and write RΨ_S(G) = i^*Rj_*G for G ∈ D^+((X_η)_et, Λ), Λ a torsion ring. For E ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ): (a) there are natural distinguished triangles i_{0*}RH_{X_0}(E) → E → Rj_{U*}j_U^*E → and RΓ_{X_0}(X, E) → RΓ(X, E) → RΓ(U, E) →; (b) restriction along X_η ⊆ U gives a natural map c_U: i^*Rj_{U*}j_U^*E → RΨ_S(j^*E), which is an isomorphism when U_S = {η}; this happens exactly when A is microbial and S_0 = V(p_A) for its height-one prime p_A, and then i^*i_{0*}RH_{X_0}(E) → i^*E → RΨ_S(j^*E) → is a distinguished triangle on X_s (for A of rank one, S_0 = {s} and the first term is Ri^!E); (c) when U_S ≠ {η}, c_U need not be an isomorphism. When A is strictly henselian with separably closed fraction field, RΨ_S is the nearby-cycle functor RΨ of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles.
hypotheses: A a valuation ring; S_0 ⊆ Spec A closed with s ∈ S_0, η ∉ S_0
f: X → Spec A quasi-compact and quasi-separated
Λ a torsion ring; E ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ)
proofSteps: (a) is the cohomology-with-supports formalism for the closed subscheme X_0 ⊆ X with open complement U (Stacks Tags 09XP, 0A45), a scheme statement requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2.
(b) Write j = j_U ∘ j_{η,U} with j_{η,U}: X_η → U; the unit id → Rj_{η,U*}j_{η,U}^* applied to j_U^*E and then i^*Rj_{U*} gives c_U. If U_S = {η}, j_{η,U} is the identity and c_U is an isomorphism.

U_S = {η} iff A is microbial and S_0 = V(p_A): for 0 ≠ a ∈ p_A, rad(aA) = p_A, so D(a) = {η}; conversely if {η} is open its closed complement is V(p) for the smallest nonzero prime p, which then has height one.
The triangle on X_s is i^* of (a) combined with c_U.

(c) Counterexample: A = C^+ of rank two (C algebraically closed), S_0 = {s}, U_S = {η, p_A}; X = S, ι: Spec k(p_A) → U_S the closed point of U_S and E = j_{U*}ι_*Λ, so j_U^*E = ι_*Λ. Then (i^*Rj_{U*}j_U^*E)_s = RΓ(U_S, ι_*Λ) = RΓ(Spec k(p_A), Λ) = Λ because A is strictly henselian and k(p_A), the residue field of O_C, is algebraically closed, while j^*E = 0 (η ∉ {p_A}), so RΨ_S(j^*E) = 0.
Identification with RΨ: for A strictly henselian with separably closed fraction field, the strict localisation at η is η (H1:valuation-nearby-cycles definition).
acceptance: Rank one, nondiscrete: A = O_C, S_0 = {s}: Ri^!E → i^*E → RΨ(E|X_η) →. For X = S and E = Λ: RΨΛ = Λ and i^*Λ → RΨΛ is the identity, so RΓ_s(Spec O_C, Λ) = 0.
Higher-rank plus ring: A = C^+ of rank two with S_0 = V(p_A) = {p_A, s} gives the triangle, while S_0 = {s} gives the counterexample of (c).
η = s: for A a field there is no closed S_0 containing s and not η, so the statement is vacuous; RΨ_S is the identity and the degenerate triangle for S_0 = ∅ is E → E → 0 →.

tests.name: supportTriangle_test_rankOne
tests.statement: For A = O_C, X = S, E = Λ: the triangle is 0 → Λ → Λ → with identity middle map; H^n_s(Spec O_C, Λ) = 0 for all n.

tests.name: supportTriangle_test_rankTwo
tests.statement: For A = C^+ of rank two, S_0 = {s}, X = S, E = j_{U*}ι_*Λ with ι the inclusion of the point p_A of U_S: (i^*Rj_{U*}j_U^*E)_s = Λ but RΨ_S(j^*E) = 0, so c_U is not an isomorphism.

tests.name: supportTriangle_test_microbial
tests.statement: For A = C^+ of rank two and S_0 = V(p_A): c_U is an isomorphism for every E.

nodes.title: Nearby-cycle cohomology of a proper scheme over a strictly henselian valuation ring
nodes.statement: Let A be a strictly henselian valuation ring with separably closed fraction field K, S = Spec A, f: X → S proper, i: X_s → X, j: X_η → X, and Λ a torsion ring (no condition relating Λ to the residue characteristic). (a) For every E ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ), restriction RΓ(X, E) → RΓ(X_s, i^*E) is an isomorphism. (b) For every F ∈ D^+((X_η)_et, Λ), the composite RΓ(X_η, F) = RΓ(X, Rj_*F) → RΓ(X_s, i^*Rj_*F) = RΓ(X_s, RΨF) is an isomorphism. (c) If moreover A is microbial and X_0 = f^{-1}(V(p_A)), then for E ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ) the isomorphisms (a) and (b) identify the local-cohomology sequence of X_0 ⊆ X (… → H^n_{X_0}(X, E) → H^n(X, E) → H^n(X_η, E) → …) with the cohomology sequence of the specialisation triangle i^*E → RΨ(E|X_η) → RΦ(E) → on X_s, where RΦ(E) is a cone of i^*E → RΨ(E|X_η); in particular H^n_{X_0}(X, E) ≅ H^{n−1}(X_s, RΦ(E)).
hypotheses: A a strictly henselian valuation ring with separably closed fraction field
f: X → Spec A proper
Λ a torsion ring
for (c): A microbial
proofSteps: Proper base change (Stacks Tag 095T; for complexes of Z/n-modules Tag 0F0C; for D^+ with torsion cohomology by the hypercohomology spectral sequence), requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2: (R^qf_*G)_{s̄} = H^q(X_{s̄}, G) for torsion G.
S is strictly local, so RΓ(S, −) is the stalk at s̄; with the Leray spectral sequence, H^q(X, G) = H^q(X_{s̄}, G). In degree 0 this is Stacks Tag 0A3S.
k(s) is separably closed, so X_{s̄} → X_s is a universal homeomorphism and has the same étale cohomology (topological invariance, Stacks Tag 04DY). This gives (a).
(b): apply (a) to Rj_*F ∈ D^+(X_et, Λ), which has torsion cohomology sheaves; RΓ(X_η, F) = RΓ(X, Rj_*F) as j is quasi-compact.

(c): for microbial A, X ∖ X_0 = X_η (special-locus-support-triangle); the restriction maps RΓ(X, E) → RΓ(X_η, E) and i^*E → RΨ(E|X_η) are compatible under (a) and (b) by naturality of the unit E → Rj_*j^*E; complete to a morphism of triangles and conclude by the five lemma on long exact sequences.
acceptance: Nondiscrete rank one: A = O_C, X = P^1_{O_C}, Λ = Z/ℓ^n: H^n(P^1_k, RΨΛ) ≅ H^n(P^1_C, Λ), which is Λ, 0, Λ(−1) for n = 0, 1, 2.
Higher-rank plus ring: A = C^+ of rank two, X = P^1: same groups; (c) applies with X_0 the fibre over V(p_A).
η = s: A = K a field, X_s = X_η = X and RΨ is the identity; (a), (b) are tautological.

Trait analogue: over the normalisation of a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring in an algebraic closure of its fraction field, (b) is the isomorphism RΓ(X_η̄, K) → RΓ(X_s̄, RΨ_η K) of SGA 7 XIII 2.1.8.3 for proper f (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0).

tests.statement: For A of residue characteristic p and Λ = Z/p, (b) holds for X = P^1: H^n(P^1_k, RΨ Z/p) ≅ H^n(P^1_C, Z/p); no prime-to-p hypothesis is used.

nodes.title: Cohomological invariance of nearby cycles under a surjective map of valuation spectra
nodes.statement: Let φ: A → B be a surjective map of valuation spectra between strictly henselian valuation rings whose fraction fields K = Frac A and L = Frac B are separably closed; S = Spec A, S' = Spec B, with generic points η, η' and closed points s, s'. Let f: X → S be of finite presentation, or of finite type with Spec A a noetherian topological space (for instance A of finite rank). Let Λ be a ring with mΛ = 0 for an integer m invertible in A (equivalently in k(s)), and let F ∈ D^+((X_η)_et, Λ), with F' its pullback to X'_{η'} for X' = X ×_S S'. Then: (i) the base-change map bc_φ(F): g_s^*RΨF → RΨF' is an isomorphism in D^+((X'_{s'})_et, Λ); (ii) the invariance map inv_φ(F): RΓ(X_s, RΨF) → RΓ(X'_{s'}, RΨF') is an isomorphism, so H^n(X_s, RΨF) ≅ H^n(X'_{s'}, RΨF') for every n; (iii) if f is proper, the conclusion of (ii) holds for every torsion ring Λ, and reads RΓ(X_η, F) ≅ RΓ(X'_{η'}, F'). No invariance is asserted for a map of valuation rings that is not surjective on spectra, and (i)–(ii) are not asserted when the residue characteristic of A divides the annihilator of Λ.
hypotheses: A, B strictly henselian valuation rings; K = Frac A and L = Frac B separably closed
φ: A → B a surjective map of valuation spectra
f: X → Spec A of finite presentation, or of finite type with Spec A a noetherian topological space
Λ a ring with mΛ = 0 for an integer m invertible in A (for (i) and (ii)); Λ an arbitrary torsion ring and f proper for (iii)
F ∈ D^+((X_η)_et, Λ)
proofSteps: φ is injective and local (surjective-valuation-base-change), so (X', S', η', s') → (X, S, η, s) is a Cartesian morphism of quadruples and inv_φ(F) is defined (invariance-comparison-map).

In the finite-type alternative, finite-rank-finite-type-reduction replaces X by an S-scheme of finite presentation with the same reduced subscheme; étale topoi of X, of its fibres and of X' are unchanged, so RΨ, bc_φ and inv_φ are unchanged.
(i) is the prime-to-residue base change theorem of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles (Hub96 4.2.4) for this Cartesian change of valuation bases, applicable because m is invertible in k(s).

(ii): k(s) ⊆ k(s') is an extension of separably closed fields (A, B strictly henselian); X_s is quasi-compact and quasi-separated over k(s); RΨF ∈ D^+ has cohomology sheaves killed by m, invertible in k(s). Invariance of étale cohomology under extension of separably closed fields (Stacks Tag 0F0B; requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2) makes pullback along g_s an isomorphism; compose with RΓ(X'_{s'}, bc_φ(F)), an isomorphism by (i).

(iii): for f proper, proper-nearby-cycle-cohomology identifies source and target of inv_φ with RΓ(X_η, F) and RΓ(X'_{η'}, F') (API invarianceMap_proper); X'_{η'} = X_η ⊗_K L and X_η is proper over the separably closed field K, so pullback is an isomorphism for every torsion coefficient sheaf (Stacks Tag 0DDG), extended to D^+ by the hypercohomology spectral sequence.
acceptance: Nondiscrete rank one: A = O_C → B = O_{C'} for complete algebraically closed C ⊆ C', X = P^1_{O_C}, Λ = Z/ℓ with ℓ ≠ p: H^2(P^1_k, RΨΛ) ≅ H^2(P^1_{k'}, RΨΛ) ≅ Λ(−1) and H^1 = 0 on both sides.
Higher-rank plus ring: A = C^+ of rank two → B = C'^+ with C'^+ ∩ C = C^+: (i)–(iii) apply; for X = P^1 the groups are Λ, 0, Λ(−1).
η = s: for fields A = K ⊆ B = L, (ii) is Stacks Lemma 90.2 (Tag 0F0B) for X over K.

Trait analogue: over the normalisation of a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring in an algebraic closure of its fraction field, (i) is the change-of-trait isomorphism of SGA 7 XIII 2.1.7.5 (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0).

tests.name: nearbyCycles_invariance_test_nonsurjective
tests.statement: For a rank-two C^+ ⊊ O_C, the inclusion C^+ → O_C is not a surjective map of valuation spectra. With X = S = Spec C^+ and G = j_!Λ the extension by zero from the open subscheme Spec O_C = S ∖ {s}: H^0(S, G) = 0 (S is strictly local and G_s = 0), while the pullback of G to Spec O_C is Λ with H^0 = Λ. No invariance is asserted for this map.

tests.name: nearbyCycles_invariance_test_artinSchreier
tests.statement: For algebraically closed fields K ⊊ L of characteristic p (valuation rings of rank 0, η = s), X = A^1_K and Λ = Z/p: by the Artin–Schreier sequence H^1(A^1_K, Z/p) ≅ K[x]/{g^p − g}, and the map to H^1(A^1_L, Z/p) ≅ L[x]/{g^p − g} misses the class of λx for λ ∈ L ∖ K. Here m = p is not invertible, so (i)–(ii) are not asserted, and (iii) does not apply as A^1 is not proper.

tests.name: nearbyCycles_invariance_test_properPTorsion
tests.statement: For algebraically closed fields K ⊆ L of characteristic p and X = P^1, (iii) gives H^n(P^1_K, Z/p) ≅ H^n(P^1_L, Z/p) for all n although m = p (Stacks Tag 0DDG).

sources.match: Orgogozo states that Huber's §4.2 concerns the cohomology of nearby cycles when the base is the spectrum of a valuation ring: public confirmation of the setting of this export.
Orgogozo: a modification of a valuative scheme has a section, so nearby cycles commute with base change over valuative S, recovering [Hub96, 4.2.4]; this supports (i) for f of finite presentation.
Gabber's remark: the base-change theorem holds for f of finite type when the underlying space of S is noetherian; this is the finite-type alternative of the hypotheses.
Illusie restates that for S the spectrum of a valuative ring one recovers Huber's result [H, 4.2.4]; supports (i).
Lu–Zheng's hypothesis mΛ = 0 with m invertible on S is the coefficient hypothesis of (i)–(ii).
Lu–Zheng: valuation-ring bases satisfy the condition under which all pairs are Ψ-good (nearby cycles commute with base change); supports (i).

nodes.title: Compactly supported cohomology of the generic fibre through nearby cycles of a compactification
nodes.statement: Let A be a strictly henselian valuation ring with separably closed fraction field K, S = Spec A, and f: X → S separated of finite presentation, with a compactification X →(j_X) X̄ →(f̄) S (j_X an open immersion, f̄ proper; one exists by Nagata's theorem over the qcqs base S). Let Λ be a torsion ring, F ∈ D^+((X_η)_et, Λ), and RΓ_c(X_η, F) = RΓ(X̄_η, j_{X,η!}F). (a) There is a natural isomorphism RΓ_c(X_η, F) ≅ RΓ(X̄_s, RΨ_{X̄}(j_{X,η!}F)), compatible with the canonical identifications between compactifications of the scheme compact-support formalism, hence independent of X̄. (b) RΨ_{X̄}(j_{X,η!}F) restricts to RΨ_X(F) on X_s; adjunction gives j_{X,s!}RΨ_X(F) → RΨ_{X̄}(j_{X,η!}F) and a distinguished triangle RΓ_c(X_s, RΨ_X F) → RΓ_c(X_η, F) → RΓ(∂_s, RΨ_{X̄}(j_{X,η!}F)|_{∂_s}) →, where ∂_s = X̄_s ∖ X_s. In particular RΓ_c(X_s, RΨ_X F) → RΓ_c(X_η, F) is an isomorphism when f is proper.
hypotheses: A a strictly henselian valuation ring with separably closed fraction field
f: X → Spec A separated of finite presentation
a compactification X ⊆ X̄ over S (open immersion followed by a proper morphism)
Λ a torsion ring; F ∈ D^+((X_η)_et, Λ)
proofSteps: Existence of X̄ and the filtered category of compactifications: Nagata's theorem over a qcqs base, requested from AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2, with the compact-support formalism for schemes (L2 extends SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2).

(a): proper-nearby-cycle-cohomology (b) for f̄ and the complex j_{X,η!}F ∈ D^+((X̄_η)_et, Λ); X̄_η is a compactification of X_η over K. Independence: for a morphism of compactifications, proper base change (Stacks Tag 095T) identifies the two push-forwards of j_!F and hence the two isomorphisms.

(b): RΨ = i^*Rj_* commutes with restriction to open subschemes, so RΨ_{X̄}(j_{X,η!}F)|_{X_s} = RΨ_X(F); the open–closed decomposition X_s ⊆ X̄_s ⊇ ∂_s gives the triangle j_{X,s!}j_{X,s}^*G → G → ι_*ι^*G → for G = RΨ_{X̄}(j_{X,η!}F) (Stacks Tag 0A45), and RΓ(X̄_s, j_{X,s!}−) = RΓ_c(X_s, −) as X̄_s is proper over k(s).
Proper f: take X̄ = X, so ∂_s = ∅.
acceptance: Degenerate: f proper, X̄ = X, ∂_s = ∅, and (b) reduces to proper-nearby-cycle-cohomology.
Boundary example (nondiscrete rank one): A = O_C, X = Spec C ⊆ X̄ = S. Then X_s = ∅, RΓ_c(X_η, Λ) = Λ, ∂_s = {s} and RΨ_S(Λ)_s = Λ: the triangle is 0 → Λ → Λ →.
Higher-rank plus ring: A = C^+ of rank two with X = Spec O_C ⊆ S: X_η = Spec C, X_s = ∅, and RΓ_c(Spec C, Λ) = Λ is carried entirely by the boundary point s.

Trait analogue: over the normalisation of a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring in an algebraic closure of its fraction field, the map of (b) is the map RΓ_c(X_s̄, RΨ_η K) → RΓ_c(X_η̄, K) of SGA 7 XIII 2.1.8.4 (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0).

tests.name: compactSupportNearbyCycles_test_boundary
tests.statement: For A = O_C and X = Spec C ⊆ X̄ = Spec O_C: RΓ_c(X_s, RΨ_X Λ) = 0 but RΓ_c(X_η, Λ) = Λ; compact support on the special fibre is not compact support on the generic fibre when f is not proper.

tests.name: compactSupportNearbyCycles_test_proper
tests.statement: For f proper and X̄ = X, the map RΓ_c(X_s, RΨ_X F) → RΓ_c(X_η, F) equals the isomorphism of proper-nearby-cycle-cohomology (b).

nodes.title: Constructibility, amplitude and finiteness of nearby-cycle cohomology over a valuation ring
nodes.statement: Let A be a strictly henselian valuation ring with separably closed fraction field K, S = Spec A, f: X → S of finite type with fibres of dimension ≤ N. Let Λ be a noetherian ring with mΛ = 0 for an integer m invertible in A, and F ∈ D^b_c((X_η)_et, Λ) with cohomology sheaves in degrees [a, b]. Then: (i) RΨF ∈ D^b_c((X_s)_et, Λ), with R^nΨF = 0 for n ∉ [a, b + 2N]; (ii) for every closed subscheme L ⊆ X_s proper over k(s) (for instance L = X_s when f is proper), each H^n(L, RΨF|_L) is a finitely generated Λ-module and vanishes for all but finitely many n; (iii) for every locally closed subscheme L ⊆ X_s, each H^n_c(L, RΨF|_L) is finitely generated; (iv) if f is proper, H^n(X_η, F) ≅ H^n(X_s, RΨF) is finitely generated, and if f is separated of finite presentation, H^n_c(X_η, F) is finitely generated.
hypotheses: A a strictly henselian valuation ring with separably closed fraction field
f: X → Spec A of finite type with fibres of dimension ≤ N (of finite presentation and separated for the compactly supported part of (iv))
Λ noetherian with mΛ = 0, m invertible in A
F ∈ D^b_c((X_η)_et, Λ) with cohomology in degrees [a, b]
proofSteps: (i) Constructibility of each R^nΨF is the constructibility theorem of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles (Hub96 4.2.5), by dévissage from sheaves to D^b_c, after spreading F out: by continuity of D^b_c along X_η = lim_{a ≠ 0} X ×_S Spec A[1/a] (request to AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2), F is the restriction of a constructible complex F_a on X_a = X ×_S Spec A[1/a], and RΨF = RΨ(j_{a!}F_a) since K is separably closed. The amplitude bound: the stalk of R^nΨG at x̄ is H^n of the Milnor tube X_(x̄) ×_S η with coefficients in a torsion sheaf G, which vanishes for n > 2N (Orgogozo, Proposition 2.3); see nearby-cycles-cohomological-amplitude and milnor-tube-stalk-formula.

(ii) and (iii): L is of finite type over the separably closed field k(s) and RΨF|_L is a constructible complex; finiteness of cohomology of proper schemes and of compactly supported cohomology with constructible coefficients over a separably closed field (SGA 4 XIV, SGA 4½ Th. finitude), requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2.

(iv) proper: proper-nearby-cycle-cohomology (b) and (ii) with L = X_s. Separated of finite presentation: compact-support-nearby-cycle-cohomology (a) identifies H^n_c(X_η, F) with H^n(X̄_s, RΨ_{X̄}(j_{X,η!}F)), finite by (i) for X̄ and (ii) with L = X̄_s.
acceptance: Nondiscrete rank one: A = O_C, X = E an elliptic curve over O_C with good reduction, F = Z/ℓ^n with ℓ ≠ p: H^1(E_s, RΨF) ≅ H^1(E_C, Z/ℓ^n) ≅ (Z/ℓ^n)^2.
Higher-rank plus ring: A = C^+ of rank two, X = P^1: the groups of (iv) are Λ, 0, Λ(−1).
η = s: A = K a field, RΨF = F and (ii)–(iii) are the finiteness theorems over K.

nodes.title: Compatibility of the valuation exports with the formal/adic comparison maps
nodes.statement: Let A be a strictly henselian microbial valuation ring with separably closed fraction field K and its valuation topology, a ∈ p_A a nonzero element of its height-one prime, S = Spec A, f: X → S locally of finite type, X^ the a-adic completion of X (of type (S) by H1:formal-adic-comparison 3.5.16), X_0 = X ×_S V(p_A), T ⊆ d(X^) the preimage of the closed point of d(Spf A) = Spa(K, A), Z = (d(X^), T) and c: Z → X_η the natural morphism. Let Λ be a torsion ring and F ∈ D^+((X_η)_et, Λ). (i) The isomorphism κ_X: RΓ(Z, c^*F) ≅ RΓ(X_s, i^*Rj_*F) of 3.5.16 has target RΓ(X_s, RΨF), RΨ the nearby-cycle functor of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles (X_η ⊆ X is open and the strict localisation at η is η). (ii) For every constructible closed subset L of X_0 contained in X_s, the sheaf-level isomorphism of 3.5.13 restricted to L gives κ_{X,L}: RΓ(d(X^, L), c_L^*F) ≅ RΓ(L, RΨF|_L), with κ_{X,X_s} = κ_X, compatible with restriction to closed L' ⊆ L and with extension by zero from open L' ⊆ L (3.5.11). (iii) Let φ: A → B be a continuous surjective map of valuation spectra to a ring B of the same kind (fraction field L), X_B = X ×_S Spec B. The morphism d(X_B^) → d(X^) maps the tube Z_B over the closed point of Spa(L, B) into Z, and pullback of tube cohomology RΓ(Z, c^*F) → RΓ(Z_B, c_B^*F_B) corresponds under κ_X and κ_{X_B} to the invariance map inv_φ(F). (iv) For A = O_C complete of rank one (necessarily nondiscrete, its fraction field C being separably closed), T = d(X^) and κ_X is RΓ(X_s, −) applied to the isomorphism i^*Rj_*F ≅ Rb_*a^*F of 3.5.13, with b: d(X^)_et → X^_et ≅ (X_s)_et and a: d(X^)_et → (X_η)_et: the algebraic nearby cycles are the analytic nearby cycles of the completion.
hypotheses: A a strictly henselian microbial valuation ring with separably closed fraction field, with its valuation topology
f: X → Spec A locally of finite type
Λ a torsion ring; F ∈ D^+((X_η)_et, Λ)
for (ii): L a constructible closed subset of X_0 contained in X_s
for (iii): φ: A → B continuous and a surjective map of valuation spectra, B of the same kind
proofSteps: (i): 3.5.16 (H1:formal-adic-comparison/valuation-ring-base-3-5-16) gives κ_X with target RΓ(X_s, i^*Rj_*F) for j: X_η → X; for microbial A this j is an open immersion (special-locus-support-triangle), and i^*Rj_* = RΨ because K is separably closed and A strictly henselian.

(ii): 3.5.13 (scheme-completion-comparison-3-5-13, with the ideal aA principal and X^ of type (S)) gives i_0^*Rj_*F ≅ Rb_*a^*F on (X_0)_et; restriction to L via 3.5.11(i) (restriction-and-extension-by-zero-3-5-11) identifies the restriction with Rλ_{(X^,L)*} of the pullback to d(X^, L) (pairs-and-pseudo-adic-supports); take RΓ(L, −). Extension by zero from open L' ⊆ L is 3.5.11(ii).

(iii): the tube over the closed point maps to the tube over the closed point because Spec(φ) sends s' to s (surjective-valuation-base-change; continuity makes d(Spf B) → d(Spf A) defined). The transformation of 3.5.13 is built from the maps φ_Z: d(Z^) → Z ×_X d(X^) of Hub96 1.9.5, natural in Z; base change along X_B → X is a morphism of pairs, so the adjunction transformation commutes with pullback, and its composite with RΓ is the square pullback/κ/κ/inv_φ (invariance-comparison-map, API invarianceMap_eq_comp_baseChange).
(iv): for rank one, V(p_A) = {s}, X_0 = X_s and T = d(X^); this is 3.5.13 itself (Hansen–Zavyalov, proof of Theorem A.4.4).
acceptance: Nondiscrete rank one: A = O_C, X = A^1_{O_C}, Λ killed by an integer prime to p: Z is the closed unit disc over C, and κ_X identifies RΓ(Z, Λ) with RΓ(A^1_k, RΨΛ) = RΓ(A^1_k, Λ) = Λ (RΨΛ = Λ by local acyclicity of the smooth morphism).

Higher-rank plus ring: A = C^+ of rank two, X = A^1_{C^+}: Z is the tube in the closed unit disc over the closed point of Spa(C, C^+), and κ_X identifies its cohomology with RΓ(A^1_k, RΨΛ) for the residue field k of C^+.
Support: for L a closed point x of X_s, κ_{X,{x}} identifies the cohomology of the open residue tube d(X^, {x}) with the stalk (RΨF)_x̄.

Trait: over the normalisation of a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring in an algebraic closure of its fraction field, (i) and (iv) are the identification of H1:formal-adic-comparison/vanishing-cycles-comparison-3-5-17 with LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0 RΨ.

nodes.title: Invariance of tube cohomology under surjective extension of algebraically closed valued fields (export to H2)
nodes.statement: Let C_3 ⊆ C_1 be a continuous extension of complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean fields with open and bounded valuation subrings C_3^+ ⊆ C_1^+ such that Spa(C_1, C_1^+) → Spa(C_3, C_3^+) is surjective (equivalently C_1^+ ∩ C_3 = C_3^+). Let X be a C_3^+-scheme of finite presentation, or of finite type when Spec C_3^+ is noetherian, X_1 = X ⊗_{C_3^+} C_1^+, and for i ∈ {1, 3} let Z_i ⊆ d(X_i^) be the tube over the closed point of Spa(C_i, C_i^+) with c_i: Z_i → (X_i)_{C_i} (H1:formal-adic-comparison 3.5.16). Let n be an integer prime to the residue characteristic p of C_3, Λ a ring with nΛ = 0, F ∈ D^+((X_{C_3})_et, Λ) and F_1 its pullback. Then pullback RΓ(Z_3, c_3^*F) → RΓ(Z_1, c_1^*F_1) is an isomorphism. In particular, for a Zariski-open V ⊆ X_{C_3} and an abelian group M killed by n, H^i(Z_3, c_3^*j_{V!}M) ≅ H^i(Z_1, c_1^*j_{V!}M) for all i. This is the algebraizable, extension-by-zero case of the input [Hub96, Theorem 4.1.1(c)] used in ECD Lemma 16.3; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2 passes from it to affinoids topologically of finite type over C_3, to perfectoid limits and to quasi-compact adic open subsets.
hypotheses: C_3 ⊆ C_1 complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean fields, continuous extension
C_i^+ ⊆ C_i open and bounded valuation subrings with C_3^+ ⊆ C_1^+ and Spa(C_1, C_1^+) → Spa(C_3, C_3^+) surjective
X of finite presentation over C_3^+ (or of finite type with Spec C_3^+ noetherian)
n prime to the residue characteristic, nΛ = 0, F ∈ D^+((X_{C_3})_et, Λ)
proofSteps: C_i^+ is a strictly henselian microbial valuation ring with algebraically closed fraction field C_i (algebraically-closed-fraction-field-strictly-henselian; the height-one prime is the maximal ideal of O_{C_i} intersected with C_i^+).
C_3^+ → C_1^+ is a continuous surjective map of valuation spectra (surjective-valuation-base-change, Spa clause).
formal-adic-compatibility (i), (iii): the pullback on tube cohomology corresponds to inv_φ(F) under κ_X and κ_{X_1}.
nearby-cycle-invariance-under-surjective-base-change (ii): inv_φ(F) is an isomorphism, n being invertible in C_3^+.
Extension by zero: j_{V!}M ∈ D^+((X_{C_3})_et, Λ) for Λ = Z/n; its pullback along c_i is c_i^*j_{V!}M (H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero).
acceptance: Nondiscrete rank one: C_3 = C_p (completed algebraic closure of Q_p) ⊆ C_1 a larger complete algebraically closed field, C_i^+ = O_{C_i}, X = G_{m,O_{C_3}}, F = Z/ℓ: the tubes are the unit circles {|x| = 1} and H^1 ≅ Z/ℓ(−1) on both sides.

Higher-rank plus ring: C_3^+ ⊊ O_{C_3} of rank two and C_1^+ = the valuation ring of C_1 with C_1^+ ∩ C_3 = C_3^+: the conclusion holds; for C_1^+ = O_{C_1} ⊋ C_3^+ the surjectivity hypothesis fails and nothing is asserted; the conclusion of ECD Lemma 16.3 fails for that map with X_2 = X_3 and U_2 the rank-one point, which is why the lemma assumes surjectivity.
Degenerate: C_1 = C_3, C_1^+ = C_3^+: the map is the identity.

nodes.title: H1 re-export of the henselian comparison theorems of H1:henselian (Hub96 §§3.1–3.2)
nodes.statement: H1 re-exports, under their H1:henselian names and with their exact hypotheses, the following declarations of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian, and constructs no henselian object of its own. (i) Henselian f-adic rings and the henselization ι: A → A^h, universal among continuous homomorphisms to henselian f-adic rings, with (A^h)^▷ = (A^▷)^h, (A^h)^+ = (A^+)^h and the completion ι^: Â → (A^h)^ an isomorphism (Hub96 3.1.1–3.1.3), together with the separately citable fact that a complete f-adic ring is henselian; the henselian pairs (B, I) occurring here are Mathlib's `HenselianRing B I`, not a second carrier. (ii) Special and pro-special subsets of Spa A and the henselization A(U) of an affinoid ring A along a pro-special subset U (Hub96 3.1.6–3.1.12). (iii) Theorem 3.2.1: for an affinoid ring A, not necessarily complete, a pro-special subset U ⊆ Spa A, Y = Spec A(U), and G a set (resp. an ind-finite group, resp. an abelian torsion group), the natural maps H^n(Y, G_Y) → H^n(U, G_U) are bijective for n = 0 (resp. n ∈ {0, 1}, resp. every n ≥ 0), U denoting the pseudo-adic space (Spa A, U); for complete A this is H^n(Spec A^▷, G) ≅ H^n(Spa A, G) (3.2.2). (iv) Gabber's affine analogue of proper base change (Hub96 Lemma 3.2.5): for a ring A henselian along an ideal I and an abelian torsion sheaf F on (Spec A)_et with restriction F_0 to (Spec A/I)_et, H^n(Spec A, F) → H^n(Spec A/I, F_0) is bijective for every n ≥ 0. (v) The relative comparisons 3.2.9–3.2.12 for schemes locally of finite type over Spec A^▷. The comparison asserted by this node: in (iii)–(v) the analytic side is H0's cohomology of the étale site of the pseudo-adic space (an instance of the D0 sheaf and E1 derived-functor carriers) and the algebraic side is the étale cohomology of schemes on the carriers LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0 uses; the coefficient scopes (sets in degree 0, ind-finite groups in degrees ≤ 1, abelian torsion groups in all degrees; torsion sheaves in (iv)) are copied, neither widened nor narrowed; so H1:formal-adic-comparison, H1:valuation-nearby-cycles, DiamondEtaleCohomology C5 and AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5 cite one theorem each.
hypotheses: Every hypothesis is that of the cited H1:henselian declaration; A in (iii) need not be complete.
Henselian pairs are Mathlib's `HenselianRing`; H1 introduces no henselian carrier (RS-05).
proofSteps: Each item is the H1:henselian declaration; H1 records an alias whose type is that declaration's type.

Carrier check: the cohomology of the pseudo-adic space U in (iii) and (v) is computed in H0's category of abelian sheaves on the étale site of (Spa A, U), whose derived functors are the D0/E1 ones; the cohomology of Y and of Spec A is étale cohomology of schemes; H1 defines no cohomology theory.
Scope check: the three coefficient ranges of 3.2.1 and the torsion hypothesis of 3.2.5 are copied verbatim.
acceptance: For complete A the export specialises to Corollary 3.2.2, H^n(Spec A^▷, G) ≅ H^n(Spa A, G), the form H1:formal-adic-comparison uses (through 3.2.9) in the proof of 3.5.13.
Every alias has, by rfl, the type of the corresponding H1:henselian declaration.
For G a non-abelian ind-finite group, the export asserts bijectivity only for n ∈ {0, 1}.

nodes.title: H1 re-export of the formal/adic specialization comparisons of H1:formal-adic-comparison, with their all-torsion scope
nodes.statement: H1 re-exports, under their H1:formal-adic-comparison names and with their exact hypotheses, the following declarations of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison, and constructs no specialization morphism, tube or nearby-cycle object of its own. (i) For a formal scheme X of type (S) (AdicSpacesPartII R2), the étale site X_et, identified with (X_red)_et, and the specialization morphism of sites λ_X: d(X)_et → X_et (Hub96 3.5.1). (ii) Pairs (X, L), the pseudo-adic support d(X, L) = (d(X), λ_X^{-1}(L)) and λ_(X,L) (3.5.3–3.5.5), with constructibility of λ^* and the stalk isomorphism (λ^*F)_x̄ ≅ F_ȳ (3.5.6). (iii) The stalk formulas for R^nλ_*: 3.5.8 under its assumption that Y_∞^ is of type (S), the filtered formula 3.5.9 without that assumption, and 3.5.10, (R^nλ_*F)_x̄ = H^n(V, M) for the punctured strict localization V. (iv) Restriction and open extension by zero, 3.5.11. (v) For a scheme X, a closed subscheme Y defined by a quasi-coherent ideal of finite type, U = X − Y, the completion X̂ of X along Y, and the hypothesis of (3.5.12) (X locally noetherian, or the ideal locally generated by one element and X̂ of type (S)): the transformation i^* ∘ R^+j_* → R^+b_* ∘ a^* of functors D^+(U_et, E) → D^+(Y_et, E), an isomorphism for every torsion ring E (3.5.13), with its global-sections and tube forms 3.5.14–3.5.15. (vi) 3.5.16 over a microbial valuation ring, not necessarily discrete. (vii) 3.5.17 over a henselian rank-one discrete valuation ring with separably closed residue field. The comparison asserted by this node is one of scope: (v)–(vii) hold for all torsion coefficient rings, p-torsion included, and are kept distinct from the prime-to-residue-characteristic base change of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles (Hub96 4.2.4) and from LPV.0's standing prime-to-p hypothesis (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.1); no H1 declaration restates 3.5.13 with a prime-to-p hypothesis, and none extends 4.2.4 to p-torsion.
hypotheses: Every hypothesis is that of the cited H1:formal-adic-comparison declaration; in particular the type-(S) assumption of 3.5.8 and the alternative hypotheses of (3.5.12).
Coefficients in (v)–(vii): an arbitrary torsion ring E and complexes in D^+.
proofSteps: Each item is the H1:formal-adic-comparison declaration; H1 records an alias whose type is that declaration's type.
Carrier check: d(X) and λ_X come from AdicSpacesPartII R2; the analytic étale sites and D^+ are H0's (instances of D0/E1); the scheme side uses LPV.0's carriers.
Scope check: the torsion hypothesis of 3.5.13–3.5.17 is 'E a torsion ring', copied without a prime-to-p clause.
acceptance: For a reduced affinoid algebra A over a complete discretely valued field with separably closed residue field of characteristic p, a uniformizer ϖ, ℓ ≠ p and x a point of Spec A°/ϖ, 3.5.10 specialises to (R^jλ_*Z/ℓ)_x ≅ H^j(Spec O^sh_{Spec A°,x}[1/ϖ], Z/ℓ) — Hansen's formula (∗), which he derives from Hub96 3.5.10.
3.5.13 with E = Z/p over a mixed-characteristic base is asserted (no prime-to-p hypothesis), and the alias has exactly this scope.
Every alias has, by rfl, the type of the corresponding H1:formal-adic-comparison declaration.

nodes.title: On a strictly henselian trait, Huber's complex of vanishing cycles (3.5.17), RΨ_L of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles and LPV.0's RΨ_η are one object with one inertia action
nodes.statement: Let A be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring (henselian, with separably closed residue field k(s) of characteristic exponent p), S = Spec A with generic point η and closed point s, k = Frac A with its valuation topology, k^sep ⊆ k̄ a separable and an algebraic closure of k, Ā the integral closure of A in k̄, A^sep the integral closure of A in k^sep, k^, k̄^, A^ and Ā^ the completions of k, k̄, A and Ā, and I = Gal(k^sep/k), which is the inertia group because k(s) is separably closed and which acts on k̄ through the restriction isomorphism Aut(k̄/k) ≅ Gal(k^sep/k) (k̄/k^sep is purely inseparable). Let X be an S-scheme, E a torsion ring prime to p, and K ∈ D^+((X_η)_et, E). Consider: (a) LPV.0's nearby-cycle complex RΨ_η(K) ∈ D^+(X_s ×_s η, E): with η̄ = Spec k^sep, S̄ = Spec A^sep, X̄ = X ×_S S̄, j̄: X_η̄ → X̄ and ī: X_s̄ → X̄, its underlying complex is ī^*Rj̄_*(K|X_η̄) (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.2.3), with I acting by transport of structure; (b) Huber's complex of vanishing cycles in Hub96 3.5.17: with X' = X ×_A Ā, j': X' ×_Ā k̄ → X' and i': X_s ×_A Ā → X', the complex i'^*Rj'_*(K|X_k̄), with Aut(k̄/k) ≅ I acting through its action on Ā; (c) RΨ_L(F) = i^*Rj_*j^*F of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles for the quadruple (X, S, η, s) and any F ∈ D^+(X_et, E) with F|X_η ≅ K, where η̃ = Spec k^sep is the strict localization of S at η, j: X_η̃ → X and i: X_s → X, with I = Gal(η̃/η) acting by transport of structure; it depends only on K. The projections X_s̄ → X_s and X_s ×_A Ā → X_s are universal homeomorphisms (integral, universally injective, surjective: the residue fields of A^sep and Ā are purely inseparable over the separably closed k(s)) and identify the étale topoi. Under these identifications there are canonical isomorphisms (c) ≅ (a) ≅ (b) in D^+((X_s)_et, E), each commuting with the action of every σ ∈ I. For the degenerate quadruple η = s (η̃ = S, j the identity), RΨ_L(F) = i^*F, which is the s-component RΨ(F)_s = i^*F of LPV.0 (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.2.1).
hypotheses: A strictly henselian discrete valuation ring; X an arbitrary S-scheme (quasi-compactness of j is automatic: j is affine).

E a torsion ring prime to p = the characteristic exponent of k(s) — the coefficient scope of LPV.0 (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.1); steps 1 and 2 use no prime-to-p hypothesis, so (b) ≅ (c) holds for every torsion ring E.
K ∈ D^+; objects of D^+(X_s ×_s η, E) are complexes on X_s̄ with continuous I-action (LPV.0 1.2.4, 1.1.3).
proofSteps: (a) ≅ (b) is the substage node ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison/huber-vanishing-cycles-are-nearby-cycles, cited, not re-proved; its argument: Ā is integral over A^sep and Spec Ā → Spec A^sep is integral, universally injective and surjective (k̄/k^sep is purely inseparable and both rings are valuation rings of the unique extensions of the valuation of the henselian field k); base change along X gives a universal homeomorphism X' → X̄ restricting to X' ×_Ā k̄ → X_η̄ and X_s ×_A Ā → X_s̄. Topological invariance of the étale site (Stacks 04DZ; supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2) identifies the étale topoi compatibly with the inclusions of the generic and special fibres, so i'^*Rj'_* corresponds to ī^*Rj̄_*.

(c) → (a). π: X̄ → X is integral (base change of Spec A^sep → S), π_* is exact on étale sheaves, and j = π ∘ j̄ because η̃ = η̄; the base-change morphism i^*Rj_* = i^*π_*Rj̄_* → π_{s*}ī^*Rj̄_* is checked on stalks at geometric points x̄ of X_s: by the strict-localization stalk formula for Rj_* (supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2) the left stalk is R^+Γ(X_(x̄) ×_S η̃, K), and by LPV.0's stalk formula (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.4) the right stalk is R^+Γ(X_(x̄) ×_{S^nr} η̄, K) with S^nr = S (A strictly henselian) and η̄ = η̃; geometric points are conservative (LPV.0 1.2.5). π_s: X_s̄ → X_s is a universal homeomorphism, so π_{s*} is the identification of topoi used in the statement.

Equivariance. In (a) σ ∈ I acts on S̄ over S, hence on X̄ over X (SGA 7 XIII 1.3.2.2: transport of structure); in (b) through Aut(k̄/k) ≅ I acting on Ā, hence on X' over X; in (c) through σ acting on η̃ over η. The maps of the two previous steps are induced by the X-morphisms X' → X̄ → X, which commute with these actions, and the stalk identifications are natural in the geometric generic point; hence all isomorphisms are I-equivariant.
η = s: the strict localization of S at s is S itself, so j = id and RΨ_L(F) = i^*F; this is LPV.0's formula RΨ(F)_s = i^*F (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.2.1).
acceptance: X = S: all three objects are the I-module K_η̄ on the point s.
X smooth over S and K = E constant: all three are E_{X_s} in degree 0 with trivial I-action (LPV.0 local acyclicity, SGA 7 XIII 2.1.5: RΦ = 0).

nodes.title: The comparison isomorphism of Hub96 3.5.17 commutes with the inertia action
nodes.statement: Let A be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring (henselian, with separably closed residue field k(s) of characteristic exponent p), S = Spec A with generic point η and closed point s, k = Frac A with its valuation topology, k^sep ⊆ k̄ a separable and an algebraic closure of k, Ā the integral closure of A in k̄, A^sep the integral closure of A in k^sep, k^, k̄^, A^ and Ā^ the completions of k, k̄, A and Ā, and I = Gal(k^sep/k), which is the inertia group because k(s) is separably closed and which acts on k̄ through the restriction isomorphism Aut(k̄/k) ≅ Gal(k^sep/k) (k̄/k^sep is purely inseparable). Let X → S be locally of finite type, E a torsion ring and K ∈ D^+((X_η)_et, E). Let X̂ be the completion of X along X_s, Y = d(X̂) its generic fibre over Spa(k^, A^), Ȳ = Y ×_{Spa(k^, A^)} Spa(k̄^, Ā^) (the completed base change Y ⊗̂_{k^} k̄^), and c: Ȳ_et → (X_η)_et the natural morphism; let X' = X ×_A Ā, i', j' as in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/trait-nearby-cycles-agree. Every σ ∈ Aut(k̄/k) extends uniquely to an isometric automorphism of k̄^ (the valuation of the henselian field k has a unique extension to k̄), acts on Ȳ over Y with c ∘ σ = c, hence on R^+Γ(Ȳ, c^*K); and σ acts on X' over X, preserving X_s ×_A Ā, hence on R^+Γ(X_s ×_A Ā, i'^*Rj'_*(K|X_k̄)). The isomorphism R^+Γ(Ȳ, c^*K) ≅ R^+Γ(X_s ×_A Ā, i'^*Rj'_*(K|X_k̄)) of Hub96 3.5.17 commutes with these two actions of σ, for every σ ∈ Aut(k̄/k).
hypotheses: X → S locally of finite type; E an arbitrary torsion ring (no prime-to-p hypothesis); K ∈ D^+.
σ acts semilinearly: the action on Ȳ is not k̄^-linear, and the statement is an equality of automorphisms of complexes of E-modules.
Neither Hub96 nor SGA 7 states this equivariance; the proof uses only the naturality of the constructions.
proofSteps: Hub96 3.5.17 is 3.5.14 applied to X' and the closed subscheme X_s ×_A Ā, composed with the identification d(X̂') ≅ Ȳ, where X̂' is the completion of X' along X_s ×_A Ā (Hub96 proof of 3.5.17, H1:formal-adic-comparison).

The identification d(X̂') ≅ Ȳ is natural in automorphisms of Ā over A: X̂' is the completed base change of X̂ along A^ → Ā^, d commutes with completed extension of the base field functorially in the formal scheme (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products (b)), and d is a functor (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-functor-d); σ acts on both sides through its action on Ā^ ⊆ k̄^.

3.5.14 is R^+Γ(X_s ×_A Ā, −) applied to the transformation i^*R^+j_* → R^+b_*a^* of 3.5.13, which is constructed from the morphisms φ_Z: d(Ẑ) → Z ×_X d(X̂) of Hub96 (1.9.5), natural in Z ∈ Et/X, and from adjunction morphisms; it is therefore natural for automorphisms of the pair (X', X_s ×_A Ā) over X, in particular for σ.

σ acts over X and K|X_k̄ is pulled back from X_η, so σ^*(K|X_k̄) ≅ K|X_k̄ canonically, and similarly σ^*c^*K ≅ c^*K; transporting the naturality square of the previous step along these isomorphisms gives the commutation.
acceptance: X = S: Ȳ = Spa(k̄^, Ā^), whose étale site is trivial, and both sides are the stalk K_η̄; σ acts on both by its Galois action.
X = A^1_A, K = Z/ℓ with ℓ ≠ p: both sides are Z/ℓ in degree 0 with trivial action (closed unit disc over k̄^).

nodes.title: Hub96 3.5.17 as an inertia-equivariant identification of the analytic generic-fibre cohomology with LPV.0's trait nearby cycles
nodes.statement: Let A be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring (henselian, with separably closed residue field k(s) of characteristic exponent p), S = Spec A with generic point η and closed point s, k = Frac A with its valuation topology, k^sep ⊆ k̄ a separable and an algebraic closure of k, Ā the integral closure of A in k̄, A^sep the integral closure of A in k^sep, k^, k̄^, A^ and Ā^ the completions of k, k̄, A and Ā, and I = Gal(k^sep/k), which is the inertia group because k(s) is separably closed and which acts on k̄ through the restriction isomorphism Aut(k̄/k) ≅ Gal(k^sep/k) (k̄/k^sep is purely inseparable). Let X → S be locally of finite type, E a torsion ring prime to p, K ∈ D^+((X_η)_et, E), and Ȳ, c as in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/formal-nearby-cycle-comparison-inertia-equivariance (Ȳ = d(X̂) ⊗̂_{k^} k̄^, the analytic geometric generic fibre of the completion of X along X_s). Then the isomorphism of Hub96 3.5.17 composed with the identification of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/trait-nearby-cycles-agree is an isomorphism R^+Γ(Ȳ, c^*K) ≅ R^+Γ(X_s, RΨ_η(K)), where RΨ_η(K) is LPV.0's nearby-cycle complex (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.2), and it is I-equivariant for I acting on Ȳ through k̄^ and on RΨ_η(K) as in LPV.0; in particular H^q(Ȳ, c^*K) ≅ H^q(X_s, RΨ_η(K)) as E[I]-modules for every q. This is the trait nearby-cycle comparison H1 exports on LPV.0's carriers; for torsion rings E with p-torsion the analytic statement is Hub96 3.5.17 itself, whose right side is Huber's object i'^*Rj'_*(K|X_k̄), outside LPV.0's coefficient scope.
hypotheses: A strictly henselian discrete valuation ring; X → S locally of finite type (no properness).
E a torsion ring prime to p (LPV.0's scope); K ∈ D^+.
proofSteps: Hub96 3.5.17 (H1:formal-adic-comparison): R^+Γ(Ȳ, c^*K) ≅ R^+Γ(X_s ×_A Ā, i'^*Rj'_*(K|X_k̄)).
ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/trait-nearby-cycles-agree: i'^*Rj'_*(K|X_k̄) ≅ RΨ_η(K) on (X_s ×_A Ā)_et ≅ (X_s)_et, I-equivariantly.
ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/formal-nearby-cycle-comparison-inertia-equivariance: the 3.5.17 isomorphism commutes with I.
Compose; equivariance of a composite of equivariant isomorphisms.
acceptance: X = S: R^+Γ(Spa(k̄^, Ā^), c^*K) = K_η̄ = RΨ_η(K)_s with the Galois action on both sides.

X = A^1_A, K = Z/ℓ with ℓ ≠ p: Ȳ is the closed unit disc over k̄^ and RΨ_η(Z/ℓ) = Z/ℓ (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.5), so H^0(Ȳ, Z/ℓ) = Z/ℓ, H^q(Ȳ, Z/ℓ) = 0 for q > 0, with trivial I-action (Berkovich 1994, Corollary 5.4, gives the same for smooth formal schemes).

X proper over A: Ȳ is the analytification of X_η ⊗_k k̄^, and composing with LPV.0's proper specialization isomorphism R^+Γ(X_η̄, K) ≅ R^+Γ(X_s̄, RΨ_η K) (LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.0/derived-functorialities-and-specialization-sequence, 2.1.8.3) gives an I-equivariant isomorphism R^+Γ(X_η̄, K) ≅ R^+Γ(Ȳ, c^*K). (Its agreement with Hub96 3.7.2 is a compatibility for H5 to prove, not an H1 acceptance item.)

LPV.2: for X proper and flat of odd relative dimension n = 2m + 1 over A whose only non-smooth point x of X_s is an ordinary quadratic point with b(x) a uniformizer, the Picard–Lefschetz formula σ(a) = a + (−1)^{m+1} ε_{b(x)}(σ)(a·δ_x)δ_x of LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.2/odd-relative-dimension-picard-lefschetz-3-3 (SGA 7 XV 3.3.6), with δ_x, the pairing and the twists as there, holds on H^n(Ȳ, Λ) through the previous item; it inherits that node's recorded gap.

nodes.title: On strictly henselian traits the valuation-base base-change map of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles is LPV.0's change-of-trait morphism
nodes.statement: Let A → A' be an injective local homomorphism of strictly henselian discrete valuation rings, S' = Spec A' → S = Spec A the induced surjective morphism of traits, k' = Frac A', separable closures chosen with k^sep ⊆ k'^sep, and I' = Gal(k'^sep/k') → I = Gal(k^sep/k) the induced map. Let X be an S-scheme, X' = X ×_S S', g: X' → X, g_s: X'_s → X_s, E a torsion ring prime to p, and F ∈ D^+(X_et, E). The base-change map g_s^*RΨ_L(F) → RΨ_{L'}(g^*F) of H1:valuation-nearby-cycles for the morphism of quadruples (X', S', η', s') → (X, S, η, s) and the map of strict localizations η̃' = Spec k'^sep → η̃ = Spec k^sep corresponds, under ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/trait-nearby-cycles-agree for S and for S', to LPV.0's change-of-trait morphism g^*RΨ → RΨg^* (SGA 7 XIII 1.3.10, derived in 2.1.7.5), I'-equivariantly. If X → S is locally of finite type, both are isomorphisms, by Hub96 4.2.4 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles/valuative-base-change-for-nearby-cycles; the morphism of quadruples is Cartesian and dominant). SGA 7 XIII 2.1.7.5 only constructs the morphism (isomorphy is conjectured for excellent S, S′ and proved in 2.1.12 in two cases). If A′ is finite over A, the H1:valuation-nearby-cycles map is an isomorphism for every X and every torsion ring E.
hypotheses: A → A' injective and local, both strictly henselian discrete valuation rings (a surjective change of traits in the sense of SGA 7 XIII 1.2.7).
E prime to p; F ∈ D^+.
For the isomorphism clause with A′ not finite over A: X → S locally of finite type (hypothesis of valuative-base-change-for-nearby-cycles).
proofSteps: Both maps are the base-change morphism of the commutative square formed by X'_η̃' → X_η̃ over g: X' → X and the inclusions of the special fibres: H1:valuation-nearby-cycles defines its map from the base-change morphism g^*Rj_* → Rj'_*g'^* restricted along i', and LPV.0 derives SGA 7 XIII 1.3.10 in the same way; the identifications of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/trait-nearby-cycles-agree are natural in the trait, so the two maps coincide.

Isomorphism for E prime to p and X → S locally of finite type: Hub96 4.2.4 (valuative-base-change-for-nearby-cycles). SGA 7 XIII 2.1.7.5 is only a morphism (2.1.11–2.1.12). For A′ finite over A: X′_η̃′ → X_η̃ and X′_s → X_s are universal homeomorphisms, so the map is an isomorphism for all X and all torsion E (test changeOfTrait_test_finite_all_torsion).
Equivariance: I' acts on k'^sep compatibly with its image in I; both maps are natural in the geometric generic points.
acceptance: A' = A[π^{1/e}] with e prime to p (π a uniformizer): I' is the open subgroup of index e in I and the base-change map is an I'-equivariant isomorphism.
The node makes no claim for a morphism of valuation rings that is not local, and none for p-torsion coefficients along a non-finite A → A'.

nodes.title: RΨ versus RΦ: Huber's 'complex of vanishing cycles' is the nearby-cycle complex, and RΦ is the cone of the analytic specialization map
nodes.statement: Pinned terminology. The object Hub96 3.5.17 calls 'the complex of vanishing cycles' RΨ_η(K), Berkovich's 'vanishing cycles functor' Ψ_η (built from his functor Θ, 'the analog of the specialization functor i^*j_* for schemes', after passing to the completed algebraic closure), and Deligne's 'faisceaux de cycles évanescents' R^iΨ(K) (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.2) are the nearby-cycle object RΨ_η of LPV.0. The vanishing complex — Deligne's 'complexe évanescent' — is LPV.0's RΦ(K'), the third vertex of the distinguished triangle sp^*i^*K' → RΨ_η(K) → RΦ(K') → (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.2.4) on X_s ×_s η, defined for K' ∈ D^+(X_et, E) with K = K'|X_η; it depends on K', not only on K. Statement. In the setting of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/lpv-trait-comparison (A a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring, X → S locally of finite type, E a torsion ring prime to p), let K' ∈ D^+(X_et, E) and K = K'|X_η. Applying R^+Γ(X_s, −) to LPV.0's triangle and composing with the isomorphism of lpv-trait-comparison gives an I-equivariant distinguished triangle R^+Γ(X_s, i^*K') → R^+Γ(Ȳ, c^*K) → R^+Γ(X_s, RΦ(K')) → (+1), whose first map is the analytic specialization map sp_an: pullback along b = λ_X̂': Ȳ_et = d(X̂')_et → (X_s ×_A Ā)_et ≅ (X_s)_et followed by R^+Γ(Ȳ, τ) for the transformation τ: b^*i'^* → a^*j'^* of Hub96 3.5.13(i) (for X' = X ×_A Ā, applied to K'|X'). Consequently H^q(X_s, RΦ(K')) is the cohomology of the cone of sp_an; it is not H^q(Ȳ, c^*K) in general.
hypotheses: A strictly henselian discrete valuation ring; X → S locally of finite type; E a torsion ring prime to p.
K' ∈ D^+(X_et, E) on the whole of X: RΦ needs the special-fibre restriction i^*K', not only K = K'|X_η.
proofSteps: LPV.0 (SGA 7 XIII 1.3.3, 2.1.2): the first map of the triangle is sp^* applied to ī^* of the unit K' → Rj̄_*j̄^*K' on X̄; under ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/trait-nearby-cycles-agree it is i'^* of the unit K'|X' → Rj'_*j'^*(K'|X').

Hub96 3.5.13(i) constructs ψ: i'^*R^+j'_* → R^+b_*a^* as the adjoint of b^*i'^*R^+j'_* → a^*j'^*R^+j'_* → a^* (the transformation τ built from the φ_Z of (1.9.5), then the counit). By naturality of τ applied to the unit and the triangle identity for (j'^*, R^+j'_*), ψ ∘ i'^*(unit) is adjoint to τ_{K'|X'}: b^*i'^*(K'|X') → a^*j'^*(K'|X'). After R^+Γ(X_s ×_A Ā, −) = R^+Γ(X_s, −) the composite R^+Γ(X_s, i^*K') → R^+Γ(X_s, RΨ_η K) ≅ R^+Γ(Ȳ, c^*K) is therefore sp_an.

Equivariance: LPV.0's triangle is a triangle in D^+(X_s ×_s η, E), hence I-equivariant, and the isomorphism of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/lpv-trait-comparison is I-equivariant; I acts trivially on R^+Γ(X_s, i^*K').
acceptance: X = S: the triangle is K'_s → K_η̄ → RΦ(K') →, the specialization map of stalks and its cone.
X smooth over A, K' = Λ constant, ℓ ≠ p: RΦ = 0 (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.5), so sp_an is an isomorphism; for X = A^1_A this is R^+Γ(A^1_s, Λ) = Λ ≅ R^+Γ(closed unit disc over k̄^, Λ).

Nodal model X = Spec A[x, y]/(xy − π), π a uniformizer, Λ = Z/ℓ with ℓ ≠ p: X_s is two affine lines meeting in one point (H^0 = Λ, H^q = 0 for q ≥ 1); by LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles:LPV.2/ordinary-quadratic-point-nearby-cycles-3-1-2 with n = 1, RΦ(Λ) is concentrated in degree 1, supported at the node, free of rank one; the triangle gives H^0(Ȳ, Λ) = Λ, H^1(Ȳ, Λ) ≅ H^1(X_s, RΦ(Λ)) free of rank one and H^q(Ȳ, Λ) = 0 for q ≥ 2, where Ȳ is the closed annulus {|π| ≤ |x| ≤ 1} over k̄^ — the cohomology of an annulus.

nodes.title: The inertia action on the analytic generic-fibre cohomology through LPV.0's variation
nodes.statement: In the setting of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/nearby-versus-vanishing-cycles (A a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring, X → S locally of finite type, E a torsion ring prime to p, K' ∈ D^+(X_et, E), K = K'|X_η), for σ ∈ I let Var(σ): RΦ(K') → RΨ_η(K) be LPV.0's variation (SGA 7 XIII 1.4.3.1, 2.1.2.5) and q: RΨ_η(K) → RΦ(K') the second map of LPV.0's triangle. Transported along the I-equivariant isomorphism of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/lpv-trait-comparison, the endomorphism σ − 1 of H^n(Ȳ, c^*K) is the composite H^n(Ȳ, c^*K) → H^n(X_s, RΦ(K')) → H^n(X_s, RΨ_η K) ≅ H^n(Ȳ, c^*K) of the second map of the analytic triangle of nearby-versus-vanishing-cycles and H^n(Var(σ)), and Var(στ) = Var(σ)qVar(τ) + Var(σ) + Var(τ). In particular I acts trivially on H^n(Ȳ, c^*K) when RΦ(K') = 0. LPV.1's monodromy operator N, defined for a unipotent action on the E[I]-module H^n(X_s, RΨ_η K), is transported to H^n(Ȳ, c^*K) by the same isomorphism; no analytic monodromy operator is constructed separately.
hypotheses: As in ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/nearby-versus-vanishing-cycles; I acts trivially on the special-fibre part (SGA 7 XIII 1.4.3).
For N: the action on H^n is unipotent, as LPV.1 requires.
proofSteps: LPV.0 variation (SGA 7 XIII 1.4.3.2, 1.4.3.4): σ = 1 + Var(σ)q on RΨ_η(K) in D(X_s ×_s η, E) and the cocycle rule; apply H^n(X_s, −).

Transport along the I-equivariant isomorphism of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/lpv-trait-comparison; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/nearby-versus-vanishing-cycles identifies H^n(q) with the second map of the analytic triangle.
Monodromy operator: LPV.1's N is defined from the E[I]-module structure alone, so an isomorphism of E[I]-modules transports it.
acceptance: X smooth over A, K' = Λ constant, ℓ ≠ p: RΦ = 0 (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.5) and I acts trivially on H^n(Ȳ, Λ); for X = A^1_A this is the trivial action on the cohomology of the closed unit disc over k̄^.
X = S: σ − 1 on K_η̄ factors through RΦ(K') = cone(K'_s → K_η̄), as in SGA 7 XIII 1.4.3.

nodes.title: Geometric field pairs, their extensions, and the surjectivity condition
nodes.statement: A geometric field pair is a complete Huber pair (C, C⁺) (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair`) in which C is an algebraically closed field, complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value, and C⁺ ⊆ C is an open and bounded valuation subring, so that C°° ⊆ C⁺ ⊆ O_C := C° and C⁺ may have any rank ≥ 1 (rank one exactly when C⁺ = O_C). Its spectrum S(C, C⁺) := Spa(C, C⁺) is the source of the geometric points of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points. An extension of geometric field pairs ι: (C, C⁺) → (C', C'⁺) is a morphism of Huber pairs, i.e. a continuous ring homomorphism ι: C → C' with ι(C⁺) ⊆ C'⁺; it is injective, ι⁻¹(O_{C'}) = O_C, and it induces the morphism of adic spaces g_ι := Spa(ι): Spa(C', C'⁺) → Spa(C, C⁺) (Tau Ceti `Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap`), which sends the point of Spa(C', C'⁺) with valuation ring V' (C'⁺ ⊆ V' ⊆ O_{C'}) to the point with valuation ring ι⁻¹(V'). Every morphism of adic spaces Spa(C', C'⁺) → Spa(C, C⁺) arises from a unique extension (global sections). The extension is surjective if g_ι is surjective on underlying sets; this is the condition 'X₁ → X₃ surjective' of ECD Lemma 16.3, and by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/surjectivity-criterion-for-field-pair-extensions it holds if and only if ι⁻¹(C'⁺) = C⁺. No condition relates the ranks of C⁺ and C'⁺, C'/C need not be algebraic, and C, C' may have characteristic 0 or p.
hypotheses: C, C' algebraically closed, complete for nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute values (if the residue characteristic is p > 0, i.e. |p| < 1, these are exactly the algebraically closed perfectoid fields: C is not discretely valued and Frobenius is surjective on O_C/p, so PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-characterisation applies; in residue characteristic 0, e.g. the completed algebraic closure of ℂ((t)), C is not perfectoid, and the nodes of this stage that use perfectoid spaces over C need residue characteristic p).
C⁺, C'⁺ open and bounded valuation subrings, of arbitrary rank.
ι continuous with ι(C⁺) ⊆ C'⁺; surjectivity is a property of ι, not part of the data.
proofSteps: The pair (C, C⁺) is a Huber pair: C⁺ is open (it contains C°°), integrally closed (a valuation ring) and contained in C° (bounded), so it is a ring of integral elements (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair).

ι is injective (C is a field, ι(1) = 1) and ι⁻¹(O_{C'}) = O_C: the pullback of the rank-one valuation of C' along the continuous ι is a continuous rank-one valuation of C, hence equivalent to that of C (mathlib:ValuationSubring.comap, mathlib:ValuationSubring.mem_comap).
g_ι := tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap applied to ι; on points it is restriction of valuations, whose valuation ring is ι⁻¹(V') (mathlib:ValuationSubring.comap).
The surjectivity criterion and the description of the image are ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/surjectivity-criterion-for-field-pair-extensions.
acceptance: For C⁺ = O_C (rank one) every extension is surjective; for C⁺ ⊊ O_C the identity extension (C, C⁺) → (C, O_C) is not surjective (its image is the generic point).
ECD Lemma 14.5(ii) replaces Spa(C₃, C₃⁺) by the smaller of the two (generalising) images, after which both extensions are surjective.
