nodes.title: The image of Spa(C', C'⁺) → Spa(C, C⁺) and the criterion ι⁻¹(C'⁺) = C⁺ for surjectivity
nodes.statement: Let ι: (C, C⁺) → (C', C'⁺) be an extension of geometric field pairs (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/geometric-field-pair-extension) and g = g_ι. (i) The points of Spa(C, C⁺) are the valuation subrings V of C with C⁺ ⊆ V ⊆ O_C; they form a chain, a point V₂ is a specialisation of V₁ iff V₂ ⊆ V₁, the closed point s is C⁺, the generic point η is O_C, and every point is a generalisation of s. (ii) g(V') = ι⁻¹(V'), and g maps the closed point s' of Spa(C', C'⁺) to the point W := ι⁻¹(C'⁺) ⊇ C⁺. (iii) The image of g is the set of generalisations of W, i.e. {V : W ⊆ V ⊆ O_C}; in particular g is generalising. (iv) Consequently the following are equivalent: g is surjective; g(s') = s; ι⁻¹(C'⁺) = C⁺. (v) If C⁺ = O_C then ι is surjective, and a composite of surjective extensions is surjective.
hypotheses: ι an extension of geometric field pairs (no condition on ranks).
proofSteps: (i) AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (i) (|Spa(C, C⁺)| is the chain of valuation rings between C⁺ and O_C, unique closed point, every point specialises to s). The chain property is mathlib:ValuationSubring.linearOrderOverring (overrings of a valuation subring are totally ordered) applied to C⁺; the order-reversing identification of overrings with prime ideals is mathlib:ValuationSubring.primeSpectrumEquiv. The description of generalisations as larger valuation rings on the same field is the Berkeley lectures' Proposition 4.2.5.

(ii) g is restriction of valuations along ι (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap); the valuation ring of the pullback is the comap (mathlib:ValuationSubring.comap, mathlib:ValuationSubring.mem_comap).

(iii) Images of generalisations are generalisations (restriction preserves inclusions of valuation rings), so the image lies in {V ⊇ W}. Conversely let W ⊆ V ⊆ O_C. By mathlib:ValuationSubring.primeSpectrumEquiv, V corresponds to a prime of W, and the primes of a valuation ring correspond order-reversingly to the convex subgroups of its value group (Bourbaki, Commutative Algebra VI §4.3; not in the pinned libraries), so V corresponds to a convex subgroup Δ of the value group Γ_W of W, and Γ_W ⊆ Γ' := value group of C'⁺ because W = ι⁻¹(C'⁺) (the valuation of W is the restriction of that of C'⁺). Let Δ' be the convex hull of Δ in Γ'; then Δ' ∩ Γ_W = Δ because Δ is convex in Γ_W. The overring V' of C'⁺ attached to Δ' satisfies ι⁻¹(V') = V. Since V ⊆ O_C, Δ lies in the convex subgroup of O_C, whose convex hull in Γ' lies in that of O_{C'} (ι⁻¹(O_{C'}) = O_C), so V' ⊆ O_{C'} and V' is a point of Spa(C', C'⁺) with g(V') = V.

(iv) By (iii) the image is all of the chain iff it contains s = C⁺ iff W = C⁺, and W is the image of s'. This is the Spa clause of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-exports/surjective-valuation-base-change, which also identifies it with surjectivity of Spec C'⁺ → Spec C⁺ (ι|_{C⁺} injective and local).
(v) If C⁺ = O_C the chain is one point. For κ ∘ ι: (κ ∘ ι)⁻¹(C''⁺) = ι⁻¹(κ⁻¹(C''⁺)) = ι⁻¹(C'⁺) = C⁺ (mathlib:ValuationSubring.comap, `comap_comap`).
acceptance: Rank two: let C⁺ ⊊ O_C be of rank two and ι = id: (C, C⁺) → (C, O_C). Then W = O_C and the image is {η} ≠ Spa(C, C⁺).
ECD Lemma 14.5(ii): the images of Spa(C_i, C_i⁺) → Spa(C₃, C₃⁺) (i = 1, 2) are generalising, hence nested, by (iii).

nodes.title: Étale cohomology over Spa(C, C⁺) is the stalk at the closed point; the comparison map is a base-change map
nodes.statement: Let (C, C⁺) be a geometric field pair, S = Spa(C, C⁺) with closed point s. (i) Every étale morphism V → S is, locally on V, an open immersion; the étale topos of S is equivalent to the topos of sheaves on the topological space |S| (the chain of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/surjectivity-criterion-for-field-pair-extensions), the stalk of an étale sheaf at a geometric point with support t is its topological stalk at t, and, since S is the only open subset containing s, the global-sections functor Γ(S_ét, −) is the stalk functor at s: it is exact, H⁰(S_ét, G) = G_s and Hⁱ(S_ét, G) = 0 for i > 0, for every abelian sheaf G. (ii) For every morphism f: Y → S of locally strongly sheafy analytic adic spaces (for instance Y locally of finite type over S, or Y perfectoid) and every abelian sheaf F on Y_ét, Hⁱ(Y_ét, F) ≅ (Rⁱf_*F)_s naturally in F. (iii) For an extension ι: (C, C⁺) → (C', C'⁺) with g = g_ι: S' → S, Y' = Y ×_S S', g_Y: Y' → Y and f': Y' → S', the pullback map g_Y^*: Hⁱ(Y_ét, F) → Hⁱ(Y'_ét, g_Y^*F) is identified, via (ii) for f and f', with the base-change map (Rⁱf_*F)_{g(s')} = (g^*Rⁱf_*F)_{s'} → (Rⁱf'_*g_Y^*F)_{s'} precomposed with the specialisation map (Rⁱf_*F)_s → (Rⁱf_*F)_{g(s')}; if ι is surjective, g(s') = s and the specialisation map is the identity.
hypotheses: S the spectrum of a geometric field pair; statements (ii)-(iii) for sheaves of abelian groups (the same holds for complexes in D⁺).
proofSteps: (i) An étale morphism is, locally on the source, an open immersion into a finite étale space (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-morphism), and finite étale spaces over S are finite disjoint unions of copies of S (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (ii)); so V → S is a local isomorphism onto open subsets, the open subsets of S form a dense subsite of S_ét, S_ét^∼ ≃ Sh(|S|), and étale stalks are topological stalks (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points (c)-(d)); through every point over s there is even a section which is an open immersion (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (iii)). Two sections through the same point agree, their equaliser being an open subset (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-diagonal) containing s, hence S. The only open neighbourhood of s is S (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (i)), so G_s = G(S); an exact functor has vanishing higher derived functors.

(ii) The Leray spectral sequence Hᵖ(S_ét, R^qf_*F) ⇒ H^{p+q}(Y_ét, F) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/leray-spectral-sequence (b), on the derived direct images of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image) degenerates by (i).

(iii) Naturality of the Leray identification for the square (f, f', g, g_Y) and the base-change transformation g^*Rf_* → Rf'_*g_Y^* (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image); the stalk of g^*G at s' is G_{g(s')} (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points (d)); by (i) for S the map H⁰(S, G) = G_s → G_{g(s')} is the specialisation map of the chain, the identity when g(s') = s (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/surjectivity-criterion-for-field-pair-extensions (iv)).
acceptance: Y = S, F = j_!M for the open {η} ⊊ S (C⁺ of rank two): H⁰(S, j_!M) = (j_!M)_s = 0, while the stalk at η is M; along the non-surjective (C, C⁺) → (C, O_C) the comparison map of (iii) is the map 0 → M, as the specialisation map predicts.
ECD Proposition 14.3, proof: the global-sections functor on Spa(C, C⁺)_ét is exact and is a point.

nodes.title: Invariance of prime-to-p étale cohomology with supports under surjective algebraically closed base extension (Hub96 4.1.1(c) in the form of ECD Lemma 16.3)
nodes.statement: Let ι: (C, C⁺) → (C', C'⁺) be a surjective extension of geometric field pairs (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/geometric-field-pair-extension), S = Spa(C, C⁺), S' = Spa(C', C'⁺), p ≥ 1 the characteristic exponent of the residue field of O_C (the residue characteristic, or 1 if it is 0), n ≥ 1 an integer prime to p and M a ℤ/nℤ-module. Let (R, R⁺) be a complete Huber pair with a morphism of pairs (C, C⁺) → (R, R⁺) such that R is topologically of finite type over C (a C-affinoid algebra) and R⁺ ⊆ R° is any open integrally closed subring containing the image of C⁺; put Y := Spa(R, R⁺) (an affinoid adic space over S, noetherian, of weakly finite type over S) and Y' := Y ×_S S' = Spa(R ⊗̂_C C', (R ⊗̂_C C')⁺), the completed tensor product with plus ring the closure of the integral closure of the image of R⁺ ⊗_{C⁺} C'⁺ (R ⊗̂_C C' is topologically of finite type over C'), with projection g_Y: Y' → Y. Let U ⊆ Y be a quasicompact open subset, j: U → Y, U' := g_Y⁻¹(U) (quasicompact open) and j': U' → Y'. Then for every i ≥ 0 the pullback map g_Y^*: Hⁱ(Y_ét, j_!M) → Hⁱ(Y'_ét, g_Y^*j_!M) = Hⁱ(Y'_ét, j'_!M) is bijective. The case U = Y is the invariance of Hⁱ(Y_ét, M); for U = ∅ both sides vanish. The theorem is not asserted when p divides n, nor for non-surjective ι (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/cohomology-over-geometric-field-pairs, acceptance).
hypotheses: ι surjective, i.e. ι⁻¹(C'⁺) = C⁺ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/surjectivity-criterion-for-field-pair-extensions).
n prime to the residue characteristic exponent p; M any ℤ/nℤ-module (not necessarily finite).

R a C-affinoid algebra (quotient of some C⟨T₁, …, T_m⟩); R⁺ any ring of integral elements containing the image of C⁺, so that Y → S is of weakly finite type (higher-rank plus rings allowed). If C⁺ = O_C and the morphism of pairs is required to be topologically of finite type, then R⁺ = R° (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded); the theorem does not need that requirement.
U quasicompact open in Y, not necessarily rational; no hypothesis on the ranks of C⁺, C'⁺.
proofSteps: Set-up. Y' exists and is affinoid (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product, with sheafiness from AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability since R ⊗̂_C C' is topologically of finite type over C'); U' is quasicompact because g_Y is quasicompact (affinoid source); g_Y^*j_! = j'_!(g_Y|_{U'})^* (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero: extension by zero commutes with pullback along any morphism for the preimage of the open).

Reformulation (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/cohomology-over-geometric-field-pairs (ii)-(iii)): with f: Y → S, f': Y' → S', the claim is that the base-change map (Rⁱf_*(j_!M))_s → (Rⁱf'_*(j'_!M))_{s'} for the geometric point g_ι: S' → S is bijective; surjectivity of ι is used exactly to have g_ι(s') = s (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/surjectivity-criterion-for-field-pair-extensions (iv)).

Classical input: this base change is Huber's Theorem 4.1.1(c) for the qcqs morphism f, as restated and applied by ECD in the proof of Lemma 16.3 (and cited by Hansen as Huber's general qcqs base change theorem 4.1.1(c)'). The algebraizable case is supplied by H1: for a finitely presented C⁺-scheme X with tubes Z ⊆ d(X^) and Z' ⊆ d((X ⊗_{C⁺} C'⁺)^) over the closed points of Spa(C, C⁺) and Spa(C', C'⁺), pullback RΓ(Z, c^*K) → RΓ(Z', c'^*K') is an isomorphism for K ∈ D⁺ with prime-to-p torsion coefficients, in particular for K = j_{V!}M with V ⊆ X_C Zariski open (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-exports/tube-cohomology-invariance-export, resting on the invariance of nearby-cycle cohomology along the surjective map Spec C'⁺ → Spec C⁺, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-exports/nearby-cycle-invariance-under-surjective-base-change (Hub96 4.2.7, with the prime-to-p base change Hub96 4.2.4 of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-nearby-cycles), and on the formal/adic comparison ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-exports/formal-adic-compatibility, i.e. Hub96 3.5.11, 3.5.13 and 3.5.16 of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison). The passage from these algebraizable tubes to the present generality (affinoids of topologically finite type that are not completions of finitely presented C⁺-algebras, arbitrary plus rings R⁺, and extension by zero from quasicompact adic opens U that are not Zariski open) is Huber's reduction in Hub96 §4.1, through strict localisations and their limits (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-formula-strict-localisation, Hub96 2.6.1; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity, Hub96 2.4.6) and the henselian comparisons (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/pro-special-comparison-theorem-3-2-1, /relative-comparison-3-2-9-3-2-12); it is not public and is recorded as a gap. The surjectivity hypothesis enters the H1 input as surjectivity of Spec C'⁺ → Spec C⁺ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:valuation-exports/surjective-valuation-base-change).

Public cross-check (not a proof step): for C⁺ = O_C, C'⁺ = O_{C'} and U = Y, Berkovich's Theorem 7.6.1 proves the analogue for k-analytic spaces (torsion prime to the residue characteristic), by induction on dimension through his weak base change theorem 5.3.1 and the case of curves; transferring it to adic spaces and to extension by zero from arbitrary quasicompact opens needs Huber's comparison of the two étale topoi (Hub96 §8.3), which is not public.
acceptance: Y = S (R = C, R⁺ = C⁺): for U = S both sides are M in degree 0 and 0 in positive degrees; for a quasicompact open U ⊊ S both sides vanish in all degrees (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/cohomology-over-geometric-field-pairs (i), s ∉ U, and s' ∉ U' by surjectivity). This is ECD Lemma 16.3 for X₂ = X₃.
ECD's instance: C, C' of characteristic p, R topologically of finite type over C with any R⁺, U any quasicompact open (the proof of ECD Lemma 16.3, after reduction to X₂ = Spa(R_perf, R⁺_perf)).
Surjectivity cannot be dropped: for C⁺ of rank two, ι = id: (C, C⁺) → (C, O_C), Y = S and U = {η}, the left side is H⁰(S, j_!M) = 0 and the right side is H⁰(Spa(C, O_C), M) = M.

nodes.title: Approximation of an affinoid perfectoid space over Spa(C, C⁺) by affinoids of topologically finite type
nodes.statement: Let (C, C⁺) be a geometric field pair, S = Spa(C, C⁺), and X = Spa(R, R⁺) an affinoid perfectoid space over S, i.e. (R, R⁺) a complete perfectoid Tate pair with a morphism of Huber pairs (C, C⁺) → (R, R⁺) (any characteristic; PerfectoidSpaces:P2/affinoid-perfectoid-space). For a finite subset I ⊆ R⁺ let S_I ⊆ R be the image of the continuous C-algebra map C⟨T_i : i ∈ I⟩ → R, T_i ↦ i, with the quotient topology, and let S_I⁺ ⊆ S_I be the integral closure of the subring generated by the image of C⁺, the elements of I and S_I°°. Put Y_I := Spa(S_I, S_I⁺) and let φ_I: X → Y_I be induced by the inclusion. Then: (i) S_I is a reduced C-affinoid algebra, (S_I, S_I⁺) is a complete Huber pair with S_I⁺ ⊆ R⁺, Y_I is a noetherian affinoid adic space over S (strongly noetherian, not perfectoid in general), and for I ⊆ J the inclusion S_I ⊆ S_J is a morphism of pairs, so I ↦ Y_I is a cofiltered system over S indexed by the finite subsets of R⁺ with compatible φ_I; (ii) R = ⋃_I S_I and R⁺ = ⋃_I S_I⁺ inside R, and the ϖ-adic topology of R⁺ = colim_I S_I⁺ is that of R (no completion is needed); (iii) |X| → lim_I |Y_I| is a homeomorphism of spectral spaces, every quasicompact open (resp. rational) subset of X is φ_I⁻¹ of a quasicompact open (resp. rational) subset of some Y_I, and two quasicompact opens of Y_I with equal preimages in X have equal preimages in some Y_J; (iv) X ~ lim_I Y_I is a perfectoid tilde-limit (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit) and hence X ~′ lim_I Y_I in the sense of Scholze 2012 Definition 7.14 (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/residue-field-tilde-limit): X is a tilde-limit of the analytic approximation spaces Y_I, which are not perfectoid, and not a categorical limit of them; (v) if char C = p, the completed perfections Y_I^perf := Spa(S_I^perf∧, S_I^{+,perf∧}) are perfectoid, Y_I^perf ~ lim_Φ Y_I with |Y_I^perf| = |Y_I| and Y_I^perf_ét ≃ Y_I,ét, and X = lim_I Y_I^perf is a limit in perfectoid spaces (the presentation of ECD Lemma 16.3), so that X_ét,qcqs ≃ 2-colim_I (Y_I^perf)_ét,qcqs; for C⁺ = O_C one has S_I⁺ = S_I° and (Y_I^perf) is the p-finite system of Scholze 2012 Lemma 6.13 with K = C; (vi) if W_I ⊆ Y_I are rational subsets containing φ_I(X), compatible under the transition maps, then (W_I) with the restricted φ_I satisfies (iii) and (iv) as well.
hypotheses: (C, C⁺) a geometric field pair; X affinoid perfectoid over S; any characteristic for (i)-(iv), (vi); characteristic p for (v).
R⁺ need not be an O_C-algebra (C⁺ may have higher rank): this is why S_I⁺ is built from C⁺, I and S_I°° rather than taken to be S_I° as in Scholze 2012 Lemma 6.13, where R⁺ is a K°-algebra.
proofSteps: (i) C⟨T_I⟩ → R is continuous (the i ∈ I are power-bounded) and its kernel is closed, so S_I is a C-affinoid algebra; it is reduced because R is uniform, hence reduced. S_I° is bounded (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/reduced-affinoid-supremum-norm), S_I⁺ ⊆ S_I° is open (it contains S_I°°) and integrally closed, so (S_I, S_I⁺) is a Huber pair. S_I → R is continuous, so S_I°° maps into R°° ⊆ R⁺; C⁺ and I map into R⁺, which is integrally closed, hence S_I⁺ ⊆ R⁺. S_I is strongly noetherian (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian for affinoid algebras; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy), so Y_I is an adic space. For I ⊆ J, C⟨T_I⟩ → C⟨T_J⟩ induces S_I ⊆ S_J, continuous, carrying S_I°° into S_J°° and hence S_I⁺ into S_J⁺.
(ii) For r ∈ R⁺, r is the image of T_r in S_{{r}}⁺; R = R⁺[1/ϖ] with ϖ ∈ C. R⁺ is open and bounded in the uniform ring R, so its ϖ-adic topology is the topology of R.

(iii) PerfectoidSpaces:P5/spa-of-filtered-colimit-of-tate-pairs (a)-(c) with A_{I,0} = S_I⁺ (a ring of definition containing ϖ): Spa(R, R⁺) = Spa(colim S_I, colim S_I⁺) → lim Spa(S_I, S_I⁺) is a homeomorphism compatible with rational subsets; the limit of spectral spaces along spectral maps is spectral (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces); quasicompact opens and their equalities descend by PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces (a)-(b).

(iv) Sectionwise density holds with U = X, since ⋃_I S_I = R (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit, final clause, R perfectoid); the Y_I are qcqs locally noetherian, so PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit gives X ~′ lim Y_I. A tilde-limit is not a categorical limit in adic spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfectoid-tilde-limit, convention (iv)).

(v) PerfectoidSpaces:P7/perfection-tilde-limit (Y_I^perf ~ lim_Φ Y_I, homeomorphic projections) and PerfectoidSpaces:P7/etale-topos-invariance-under-inseparable-towers (Scholze 2012 Corollary 7.19); R⁺ is perfect, so ⋃_I (S_I⁺)^{1/p^∞} = R⁺ and R⁺/ϖᵐ = colim_I S_I^{+,perf∧}/ϖᵐ as in the proof of Scholze 2012 Lemma 6.13(i), whence X = lim_I Y_I^perf (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/cofiltered-limits-of-affinoid-perfectoid-spaces) and the 2-colimit description of X_ét,qcqs (PerfectoidSpaces:P5/finite-stage-descent-of-qcqs-etale-objects). For C⁺ = O_C, S_I⁺ contains the image of O_C⟨T_I⟩ (its tail lies in S_I°°), so S_I⁺ = S_I° by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-power-bounded-integral, and the system is that of PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-direct-limits-of-p-finite-affinoids.

(vi) A rational W_I containing φ_I(X) has φ_I⁻¹(W_I) = X; restriction of the system to such subsets keeps (iii) (a closed subset of the limit containing the image of |X|) and (iv) (the maps O(Y_I) → R factor through O(W_I)); cf. PerfectoidSpaces:P5/limit-restriction-to-rational-subsets.
acceptance: X = S: S_I = C and S_I⁺ = C⁺ for all I, so Y_I = S and the system is constant.

The perfectoid closed unit disc X = Spa(C⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩, R⁺) over S in characteristic p, R⁺ the completed integral closure of C⁺[T^{1/p^∞}] + C°°⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩: for I = {T} one gets S_I = C⟨T⟩ with S_I⁺ the integral closure of C⁺[T] + C°°⟨T⟩, the classical disc over S, and for I = {T^{1/pᵏ}} the disc in the variable T^{1/pᵏ}.

nodes.title: Base change of the finite-type approximation along an extension of geometric field pairs
nodes.statement: In the situation of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/finite-type-approximation-of-perfectoid-affinoids, let ι: (C, C⁺) → (C', C'⁺) be an extension of geometric field pairs (not necessarily surjective), S' = Spa(C', C'⁺), X' := X ×_S S' and Y_I' := Y_I ×_S S' (or W_I ×_S S' for a restricted system as in (vi) there). Then: (i) X' = Spa(R ⊗̂_C C', (R ⊗̂_C C')⁺) is affinoid perfectoid and Y_I' = Spa(S_I ⊗̂_C C', (S_I ⊗̂_C C')⁺) is a noetherian affinoid adic space topologically of finite type over S'; (ii) the images of the S_I ⊗̂_C C' in R ⊗̂_C C' have dense union, the plus ring of X' is the closure of the integral closure of the union of the images of the plus rings of the Y_I', and X' ~ lim_I Y_I', hence X' ~′ lim_I Y_I' and |X'| ≅ lim_I |Y_I'|; (iii) for a quasicompact open U_I ⊆ Y_I, the preimage in X' of φ_I⁻¹(U_I) is the preimage of U_I' := (Y_I' → Y_I)⁻¹(U_I) under X' → Y_I'.
hypotheses: The approximation system of the base; ι any extension of geometric field pairs.
proofSteps: (i) PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property (X' affinoid perfectoid; C' is perfectoid); AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product with AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability for Y_I'.

PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-from-completed-colimit (Tate case, compatible pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ C) gives the homeomorphism, the density and, R ⊗̂_C C' being perfectoid, X' ~ lim Y_I'; PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limit-implies-residue-field-tilde-limit gives ~′.

nodes.title: Invariance of prime-to-p étale cohomology with supports of affinoid perfectoid spaces under surjective algebraically closed base extension
nodes.statement: Let ι: (C, C⁺) → (C', C'⁺) be a surjective extension of geometric field pairs, S = Spa(C, C⁺), S' = Spa(C', C'⁺), p the residue characteristic exponent, n prime to p and M a ℤ/nℤ-module. Let X = Spa(R, R⁺) be an affinoid perfectoid space over S (any characteristic), X' := X ×_S S' (affinoid perfectoid) with projection g_X: X' → X, U ⊆ X a quasicompact open subset, j: U → X, U' := g_X⁻¹(U) and j': U' → X'. Then for every i ≥ 0 the pullback g_X^*: Hⁱ(X_ét, j_!M) → Hⁱ(X'_ét, j'_!M) is bijective, where X_ét, X'_ét are the étale sites of the perfectoid spaces (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-of-perfectoid-space). This is the assertion proved in ECD's proof of Lemma 16.3 ('more generally ... X₂ any perfectoid space over X₃'), for affinoid X₂; the proof below uses neither diamonds nor ECD Theorem 16.1 or 14.12.
hypotheses: ι surjective; n prime to p; X affinoid perfectoid over S; U quasicompact open.
proofSteps: Approximation (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/finite-type-approximation-of-perfectoid-affinoids): X ~′ lim_I Y_I with Y_I = Spa(S_I, S_I⁺) topologically of finite type over S; by (iii) there there are I₀ and a quasicompact open U_{I₀} ⊆ Y_{I₀} with U = φ_{I₀}⁻¹(U_{I₀}). For I ⊇ I₀ let U_I be the preimage of U_{I₀} in Y_I and j_I: U_I → Y_I; then j_!M = φ_I^*(j_{I!}M) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero). This is the finite-stage descent of the étale datum j_!M.

Base change (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/field-extension-of-finite-type-approximations): X' ~′ lim_I Y_I' with Y_I' = Y_I ×_S S', and j'_!M = φ_I'^*(j'_{I!}M) for j'_I: U_I' → Y_I', U_I' the preimage of U_I.

Passage to the cohomological limit (PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison (iii), i.e. Scholze 2012 Corollary 7.18, the perfectoid extension of Huber's continuity ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity): Hⁱ(X_ét, j_!M) = colim_{I ⊇ I₀} Hⁱ(Y_I,ét, j_{I!}M) and Hⁱ(X'_ét, j'_!M) = colim_{I ⊇ I₀} Hⁱ(Y'_I,ét, j'_{I!}M), and the identifications commute with the pullbacks along X' → X and Y_I' → Y_I (functoriality of pullback on cohomology, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image).

Finite level: for each I ⊇ I₀, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/invariance-for-affinoids-of-finite-type applied to (S_I, S_I⁺), U_I and ι gives bijections Hⁱ(Y_I,ét, j_{I!}M) → Hⁱ(Y'_I,ét, j'_{I!}M), compatible with the transition maps; a filtered colimit of bijections is a bijection.

The analytic approximation spaces Y_I are noetherian adic spaces to which the classical theorem applies; X and X' are their perfectoid tilde-limits. In characteristic p one may equivalently pass through the p-finite perfectoid spaces Y_I^perf ((v) of the approximation node): their étale topoi are those of the Y_I, and X = lim Y_I^perf in perfectoid spaces.
acceptance: X = S: this is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/invariance-for-affinoids-of-finite-type for Y = S, and gives ECD Lemma 16.3 for X₂ = X₃.

X the perfectoid closed unit disc over S, U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}: descends to the rational subset {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} of Y_{{T}} = the classical disc, and the theorem reduces to the classical disc and its base change to C'.

nodes.title: Cohomology of extension by zero on X₁ ×_{X₃} X₂ for spectra of geometric field pairs (ECD Lemma 16.3)
nodes.statement: Let X_k = Spa(C_k, C_k⁺), k = 1, 2, 3, be spectra of geometric field pairs and X₁ → X₃ ← X₂ morphisms (induced by extensions ι₁: (C₃, C₃⁺) → (C₁, C₁⁺), ι₂: (C₃, C₃⁺) → (C₂, C₂⁺)) with X₁ → X₃ surjective. Let j₂: U₂ → X₂ be a quasicompact open subset, assume the residue characteristic p of C₃ is positive (so that the C_k are perfectoid fields; in ECD they have characteristic p), let M be an abelian group killed by some n prime to p, W := X₁ ×_{X₃} X₂ (an affinoid perfectoid space) and j₂!M also its pullback to W. Then Hⁱ(W_ét, j₂!M) = 0 for all i ≥ 0 unless U₂ = X₂ and i = 0, in which case pullback from X₂ gives H⁰(W_ét, j₂!M) = M.
hypotheses: X₁ → X₃ surjective; no condition on X₂ → X₃; residue characteristic p > 0; n prime to p.
proofSteps: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/invariance-for-perfectoid-affinoids with (C, C⁺) = (C₃, C₃⁺), ι = ι₁, X = X₂ (affinoid perfectoid over X₃, C₂ being a perfectoid field) and U = U₂: Hⁱ(W_ét, j₂!M) ≅ Hⁱ(X₂,ét, j₂!M).

s₂ ∈ U₂ iff U₂ = X₂: X₂ is the only open subset containing its closed point s₂ (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split (i)).

nodes.title: Connectedness over Spa(C, C⁺) is detected over the generic point Spa(C, O_C)
nodes.statement: Let (C, C⁺) be a geometric field pair, S = Spa(C, C⁺) with generic point η (valuation ring O_C), and Z a quasicompact quasiseparated analytic adic space over S (for instance an affinoid perfectoid space over S, or an affinoid adic space topologically of finite type over S). Let Z° := Z ×_S Spa(C, O_C). Then (i) the projection Z° → Z is a homeomorphism onto the subspace h⁻¹(η) of points of Z lying over η (h: Z → S); for affinoid Z = Spa(A, A⁺), Z° = Spa(A, A°⁺) with A°⁺ the closure of the integral closure of A⁺·O_C, and h⁻¹(η) = {z : |c(z)| ≤ 1 for all c ∈ O_C}; (ii) every z ∈ Z has a unique maximal generalisation z̃, and z̃ ∈ Z°; (iii) Z is connected if and only if Z° is connected: a decomposition of Z into disjoint open and closed subsets restricts to one of Z°, and a decomposition Z° = A ⊔ B into disjoint open and closed subsets extends to the decomposition Z = Ā ⊔ B̄ by closures.
hypotheses: Z quasicompact and quasiseparated (so |Z| is spectral) and analytic over S.
proofSteps: (i) For affinoid Z the fibre product is the affinoid Spa(A ⊗̂_C C, ·) = Spa(A, A°⁺) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product; PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-fibre-product-universal-property in the perfectoid case), and Spa(A, A°⁺) ⊆ Spa(A, A⁺) is the subspace where |O_C| ≤ 1, i.e. where the restriction to C has valuation ring containing, hence equal to, O_C (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/surjectivity-criterion-for-field-pair-extensions (i)); the general case glues over an affinoid cover.

(ii) Generalisations of an analytic point form a chain whose maximal element is the rank-one generalisation (Berkeley Proposition 4.2.5); its restriction to C is a rank-one valuation, hence the point η.

(iii) '⇐': an open and closed A ⊆ Z is stable under generalisation, so A ≠ ∅ implies A ∩ Z° ≠ ∅ by (ii). '⇒': h⁻¹(η) is pro-constructible (the preimage of the intersection of the quasicompact open neighbourhoods of η; DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets), so A and B, being closed in Z°, are pro-constructible in Z and their closures are their sets of specialisations (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/closure-of-pro-constructible). Every z specialises its maximal generalisation z̃ ∈ Z°, so Ā ∪ B̄ = Z. If z ∈ Ā ∩ B̄ then z generalises to a ∈ A and b ∈ B, which are comparable by (ii); A and B are open and closed in Z°, hence stable under generalisation and specialisation inside Z°, a contradiction. Closures are closed, so Ā, B̄ are complementary closed, hence open, subsets.
acceptance: Z = S: Z° = {η} and both are connected.
Z = S ⊔ S (disconnected): Z° = {η} ⊔ {η}, disconnected, as (iii) requires.
ECD Lemma 14.6, proof: the reduction to C⁺ = O_C and C'⁺ = O_{C'}.

nodes.title: Connectedness of adic spaces of finite type over an algebraically closed field is invariant under complete field extension
nodes.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value, C' a complete nonarchimedean field extension of C (not necessarily algebraically closed), and Y a quasi-separated adic space locally of finite type over Spa(C, O_C), with Y' := Y ×_{Spa(C,O_C)} Spa(C', O_{C'}). Then Y is connected if and only if Y' is connected. For affinoid Y = Spa(A, A°) (A a C-affinoid algebra) this says: A has no idempotents other than 0 and 1 iff A ⊗̂_C C' has none.
hypotheses: C algebraically closed (so every nonempty quasi-separated rigid space over C has a C-rational point); C'/C any complete extension.
Y quasi-separated, locally of finite type over Spa(C, O_C) (rank-one base; the higher-rank case is reduced to this one by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/connectedness-via-maximal-generalisations).
proofSteps: Connectedness and idempotents: for a sheafy adic space, decompositions into disjoint open and closed subsets correspond to idempotents of global sections (sheaf property); for a rigid space, disjoint admissible covers correspond to idempotents of Γ(Z, O_Z) (Conrad §2.1). For Y = r(X), X quasi-separated rigid (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-quasi-separated-equivalence), the ringed topoi agree (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-topos-equivalence), so Y is connected iff X is.

Base field extension: Y' = r_{C'}(X ×_C C') for Conrad's ground-field extension of quasi-separated rigid spaces (affinoid-locally Sp(A) ↦ Sp(A ⊗̂_C C')); for affinoid Y this is the affinoid fibre product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-fibre-product), and in general the compatibility of r with ground-field extension is supplied by AdicSpacesPartII:R1.
X has a C-rational point: residue fields of C-affinoid algebras at maximal ideals are finite over C, hence equal to C (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite).

Conrad's Theorem 3.2.1: a quasi-separated connected rigid space with a k-rational point stays connected after any extension k'/k. For k algebraically closed, Conrad's proof reduces to a connected affinoid Sp(A) and shows that Spec of the reduction Ã stays connected over the residue field of C' (EGA IV₂ 4.4.4 for k̃ algebraically closed, which is tauceti:TauCeti.connectedSpace_primeSpectrum_tensorProduct_of_isAlgClosed: a connected algebra over an algebraically closed field stays connected after any field extension), using the isomorphism Ã ⊗_{k̃} k̃' ≅ (A ⊗̂_k k')~ (Bosch, supplied by AdicSpacesPartII:R0).

Converse: Y' → Y is surjective (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points; every point of Y has a compatible point over Spa(C', O_{C'})), so a nontrivial decomposition of Y pulls back to a nontrivial one of Y'.
acceptance: The closed unit disc Spa(C⟨T⟩, O_C⟨T⟩) is connected and so is its base change to any C'.
The affinoid Spa(C⟨T⟩/(T² − T)) (two points) is disconnected, and stays so over C'.

nodes.title: Connected affinoid perfectoid spaces over Spa(C, C⁺) stay connected after algebraically closed base extension (ECD Lemma 14.6)
nodes.statement: Let (C, C⁺) be a geometric field pair, X = Spa(C, C⁺), Z → X a connected affinoid perfectoid space over X, and X' = Spa(C', C'⁺) → X the spectrum of a geometric field pair with any morphism to X (an extension ι, not necessarily surjective). Then Z' := Z ×_X X' is connected (and nonempty). C may have characteristic 0 or p.
hypotheses: Z connected (in particular nonempty) affinoid perfectoid over X; X' → X arbitrary.
proofSteps: Rank reduction (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/connectedness-via-maximal-generalisations): Z° := Z ×_X Spa(C, O_C) is connected, and Z' is connected if Z'° := Z' ×_{X'} Spa(C', O_{C'}) is. Since ι⁻¹(O_{C'}) = O_C, Spa(C', O_{C'}) → X factors through Spa(C, O_C) (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/surjectivity-criterion-for-field-pair-extensions (ii)), so Z'° = Z° ×_{Spa(C,O_C)} Spa(C', O_{C'}) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/fibre-product-associativity-and-unit), and Z° is affinoid perfectoid. Hence assume C⁺ = O_C and C'⁺ = O_{C'}.
Approximation (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/finite-type-approximation-of-perfectoid-affinoids): Z ~′ lim_I Y_I with Y_I = Spa(S_I, S_I°) the adic spaces of reduced C-affinoid algebras.

Connected members: each Y_I has finitely many connected components, each an open and closed rational subset (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-locally-finitely-many-components); as Z is connected and nonempty, φ_I(Z) lies in exactly one of them, Y_I⁰; for I ⊆ J the transition map sends the connected Y_J⁰ into Y_I⁰ (its image is connected and meets Y_I⁰). By (vi) of the approximation node, Z ~′ lim_I Y_I⁰ and |Z| ≅ lim_I |Y_I⁰|.

Base change (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/field-extension-of-finite-type-approximations): |Z'| ≅ lim_I |Y_I⁰'| with Y_I⁰' := Y_I⁰ ×_X X', a spectral space; Z' is nonempty because Z' → Z is surjective (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points).

Finite-stage descent of a disconnection: if Z' = A ⊔ B with A, B nonempty, open and closed (hence quasicompact), then by PerfectoidSpaces:P5/quasicompact-opens-in-limits-of-spectral-spaces (a)-(d) there is J with quasicompact opens A_J, B_J ⊆ Y_J⁰' that are open and closed, complementary and have preimages A, B, hence are nonempty: Y_J⁰' is disconnected.
Contradiction with ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2/geometric-connectedness-of-finite-type-spaces, since Y_J⁰ is a connected affinoid topologically of finite type over Spa(C, O_C).

nodes.title: Taut locally spectral spaces and taut morphisms
nodes.statement: A locally spectral space T (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/locally-spectral-space) is taut if it is quasi-separated (the intersection of two quasi-compact open subsets is quasi-compact) and the closure of every quasi-compact open subset of T is quasi-compact; for quasi-separated T this is equivalent to asking that the closure of every quasi-compact subset be quasi-compact. A spectral map g : T' → T of locally spectral spaces is taut if g⁻¹(W) is taut for every taut open subset W ⊆ T. An adic space, or a morphism of adic spaces, is taut if its underlying locally spectral space, or spectral map, is. Examples fixed by the definition: every quasi-compact quasi-separated space is taut; a quasi-separated space admitting a locally finite covering by quasi-compact open subsets is taut; every quasi-compact quasi-separated spectral map is taut; the composite of taut maps is taut. Non-example: the adic space obtained by gluing two copies of the closed unit disc over an analytic field along the complement of the origin is not taut, because that complement is not quasi-compact.
hypotheses: T locally spectral; quasi-separatedness is part of the definition, never an extra hypothesis
tautness of a morphism quantifies over taut open subsets of the target, not over quasi-compact ones
proofSteps: Equivalence of the two forms for quasi-separated T: if A ⊆ T is quasi-compact, cover A by finitely many quasi-compact opens with union U; then closure(A) ⊆ closure(U), which is quasi-compact, and closure(A) is closed in it, hence quasi-compact (mathlib:IsCompact, mathlib:closure).
qcqs spaces: the closure of any subset is a closed subset of a quasi-compact space, hence quasi-compact.

Locally finite quasi-compact covers: let T = ⋃ V_i be locally finite with V_i quasi-compact open and U ⊆ T quasi-compact open; U meets only finitely many V_i (every point of U has a neighbourhood meeting finitely many V_i, and U is quasi-compact). If x ∈ closure(U) and x ∈ V_j, the open V_j meets U, so V_j is one of those finitely many; hence closure(U) lies in a finite union of the V_i, which is quasi-compact, and is closed in it (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 8.1.10).
Composition: for g : T' → T and h : T'' → T' taut and W ⊆ T taut open, g⁻¹(W) is a taut open subset of T', so h⁻¹(g⁻¹(W)) is taut.

Non-example: in the doubled closed disc the two copies D_1, D_2 of the closed disc are quasi-compact open subsets whose intersection is the punctured disc {0 < |T| ≤ 1}, which is not quasi-compact; so the space is not quasi-separated and hence not taut (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 8.1.11).
acceptance: The closed unit disc Spa(K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) and every affinoid adic space are taut.
The analytic affine line A^{1,ad}_K (AdicSpacesPartII:R1/analytic-affine-space) is taut: the annuli {|ϖ|^{-k} ≤ |T| ≤ |ϖ|^{-k-1}} and the unit disc form a locally finite quasi-compact open cover.
The doubled disc of Kedlaya–Liu Remark 8.1.11 is not taut.

nodes.title: Compactifiable morphisms: the classical eligible class for proper support
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space). f is compactifiable if it is separated (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-morphism), locally of +weakly finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/plus-weakly-finite-type) and taut (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/taut-spaces-and-morphisms). This is the class on which Huber's proper-support direct image R⁺f_! is defined; it is the class 'separated, taut, locally +-weakly finite type' of Zavyalov's comparison with Hub96 Theorem 5.4.3. Distinguished subclasses: 𝓘, the quasi-compact open immersions; 𝓟, the proper morphisms (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/universally-closed-and-proper-morphism); 𝓔, the compactifiable morphisms that are quasi-compact (equivalently of +weakly finite type). The class contains every proper morphism, every quasi-compact open immersion, every open immersion with taut source, every separated quasi-compact étale morphism (Hub96 Lemma 5.1.3(iv), as quoted by Zavyalov), every separated smooth morphism of finite type between qcqs spaces, and it is closed under composition. It is stable under base change along any morphism of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces when f is quasi-compact (then the base change is again quasi-compact quasi-separated, hence taut).
hypotheses: X, Y locally noetherian and analytic; no morphism outside this category is called compactifiable
separatedness and the plus-ring condition are those of AdicSpacesPartII R0; 'locally of finite type' (the anchor's notion) implies 'locally of +weakly finite type'
base-change stability is asserted only for quasi-compact f; for a general taut f it is the content of Hub96 Lemma 5.1.3, which is not public
proofSteps: Proper ⇒ compactifiable: proper = +weakly finite type, separated, universally closed; a quasi-compact separated morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence taut (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/taut-spaces-and-morphisms, API IsTautMap.of_qcqs).
Open immersions: separated, locally of finite type (hence locally +wft, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/finite-type-morphism-classes) and taut when the source is taut or the immersion is quasi-compact.
Separated quasi-compact étale morphisms are quasi-compact quasi-separated, hence taut; they are locally of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/differentials-unramified-smooth-etale).
Composition: separatedness and local +weakly finite type are stable under composition (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/base-change-stability), tautness by the composition API of the taut node.

Quasi-compact base change: separatedness and local +wft are stable under base change (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/base-change-stability, fibre products AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-products-existence); the base change of a quasi-compact quasi-separated map is quasi-compact quasi-separated, hence taut.
acceptance: The relative closed unit disc B_S → S = Spa(C, C⁺) (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-closed-polydisc) is compactifiable and quasi-compact, i.e. lies in 𝓔.
The open unit disc D → Spa(C, O_C) is compactifiable but not quasi-compact.
The doubled disc over Spa K is locally of finite type but neither separated nor taut, hence not compactifiable.

uses.how: R⁺f_! is defined exactly for compactifiable f
the relative ball B × Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(C, C⁺) and its restrictions to quasi-compact opens U ⊆ Spa(C, C⁺) must lie in the class
Rf_! and its right adjoint are 'well-behaved' for separated taut morphisms of rigid spaces
the analytification of a separated morphism of finite type is compactifiable, as used for the algebraic/analytic comparisons

nodes.title: Pseudo-adic support spaces and their étale topoi
nodes.statement: A pseudo-adic support space is a pair (X, S) of a locally noetherian analytic adic space X and a subset S ⊆ |X| that is convex (if s, s' ∈ S and s specialises to x which specialises to s', then x ∈ S) and locally pro-constructible (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/pro-constructible-subsets). Its étale site (X, S)_ét is the site (X_ét, J_S) of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/pseudo-adic-etale-site (the category of the étale site of X with the Grothendieck topology in which a family (U_i → U) is a covering when the images of the U_i cover the points of U lying over S); this node adds no new site, only Huber's conditions on S and the conventions (i)–(iv) below; this topology is finer than the étale topology, so its topos Sh((X, S)_ét, Λ) is a subtopos of Sh(X_ét, Λ): the inclusion i_{S*} is fully faithful with exact left adjoint i_S^* (sheafification for the S-topology). Points: the geometric points of (X, S) are the geometric points of X (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points) whose support lies in S, and they form a conservative family. Pinned conventions: (i) (X, |X|)_ét = X_ét and, for S open, (X, S)_ét is the étale site of the open adic subspace S; (ii) a closed subset Z ⊆ |X| is convex and pro-constructible, so (X, Z) is a pseudo-adic support space, and for the open complement U there is the recollement triangle j_!j^*K → K → i_{Z*}i_Z^*K → K[1] with j_! of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero; (iii) a closed subset that is not open is never treated as an adic subspace: the boundary X̄ ∖ X of a universal compactification and the fibre f⁻¹(s) over the closed point s of Spa(C, C⁺) are pseudo-adic support spaces and in general not adic spaces; (iv) for f : X → Y and a subset T ⊆ |Y| with the same properties, f⁻¹(T) is convex and locally pro-constructible when f is spectral, so f induces (X, f⁻¹T) → (Y, T).
hypotheses: X locally noetherian analytic; S ⊆ |X| convex and locally pro-constructible
Λ a ring; sheaves are sheaves of Λ-modules on Et/X for the S-topology
The site is H0's (X_ét, J_S), whose topology is finer than the étale topology; no new adic space is attached to S
proofSteps: The S-coverings form a pretopology on Et/X: isomorphisms cover, coverings compose, and stability under base change follows from the surjectivity of |U ×_V W| onto compatible pairs of points (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/fibre-product-points).

Every X_ét-covering is an S-covering, so the S-topology is finer than the étale topology; S-sheaves are étale sheaves, and the inclusion i_{S*} has the exact left adjoint i_S^* given by S-sheafification (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point is only used for points).

Points: for a geometric point ξ of X supported in S the fibre functor of AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points sends S-coverings to jointly surjective maps because an S-covering is surjective over the support of ξ; conservativity follows from AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-enough-points applied to the S-local objects.
Closed subsets are convex and pro-constructible (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/closure-of-pro-constructible); the recollement triangle is checked on stalks at geometric points supported in U and in Z.

(X, |X|) and open S: the S-topology coincides with the étale topology of the open subspace S because every étale map to S is an object of Et/X (AdicSpacesPartII:R4/etale-site-functoriality, open immersions).
acceptance: For S = Spa(C, C⁺) and its closed point s, Sh((S, {s})_ét) is equivalent to the category of sets (Λ-modules) and H^q((S,{s}), F) = 0 for q > 0.
In the universal compactification B̄ = B ∪ {x_∞} of the closed unit disc over Spa(C, O_C), {x_∞} is closed and not open, so (B̄, {x_∞}) is a pseudo-adic support space and not an adic subspace.
Huber's d(X, L) = (d(X), λ_X⁻¹(L)) of H1:formal-adic-comparison is an instance with X = d(𝔛).

nodes.title: Huber's universal compactification of a compactifiable morphism
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be compactifiable (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/compactifiable-morphism). There are an adic space X̄ = X̄^{/Y}, an open embedding j : X → X̄ and a partially proper morphism f̄ : X̄ → Y (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/partially-proper-morphism) with f = f̄ ∘ j, such that for every partially proper morphism g : Z → Y composition with j is a bijection Hom_Y(X̄, Z) → Hom_Y(X, Z). Affinoid charts: if Y = Spa(A, A⁺) and X = Spa(B, B⁺) with B topologically of finite type over A, then X̄ = Spa(B, B'⁺) where B'⁺ ⊆ B⁺ is the integral closure in B of the subring generated by the image of A⁺ and the topologically nilpotent elements B°°, and j is the identity of B. The rank-one points of X̄ and of X coincide; every point of X̄ ∖ j(X) is a specialisation of a point of j(X), and X̄ ∖ j(X) is closed, generally not open, and is treated only as a pseudo-adic support space (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/pseudo-adic-support-space). The construction is functorial in f, compatible with open immersions into X and with base change along Y' → Y when f is quasi-compact ((X ×_Y Y')‾^{/Y'} = X̄^{/Y} ×_Y Y'), and X̄ = X when f is partially proper.
hypotheses: f compactifiable: separated, locally of +weakly finite type, taut
Y locally noetherian analytic; X̄ is in general not locally of finite type over Y (its plus rings are minimal), so f̄ is partially proper but not smooth even when f is smooth
proofSteps: Affinoid case: (B, B'⁺) is a Huber pair (B'⁺ is open, integrally closed, contains B°° and lies in B°), and for an affinoid field (K, K⁺) with a map A → K, a map B → K with B°° ↦ K°° extends to (B, B'⁺) → (K, K⁺) exactly when A⁺ ↦ K⁺; hence Spa(B, B'⁺)(K, K⁺) = X(K, K°) ×_{Y(K,K°)} Y(K, K⁺), the valuative description whose diamond analogue is ECD Proposition 18.6 and 18.7(iv).
Partial properness of Spa(B, B'⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺): by the valuative criterion AdicSpacesPartII:R0/separated-proper-partially-proper (Huber 1.3.9) using the valuative description.

Universal property in the affinoid case: a map X → Z over Y with Z partially proper extends uniquely along each point Spa(K, K⁺) → X̄ by the valuative criterion for Z; the extension is a morphism of adic spaces because its restriction to rational charts is determined by B.

Gluing: for f locally of +weakly finite type, separated and taut, the affinoid compactifications of an affinoid cover of X glue along the compactifications of the pairwise intersections; separatedness gives uniqueness of the gluing maps and tautness makes the glued space have quasi-compact closures of quasi-compact opens. This global gluing is Hub96 Theorem 5.1.5, whose proof is not public (gap: universal compactification beyond the affinoid case).
Points: X̄(K, K°) = X(K, K°) shows that rank-one points agree; every point of X̄ is a specialisation of its maximal generalisation, which is rank one and lies in X.
Base change for quasi-compact f and X̄ = X for partially proper f: from the valuative description and the universal property.
acceptance: Closed unit disc over S = Spa(C, O_C): X̄ = Spa(C⟨T⟩, B'⁺) with B'⁺ the integral closure of O_C + C°°⟨T⟩; X̄ ∖ X is the single rank-two point x_∞ specialising the Gauss point in the direction T → ∞.
If f is proper then X̄ = X and j is the identity.
For the open unit disc D over Spa(C, O_C), which is partially proper, D̄ = D.

nodes.title: For quasi-compact f the compactification is a quasi-compact open immersion followed by a proper map
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be compactifiable and quasi-compact (i.e. of +weakly finite type), with universal compactification f = f̄ ∘ j (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/universal-compactification). Then (i) f̄ : X̄ → Y is proper; (ii) j is a quasi-compact open immersion; (iii) f and f̄ have the same rank-one fibres, so dim f̄ = dim f for the relative dimension computed on rank-one fibres (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-dimension-rank-one-fibres) and the topological transcendence dimensions of ECD Definition 21.1–21.2 agree. In particular every f ∈ 𝓔 factors as f = p ∘ i with i ∈ 𝓘 and p ∈ 𝓟.
hypotheses: f compactifiable and quasi-compact
Y locally noetherian analytic
proofSteps: (i) f̄ is partially proper; on affinoid charts X̄ = Spa(B, B'⁺) is quasi-compact over Spa(A, A⁺), so f̄ is quasi-compact when f is, and proper = partially proper + quasi-compact (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/proper-iff-partially-proper-quasi-compact).

(ii) On affinoid charts j is the identity of B, a rational subset in Spa(B, B'⁺) cut out by |b| ≤ 1 for finitely many b ∈ B⁺ generating B⁺ over B'⁺ up to integral closure (local +weak finiteness), hence quasi-compact; quasi-compactness is local on the target.

(iii) Rank-one points of X̄ and X coincide (API compactification.rankOne_points), and for lft f the relative dimension is detected on rank-one fibres (AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/relative-dimension-rank-one-fibres); the transcendence-degree dimension depends only on completed residue fields of maximal generalisations. The general equality dim.tr f̄ = dim.tr f is Hub96 Corollary 5.1.14 as quoted by Zavyalov.
acceptance: For the closed unit disc over Spa(C, C⁺), B → B̄ is a quasi-compact open immersion and B̄ → Spa(C, C⁺) is proper of relative dimension 1.
Non-example: for the open unit disc (not quasi-compact) the compactification is D itself and D → Spa(C, O_C) is partially proper but not proper.

sources.match: Restates Hub96 Corollary 5.1.6: every quasi-compact compactifiable morphism is a quasi-compact open immersion followed by a proper morphism.
Restates Hub96 Corollary 5.1.14 (dimension of the compactification equals that of f; the overbar on the first f is lost in the text layer).
Diamond analogue of (i): the canonical compactification of a quasi-compact separated map is proper.

nodes.title: Sections with proper support: f_! for partially proper f
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a partially proper morphism of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces with f taut (so f is compactifiable) and Λ a ring. For an étale sheaf F of Λ-modules on X, f_!F ⊆ f_*F is the subsheaf whose sections over V ∈ Y_ét are the s ∈ F(X ×_Y V) whose support supp(s) (a closed subset of X ×_Y V) is quasi-compact over V: supp(s) ∩ f⁻¹(W) is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open W ⊆ V. Equivalently, when Y is affinoid, f_!F = colim_U f_*(j_{U!}(F|_U)) over the filtered system of quasi-compact open subsets U ⊆ X, where j_U : U → X is the inclusion (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero). f_! : Sh(X_ét, Λ) → Sh(Y_ét, Λ) is left exact, commutes with filtered colimits, equals f_* when f is proper, and R⁺f_! denotes its right derived functor on D⁺(X_ét, Λ) (via injective resolutions, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/derived-direct-image). Stalk formula: for a geometric point ȳ = Spa(C, C⁺) → Y, (f_!F)_ȳ is the group of sections of F over X ×_Y Spa(C, C⁺) with support quasi-compact.
hypotheses: f partially proper and taut; Y locally noetherian analytic
supports are quasi-compact relative to the base, never compact in a Hausdorff sense: the relevant spaces are not Hausdorff
proofSteps: Support: supp(s) = {x : s_x̄ ≠ 0} is closed because sections vanishing at a geometric point vanish on an étale neighbourhood (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/etale-site-and-geometric-points).
Sheaf property: supports are local on V and quasi-compactness over V can be checked on a quasi-compact open cover of V.

Colimit form: for Y affinoid and X taut (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/taut-spaces-and-morphisms), a closed subset Z ⊆ X is quasi-compact iff it lies in some quasi-compact open U (cover Z by finitely many quasi-compact opens; conversely Z ⊆ U ⊆ closure(U), which is quasi-compact by tautness); a section of f_*(j_{U!}F|_U) is exactly a section of F with support closed in X and contained in U.

Left exactness and filtered colimits: sections with quasi-compact support form a left exact subfunctor of f_*; on quasi-compact supports f_* commutes with filtered colimits (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites).
Proper f: X ×_Y V → V is quasi-compact, so every closed support is quasi-compact over V and f_! = f_*.
Derived functor: Sh(X_ét, Λ) has enough injectives (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-sheaves-of-modules), so R⁺f_! exists; this is Hub96 Definition 5.3.1 as quoted by Zavyalov.

Stalk formula: for a geometric point ȳ = Spa(C, C⁺) → Y, (f_!F)_ȳ is the colimit over étale neighbourhoods V of ȳ of the sections over X ×_Y V with support quasi-compact over V; by the colimit form it is colim_U of the stalks of f_*(j_{U!}(F|_U)) = (f|_{W_U})_*(j_{U!}(F|_U)) for a quasi-compact open W_U containing the (quasi-compact) closure of U, and the stalk formula for the quasi-compact quasi-separated f|_{W_U} (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-formula-strict-localisation (a)–(b), degree 0) identifies this with the sections over X ×_Y Spa(C, C⁺) with quasi-compact support.
acceptance: For the open unit disc f : D → Spa(C, O_C), f_!Λ = 0 while f_*Λ = Λ.
For P¹ → Spa(C, C⁺) (proper), f_! = f_*.

uses.how: R⁺f_! = R⁺f̄_! ∘ j_! uses this functor for the partially proper f̄
the colimit form over quasi-compact opens

nodes.title: Huber's proper-support direct image R⁺f_!
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be compactifiable (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/compactifiable-morphism), f = f̄ ∘ j its universal compactification (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/universal-compactification) and Λ a ring. The proper-support direct image is R⁺f_! := R⁺f̄_! ∘ j_! : D⁺(X_ét, Λ) → D⁺(Y_ét, Λ), where j_! is extension by zero along the open embedding j (exact; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero) and R⁺f̄_! is the derived functor of sections with proper support for the partially proper f̄ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/partially-proper-lower-shriek). Its cohomology sheaves are R^q f_!K, and for Y = Spa(C, C⁺) the groups H^q_c(X, K) := H^q(Y, R⁺f_!K) = (R^q f_!K)(Y) are the compactly supported cohomology groups (global sections over Spa(C, C⁺) is exact). There is a natural forget-supports transformation R⁺f_! → R⁺f_*, an isomorphism when f is proper. When f is quasi-compact, R⁺f_! ≅ Rf̄_* ∘ j_! with f̄ proper (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/compactification-proper-factorisation). When nΛ = 0 with n invertible in O_Y⁺ and f is locally of finite type of finite relative dimension, R⁺f_! has finite cohomological dimension (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/lower-shriek-cohomological-dimension) and extends uniquely to a triangulated functor Rf_! : D(X_ét, Λ) → D(Y_ét, Λ) commuting with direct sums, computed on K-injective replacements (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/k-injective-and-k-flat-replacements).
hypotheses: f compactifiable between locally noetherian analytic adic spaces
Λ any ring for the definition on D⁺; the unbounded extension, base change and duality statements require nΛ = 0 with n invertible in O_Y⁺
H^q_c is always relative to the base; for the absolute case the base is Spa(C, C⁺) and C⁺ is part of the data
proofSteps: Well-definedness on D⁺: j_! is exact and preserves D⁺; R⁺f̄_! is a right derived functor on D⁺ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/partially-proper-lower-shriek).
Forget supports: the inclusion f̄_! ⊆ f̄_* and j_! → Rj_* (adjoint to the identity on j^*) give R⁺f̄_! j_! → Rf̄_* j_! → Rf̄_* Rj_* = Rf_*; for f proper, j = id and f̄_! = f̄_*.
Quasi-compact f: f̄ proper, so f̄_! = f̄_* (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/compactification-proper-factorisation).

Unbounded extension: if R^q f_! vanishes for q > N on sheaves, R⁺f_! is way-out in both directions and extends to D(X_ét, Λ) by applying it to K-injective replacements of truncations, as in Zavyalov Lemma 9.1 Step 2 (EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/k-injective-and-k-flat-replacements, EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/enhanced-derived-category).
acceptance: For the closed unit disc f : B → Spa(C, O_C) and n invertible in O_C: R²f_!μ_n ≅ ℤ/n and R^q f_!μ_n = 0 for q ≠ 2, while Rf_*μ_n = μ_n in degree 0 (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/relative-ball-compact-support).
For an open immersion j with taut source, R⁺j_! = j_! (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/lower-shriek-proper-and-etale-cases).

nodes.title: Henselian comparison: proper schemes over C⁺ and over C⁺/ϖ
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring henselian along an ideal I (mathlib:HenselianRing), π : 𝒫 → Spec A a proper morphism of finite presentation, and K ∈ D⁺(𝒫_ét) with torsion cohomology sheaves. Then restriction RΓ(𝒫, K) → RΓ(𝒫 ⊗_A A/I, K|) is an isomorphism. Applied twice with the notation C an algebraically closed field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value, with residue characteristic p ≥ 0; C⁺ ⊆ C an open and bounded valuation subring of arbitrary rank; S = Spa(C, C⁺), with closed point s and generic point η = Spa(C, O_C); n ≥ 1 an integer prime to p (so n is invertible in C⁺); μ_n the étale sheaf of n-th roots of unity and Λ(1) = Λ ⊗ μ_n, and ϖ ∈ C⁺ a pseudo-uniformiser: (i) C⁺ is ϖ-adically complete, hence henselian along ϖC⁺ (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/complete-f-adic-ring-is-henselian), so RΓ(𝒫, K) ≅ RΓ(𝒫_0, K|) for 𝒫_0 = 𝒫 ⊗ C⁺/ϖ; (ii) C⁺/C°° is a valuation ring of the algebraically closed residue field of C, hence strictly henselian local with algebraically closed residue field k_s, and RΓ(𝒫_0, K) ≅ RΓ(𝒫_s, K|) for the fibre 𝒫_s over the closed point.
hypotheses: π proper and finitely presented
torsion coefficients
A henselian along I
proofSteps: Proper base change for schemes (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2, after a limit argument reducing to finite type over a noetherian ring, DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites) identifies the restriction of Rπ_*K to Spec A/I with Rπ_{0*}(K|).

Huber's Lemma 3.2.5 (Gabber's affine theorem; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/affine-henselian-comparison-3-2-5) gives RΓ(Spec A, G) ≅ RΓ(Spec A/I, G|) for torsion G, applied to the cohomology sheaves of Rπ_*K and assembled by the hypercohomology spectral sequence.

Composition gives the statement; (i) uses completeness of C⁺ (open subring of the complete field C) and the complete-implies-henselian node; (ii) uses that a valuation ring with algebraically closed fraction field is strictly henselian, and that the radical of ϖC⁺ is C°°, so 𝒫_0 and 𝒫 ⊗ C⁺/C°° have the same étale site (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2, topological invariance).
acceptance: 𝒫 = P¹_{C⁺}: RΓ(P¹_{C⁺}, μ_n) ≅ RΓ(P¹_{k_s}, μ_n), giving H²(P¹_{C⁺}, μ_n) ≅ ℤ/n via the degree.

nodes.title: Formal-model transfer: compactly supported cohomology of tubes over Spa(C, C⁺)
nodes.statement: Notation: C an algebraically closed field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value, with residue characteristic p ≥ 0; C⁺ ⊆ C an open and bounded valuation subring of arbitrary rank; S = Spa(C, C⁺), with closed point s and generic point η = Spa(C, O_C); n ≥ 1 an integer prime to p (so n is invertible in C⁺); μ_n the étale sheaf of n-th roots of unity and Λ(1) = Λ ⊗ μ_n; ϖ ∈ C⁺ a pseudo-uniformiser. Let 𝒫 be a proper flat finitely presented C⁺-scheme with special fibre 𝒫_0 = 𝒫 ⊗ C⁺/ϖ, P := 𝒫_C ×_{Spec C} S (Huber's fibre product), which equals the generic fibre d(𝒫̂) of the ϖ-adic completion (a formal scheme of type (S)), and λ : P_ét → (𝒫_0)_ét the specialisation morphism of sites; similarly λ_S : S_ét → Spec(C⁺/ϖ)_ét, an equivalence of topoi (both are the topos of the chain of valuation rings between C⁺ and O_C, since étale maps to either side split locally). For an open subscheme 𝒰 ⊆ 𝒫_0 let U := λ⁻¹(𝒰) ⊆ P (an open subspace, quasi-compact if 𝒰 is), f_U : U → S and π_𝒰 : 𝒰 → Spec(C⁺/ϖ). Then for every K ∈ D⁺(U_ét, Λ) with Λ torsion there is a natural isomorphism λ_{S*} R f_{P*}(j_{U!} K) ≅ Rπ_{𝒰!} Rλ_{U*} K, where j_U : U ⊆ P is the open inclusion and f_P : P → S the proper structure map (for quasi-compact U the left side is the proper-support direct image of U → S, see ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/relative-ball-compact-support), compatible with open immersions 𝒰' ⊆ 𝒰 (extension by zero on both sides), with restriction to open subsets of S (localisation of C⁺) and with the trace-type maps induced by finite flat maps of models. If moreover 𝒫 is smooth over C⁺ along 𝒰 and K = L|_U for a locally constant constructible L on 𝒫_C with torsion invertible in C⁺, then Rλ_{U*}K ≅ L_0 (the corresponding locally constant sheaf on 𝒰), so λ_{S*} R f_{P*}(j_{U!} L) ≅ Rπ_{𝒰!} L_0: compactly supported cohomology of the tube is compactly supported cohomology of the special fibre.
hypotheses: 𝒫 proper flat of finite presentation over C⁺; C⁺ of arbitrary rank (the ϖ-adic completion is of type (S) because 𝒫̂[1/ϖ] is strongly noetherian)
Λ torsion; the smooth clause needs torsion invertible in C⁺
U is the open tube of an open of the special fibre; tubes of closed or locally closed subsets are pseudo-adic and are treated through ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison, not here
proofSteps: P = d(𝒫̂): Hub96 Proposition 1.9.6 for the proper (hence separated and universally specialising) 𝒫 → Spec C⁺ (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison, AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-functor-d); U = d(𝒰̂) is the open subspace of the open formal subscheme 𝒰̂ (same node), and P → S is proper.

Functoriality of specialisation: λ_S ∘ f_P = π_0 ∘ λ_P as morphisms of sites for the adic morphism 𝒫̂ → Spf C⁺ (Hub96 3.5.4, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison/pairs-and-pseudo-adic-supports, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison/specialization-morphism-of-sites-lambda), hence λ_{S*}Rf_{P*} ≅ Rπ_{0*}Rλ_{P*}.

Extension by zero: Rλ_{P*} ∘ j_{U!} ≅ i_{𝒰!} ∘ Rλ_{U*} (Hub96 Corollary 3.5.11(ii) with L' = 𝒰 open in L = 𝒫_0; ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison/restriction-and-extension-by-zero-3-5-11).
Rπ_{0*} ∘ i_{𝒰!} = Rπ_{𝒰!} for the proper π_0 (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2, after a limit argument from finite type over a noetherian ring).

Smooth clause: Rλ_{U*}(L|_U) is the restriction to 𝒰 of i^*Rj_*L (Hub96 Theorem 3.5.13, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison/scheme-completion-comparison-3-5-13), and for 𝒫 smooth over C⁺ along 𝒰 and L locally constant with torsion invertible in C⁺ the nearby cycles are trivial, i^*Rj_*L ≅ L_0 (local acyclicity of smooth morphisms, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2; Berkovich's Corollary 5.4 for smooth formal schemes over O_C).

λ_S is an equivalence: étale maps to S split near the closed point (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/geometric-point-etale-split) so S_ét is the topos of |S|; all localisations of the valuation ring C⁺/C°° are strictly henselian, so Spec(C⁺/ϖ)_ét is the topos of |Spec(C⁺/C°°)|; λ_S(x) = {a ∈ C⁺ : |a(x)| < 1} is a homeomorphism of these chains.
acceptance: 𝒫 = P¹_{C⁺}, 𝒰 = A¹ ⊆ P¹_0: U = B_S is the relative closed ball and λ_{S*}Rf_{P¹*}(j_!Λ) ≅ Rπ_{A¹!}Λ = Λ(−1)[−2] (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/relative-ball-compact-support).
𝒰 = 𝒫_0: U = P and the statement is RΓ(P, K) ≅ RΓ(𝒫_0, Rλ_*K), Hub96 Corollary 3.5.14.
𝒰 = A¹ ∖ {0}: U is the annulus {|T| = 1} over S, with H¹_c and H²_c those of G_{m,k_s}.

nodes.title: Proper base change to the pseudo-adic closed fibre over Spa(C, C⁺)
nodes.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed field complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value, C⁺ ⊆ C an open and bounded valuation subring, S = Spa(C, C⁺) with closed point s, f : X → S a proper morphism with X locally noetherian, and Λ with nΛ = 0 for some n invertible in C⁺. Let X_s = (X, f⁻¹(s)) be the pseudo-adic closed fibre (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/pseudo-adic-support-space). Then for every K ∈ D⁺(X_ét, Λ) the restriction map RΓ(X, K) → RΓ(X_s, K|_{X_s}) is an isomorphism; equivalently, RΓ(X, K) = 0 whenever K|_{X_s} = 0, e.g. for K = j'_!L with j' : f⁻¹(S ∖ {s}) → X the open complement.
hypotheses: f proper (AdicSpacesPartII:R0), X locally noetherian analytic
n invertible in C⁺: the p-torsion analogue is not asserted
X_s is a pseudo-adic support space, not an adic subspace
proofSteps: Equivalence of the two forms: the recollement triangle j'_!j'^*K → K → i_{s*}i_s^*K for the closed subset f⁻¹(s) and its open complement (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/pseudo-adic-support-space) reduces the isomorphism to RΓ(X, j'_!L) = 0.

Dévissage: RΓ(X, −) commutes with filtered colimits on the quasi-compact quasi-separated X (DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites), every torsion sheaf is a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/classical-constructible-sheaves), and bounded below complexes reduce to sheaves by the hypercohomology spectral sequence; so it suffices to treat L constructible.

Algebraisable case: if X = d(𝒫̂) for a proper flat finitely presented C⁺-scheme 𝒫 and L is the pullback of a constructible sheaf on the generic fibre, the statement is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/formal-model-transfer combined with ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/henselian-proper-base-change: both sides are computed on the special fibre 𝒫 ⊗ C⁺/ϖ, the right side on its fibre over the closed point of Spec(C⁺/ϖ) (Hub96 3.5.16, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:formal-adic-comparison/valuation-ring-base-3-5-16), and these agree by proper base change for schemes over the strictly henselian valuation ring C⁺/C°° (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2).

General case: Hub96 Proposition 4.4.3, as quoted by Zavyalov. Its proof is not public (gap: proper base change at the closed point for non-algebraisable proper X). The public route is ECD Theorem 19.2: reduce to a Zariski–Riemann space of an algebraically closed field (ECD Lemma 19.4), where the statement follows from proper base change for schemes; transplanting this reduction to proper adic spaces over Spa(C, C⁺) requires a cover of X by spaces of the form Spa(C', C'⁺)-families, which the diamond proof supplies and the classical setting does not.
acceptance: X = P¹_S = P^{1,ad} over S = Spa(C, C⁺) and K = Λ: H^q(P¹_S, Λ) ≅ H^q(P¹_{k_s}, Λ) with k_s the residue field of C⁺ (algebraically closed): Λ, 0, Λ(−1) in degrees 0, 1, 2.
If C⁺ = O_C then f⁻¹(s) = |X| and the statement is empty.

nodes.title: Proper base change for extension by zero: j_!Rg_* ≅ Rf_*j'_!
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper morphism of locally noetherian analytic adic spaces, j : U → Y an étale morphism (for instance an open immersion), g : X_U = X ×_Y U → U and j' : X_U → X the base changes, and Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n ≥ 1 invertible in O_Y⁺ (equivalently, n prime to the residue characteristic of every point of Y). The natural transformation α : j_! Rg_* → Rf_* j'_!, adjoint to f^*j_!Rg_* ≅ j'_!g^*Rg_* → j'_! (base change for j_!, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/supports-and-extension-by-zero, followed by the counit), is an isomorphism of functors D⁺(X_{U,ét}, Λ) → D⁺(Y_ét, Λ); if Rf_* has finite cohomological dimension it is an isomorphism on D(X_{U,ét}, Λ). Equivalently, R f_* commutes with restriction to the pseudo-adic closed complement of U: this is the classical meaning of ECD's Theorem 19.2.
hypotheses: f proper
Λ a ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n ≥ 1 invertible in O_Y⁺ (equivalently, n prime to the residue characteristic of every point of Y)
j étale; the case of open immersions is the one used for the compactly supported pushforward
proofSteps: Definition of α as stated (Zavyalov, Proposition 9.3, proof of Part (1)).

Locality: the question is étale local on Y and U, so Y, U may be taken affinoid; by Huber's Lemma 2.2.8 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/etale-local-open-finite-etale-factorisation) j is locally an open immersion followed by a finite étale map, and it suffices to treat these two cases.
Finite étale j: étale locally on Y, U is a disjoint union of copies of Y, where α is evidently an isomorphism.

Open immersion j: by way-out arguments (on D⁺; on D under the finite cohomological dimension hypothesis of the statement) reduce to K a sheaf; check on stalks at geometric points ȳ = Spa(C, C⁺) → Y. By the stalk formula for proper pushforward (Hub96 2.6.1, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/stalk-formula-strict-localisation) and base change for j_!, both sides become global sections over X ×_Y Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(C, C⁺) with U replaced by its preimage, an open subset of Spa(C, C⁺).

If the preimage is all of Spa(C, C⁺) the map is the identity; otherwise the left side has zero stalk at the closed point and the right side is RΓ(X ×_Y Spa(C, C⁺), j'_!K), which vanishes by ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H3/proper-closed-fibre-vanishing.
acceptance: For Y = Spa(C, C⁺) with C⁺ ≠ O_C of finite rank (so that the generic point U = Spa(C, O_C) is an open subset, and U ≠ Y) and X = P¹_Y: both sides of α applied to Λ have zero stalk at the closed point.
For U = Y, α is the identity.
