nodes.title: A finite étale factor near an analytic point
nodes.statement: Let (A,A⁺) be an adic Banach ring and Spec(A′)→Spec(A) a surjective étale morphism. For every α∈M(A) there is a rational localization (A,A⁺)→(B,B⁺) encircling α for which A′⊗_A B decomposes as a finite product of rings, with at least one factor faithfully finite étale over B. Encircling is the neighborhood notion of KL §2.4; replacing it by an arbitrary rational subset containing α loses the neighborhood assertion. The algebra A′⊗_A B is the algebraic base change of the scheme cover, not an unspecified completion.
proofSteps: Choose a prime of A′ over the support prime of α and extend the norm to its residue field.
Apply the local Jacobian criterion and KL 2.4.17 to obtain a rational neighborhood on which the étale component has an invertible Jacobian.
Separate the component and use the point lying above α to retain a faithfully finite étale factor, as in KL 8.4.1.
acceptance: For a faithfully finite étale A′/A, choose the identity localization and the whole A′ as the factor.
A non-surjective open immersion need not supply a faithful factor near a point outside its image.

sources.match: The finite factor is obtained near every analytic point.

nodes.title: A scheme rational local system acquires a local lattice
nodes.statement: Let (A,A⁺) be an adic Banach ring, V a scheme étale ℚ_p-local system on Spec(A), and α∈M(A). There is a rational localization (A,A⁺)→(B,B⁺) encircling α such that V|_Spec(B) is isomorphic to T⊗ℚ_p for an integral ℤ_p-local system T on Spec(B).
proofSteps: Present V étale-locally by isogeny integral systems using scheme stackification.
Apply the finite-factor lemma near α.
Apply effective descent of isogeny local systems along a faithfully finite étale ring map (KL Lemma 1.4.8), imported from SF.2.
acceptance: Let (A,A⁺) be an adic Banach ring, V a scheme étale ℚ_p-local system on Spec(A), and α∈M(A). There is a rational localization (A,A⁺)→(B,B⁺) encircling α such that V|_Spec(B) is isomorphic to T⊗ℚ_p for an integral ℤ_p-local system T on Spec(B).

sources.match: The proof uses Lemma 1.4.8 and Lemma 8.4.1.

nodes.title: Adic and étale presentations of preadic local systems
nodes.statement: The integral and rational local-system categories of KL Definition 8.4.3 are unchanged if preadic étale covering families replace the adic open covering families in the descent presentation. The comparison functors preserve pullback, rank, tensor product and dual; on strongly sheafy spaces they agree with the corresponding local-system categories on A1’s ordinary étale site. The assertion extends the local-system categories, not every torsion cohomology theorem of H0, to arbitrary preadic spaces.
proofSteps: Use local factorization of preadic étale maps into a rational localization and a finite étale map, supplied by A1.
Descend integral systems along finite étale maps and rational systems along their stack descent.
Compare on common refinements to construct inverse equivalences, as KL Remark 8.4.4.
acceptance: The integral and rational local-system categories of KL Definition 8.4.3 are unchanged if preadic étale covering families replace the adic open covering families in the descent presentation. The comparison functors preserve pullback, rank, tensor product and dual; on strongly sheafy spaces they agree with the corresponding local-system categories on A1’s ordinary étale site. The assertion extends the local-system categories, not every torsion cohomology theorem of H0, to arbitrary preadic spaces.

nodes.title: Bounded lattices in an integral local system
nodes.statement: For an integral ℤ_p-local system T on a preadic X and m≥0, define L_m(T)(Y) to be isomorphism classes of pairs (T′,ι), with T′ integral on Y and ι:T_Y⊗ℚ_p ≅ T′⊗ℚ_p satisfying p^mι∈Hom(T_Y,T′) and p^mι⁻¹∈Hom(T′,T_Y). It is represented by a finite étale preadic X-space. At a geometric point it is the finite set of lattices between p^m T_x and p^(−m)T_x; the two inequalities are both required. It has an inclusion relation represented by a finite étale subspace of L_m(T)×_X L_m(T) and a canonical operation taking the sum of finitely many bounded lattices. These are the analytic transports of KL Remark 1.4.7, used in Proposition 8.4.6.
proofSteps: Import the finite étale bounded-lattice scheme L_m(T), its inclusion relation and finite sums from SF.2 (KL Remark 1.4.7).
Apply the finite-étale algebra/space correspondence of A1 on each affinoid.
Glue along overlaps; base change of the finite mod-p-power lattice data gives representability without a sheafiness assumption on X.
acceptance: For an integral ℤ_p-local system T on a preadic X and m≥0, define L_m(T)(Y) to be isomorphism classes of pairs (T′,ι), with T′ integral on Y and ι:T_Y⊗ℚ_p ≅ T′⊗ℚ_p satisfying p^mι∈Hom(T_Y,T′) and p^mι⁻¹∈Hom(T′,T_Y). It is represented by a finite étale preadic X-space. At a geometric point it is the finite set of lattices between p^m T_x and p^(−m)T_x; the two inequalities are both required. It has an inclusion relation represented by a finite étale subspace of L_m(T)×_X L_m(T) and a canonical operation taking the sum of finitely many bounded lattices. These are the analytic transports of KL Remark 1.4.7, used in Proposition 8.4.6.

nodes.title: Local integral lattices for preadic rational systems
nodes.statement: For an adic Banach ring (A,A⁺), a rational local system V on Spã(A,A⁺), and α∈M(A), there is a rational localization (A,A⁺)→(B,B⁺) encircling α such that V|_Spã(B,B⁺) is an isogeny ℤ_p-local system. No global lattice and no strong-sheafiness assumption is asserted.
proofSteps: Represent bounded changes of lattice by L_m(T) using the previous construction and KL 8.2.17(a).
Use henselian finite étale approximation (KL 1.2.8 and 2.4.17) to find a rational neighborhood and faithfully finite étale cover carrying a lattice with descent datum.
Use KL 1.4.8 to descend the lattice up to isogeny.
acceptance: A constant ℚ_p-system has its constant integral lattice on the identity neighborhood.
A noncompact global monodromy example still has local lattices.

sources.match: The statement applies to a rational local system on the preadic spectrum.

nodes.title: Rational descent by isogeny lattices on a strong cover
nodes.statement: Every rational local system on Spã(A,A⁺), for an adic Banach ring (A,A⁺), admits a descent presentation by isogeny ℤ_p-local systems on a strong rational covering family. Strong has KL’s meaning (Definition 2.4.14, p. 42): a finite family of rational subspaces of M(A) whose relative interiors in M(A) cover M(A); it induces a rational covering of Spã(A,A⁺). Compactness of M(A) extracts such a finite family from the encircling neighbourhoods of Proposition 8.4.6. Transition maps are rational isomorphisms satisfying the cocycle; they are not required to preserve the chosen integral lattices.
proofSteps: Choose the neighborhoods of Proposition 8.4.6 for all points of M(A).
Take a finite strong covering by compactness.
Restrict V’s descent isomorphisms to intersections; the cocycle is inherited.
acceptance: Every rational local system on Spã(A,A⁺), for an adic Banach ring (A,A⁺), admits a descent presentation by isogeny ℤ_p-local systems on a strong rational covering family. Strong has KL’s meaning (Definition 2.4.14, p. 42): a finite family of rational subspaces of M(A) whose relative interiors in M(A) cover M(A); it induces a rational covering of Spã(A,A⁺). Compactness of M(A) extracts such a finite family from the encircling neighbourhoods of Proposition 8.4.6. Transition maps are rational isomorphisms satisfying the cocycle; they are not required to preserve the chosen integral lattices.

nodes.title: Integral local systems agree on Spec and preadic Spa
nodes.statement: For every adic Banach ring (A,A⁺), the natural tensor functor ℤ_p-Loc(Spec A)→ZpLocalSystem(Spã(A,A⁺)) is an equivalence, and induces an equivalence on the isogeny categories. Its mod-pⁿ functors are the finite-étale algebra/space comparisons of A1. This does not assert an equivalence of the full étale topoi or an equivalence of their rational stackifications.
proofSteps: Integral local systems are determined by compatible finite étale covers at every coefficient level (KL Remark 1.4.3).
Apply effective rational-localization descent of finite étale algebras (KL Theorem 2.6.9), requested from R0/A1.
Glue the compatible coefficient transitions, then rationalize morphisms.
acceptance: For every adic Banach ring (A,A⁺), the natural tensor functor ℤ_p-Loc(Spec A)→ZpLocalSystem(Spã(A,A⁺)) is an equivalence, and induces an equivalence on the isogeny categories. Its mod-pⁿ functors are the finite-étale algebra/space comparisons of A1. This does not assert an equivalence of the full étale topoi or an equivalence of their rational stackifications.

nodes.title: Rational Spec–Spa comparison is fully faithful
nodes.statement: For an adic Banach ring (A,A⁺), the natural tensor functor ℚ_p-Loc(Spec A)→QpLocalSystem(Spã(A,A⁺)) is fully faithful. It need not be essentially surjective, even for reduced affinoid algebras over an analytic field; an explicit case is the rank-one system glued by p on the smooth connected strictly affinoid subspace of a Tate curve in KL Example 8.5.17. When A is normal noetherian (KL Remark 8.4.8 infers normality from integrality of A, which does not suffice; normality is assumed here), source objects admit a global ℤ_p-lattice by KL Remark 1.4.9, whereas the analytic category can contain continuous representations of de Jong’s non-profinite analytic fundamental group with noncompact image. The latter are outside the source image.
proofSteps: Use local isogeny lattice presentations on a finite strong rational cover.
Descend rational Hom by integral descent after multiplying by one common p-power.
For failure of essential surjectivity combine the normal-noetherian scheme global-lattice criterion with de Jong’s analytic representation description, as KL Remark 8.4.8.
acceptance: For an adic Banach ring (A,A⁺), the natural tensor functor ℚ_p-Loc(Spec A)→QpLocalSystem(Spã(A,A⁺)) is fully faithful. It need not be essentially surjective, even for reduced affinoid algebras over an analytic field; an explicit case is the rank-one system glued by p on the smooth connected strictly affinoid subspace of a Tate curve in KL Example 8.5.17. When A is normal noetherian (KL Remark 8.4.8 infers normality from integrality of A, which does not suffice; normality is assumed here), source objects admit a global ℤ_p-lattice by KL Remark 1.4.9, whereas the analytic category can contain continuous representations of de Jong’s non-profinite analytic fundamental group with noncompact image. The latter are outside the source image.

sources.match: The source explicitly distinguishes integral equivalence from rational full faithfulness.
The affinoid example to which Remark 8.4.8 refers; the rank-one system is glued by multiplication by p.

nodes.title: Extensions of scheme isogeny systems descend from Spa
nodes.statement: Let (A,A⁺) be an adic Banach ring and V_i=T_i⊗ℚ_p, i=1,2, isogeny integral local systems on Spec A. Every short exact sequence 0→V_1→V→V_2→0 in QpLocalSystem(Spã(A,A⁺)) is the pullback of an extension of isogeny ℤ_p-local systems on Spec A. This extension closure does not imply that every analytic rational local system has a global lattice.
proofSteps: On a finite strong rational cover, write the extension classes in Ext(T_2,T_1)⊗ℚ_p.
Rescale T_1 by a common power of p to make the classes integral and then to kill their overlap differences over B_i⊗̂_A B_j.
Glue integral extensions on Spa and apply the integral Spec–Spa equivalence (KL Remark 8.4.9).
acceptance: Let (A,A⁺) be an adic Banach ring and V_i=T_i⊗ℚ_p, i=1,2, isogeny integral local systems on Spec A. Every short exact sequence 0→V_1→V→V_2→0 in QpLocalSystem(Spã(A,A⁺)) is the pullback of an extension of isogeny ℤ_p-local systems on Spec A. This extension closure does not imply that every analytic rational local system has a global lattice.

sources.match: The rational extensions descend after two common denominator clearings.

nodes.title: De Jong étale covering spaces
nodes.statement: For a k-analytic Berkovich space X, an analytic étale covering map f:Y→X means that every x∈X has an ordinary open neighborhood U such that f⁻¹(U) is a disjoint union of spaces finite étale over U. A topological covering is the case where these finite étale pieces are isomorphisms. Cov_X is the category of these maps over X, including the empty map; it is not the category of all étale maps and is not silently enlarged to arbitrary disjoint unions. On Hausdorff strictly k-analytic spaces, transport this definition to the corresponding taut adic spaces via Huber’s equivalence with Hausdorff strictly k-analytic spaces (requested from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0). For a quasi-separated rigid space X, de Jong §5 requires, when X is affinoid, that Y be paracompact and that every analytic point have a wide affinoid neighbourhood U with Y×_X U a disjoint union of affinoids finite étale over U, and in general that every base change to an affinoid X′ be such a covering; for X coming from a Hausdorff strictly k-analytic space this agrees with Definition 2.1. The weaker condition over an admissible affinoid covering (de Jong’s almost étale covering maps) is not used.
proofSteps: Use the Berkovich carrier and its comparison with taut adic spaces (TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0) and A1’s finite étale morphisms.
Define the local finite-étale condition on ordinary open neighborhoods.
Transport the rigid version along the equivalence, retaining its neighborhood qualification.

A topological covering is the case where these finite étale pieces are isomorphisms. Cov_X is the category of these maps over X, including the empty map; it is not the category of all étale maps and is not silently enlarged to arbitrary disjoint unions. On Hausdorff strictly k-analytic spaces, transport this definition to the corresponding taut adic spaces via Huber’s equivalence with Hausdorff strictly k-analytic spaces (requested from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0). The weaker condition over an admissible affinoid covering (de Jong’s almost étale covering maps) is not used.

nodes.title: Étale descent and quotients for analytic coverings
nodes.statement: A sheaf of sets on X_ét is representable by a de Jong covering iff it is so after an étale covering of X. If Y→X is such a covering and R⊆Y×_X Y is an equivalence relation that is a union of connected components, then the quotient étale sheaf Y/R is representable by a de Jong covering. Coverings are separated and stable under base change; their images are unions of connected components. The quotient assertion retains the connected-component condition on R.
proofSteps: Étale-locally reduce to a finite Galois covering of a neighborhood.
A finite group preserves finite unions of the covering components, so scheme finite-étale descent constructs the local quotients.
Glue the local representing spaces; use the same local finite-étale reduction for R, as de Jong Lemmas 2.2–2.4.

If Y→X is such a covering and R⊆Y×_X Y is an equivalence relation that is a union of connected components, then the quotient étale sheaf Y/R is representable by a de Jong covering. Coverings are separated and stable under base change; their images are unions of connected components. The quotient assertion retains the connected-component condition on R.

nodes.title: The fibre functor on analytic coverings
nodes.statement: For a geometric point x:M(K)→X with K algebraically closed complete, define F_x:Cov_X→Set by F_x(Y)=Y×_X M(K), viewed as its discrete set of K-points. Morphisms act by the induced maps on fibres. The functor preserves finite fibre products and existing disjoint unions. Its restrictions to finite étale and topological coverings define the algebraic and topological fibre functors. The same fibre functor on the corresponding taut adic space uses Spa(K,O_K); it agrees with A1’s geometric stalk on a represented covering.
proofSteps: Use the splitting of finite étale spaces over an algebraically closed field on each local component.
Take the resulting discrete fibre and induced maps.
Identify the represented sheaf stalk with this fibre through A1 and R1.

nodes.title: De Jong analytic étale fundamental group
nodes.statement: For a connected k-analytic space X with geometric point x, define π₁^an(X,x)=Aut(F_x), where F_x is the fibre functor on de Jong covering spaces. Give it the topology whose identity neighborhoods are stabilizers H(Y,y) of y∈F_x(Y), Y∈Cov_X; finite intersections and conjugates again occur. This topological group need not be profinite. Restriction to finite étale coverings gives a continuous map to the profinite algebraic fundamental group π₁^alg; restriction to topological coverings gives the topological covering group. On taut strictly analytic adic spaces this is the transported analytic group. Scheme IG.0 is not a supplier for this definition.
proofSteps: Define automorphisms of the fibre functor and point stabilizers.
Finite fibre products and the identity γH(Y,y)γ⁻¹=H(Y,γy) give a subgroup neighborhood basis.
Use restriction of natural automorphisms for the algebraic and topological comparison maps.

nodes.title: Prodiscreteness of the analytic fundamental group
nodes.statement: For π=π₁^an(X,x), the natural map π→lim_H π/H, over the point-stabilizer neighborhood system with quotient maps, is a homeomorphism of spaces. Thus π is Hausdorff and prodiscrete in de Jong’s sense. The stabilizers need not be normal and this formula is not a presentation as an inverse limit of finite groups.
proofSteps: A compatible system of cosets acts consistently on each covering fibre.
The resulting permutations commute with all covering morphisms and hence define an element of Aut(F_x).
Stabilizer neighborhoods identify the topology (de Jong Lemma 2.7).

nodes.title: Paths between analytic fibre functors
nodes.statement: For a connected k-analytic Berkovich X and any geometric points x,x′, there exists a natural isomorphism F_x≅F_x′ on de Jong covering spaces. A choice induces a continuous isomorphism of analytic fundamental groups, unique up to inner conjugation; no canonical path is asserted.
proofSteps: Reduce to connected affinoid neighborhoods and use arcwise connectedness supplied by R1’s Berkovich geometry.
For each finite open covering along an arc, compose paths in finite étale Galois categories on successive overlaps.
The possible compositions form nonempty compact sets compatible under refinement; their inverse limit supplies the natural isomorphism (de Jong Theorem 2.9).

nodes.title: Duality for analytic coverings and continuous actions
nodes.statement: For connected X with geometric point x, F_x:Cov_X→π₁^an(X,x)-Set is fully faithful and every transitive continuous discrete action occurs. The category of arbitrary disjoint unions of objects of Cov_X is equivalent to all continuous discrete π₁^an-sets. The original Cov_X itself is not asserted equivalent to all such sets: arbitrary disjoint unions need not satisfy the uniform local covering condition. Restriction to finite étale covers is an equivalence with finite continuous π₁^alg-sets.
proofSteps: Paths identify connected components of a covering with group orbits on its fibre.
Morphisms are recovered from componentwise graphs in fibre products, giving full faithfulness.
For an open stabilizer construct the desired transitive orbit by quotienting a covering by a union of components, then take formal disjoint unions (de Jong Theorem 2.10(i)).
acceptance: The regular action of the discrete deck group of a connected topological Galois cover recovers that cover.
Finite covering fibres agree with the ordinary finite-étale Galois category.

nodes.title: π₁^alg as the profinite completion of analytic monodromy
nodes.statement: The algebraic group π₁^alg(X,x) is profinite. Every continuous homomorphism π₁^an(X,x)→G to a profinite group factors uniquely through π₁^alg(X,x), and the canonical maps to π₁^alg and π₁^top have dense image. The map to π₁^alg is not surjective in general: for two projective lines over an algebraically closed field glued at 0 and ∞, π₁^alg = ℤ̂ and the map factors through ℤ ⊂ ℤ̂ (de Jong Remark 2.11(i)). A continuous representation on a finite-free ℤ_p-module factors through π₁^alg, since GL_r(ℤ_p) is profinite; a representation on ℚ_p may have noncompact image and need not do so.
proofSteps: Use finite covering duality for each finite quotient of G and pass to the profinite limit.
The fully faithful inclusions of finite and topological covering categories give density (de Jong Theorem 2.10(iii)–(iv)).
Apply the universal property to GL_r(ℤ_p), importing its profinite structure from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1.

nodes.title: Analytic rational local systems and continuous representations
nodes.statement: For a connected k-analytic space X and geometric point x, the geometric fibre functor is a ℚ_p-linear tensor equivalence between de Jong’s étale ℚ_p-local systems (the stackification of integral systems after rationalizing morphisms) and continuous finite-dimensional ℚ_p-representations of π₁^an(X,x). On Hausdorff strictly analytic spaces this identifies KL Definition 8.4.3 with de Jong Definition 4.1 (KL asserts this for X = Spa(A,A°), A affinoid; the general case uses that lisse sheaves are overconvergent and H0/berkovich-overconvergent-sheaf-equivalence). Integral rationalizations correspond exactly to representations admitting a π₁^an-stable ℤ_p-lattice; representations with noncompact image have none. The group is the analytic covering group, not the scheme group of Spec A.
proofSteps: The sheaf of lattices of a rational local system is represented locally by disjoint finite étale covers, hence globally by a de Jong covering by Lemma 2.3.
Its fibre and the fibres of the universal integral system recover a continuous vector-space action.
Conversely a continuous action acts on the discrete lattice set; choose an orbit and the associated covering, build its stable integral system, and descend its rationalization (de Jong Theorem 4.2).

nodes.title: Open local integral lattices in the analytic setting
nodes.statement: Every rational local system on a k-analytic Berkovich space has a presentation by integral lattices on ordinary open neighborhoods with rational overlap isomorphisms. At a point x, the compact absolute Galois group of H(x) stabilizes a lattice in the fibre; the lattice covering then has a point with H(y)=H(x), producing a local section. On affinoids this agrees with the encircling rational-neighborhood assertion of KL Proposition 8.4.6 through the Berkovich/preadic comparison.
proofSteps: Use compactness of the pointwise Galois action to choose a stable lattice.
Apply the locally finite-étale structure of the lattice covering to obtain a section on an ordinary neighborhood.
Refine by wide affinoid neighborhoods to compare with KL (de Jong Corollary 4.4).

nodes.title: Noncompact rational monodromy
nodes.statement: Let E_q be a Tate elliptic curve over an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field of characteristic zero, with 0<|q|<1. The topological covering G_m^an→E_q has deck group q^ℤ≅ℤ. Compose π₁^an(E_q,x)→π₁^top(E_q,x)≅ℤ, which is surjective because its image is dense (de Jong Theorem 2.10(iv)) in the discrete deck group ℤ, with a↦p^a∈ℚ_p×. The resulting rank-one rational local system has local integral lattices but no global integral lattice: p^ℤ is noncompact and multiplication by p cannot stabilize a nonzero finite-free ℤ_p-lattice of rank one. This is a discriminating example for rational stackification. The reduced-affinoid failure of rational Spec–Spa equivalence is the separate assertion of KL Remark 8.4.8, not a claim that E_q is affinoid.
proofSteps: Import Tate uniformization G_m^an/q^ℤ ≅ E_q and the simple connectedness of |G_m^an| from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.7, so G_m^an→E_q is the universal topological covering with deck group ℤ.
Use de Jong’s representation equivalence for the rank-one action.
A lattice p^bℤ_p is carried to p^(b+1)ℤ_p, so cannot be invariant under the generator.
acceptance: The noncompact system still has the local lattices of Proposition 8.4.6.
On a geometric point every continuous Galois representation has a stable integral lattice.

nodes.title: Noetherian models of an integral perfectoid ring
nodes.statement: Let R be a p-torsion-free integral perfectoid ℤ_p-algebra with R = (R[1/p])°, and put X = Spa(R[1/p],R). Choose the filtered system of finite-type ℤ_p-subalgebras R_j of R, enlarged to their integral closures in R_j[1/p]. Write R_j^h for the henselization along p. The inclusions R_j → R extend uniquely to R_j^h → R, and R = colim_j R_j^h as rings. The adic system X_j = Spa(R_j[1/p],R_j) has common ideal of definition (p); its completed colimit presents X. This is approximation data, not a claim that R is Noetherian or that X is an ordinary categorical inverse limit.
proofSteps: R is reduced (Česnavičius 4.3). The integral closure of a finite-type R_j in R_j[1/p] lies in R, because R = (R[1/p])° is integrally closed in R[1/p], and it is finite over R_j because ℤ_p-algebras of finite type are Nagata (EGA IV₂ 7.8.3 (ii)–(iii) and 7.8.6 (ii), as Česnavičius cites; Stacks 0334, 0335); the enlarged stages stay filtered with union R. No node or baseline declaration supplies the Nagata property: it is recorded as a gap; alternatively keep the finite-type R_j as noetherian ring of definition and use its integral closure only as plus ring, which changes neither Spa (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa_integralClosure) nor the henselization R_j^h[1/p].

R is p-adically complete, so (R, pR) is henselian (mathlib:IsAdicComplete.henselianRing); by the universal property of the henselization of pairs (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselisation-of-pairs) R_j → R extends uniquely to R_j^h → R, and since henselization commutes with filtered colimits (Stacks 0A04), colim_j R_j^h = R^h = R.
Every element of R already belongs to a finite-type subalgebra; compatibility gives the asserted filtered colimit. Keep the completion and analytic topology as additional data.

Choose the filtered system of finite-type ℤ_p-subalgebras R_j of R, enlarged to their integral closures in R_j[1/p]. Write R_j^h for the henselization along p. nodes.title: The perfectoid model system is a tilde-limit
nodes.statement: For the model system in perfectoid-noetherian-approximation, X = Spa(R[1/p],R) satisfies X ∼ lim_j X_j: its underlying topological space is the inverse limit of |X_j|, rational subsets are pulled back from a finite stage, and the colimit of finite-stage rings of sections has dense image on rational affinoids. These are the separate topological and density clauses of HuberTildeLimit; no universal mapping property of an ordinary inverse limit is asserted.
proofSteps: (4.10.6): ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/spa-of-colimit-huber-pair (ii)–(iv) for the Huber pairs (R_j[1/p], R_j) with rings of definition R_j and ideals of definition pR_j: Spa(R[1/p], R) → lim_j Spa(R_j[1/p], R_j) is a homeomorphism and every rational subset comes from a finite stage.

X_j is the adic space of the completion (R̂_j[1/p], R̂_j), which has a noetherian ring of definition (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space), and X is an adic space because R[1/p] is perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy).

Density and the tilde-limit: ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/huber-tilde-limit-affinoid-criterion (2) with condition (P2), since colim_j R̂_j/p^n = colim_j R_j/p^n = R/p^n; so X is colimit-presented by the X_j and rational subsets defined at a finite stage have dense colimit of sections.

These are the separate topological and density clauses of HuberTildeLimit; no universal mapping property of an ordinary inverse limit is asserted.

nodes.title: Étale-site descent for the perfectoid model system
nodes.statement: For the system X ∼ lim_j X_j above, qcqs étale X-spaces, their morphisms, finite fibre products and finite covering families descend to some X_j and two descended data agree after a further stage. Thus the qcqs étale site of X is the filtered 2-colimit of the qcqs étale sites of X_j. This is the colimit-presented case of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-topos-of-tilde-limit (Česnavičius footnote 3: noetherian stages, perfectoid completed limit); it is not inferred from the topological part of a tilde-limit alone, and the perfectoid hypothesis enters only through the sheafiness of X and of its rational localisations.
proofSteps: Apply ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/etale-topos-of-tilde-limit (i)–(iv) to the colimit-presented tilde-limit X ∼ lim X_j of perfectoid-model-tilde-limit: X and the X_j are qcqs locally strongly sheafy analytic (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-tate-rings-are-strongly-sheafy; noetherian stages); rational localisations stay colimit-presented (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-base-change (a)) and finite étale descent is the henselian argument of that node, with no perfectoid hypothesis on the stages.

The étale site of X used there (AdicEtaleGeometry:A1) is that of Česnavičius's footnote 2 and Scholze 2012 Definitions 7.1, 7.11 (PerfectoidSpaces:P3/perfectoid-vs-analytic-finite-etale (b), (d)); on the stages it is Huber's (Hub96 2.2.8).
Descend the finite gluing diagrams and covering conditions; refine until their equalities hold.

nodes.title: Finite hypercover data descend through the model system
nodes.statement: For a finite locally constant abelian sheaf G_j on X_j and G its pullback to X, every finite truncation of a qcqs étale hypercover of X together with the coefficient cocycle needed to compute a fixed H^q(X,G) descends to a later X_k. Coboundaries and identifications descend after another refinement. Consequently colim_{k≥j} H^q(X_k,G_k) ≅ H^q(X,G) for every q≥0. This is continuity of cohomology, not commutation with an inverse limit of coefficient groups.

Only finitely many levels and finite diagrams occur for a fixed degree and cocycle; descend them using the 2-colimit site.
Descend the additional data witnessing equality of cocycles to obtain both injectivity and surjectivity.

nodes.title: Canonical logarithmic structure of a semistable formal model
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of ℚ_p, ϖ a uniformizer and k its residue field. Let 𝔛 be a semistable formal O_K-scheme, or a base change of such a scheme from the integers of a subfield (node semistable-formal-scheme), with no quasi-compactness assumption. Import its canonical divisorial log structure M from CR.5. On étale formal opens U, M(U) consists of sections of O_𝔛(U) invertible on U_K; its groupification is identified with O(U_K)× as in CDN §2.1.1. The reduced special fibre Y carries the induced log structure relative to the log point (k,ℕ→k,1↦0). This node identifies the formal analytic carrier with the imported log carrier; it does not define log schemes again.

Apply the semistable canonical-log identification used by CDN, citing Berkovich 1996 Theorem 2.3.1 as an explicit supplier interface.
Restrict the log structure to the special fibre and retain its map to the log point.

Berkovich's identification (CDN's [8, Th. 2.3.1], a preprint) for semistable 𝔛: Zariski-locally an étale U over O_K{X_1,…,X_n}/(X_1⋯X_r − ϖ) is regular, the special-fibre components through a point are the Cartier divisors D_i = (X_i = 0), and a section f invertible on U_K has divisor Σa_iD_i, so f/ΠX_i^{a_i} has trivial divisor and is a unit; hence M = O^×·X^ℕ, the divisorial log structure of CR.5. For base-change charts O_K{X}/(X_1⋯X_r − ϖ_F), e(K/F) > 1, the D_i are not Cartier (at a node X_1X_2 = uϖ_K^e the class of D_1 has order e), so this argument does not apply; there the identification M = O ∩ O[1/p]^× is the log-regular statement to be supplied with the CR.5 request (requests[29]).

nodes.title: Symbols factor through the mod-p-squared log model
nodes.statement: Put (𝔛₂,M₂)=(𝔛,M) modulo p². The mod-p nearby-cycle symbols used in CDN §2.1.1 factor through i^*(M₂^gp)^{⊗q}; the kernel of i^*M^gp → i^*M₂^gp is 1+p²O_𝔛, and a section congruent to 1 modulo p² has zero image in the sheaf R¹Ψℤ/p(1) (for p = 2 only after an étale refinement). This supplies the actual domain of the U/V filtration, without replacing the whole generic fibre by its special fibre.
proofSteps: For p odd, u = 1+p²x is a p-th power in O_𝔛(U): the binomial series Σ binom(1/p,n)p^{2n}x^n converges (valuation n − v_p(n!) → ∞). For p = 2 the series does not converge (5 is not a square in ℤ₂); instead, on the formal étale cover U' = U[y]/(y²+y−x), (1+2y)² = 1+4x, so the Kummer class of u dies in the sheaf R¹Ψℤ/2(1).
Pass to cup symbols and the reduced log groupification.

nodes.statement: Étale locally on 𝔛, a semistable formal chart is the completion of a semistable O_K-scheme T (in the base-change case, of a scheme T étale over Spec(O_F[X_1,…,X_n]/(X_1⋯X_r − ϖ_F)) ⊗_{O_F} O_K, i.e. an étale neighbourhood in Hyodo's 𝒳 ⊗_{O_K} O_L), with the same reduced special fibre Y and the same induced canonical log structure modulo p². For f:X→Y between taut rigid spaces the square of θ_X,θ_Y,f,u(f) commutes, with the canonical pullback identification θ_X^*u(f)^*≅f^*θ_Y^*.

It sends jointly surjective families to jointly surjective families: images of partially proper maps are stable under specialisation, and every point of X specialises from its rank-one generalisation, the rank-one points forming |u(X)| (Zavyalov Lemma A.7 (3)). nodes.title: Overconvergent étale sheaves

Ab_ov(X_et) is the full subcategory of such sheaves. The quantifier includes geometric points with higher-rank plus rings and their specialization maps; it is not only a condition on closed points or on a chosen rank-one subspace.

nodes.title: Maximal stalks detect maps of overconvergent sheaves
nodes.statement: On a locally strongly sheafy analytic adic space X (for instance any rigid space, taut or not), equality of two morphisms between overconvergent abelian sheaves can be checked at geometric points over maximal points of X. A morphism between them is an isomorphism if and only if those maximal geometric stalk maps are isomorphisms. Every geometric point η₂: Spa(C, C⁺) → X receives the specialisation η₁ → η₂ from η₁: Spa(C, O_C) → Spa(C, C⁺) → X, which lies over the unique rank-one generalisation of the support of η₂, and overconvergence transports the stalk test; this does not say that an arbitrary unrelated family of stalk maps extends to a sheaf morphism.

Apply the enough-points criterion on the full adic étale topos.

nodes.title: Relative pure dimension for the trace
nodes.statement: Import dimension of a locally spectral space as the supremum of lengths of strict specialization chains, pure dimension d as dimension d on every nonempty open, and dim(f)=sup_y dim(f⁻¹(y)) from AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/dimension-of-adic-spaces (Huber 1.8.1, verbatim Zavyalov Definition 5.3.1) and A2/relative-dimension-rank-one-fibres (Huber 1.8.7). A morphism has relative pure dimension d when every nonempty fibre has pure dimension d. Smooth partially proper rigid morphisms of relative pure dimensions d,e compose in dimension d+e. For smooth partially proper f between taut rigid spaces of relative pure dimension d, u(f) is smooth of pure dimension d in Berkovich's sense, as Zavyalov uses after Lemma A.8 in the proof of Theorem 5.3.3. These are geometry data, not a new cohomological definition; empty fibres do not become a surjectivity hypothesis.

nodes.title: Top-degree Leray composition

nodes.title: The smooth relative trace in arbitrary dimension
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nontrivially rank-one valued field, n>0 invertible in K and Λ=ℤ/n. (Zavyalov §5 assumes O_K of mixed characteristic (0, p) and allows every n; Berkovich §7.2 needs only n prime to char K and Zavyalov's Appendix A holds for every complete rank-one K, so the construction applies verbatim.) For a smooth partially proper rigid f:X→Y of relative pure dimension d, define t_f:R^{2d}f_!Λ_X(d)→Λ_Y by θ_Y^* of the Berkovich trace on taut affinoid-base neighbourhoods, using α_f. The map has geometric-maximal-fibre compatibility, t_g⊙t_f=t_{g∘f}, the étale counit normalization at d=0, and is surjective when every fibre is nonempty. This is Zavyalov Theorem 5.3.3; it constructs a trace without asserting p-torsion duality.

Transfer the normalized Berkovich trace through θ^* and α_f on each taut piece.
Use the canonical fibre identifications to show agreement of these already constructed sheaf morphisms on overlaps, then glue.
Transfer composition and dimension-zero normalization; surjectivity follows from the Berkovich trace and maximal-point surjectivity.

nodes.title: The ℤ_p trace for smooth proper formal generic fibres
nodes.statement: For a smooth proper morphism f:𝔛→𝔜 of smooth formal O_K-schemes of relative equidimension d, with K of mixed characteristic (0,p) (the export to Guo–Reinecke Theorem 7.16 requires moreover K discretely valued with perfect residue field, their standing hypothesis), construct t_{f_η}:R^{2d}f_{η,*}Ẑ_p(d)→Ẑ_p for the pro-étale sheaf Ẑ_p = lim_r ν^*ℤ/p^r (Guo–Reinecke's coefficients; Zavyalov §5.5) as the composite R^{2d}f_{η,*}Ẑ_p(d) → lim_r ν^*R^{2d}f_{η,*}ℤ/p^r(d) → lim_r ν^*ℤ/p^r of the compatible finite-level traces. nodes.title: The analytic covering of integral lattices
nodes.statement: For an étale ℚ_p-local system V on a k-analytic X, let Lat(V) be the étale sheaf whose sections are finite-free integral ℤ_p-lattices in V, with inclusion after rationalization equal to V. nodes.title: Semistable formal O_K-schemes and their base changes from a subfield
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of ℚ_p with uniformizer ϖ_K. A formal O_K-scheme 𝔛 is semistable if Zariski-locally on 𝔛 there is an étale morphism (node formal-etale-morphism) to Spf(O_K{X_1,…,X_n}/(X_1⋯X_r − ϖ_K)) for some 1 ≤ r ≤ n (CDN §2.1.2). For a subfield F ⊆ K with uniformizer ϖ_F, 𝔛 is a semistable base change from O_F if 𝔛 ≅ 𝔛′ ×_{Spf O_F} Spf O_K with 𝔛′ semistable over O_F (CDN §2.1.1). Every 𝔛 of either class is Zariski-locally étale over some Spf(O_K{X_1,…,X_n}/(X_1⋯X_r − ϖ_F)) (F = K in the first case); this local class is stable under étale morphisms 𝔘 → 𝔛 and Zariski restriction (as is the semistable class; the global base-change class is not evidently so) and is the one the étale-local BKH arguments use. All these formal schemes are locally noetherian (hence of type (S)), flat over O_K, with reduced special fibre 𝔛 ⊗ k. No quasi-compactness is imposed. When K/F is ramified, base changes need not be regular (Hyodo's 𝒳 ⊗_{O_K} O_L), so they are not semistable over O_K.
hypotheses: K/ℚ_p finite; F ⊆ K a subfield (hence also finite over ℚ_p); ϖ_K, ϖ_F uniformizers.
proofSteps: Flatness, reduced special fibre and (for the first class) regularity hold on the standard chart and are preserved by étale maps (formal-etale-morphism).

O_K{X_1,…,X_n}/(X_1⋯X_r − ϖ_K) is a noetherian ϖ-adic ring; étale formal schemes over a locally noetherian one are locally noetherian, hence of type (S) (AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-schemes-of-type-S).

Local description of the base-change class: base change along Spf O_K → Spf O_F of the étale chart maps of 𝔛′ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-fibre-product). Stability of the local class under étale maps: composites of étale maps are étale. The étale-local arguments therefore work in the local class, which contains the étale site of every 𝔛 of either global class.
acceptance: Every node of the formal BKH chain quantifies over the union of the two classes, as CDN §2.1.1 does.
Spf O_K{X,Y}/(XY − ϖ_K) is semistable; Spf O_K{X,Y}/(XY − ϖ_F) with e(K/F) = 2 is in the base-change class only.

api.statement: The local class: Zariski-locally étale over Spf(O_K{X_1,…,X_n}/(X_1⋯X_r − ϖ_F)) for a fixed subfield F; stable under étale maps (of_etale) and containing both global classes.

api.name: FormalScheme.IsSemistableBaseChange
api.statement: 𝔛 ≅ 𝔛′ ×_{Spf O_F} Spf O_K with 𝔛′ semistable over O_F, F ⊆ K.

api.name: FormalScheme.IsSemistable.toBaseChange
api.statement: Semistable over O_K implies the base-change class with F = K.

api.name: FormalScheme.IsSemistableBaseChange.isTypeS
api.statement: Members are locally noetherian, hence of type (S), so λ_𝔛 and d(𝔛) are defined.

api.name: FormalScheme.IsSemistable.completion
api.statement: The ϖ-adic completion of a scheme étale over O_K[X_1,…,X_n]/(X_1⋯X_r − ϖ_K) (CR.5 standard chart) is semistable.

api.name: FormalScheme.standardSemistableChart
api.statement: Spf(O_K{X_1,…,X_n}/(X_1⋯X_r − ϖ_K)) for 1 ≤ r ≤ n.

tests.name: semistableFormal_smooth
tests.statement: For r = 1, O_K{X_1,…,X_n}/(X_1 − ϖ_K) ≅ O_K{X_2,…,X_n}, so every smooth formal O_K-scheme is semistable.

tests.name: semistableFormal_node
tests.statement: Spf(O_K{X,Y}/(XY − ϖ_K)) is semistable, with special fibre Spec k[X,Y]/(XY), two lines meeting in one point.

tests.name: semistableFormal_ramifiedBaseChange
tests.statement: If ϖ_F = uϖ_K² (u ∈ O_K^×), Spf(O_K{X,Y}/(XY − ϖ_F)) lies in the base-change class but is not semistable over O_K: at the origin of the special fibre the maximal ideal (ϖ_K, X, Y) needs three generators in a ring of dimension 2, so it is not regular.

tests.name: semistableFormal_nonreduced
tests.statement: Spf(O_K{X}/(X² − ϖ_K)) is in neither class over O_K: its special fibre Spec k[X]/(X²) is not reduced.

nodes.title: Formal nearby cycles mod p are generated by symbols; the U/V filtration is finite and exhaustive
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 be as in semistable-formal-canonical-log-comparison, e = v_K(p) and q ≥ 0. The symbol map sym_q: i^*(M₂^gp)^{⊗q} → R^qΨ_𝔛ℤ/p(q) (formal-symbols-mod-p-squared) is an epimorphism of étale sheaves on Y, i.e. U⁰ = R^qΨ_𝔛ℤ/p(q). With m₀ = ⌈pe/(p−1)⌉, the chain 0 = U^{m₀} ⊂ V^{m₀−1} ⊂ U^{m₀−1} ⊂ … ⊂ U¹ ⊂ V⁰ ⊂ U⁰ = R^qΨ_𝔛ℤ/p(q) is a finite exhaustive filtration whose successive quotients are the sheaves of CDN Theorem 2.4(1)–(3). This is the form in which CDN §2.2 (Étape 2) use Theorem 2.4.
hypotheses: 𝔛 semistable over O_K or a semistable base change from the integers of a subfield (semistable-formal-scheme); no quasi-compactness.
proofSteps: Surjectivity of a morphism of étale sheaves is local: reduce to an algebraized chart 𝔛 = T^ (semistable-formal-local-algebraization).

On T, i^*R^qj_*ℤ/p(q) is generated locally by symbols: Hyodo (1.6.1) (semistable, including base change to a finite L/K), Bloch–Kato (1.4) in good reduction — the algebraic input of the gap on the algebraic Bloch–Kato–Hyodo supplier.
The completion isomorphism (2.5) commutes with symbols (semistable-algebraic-formal-symbol-comparison), so the formal symbols generate R^qΨ_𝔛ℤ/p(q).
Finiteness and the quotients: formal-bkh-ramification-cutoff and the three graded-piece theorems.
acceptance: q = 1: R¹Ψℤ/p(1)/U¹ is an extension of Ω¹_{Y/k,log} by F_p (CDN Remarque 2.6(1)), now with U⁰ = R¹Ψℤ/p(1).
𝔛 = Spf O_K, q = 1: the stalk (K^ur)^×/((K^ur)^×)^p is generated by Kummer classes of units and of ϖ.

sources.match: CDN use Theorem 2.4 as a finite filtration of the whole of R^jΨF_p(j), i.e. with U⁰ = R^jΨ.
Hyodo: the algebraic sheaves M^q_n are generated locally by symbols (U⁰M^q_n = M^q_n).
Bloch–Kato: the same in good reduction.

requests.need: (A) Limits of fibred coherent topoi and their cohomology (SGA 4 VI 8.2–8.3 and 8.7.7, as used in ECD Proposition 14.9): if a site C is the filtered 2-colimit of coherent sites C_i along continuous finite-limit-preserving functors, every object, morphism and finite covering of C coming from a finite stage, then the topos of C is the projective limit of the fibred topos (C_i~), and for a sheaf F_0 on C_0 with pullbacks F_i and F the map colim_i H^n(C_i, F_i) → H^n(C, F) is bijective (n = 0 for sheaves of sets, n ≤ 1 for sheaves of groups, all n for abelian sheaves). The existing D0 node filtered-colimits-and-cohomology-on-coherent-sites treats filtered colimits of sheaves on one topos, not limits of topoi. (B) Cohomology of a cofiltered limit of spectral spaces along spectral maps: for X = lim X_i and an abelian sheaf F_i on X_i, colim_{j ≥ i} H^n(X_j, F_i|) → H^n(X, F_i|) is bijective (SGA 4 VI 8.7.7; Huber 1993, Proposition 1.1(b)); D0/cofiltered-limits-of-spectral-spaces supplies only the topology.

For an affinoid ring (A, A⁺) with completion (Â, Â⁺): the map Spa(Â, Â⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism identifying rational subsets (Wedhorn Proposition 7.48; Huber 1993 Proposition 3.9), and f ∈ A⁺ iff |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ Spa(A, A⁺) (Wedhorn Proposition 7.52 (1)); neither is a declaration at the pinned Tau Ceti commit (only the rational-localisation homeomorphisms spaLocalizationHomeomorph exist).

Stalks of the structure presheaves of Spa(A, A⁺): O_{X,x} is a local ring whose maximal ideal is the support of v_x (Wedhorn Proposition 8.6; anchor Layer 3.3), and O⁺_{X,x} = {f ∈ O_{X,x} : v_x(f) ≤ 1}, the preimage of the valuation ring k(x)⁺; the pinned tree has rational localisation but no stalks.

(A) The category of (analytic) adic spaces with open subspaces, gluing and morphisms from affinoids, on which A1's sites and the tilde-limit predicate are stated; the pinned tree has Spa and rational localisation but no adic-space category or structure sheaf as a sheaf. (B) The adic space Spa(Â, Â⁺) of a complete Huber pair satisfying Huber's condition (structure sheaf as a sheaf, locally ringed space), which pseudo-adic spaces (Spa(Â, Â⁺), U) and their fibre products with schemes are built on.

(A) Noetherian approximation for qcqs schemes: limits of directed systems with affine transition maps, a finite type morphism of qcqs schemes as a limit of finitely presented ones along closed immersions, and continuity of étale cohomology H^p(lim X_i, colim f_i^{-1}F_i) = colim H^p(X_i, F_i) (Stacks Theorem 59.51.3, Tag 09YQ), used for ind-étale maps such as A → A^h. (B) General-scheme continuity: for a cofiltered limit X = lim X_a of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition maps and a complex F_0 ∈ D^+((X_{a_0})_et) with pullbacks F_a, F, the maps colim_a H^q(X_a, F_a) -> H^q(X, F) are isomorphisms; and its consequences (a) for a pro-open immersion u: X_(s) = X ×_S Spec O_{S,s} -> X, u^* Ru_* ≅ id on D^+; (b) base change of Rh_* along the strict localization S(η̄) -> S (a limit of étale maps) for qcqs h; (c) continuity along S(η̄) = lim over finite separable subextensions. Used for Milnor tubes X_(x̄) ×_S S(η̄), strict localizations of valuation spectra and the discreteness of the Galois action. (C) Nagata compactification X → X̄ → Spec A (open immersion followed by a proper morphism) of a separated morphism of finite presentation over the spectrum of an arbitrary valuation ring A (qcqs, nonnoetherian base), filteredness of the category of such compactifications, and the scheme compact-support cohomology RΓ_c(X_η, −) := RΓ(X̄_η, j_!−) with torsion coefficients, with canonical identifications between compactifications. (D) (RT-AREA-etale/15) Continuity of Hom and of D^b_c along cofiltered limits of qcqs schemes with affine transition maps: colim_a Hom(F_a, G_a) ≅ Hom(F, G) and 2-colim_a D^b_c(X_a, Λ) ≃ D^b_c(lim_a X_a, Λ) for noetherian torsion Λ (Abe Lemma 1.4 form). Used to spread a constructible complex on X_η = lim_{a≠0} X ×_S Spec A[1/a] out to a finite stage.

(A) Scheme étale cohomology inputs (SF.2 integrates the upstream CohomologicalPointCounting scheme-étale suppliers and the ECD scheme contracts SCH_BC, SCH_SHEAVES and SCH_SUPPORT_NOETH, as its stage text says): the Stacks proof of Gabber's theorem 59.82.7 — Lemmas 59.82.1–59.82.6 with their inputs (constructible approximation 59.73.2 and 59.51.4, Section 59.80 on schemes over strictly henselian bases, Lemma 15.11.16) and long exact sequences of torsion étale cohomology; the base change theorems for integral (SGA 4 VIII 5.6) and proper (SGA 4 XII 5.1, Stacks Section 59.91) morphisms; EGA IV 18.1.1 (étale maps lift along closed immersions locally) and 18.10.8 (étale maps to a normal integral scheme with separably closed function field are local isomorphisms); vanishing of positive-degree torsion étale cohomology on spectra of filtered colimits of finite products of a separably closed field. (B) Scheme-level étale cohomology used by the formal/adic comparison, for an arbitrary torsion coefficient ring E (not only torsion prime to the residue characteristics): (a) small étale sites with i^*, j_*, j_!, R⁺j_* on D⁺(−, E) for open/closed immersions; (b) stalks at geometric points as colimits over étale neighbourhoods, strict henselisations O^sh as limits of pointed affine étale neighbourhoods, and (R^q f_* F)_ȳ = H^q(X ×_Y Spec O^sh_{Y,ȳ}, F) for qcqs f; (c) topological invariance of the small étale site for universal homeomorphisms (Stacks 04DZ, 039R) as an equivalence of sites and topoi; (d) Zariski-local lifting of étale morphisms along closed immersions, and spreading out of étale κ(y)-algebras to étale neighbourhoods of y; (e) étale cohomology commutes with cofiltered limits of qcqs schemes along affine transition maps (Stacks 09YQ); (f) constructible sheaves of Λ-modules (Λ noetherian) with their stratification description; (g) étale maps to the spectrum of a strictly henselian local ring have sections through points over the closed point; (h) proper base change, used in acceptance tests only. (C) (catalogued upstream as CohomologicalPointCounting EtaleBaseChange 3-8) Scheme-level étale theory on the carrier mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.smallEtaleTopology: (1) the strict henselization A^sh of a local ring A at a separable closure of its residue field, with its universal property among local maps to strictly henselian rings and the identification Aut_A(A^sh) ≅ Gal(κ^sep/κ); strict localizations X_(x̄) of schemes at geometric points; (2) pullback and derived push-forward of sheaves of Λ-modules along arbitrary morphisms, their base-change morphisms and the pasting law; (3) the stalk formula (R^q h_* G)_x̄ = H^q(X ×_Y Y_(x̄), G) for quasi-compact quasi-separated h; (4) étale base change; (5) proper base change for torsion coefficients along an arbitrary morphism of schemes; (6) topological invariance of the small étale site under universal homeomorphisms (Stacks 04DZ). (D) (catalogued upstream as CohomologicalPointCounting ConstructibleEtale 7-9) Constructible sheaves of B-modules (B noetherian) on quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, not necessarily noetherian: definition by finite partitions into constructible locally closed subschemes; abelian subcategory stable under kernels, cokernels and extensions; generators j_{U!}B for U -> X étale quasi-compact (SGA 4 IX 2.7); every sheaf of ℤ/n-modules is the filtered colimit of its constructible subsheaves; D^b_c and D^b_{ctf} with derived tensor products over ℤ/n -> B; étale cohomological dimension ≤ 2 dim for schemes of finite type over a separably closed field; finiteness and constructibility of higher direct images for proper morphisms over a field. (E) (catalogued upstream as ECD SCH BC) Scheme étale cohomology inputs, stated for the small étale site: (a) proper base change g^{-1}Rf_*E ≅ Rf'_*g'^{-1}E for a proper morphism f and torsion sheaves, complexes of Z/nZ-modules and D^+ with torsion cohomology (Stacks 095T, 0F0C), with its consequence RΓ(X, E) ≅ RΓ(X_s, E|X_s) for X proper over a strictly henselian local ring (Stacks 0A3S in degree 0); (b) invariance of étale cohomology under an extension K/k of separably closed fields: for qcqs X over k and E ∈ D^+ with torsion invertible in k (Stacks 0F0B), and for proper X over k and every torsion sheaf (Stacks 0DDG); (c) finiteness of H^q(X, E) for X proper and of H^q_c(X, E) for X separated of finite type over a separably closed field, with E ∈ D^b_c over a noetherian torsion ring (SGA 4 XIV, SGA 4½ Th. finitude); the Stacks Project proves (c) only for curves (Situation 83.1). (F) (catalogued upstream as ECD SCH SHEAVES) Cohomology with supports on the small étale site of a scheme: the triangles i_*RH_Z(F) → F → Rj_*(F|U) → and RΓ_Z(X, K) → RΓ(X, K) → RΓ(U, K) → for a closed subscheme Z with open complement U (Stacks 09XP, 0A45); topological invariance of the small étale site under universal homeomorphisms (Stacks 04DY), compatibly with base change; pullback maps on étale cohomology along morphisms of schemes. (G) (catalogued upstream as ECD SCH BC) Scheme-level étale facts on the carriers LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.0 uses (integration owner SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2): (a) for a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism j: V → X of schemes, a geometric point x̄ of X with strict henselization X_(x̄), a torsion ring E and K ∈ D^+(V_et, E), the stalk formula (Rj_*K)_x̄ ≅ R^+Γ(V ×_X X_(x̄), K); (b) for an integral morphism π: X' → X, π_* is exact on étale sheaves of E-modules and the base-change morphism g^*π_* → π'_*g'^* is an isomorphism for every g: Z → X; (c) topological invariance: an integral, universally injective, surjective morphism induces an equivalence of small étale sites (Stacks Tag 04DZ), compatible with pullback and pushforward along morphisms of the base. (H) (catalogued upstream as ECD SCH BC) (a) Proper base change for proper finitely presented morphisms and bounded-below torsion complexes over arbitrary affine bases, (Rπ_*K)|_{Spec A/I} ≅ Rπ_{0*}(K|), obtained from the noetherian case by limits; (b) local acyclicity of smooth morphisms: for 𝒫 smooth over a valuation ring V with algebraically closed fraction field and L locally constant constructible with torsion invertible on V, the nearby cycles i^*Rj_*L equal L on the special fibre; (c) topological invariance of the étale site under universal homeomorphisms (Spec(C⁺/ϖ) versus Spec(C⁺/C°°)). (I) (catalogued upstream as ECD SCH SUPPORT NOETH) Compactly supported pushforward Rπ_! for separated finitely presented morphisms, independent of the compactification, extended from noetherian bases to limits of them (the bases Spec(C⁺/ϖ)), with the values RΓ_c(A¹_κ, μ_n) = ℤ/n[−2] and RΓ_c(G_{m,κ}, ℤ/n) over algebraically closed κ and the compactification W ⊆ W̄ of a separated curve over a field. Review note (REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0): Mathlib at the pinned commit already has the points of the small étale site of a scheme attached to geometric points (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.pointSmallEtale), their conservativity (isConservativeFamilyOfPoints_pointSmallEtale'), the HasEnoughPoints instance and the Grothendieck abelian sheaf categories of smallEtaleTopology; items (B)(b) and (C) ask only for strict henselisations as limits of étale neighbourhoods and the stalk formula for R^q f_*, on those declarations.

A complete nonarchimedean field k is strongly noetherian (k⟨T₁, …, Tₙ⟩ is noetherian, BGR 5.2.6), so that by Tau Ceti IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType.isStronglyNoetherian every Tate algebra topologically of finite type over k is strongly noetherian and Spa(A, A°) is an adic space satisfying Huber's condition; the propagation to topologically finite type algebras is already in the pinned Tau Ceti.

(A) The trait nearby-cycle object RΨ_η(K) := ī^*R⁺j̄_*(K|_{X_η̄}) on X_s ×_s η with its continuous Gal(η̄/η)-action and the triangle sp^*i^*K → RΨ_η(K_η) → RΦ(K) →, defined for an arbitrary torsion coefficient ring E (SGA 7 XIII 2.1.2 uses no prime-to-p hypothesis in the definition), the prime-to-p hypothesis being attached only to the theorems that need it; and its functoriality for the change of trait to the normalisation S̄ = Spec Ā in k(η̄), with the colimit description over finite subextensions that gives continuity of the action. Huber's Corollary 3.5.17 holds for every torsion ring, and H1:formal-adic-comparison identifies Huber's 'complex of vanishing cycles' with this object rather than creating a second trait RΨ. (B) State Ψ_η = ī^*j̄_* (SGA 7 XIII 1.3.2) and its derived functor RΨ_η (2.1.2) for an arbitrary torsion coefficient ring — the derivation 2.1.2 does not use the prime-to-p hypothesis 2.1.1 — keeping that hypothesis only on the theorems that need it (local acyclicity 2.1.5, smooth base change 2.1.7.2, change of trait 2.1.7.5), so that the all-torsion comparison Hub96 3.5.17 is a statement about LPV.0's object for p-torsion coefficients as well.
Continuous cohomology of discrete modules in all degrees and its description as the colimit over finite quotients, used for H^q(P, M) with P pro-p.

The definition of the ℓ-cohomological dimension cd_ℓ(G) of a profinite group (via ℓ-primary torsion discrete modules on Mathlib's continuousCohomology), used to state cd_ℓ(G_K) = cd_ℓ(Gal(K^t/K)) for ℓ ≠ p.

The monodromy operator N (finite logarithm of a unipotent inertia action, with the tame character t_ℓ) defined for an arbitrary finite E[I]-module with unipotent continuous I-action, E = Z/ℓ^n with ℓ ≠ p, and functorial for E[I]-module isomorphisms, so that it transports along the I-equivariant isomorphism H^n(Ȳ, c^*K) ≅ H^n(X_s, RΨ_η K) of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1/lpv-trait-comparison.

Reduction commutes with completed ground-field extension (Bosch, Math. Ann. 229 (1977) §6 Satz 4, as used in Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces, proof of Theorem 3.2.1): for an algebraically closed complete nonarchimedean field k, a complete extension k'/k and a reduced k-affinoid algebra A, with Ã := A°/A°° the reduction, the natural map Ã ⊗_{k̃} k̃' → (A ⊗̂_k k')~ is an isomorphism of k̃'-algebras; in particular Spec of the reduction of A ⊗̂_k k' is connected when Spec Ã is (EGA IV₂ 4.4.4 over the algebraically closed k̃), and Sp(B) is connected iff Spec(B̃) is.

Ground-field extension of quasi-separated rigid spaces over a complete rank-one field K and a complete extension K'/K: X ↦ X ×_K K' glued from Sp(A) ↦ Sp(A ⊗̂_K K') (Conrad, Irreducible components, §3.1 and Appendix), with the compatibility r_{K'}(X ×_K K') ≅ r_K(X) ×_{Spa(K,K°)} Spa(K', K'°) of Huber's functor r, and the consequence of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-topos-equivalence that a quasi-separated rigid space X is connected (no disjoint admissible cover by nonempty admissible opens) iff r_K(X) is connected.

The nodes AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-functor-d and AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison stated for ϖ-adic completions of finitely presented C⁺-schemes with C⁺ ⊆ C an open bounded valuation subring of arbitrary rank (type (S)(b) with s = ϖ): d(Spf C⁺⟨T⟩) = Spa(C⟨T⟩, C⁺⟨T⟩), d(𝒫̂) ≅ 𝒫_C ×_{Spec C} Spa(C, C⁺) for proper 𝒫, and d(𝒰̂) = λ⁻¹(𝒰) for opens 𝒰 of the special fibre.

For KL §1.4: finite-free inverse-system ℤ_p-local systems on schemes; the isogeny category; étale stackification defining ℚ_p-local systems; KL Remark 1.4.7 bounded-lattice moduli with finite étale representability, inclusion and finite sums; effective descent along faithfully finite étale ring maps (Lemma 1.4.8); the global-lattice criterion for normal noetherian schemes (Remark 1.4.9); descent of rational Hom and integral extension classes. These scheme carriers and generic descent are imports, not a second scheme local-system theory in H0.

Strong rational coverings of Spa(A,A⁺) in KL's sense (Definition 2.4.14: finite families of rational subspaces whose relative interiors cover M(A)) and rational localizations encircling a point α ∈ M(A) (KL §2.4, p. 40), for arbitrary adic Banach rings. neededBy: etale-cover-finite-factor-near-analytic-point, preadic-rational-isogeny-descent. Preadic spaces themselves, their affinoids and rational gluing are AdicEtaleGeometry:A1/yoneda-adic-analytic-tate-local and A1/yoneda-adic-open-immersions (narrowed by REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0).

Only the residue: the étale site of an arbitrary analytic preadic space (A1/etale-site-generalized is stated for X an analytic adic space viewed as a Yoneda-adic space) and KL Lemma 8.2.17(b) local factorization for such X. neededBy: etale-cover-finite-factor-near-analytic-point, preadic-local-system-etale-descent. Lemma 8.2.17(a), Theorem 2.6.9 and Spa^Y(A, A⁺)_fét ≃ FÉt(A)^op are already A1/etale-site-generalized and A1/finite-etale-rational-descent (narrowed by REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0).

Generic category-valued descent and stackification on an affinoid basis, with equivalence under common refinement, coherent pullback and descent of morphisms. H0 supplies the integral/rational local-system instances; D0 owns this generic categorical operation.

Berkovich k-analytic spaces (Berkovich 1993 §1) with their underlying topology: Hausdorff, locally compact, locally arcwise connected, connected affinoids arcwise connected (Berkovich 1990 Theorem 3.2.1, used in de Jong Theorem 2.9); the equivalence of Hausdorff strictly k-analytic spaces with taut adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(k, k°) (Huber 1996 Proposition 8.3.1, restated in Scholze 2012 Theorem 2.24), sending M(A) to Spa(A, A°) and finite étale maps to finite étale maps. AdicSpacesPartII:R1 (analytification of schemes) does not cover these; corrected by REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0.

Finite-presentation and finite-étale coefficient descent plus all-degree affine scheme cohomology continuity for colim R_j^h[1/p], as used in Česnavičius 4.10. L2 also owns the RT-AREA-etale/15 Noetherian approximation and Hom/D^b_c continuity consumed by GeneralBasesFourier.

(CR.5:log-algebra) For the standard semistable chart O_K[X_1,…,X_n]/(X_1⋯X_r − ϖ_K) and for its base changes O_K[X]/(X_1⋯X_r − ϖ_F) from a subfield F: the divisorial log structure O ∩ O[1/p]^× with its chart ℕ^r → O, its identification with O ∩ O[1/p]^× for these log regular charts (needed for the base-change charts, whose components are not Cartier), its pullback to O/p² and to the special fibre Y, and compatibility with étale maps and ϖ-adic completion; the sheaves Ω^q_{Y/k} of log differentials of (Y, M_Y) relative to the log point (k, ℕ→k, 1↦0), the log de Rham differential d, dlog: M_Y^gp → Ω¹_{Y/k}, B^q = dΩ^{q−1}, Z^q = ker d and the additive subsheaf Ω^q_{Y/k,log} generated by dlog wedges, with étale pullback. (Sharpened by REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0.)

Zavyalov A.6–A.11 on the Berkovich side: Hausdorff strictly K-analytic spaces and their morphisms; boundaryless morphisms (Temkin's criterion via reductions of germs), proper morphisms via formal models, quasi-étale and quasi-smooth morphisms and the equivalences smooth = quasi-smooth + boundaryless, étale = quasi-étale + boundaryless (Ducros 5.4.8); separatedness of u(f) for separated f; and the equivalence s′ between Hausdorff strictly K-analytic spaces and taut adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K) with |u(X)| = X_max. Supplier: TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0. (Supplier corrected from AdicSpacesPartII:R1 by REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0; relative pure dimension is AdicEtaleGeometry:A2/dimension-of-adic-spaces and A2/relative-dimension-rank-one-fibres.)

The strict Berkovich étale site and strict/full topos comparison used in Zavyalov A.13–A.14, together with the site functor s₀ inducing θ. This extends the existing analytic-site direction and must be assigned as an early A1 Part II interface rather than duplicated as general site foundations here.

For f smooth proper with Y a rigid K-space (K of characteristic 0): inverse limits of epimorphic systems on Y_proét (E2/surjective-system-derived-limit, E2/inverse-limit-relative-epis) applied to (ν^*R^{2d}f_*ℤ/p^r(d))_r, whose transition maps are epimorphisms by the 2d-bound, giving R^{2d}f_{proét,*}Ẑ_p(d) ≅ lim_r ν^*R^{2d}f_*ℤ/p^r(d) and the vanishing of R^{2d+1}f_{proét,*}Ẑ_p(d) used for surjectivity. (Supplier corrected from AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2 by REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0.)

For the classical completion-comparison instance: coherence of derived base-change mates under a map of commutative site squares, including restriction to support. This generic adjunction/coherence proof is imported; the formal/adic square and its support are H1’s instance.

For the proper finite-local-coefficient duality exports: derived tensor/internal-Hom compatibility with exact θ^*, and the finite-coefficient Ext calculation used by Berkovich 7.4.10. D0/E1 own the general derived calculation; H3 owns its classical analytic trace instance. It also covers tensor/internal-Hom compatibility of θ^* for finite locally free coefficient sheaves (moved here from a former D0 request by REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0).

The Grothendieck spectral sequence of a composite G ∘ F of additive left exact functors between abelian categories with enough injectives, F sending injectives to G-acyclic objects: a convergent first-quadrant spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = R^pG(R^qF(A)) ⇒ R^{p+q}(G ∘ F)(A), natural in A, built from Mathlib spectral objects; applied to Rh_* ∘ Rg_* on sites. DiamondsAndVStacks:D0/cech-to-derived-comparison constructs it in its proof but states only the global Leray sequence H^p(X, R^q f_*F) ⇒ H^{p+q}(Y, F). Added by REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0.

For 0 < |q| < 1 over a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field: Tate uniformization G_m^an/q^ℤ ≅ E_q^an, with |G_m^an| simply connected (so G_m^an → E_q^an is the universal topological covering with deck group q^ℤ ≅ ℤ), and the same for a connected affinoid domain of E_q containing the skeleton circle (as in Kedlaya–Liu Example 8.5.17). Added by REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0.

For a finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector space V: GL(L) is an open profinite subgroup of GL(V) for every ℤ_p-lattice L, and a subgroup of GL(V) with compact closure stabilizes a lattice (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 1.4.4: T_{m+1} = G·T_m). Added by REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0; replaces citations of ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1, whose scope is continuous cohomology.

Every point x of an analytic adic space has a unique rank-one (maximal) generalisation, and the generalisations of x form a chain under specialisation (Huber 1996 Lemma 1.1.10; Wedhorn §8.1), compatibly with morphisms of analytic adic spaces. Added by REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0.

coverage.note: Narrowed by RS-05: classical analytic instances of the common sheaf/derived carriers on A1's étale and pro-étale sites (Mathlib sheaves, SheafOfModules, DerivedCategory.Plus, rightDerivedFunctorPlus; D0 Čech/Leray; E1 enhancement), local systems, Huber constructibility, Tate twists, supports and extension by zero, geometric stalks at higher-rank field pairs, the strict-localisation stalk formula, affinoid-local descriptions, Leray, Čech-to-derived, Cartan–Leray, the pro-étale/étale comparison, and the general Huber tilde-limit with separate topological and density conditions, its affinoid criterion, base change and cohomological continuity. Ann. 295) together with the Zariski–Riemann vanishing; the comparison theorems 3.2.1–3.2.3, 3.2.9–3.2.12 are stated with hypotheses from verified excerpts and public restatements (Hansen), their core proofs being Huber 1996 §§3.3–3.4. Every target of the stage text is realised by a node: the form of Hub96 Theorem 4.1.1(c) used in ECD Lemma 16.3, with extension by zero from quasicompact opens and the surjectivity condition (geometric-field-pair-extension, surjectivity-criterion-for-field-pair-extensions, cohomology-over-geometric-field-pairs, invariance-for-affinoids-of-finite-type); approximation of perfectoid affinoids by affinoids of topologically finite type and, in characteristic p, by their p-finite perfections, with the tilde-limit / perfectoid-limit distinction (finite-type-approximation-of-perfectoid-affinoids, field-extension-of-finite-type-approximations); finite-stage descent of the quasicompact open and passage to the cohomological limit (invariance-for-perfectoid-affinoids); ECD Lemma 16.3 itself (extension-by-zero-over-geometric-field-pairs); geometric-connectedness invariance as separate theorems with proofs (connectedness-via-maximal-generalisations, geometric-connectedness-of-finite-type-spaces, geometric-connectedness-of-perfectoid-base-change). Every target of the stage is realised by a node; Huber's reduction of 4.1.1(c) from the algebraizable tube case to arbitrary affinoids, plus rings and quasicompact opens (Hub96 §4.1 only) is a gap.

67 nodes cover every target of the stage text (38 for the curve stage text, the rest the general smooth trace and duality proposed for a suffix H3:smooth-duality): Huber's proper-support direct image on the classical eligible class (taut, compactifiable, universal compactification, sections with proper support, R⁺f_! = R⁺f̄_! ∘ j_!), pseudo-adic support subsets implemented internally, independence of the factorisation, composition, the proper and étale cases, localisation (open–closed triangle and quasi-compact exhaustion), proper base change for extension by zero and for arbitrary base maps, base change and projection formula for R⁺f_!, finite cohomological dimension (Hub96 5.5.8); for smooth curves over Spa(C, C⁺) the flat quasi-finite trace, the henselian comparison and formal-model transfer, the relative ball computation, the local residue computation, the trace (Hub96 7.2.2) with its normalisation and compatibilities with finite étale maps, restrictions, base change and the algebraic trace, Poincaré duality (Hub96 7.5.3) in a form without any right adjoint, the open-extension-by-zero compatibility of ECD Proposition 23.10(iii), finiteness and the perfect pairing. The added public Zavyalov/Berkovich chain gives θ/overconvergence support comparison, the rigid relative 2d bound, the arbitrary-dimensional smooth trace and its normalizations, prime-to-residue proper duality and finiteness with local-system coefficients, and the Guo–Reinecke ℤ_p normalization export. The trace can use p-power coefficients in mixed characteristic, while classical duality retains coefficients invertible in O_K. The new results use O_K and do not settle arbitrary C⁺.

Proper base change for non-algebraizable proper adic spaces (Hub96 4.4.3), and the general higher-rank-point/compactifiable cohomological-dimension assertions (5.3.11, 5.5.8), remain beyond the old formal-model/ball cases and the new partially proper rigid 2d bound.
Gluing and properness of the universal compactification (Hub96 5.1.5, 5.1.6, 5.1.14) and the Huber–Berkovich comparison (§8.3) are gaps.
Close the explicitly requested integral inverse-limit trace proof and relative tensor/Hom/base-change coherence; read the Huber proofs imported by Zavyalov A.15/A.18 and 5.3.2.
Invariance under surjective extensions Spa(C′, C′⁺) → Spa(C, C⁺) for proper pushforward with arbitrary torsion coefficients (Hub96 4.3.2; gap), beyond the affinoid j_!M case supplied by H2.
The non-quasi-compact R⁺f_! statements (quasi-compact exhaustion, general composition) for arbitrary coefficients (Hub96 §§5.3–5.4; gap); for n invertible in O⁺ they follow from Zavyalov Theorem 9.4.

gaps.title: Huber Proposition 2.4.4 for arbitrary tilde-limits (finite étale descent)
gaps.detail: For a tilde-limit X ∼ lim X_i of qcqs locally noetherian analytic adic spaces whose affinoids are not known to be colimit-presented (plus rings congruent to colim A_i⁺ modulo every power of ϖ), the descent of finite étale algebras from X to a finite stage — hence the identification of the étale topos of X with the projective limit, and Huber Corollary 2.4.6 in full generality — is proved only in Huber 1996 §2.4, which is not public. Scholze 2012 Theorem 7.17 transcribes the proof for perfectoid X; Scholze–Weinstein Conjecture 2.4.6 records the general statement as a conjecture. Public proofs cover completed colimits, strict localisations and their base changes (the colimit-presented case), which is every use inside H0.

gaps.title: Huber Remark 2.4.3: base change of arbitrary tilde-limits
gaps.detail: Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 2.4.3 (Y ∼ lim Y_j for any map Y_i → X_i) is proved by reference to Huber 1996 Remark 2.4.3. H0 proves the statement for colimit-presented tilde-limits and maps topologically of finite type or étale; the general statement (used through PerfectoidSpaces P7 for perfectoid towers, where P7 supplies its own proof) has no public proof. Review note (REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0): AdicSpacesPartII:R5/tilde-limit-base-change plans Huber Remark 2.4.3 (ii) (base change of qcqs tilde-limits along maps locally of weakly finite type) with a proof sketch; it depends on H0 (it cites H0/tilde-limits-and-cohomological-continuity for Remark 2.4.3 (i), whose criterion is now the API item AdicSpace.IsTildeLimit.of_bijective of H0/huber-tilde-limit), so H0 cannot cite it; what remains open here is Scholze–Weinstein 2.4.3's generality of arbitrary maps. With the corrected proof, H0/tilde-limit-base-change (a) holds for any adic morphism of complete Tate pairs with sheafy completed tensor products.

gaps.title: Identification with Huber's pseudo-adic étale sites and constructibility
gaps.detail: Huber defines pseudo-adic spaces and their étale sites (Hub96 §§1.10, 2.3) and constructible sheaves on them (Hub96 §2.7, Definition 2.7.2, Lemmas 2.7.3, 2.7.11); these texts are not public. H0 defines the étale site of (X, S) as (X_ét, J_S) and constructibility by locally closed constructible stratifications (after ECD Definition 20.1 and the restatements of Bhatt–Hansen and Hansen). The agreement of these definitions with Huber's, needed to import Hub96 statements on pseudo-adic spaces and constructible sheaves (H1:formal-adic-comparison 3.5.3–3.5.6 and step IX of 3.6.1; H4 6.2.2), is not verified against the source.

gaps.title: Continuity and stalk formula for pseudo-adic tilde-limits
gaps.detail: Huber Corollary 2.4.6 and Proposition 2.6.1 are stated for pseudo-adic spaces; H0 proves the adic versions (S = |X|) for colimit-presented tilde-limits. The pseudo-adic versions (for example (Spa A, U) ∼ lim of rational neighbourhoods for a pro-special U, used by H1:henselian 3.2.1) rest on Hub96 §2.4–§2.6 and on the identification gap above.

gaps.title: Density of colim O(V_i) in O(V) for an arbitrary affinoid V of a tilde-limit
gaps.detail: The PerfectoidSpaces P8 request asks for density of lim→ O(V_i) in O(V) for a tilde-limit of affinoids. H0 supplies it when V is a rational subset defined at a finite level of an affinoid with global density (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/tilde-limit-density-rational-restriction), in particular for colimit-presented systems; for an arbitrary affinoid V ∼ lim V_i the density condition of the definition is local and the global statement is not derived. For perfectoid V the good-affinoid theory of PerfectoidSpaces P7 supplies it. Review note (REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0): PerfectoidSpaces:P8/closed-loci-in-towers cites only the stage ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0; it should cite H0/huber-tilde-limit and, for density at finite-level rational V, H0/tilde-limit-density-rational-restriction (b).

gaps.title: Huber 1996 §§3.3–3.4 (Theorem 3.3.3, Lemmas 3.4.2–3.4.5, Appendix A.5) are not public
gaps.detail: The comparison morphism γ (the reduction to discrete affinoid rings 3.4.4–3.4.5 and the equivalence between the étale topoi of X‴ = V ×_𝒰 X′ and X′ over the tube V ⊆ Spa(A(U), (G^h)^c)) and the proof that γ^* is bijective under condition (b) of 3.2.10 (Theorem 3.3.3 and Lemmas 3.4.2–3.4.3 on primary generalisations) are only in Huber's book. The reviewed decomposition read the set-up of 3.3.3, the statements of 3.4.2–3.4.3 and the derivation of 3.2.12 (verified excerpt p. 193), not the conclusion of 3.3.3 nor the proofs. Public partial substitutes: Hansen, Theorem 1.7 (the case U = Spa A for affinoid rigid spaces, from the constant case) and the complete case U = Spa(A, A⁺), where γ is the canonical morphism. What closes it: a public restatement of 3.3.3 (for instance in Huber's habilitation or in subsequent literature) or a direct proof from affine-henselian-comparison-3-2-5, zariski-riemann-cohomology-vanishing and strict-localisation-stalk-formula.

gaps.title: Proof steps (1)–(4) of Huber 1996 Proposition/Definition 3.1.12 (saturated triples) are not public
gaps.detail: Independence of A(U) from the presentation and from (B, P), the presheaf property and functoriality rest on: (1) (X^c)^h ≅ (X^h)^c; (2) recovery of L and M from V(X) for henselian saturated triples; (3) the universal property of the saturated henselization among henselian saturated triples Z with im V(f) ⊆ r^{-1}(U) (verified excerpt); (4) r^{-1}(U) is the set of primary generalisations of U. The inputs (valuation spectra, the retraction r: Spv A^▷ → Spv(A^▷, Q)) are public (Huber 1993, Math. Z. 212), the four steps are only in Huber 1996.

Z. 1994 [Hu4, 3.4.11]) and Example 3.2.4 (acyclicity of relative closed and open polydiscs for prime-to-p torsion; its open-polydisc part uses Huber 1996, 3.9.2) have neither a verified excerpt nor a public restatement in the library; Berkovich's IHÉS paper proves only the open-polydisc analogue for Berkovich spaces. Under the source rule they are recorded here and in coverage; the disc computations belong to ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H4.

Next action: obtain a public treatment of cohomology of henselian tubes (Fujiwara, 'Theory of tubular neighborhood in étale topology', Duke Math. J. 80 (1995)) and restate steps (V)–(IX) from it, or read Hub96 §§2.5–2.7 and §3.3–3.4 and record their statements as nodes of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H0/H1:henselian.

Their proofs (Hub96 §§3.3–3.4) are recorded as a gap of ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H1:henselian/relative-comparison-3-2-9-3-2-12; this packet only consumes the statements.

gaps.title: Berkovich's public comparison theorems are for Berkovich spaces over rank-one bases
gaps.detail: Berkovich 1994 Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.3 state i^*(R^q j_*F) ≅ R^qθ(F^) and R^qΨ_η(F) ≅ R^qΨ_η(F^) for torsion sheaves on schemes locally finitely presented over a henselian valuation ring of rank ≤ 1, for Berkovich analytic generic fibres. They support the rank-one (β) case of 3.5.13 and 3.5.16–3.5.17 as public restatements but do not replace the adic proofs: transporting them to d(X^) needs the comparison of étale topoi of Berkovich spaces and adic spaces (Hub96 §8.3, not public) and they do not cover higher-rank microbial bases or case (α). Next action: record a public comparison of étale topoi of good Berkovich spaces with taut adic spaces (Huber 1996 §8.3 has no public restatement in the library) or keep the adic proofs as the route.

gaps.title: Hub96 §4.2 is not public
