The quadruple, RΨ_L, its Galois action and base-change map, 4.2.3, 4.2.4 and 4.2.5 are stated from public restatements: Orgogozo (Introduction; Remarque 4.4, which says Théorème 1.1 recovers Proposition 4.2.4 of [Hub96] and describes the scope of Huber's proof), Illusie (Remark 3.3(c)), Hansen–Zavyalov (Lemma A.4.3: the i^*Rj_* construction coincides with [Hub96, Section 4.2] over a henselian rank-one valuation ring). The exact Hub96 wording (the letter L in RΨ_L, taken here as a separable closure of k(η); the precise hypotheses of 4.2.3–4.2.5) is not verified against the book. Next action: a reviewer with the book checks pp. 240–253 against these nodes.

gaps.title: Hub96 4.2.3 henselian-localisation argument
gaps.detail: The identification of Milnor-tube and Milnor-fibre cohomology over a valuation base (comparison with geometric η) is publicly stated only as a consequence of Orgogozo's Théorème 5.1 plus the section of a modification over a valuative scheme. Huber's own argument ('henselian localization', 4.2.3) is not public. Next action: read Hub96 4.2.3 and its proof.

gaps.title: Hub96 induction on generic-fibre dimension via Gauss valuations
gaps.detail: The stage's proof plan reduces 4.2.4/4.2.5 by induction on dim X_η, fibring over projective space and passing to strictly henselized Gauss valuation rings at generic points of special fibres (gauss-valuation, gauss-extension-tame-inertia-comparison). The exact induction step (which fibration, which base change of quadruples, how the tame comparison enters) is only in Hub96 §4.2 and is not publicly restated; Orgogozo's public proof uses a different induction (de Jong's plurinodal fibrations). Next action: read the proof of Hub96 4.2.4.

gaps.title: Hub96 4.2.10 Galois-surjectivity/defectless calculation
gaps.detail: Only the tame part is supported publicly: along a strictly henselized Gauss extension the tame quotients agree (gauss-extension-tame-inertia-comparison, from Gabber–Ramero 6.2.5, 6.2.17, 6.2.18). Whether Gal(E^s/E) -> Gal(K^s/K) is surjective, and the defectless hypothesis under which Hub96 4.2.10 proves it, are not public; without it the tame comparison applies only to modules on which wild inertia acts trivially. Next action: read Hub96 4.2.10.

gaps.title: Hub96 4.2.5 controlling constructible submodule (pp. 249–250)

gaps.title: Public alternative route: Orgogozo's modification theorem
gaps.detail: The statements of 4.2.3 (tube = fibre), 4.2.4 (base change, even for non-dominant T) and 4.2.5 (constructibility, for B = ℤ/n) follow publicly from Orgogozo's Théorèmes 1.1, 5.1 and 6.1 together with the fact that a modification of the spectrum of a valuation ring has a section (Orgogozo Remarque 4.4; Illusie Remark 3.3(c)). That route rests on de Jong's alterations (plurinodal fibrations), Gabber's lemma, cohomological descent for proper hypercoverings and Gruson–Raynaud flattening. De Jong's alterations are owned by AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5, which consumes this stage, so importing the route here would create a stage cycle; no other roadmap owns Orgogozo's theorem. It is therefore not used as a proof step. Placing Orgogozo's theorem and the alteration inputs in a stage upstream of both L5 and this stage would make the route available. Review correction (REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0): Orgogozo's essential input is de Jong's plurinodal-fibration theorem ([dJ97] Families of curves and alterations, Theorem 5.10; Illusie Lemma 4.2.1 and Orgogozo's introduction), which no stage preceding H1:valuation-nearby-cycles plans; AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L5 plans de Jong 1996 Theorems 4.1 and 6.5, not [dJ97, 5.10]. Lu–Zheng arXiv:1712.10216v7 Example 4.26(2) states the general Ψ-goodness publicly, by the same route.

Next action: obtain Hub96 §4.1 or a public account of its reduction; or reduce (c) to rational U by Mayer–Vietoris for extension by zero and treat rational U, (b) and (a) through the pseudo-adic and henselian comparisons of H1:henselian and H1:formal-adic-comparison.

gaps.title: Proper base change at the closed point of Spa(C, C⁺) for non-algebraisable proper spaces (Hub96 Proposition 4.4.3)
gaps.detail: RΓ(X, j'_!F) = 0 for proper X over Spa(C, C⁺) and F vanishing on the pseudo-adic closed fibre is Hub96 Proposition 4.4.3, quoted by Zavyalov (proof of Proposition 9.3). The case of X = d(𝒫̂) for a proper C⁺-scheme 𝒫 and algebraic sheaves is proved here from Hub96 3.5.14–3.5.16 (H1:formal-adic-comparison) and henselian proper base change; this covers P¹ and projective curves. gaps.title: Cohomological dimension of proper pushforward from compactifications and over higher-rank points (Hub96 Propositions 5.3.11 and 5.5.8)
gaps.detail: The bound R^q f_! = 0 for q > 2d is restated by ECD (5.5.8 for the ball) and Zavyalov (5.3.11); the rank-one absolute bound is Hub96 2.8.3 as restated by Hansen and Berkovich 5.3.8. The passage to the non-locally-of-finite-type compactification X̄ and to closed fibres over higher-rank points Spa(C, C⁺) is only in Hub96. For the relative ball and P¹ over any Spa(C, C⁺) the bound is proved directly by formal-model transfer (node relative-ball-compact-support). Review (REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0): Wider than recorded. lower-shriek-cohomological-dimension presented the rank-one case as proved from Hub96 2.8.3 and the open–closed triangle; it is not (X̄ is not locally of finite type, and the triangle needs the cohomological dimension of X̄ and of its pseudo-adic boundary, i.e. Hub96 5.3.11). Only the relative ball and P¹ (relative-ball-compact-support) are proved directly; partially-proper-relative-dimension-vanishing (G10) imports 5.3.11 through Zavyalov 5.3.2. Transitive consumers through lower-shriek-cohomological-dimension: proper-support-direct-image (unbounded extension), flat-quasi-finite-trace (R^qφ_! = 0), curve-trace (derived trace), curve-poincare-duality (amplitudes), curve-cohomology-finiteness.

gaps.title: Huber–Berkovich comparison (Hub96 Proposition 8.3.1, Lemma 8.1.8, Theorem 8.3.5)
gaps.detail: The equivalence between taut adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(k, k°) and Hausdorff strictly k-analytic Berkovich spaces (restated by Scholze 2012, Theorem 2.24) and the agreement of étale cohomology for overconvergent sheaves (restated by Hansen) are used to import Berkovich's local structure of smooth curves (3.6.1–3.6.2) and his cohomology computations for affinoid and proper curves. Their proofs are in Hub96 §8.3 only. Alternative: reprove the local structure of smooth adic curves over Spa(C, O_C) directly from semistable reduction (Bosch–Lütkebohmert) on the adic side.

gaps.title: Trace isomorphism and Poincaré duality over higher-rank points Spa(C, C⁺) for curves without local smooth formal models (Hub96 Theorems 7.2.2 and 7.5.3, plus-ring case)
gaps.detail: Over Spa(C, O_C) the trace, its isomorphism property and Poincaré duality are proved by transplanting Berkovich §§6–7. Over Spa(C, C⁺) with C⁺ ≠ O_C, the trace is defined formally from the generic point, and constancy of R²f_!μ_n (hence the trace isomorphism) is proved for tubes of smooth C⁺-models (balls, discs, annuli, P¹) by formal-model transfer. The Berkovich-style duality proof needs, over Spa(C, C⁺), the trace isomorphism for arbitrary connected étale neighbourhoods V → Y with connected fibres and the effacement lemma with local algebraisation; both are Hub96-only. This is exactly ECD's appeal 'In this case, the result follows from [Hub96, Theorem 7.5.3]' for X = Spa(C, C⁺). Zavyalov's foundational paper announces a companion paper [Zav22] with a 'formal' proof of Poincaré duality in non-archimedean geometry; it was not read, and a proof through a right adjoint Rf^! would not be admissible for this stage. Review (REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0): The detail says constancy of R²f_!μ_n is proved for 'tubes of smooth C⁺-models (balls, discs, annuli, P¹)'. formal-model-transfer treats only tubes λ⁻¹(𝒰) of opens of a smooth special fibre (good-reduction affinoids: the ball, the circle {|T| = 1}, P¹); open discs follow by exhaustion by balls, but annuli of positive width have no good reduction and are not covered. Correct the list to 'balls, the unit circle, P¹, and open discs by exhaustion'. The detail correctly says duality over Spa(C, C⁺), C⁺ ≠ O_C, is unproved even for the relative ball; the coverage text should say the same (see questions).

gaps.title: Invariance under surjective extensions Spa(C', C'⁺) → Spa(C, C⁺) for proper pushforward (Hub96 Corollary 4.3.2)
gaps.detail: Zavyalov's proof of Lemma 9.1(3) reduces base change for Rf_* to Hub96 Corollary 4.3.2. The invariance of étale cohomology under extension of algebraically closed affinoid fields belongs to ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology:H2 (Hub96 4.1.1(c) in ECD Lemma 16.3's form); whether H2's statement covers proper spaces over Spa(C, C⁺) and their pseudo-adic closed fibres must be checked against H2's nodes. The dependency adds an internal stage edge H2 → H3. Review (REV-ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0): Exact H2 suppliers exist: H2/invariance-for-affinoids-of-finite-type (affinoids of topologically finite type over C, sheaves j_!M with M a ℤ/n-module, n prime to p, U quasi-compact open) and H2/cohomology-over-geometric-field-pairs (iii) (pullback = base-change map). With a finite affinoid cover and Čech this gives invariance for proper X over Spa(C, C⁺) with these coefficients; arbitrary torsion sheaves (needed for base change of Rf_* of an arbitrary sheaf) still need a dévissage that no node writes, so the gap narrows but stays. No cycle: the H2 nodes depend only on H0/H1. The roadmap stage H3 does not list H2 in requires and there is no H2 → H3 stage edge; add it as the detail says.

Math. 91 (1988), §1 (K henselian discretely valued of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field, 𝒳/O_K semistable, M^q_{n,L} = i_L^*R^qj_{L*}ℤ/pⁿ(q) for every finite L/K, which is CDN's base-change case): symbols generate (1.6.1); gr⁰ (1.7.1); p ∤ m (1.7.2); p | m (1.7.3); U^{e′}M^q_1 = 0 (1.7.4, endpoint included); ω^q are log differentials relative to the log point.
